passages.title: A Brief History of Humans and Food

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: A Brief History of Humans and Food

source.text: A Brief History of Humans and Food

translation.text: 人类与食物简史

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: During the journey from our hunter-gatherer ancestors to the present day, there have been three seismic changes that have impacted the food we eat: the discovery of cooking, the emergence of agriculture, and the invention of methods of preserving food.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 人类从以狩猎采集为生的祖先一路发展至今，期间有三次巨大变革深刻影响了我们所吃的食物：烹饪的发现、农业的兴起，以及食物保存方法的发明。

source.text: During the journey from our hunter-gatherer ancestors to the present day, there have been three seismic changes that have impacted the food we eat: the discovery of cooking, the emergence of agriculture, and the invention of methods of preserving food.

translation.text: 人类从以狩猎采集为生的祖先一路发展至今，期间有三次巨大变革深刻影响了我们所吃的食物：烹饪的发现、农业的兴起，以及食物保存方法的发明。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The 19th-century scientist Charles Darwin thought that cooking, after language, was the greatest discovery made by man. All of us eat some raw food, such as fruit and vegetables, but the great majority of food we consume is cooked. Cooking can turn plants that are inedible into edible food by destroying toxic chemicals that plants often manufacture to protect themselves against attack by insects or other herbivorous animals. These toxic chemicals are referred to as “plant secondary compounds” because they are not directly involved in the plant’s normal growth, development, and reproduction, and are produced purely as chemical defenses. They give many of the plants we consume, such as coffee or Brussels sprouts, their bitter taste.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 19世纪的科学家达尔文（Charles Darwin）认为，烹饪是人类仅次于语言的最伟大发现。我们每个人都会吃一些生食，例如水果和蔬菜，但我们食用的绝大多数食物都是熟食。烹饪可以破坏植物常为抵御昆虫或其他食草动物的侵害而产生的有毒化学物质，从而使原本不能食用的植物变得可以食用。这些有毒化学物质被称为“植物次生化合物”，因为它们不直接参与植物正常的生长、发育和繁殖，而完全是作为化学防御物质产生的。正是这些物质使我们食用的许多植物，例如咖啡或抱子甘蓝，带有苦味。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Cooked food is often more digestible because heat breaks down tough cellulose cell walls in plants or tough connective tissue in animals. Chewing raw turnip, a plate of uncooked rice, or a raw leg of lamb is much harder work than eating the cooked equivalent. The energy expended in chewing to break down the tough material is replaced by energy from the fuel used in cooking the food, so the ratio of energy gained to energy expended by the body is greater when food is cooked.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 熟食往往更容易消化，因为加热会分解植物中坚韧的纤维素细胞壁，或动物体内坚韧的结缔组织。咀嚼生芜菁、一盘生米或一条生羊腿，要比吃相应的熟食费力得多。咀嚼并分解这些坚韧食材原本需要人体消耗能量；烹饪后，完成这项工作所需的能量改由烹饪食物所用的燃料提供。因此，食物煮熟后，人体获得的能量与自身消耗的能量之比更高。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Until the development of agriculture, hunter-gatherers spent up to seven hours a day gathering food. This all began to change around 10,500 years ago with the advent of farming, which led to dramatic changes in human societies. People began to create a variety of new tools to aid survival, and in turn, populations increased in size. These changes led to the possibility of specialization of different tasks within society. Around this time, writing became more sophisticated and allowed people to maintain records of the harvest and taxes. Eventually, formalized structures of government were established as people settled in one area.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在农业发展起来以前，狩猎采集者每天要花多达7小时采集食物。大约10,500年前，农耕的出现开始改变这一切，并给人类社会带来了巨大变化。人们开始制造各种有助于生存的新工具，人口规模也随之扩大。这些变化使社会内部对不同任务进行专业分工成为可能。大约在这一时期，文字变得更加完善，使人们能够保存收成和税收记录。最终，随着人们在固定地区定居，正式的政府体制得以建立。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The arrival of agriculture meant that, for the first time, our ancestors had more food than they could eat immediately. This, combined with the seasonality of production, led them to discover methods of preserving food: smoking, drying, adding acid by fermentation, or adding salt. These four methods all share one feature in common—they make the food a more hostile environment for bacteria that can cause it to spoil. They also tend to slow down natural chemical reactions in the food that would cause decay.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 农业的出现意味着，人类祖先第一次拥有了多得无法立即吃完的食物。再加上生产具有季节性，这促使他们发现了保存食物的方法：熏制、干燥、通过发酵增加酸度，或加盐。这四种方法有一个共同点——它们都会使食物成为一个更不利于细菌生存的环境，而这些细菌会导致食物变质。它们也往往会减缓食物中那些会引发腐坏的自然化学反应。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Although foods today are still preserved in these ancient ways, two more recent methods of preserving food have become more common: canning and freezing. Canning was invented by a Frenchman, Nicolas Appert, in the early 19th century. He sealed food in bottles fabricated from glass and then heated them in boiling water to cook the contents. Appert’s method had great advantages over older methods of food preservation: it could be applied to a wide range of foods, and the flavor and texture were similar to freshly cooked products. His idea was soon copied by an Englishman, Peter Durand. Until this point, containers had been too heavy to be widely used, but Durand produced the first ones which were lightweight and resistant to damage. Two years later, in 1812, two Englishmen, Bryan Donkin and John Hall, started the commercial canning of food, although the real rise in popularity of canning had to wait until the invention of the can opener in 1855. Until then, cans were opened with a chisel and hammer. Canning is an extremely effective way of preserving food: one can containing meat, dating back to 1824, was opened in 1939, and the contents were still in good condition.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 尽管如今人们仍用这些古老方式保存食物，但另外两种较新的食物保存方法已经变得更为常见：罐藏和冷冻。19世纪初，法国人 Nicolas Appert 发明了罐藏法。他把食物密封在玻璃瓶中，再把瓶子放进沸水中加热，将其中的食物煮熟。与较早的食物保存方法相比，Appert 的方法具有显著优势：它可以用于多种食物，而且食物的风味和质地与刚烹制好的食品相似。他的想法很快被英国人 Peter Durand 仿效。在此之前，容器一直过于沉重，无法广泛使用；而 Durand 制造出了第一批既轻便又不易损坏的容器。两年后的1812年，两名英国人 Bryan Donkin 和 John Hall 开始对食品进行商业罐藏，不过罐藏法要到1855年开罐器发明后才真正流行起来。在那以前，罐头要用凿子和锤子打开。罐藏是一种极其有效的食物保存方法：一只可追溯到1824年的肉罐头在1939年被打开时，其中的食物状态依然良好。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In the 21st century, the dominance of canning as a method of food preservation has been overtaken by freezing. Chilling food to keep it fresh is an old idea. The earliest mentions of icehouses, thick-walled buildings, half underground, date back to 1700 BC in northwest Iran. In early 16th-century Italy, water was mixed with chemicals to lower its freezing point to -18 degrees Celsius. Several centuries later, frozen fish and other goods were transported by ship from Australia to England. However, the modern frozen food industry was started in the 1920s by an American, Clarence Birdseye. While on a fishing trip with the Inuit in the Canadian Arctic, Birdseye observed that rapid freezing creates smaller ice crystals and therefore causes less damage to food—a discovery he had not expected. Nevertheless, the major growth in demand for frozen food came with the arrival of freezers in ordinary people’s homes. The advantages of frozen over canned food include the fact that the flavor and consistency are often identical to the fresh product, and freezing can be used to preserve a wide variety of foods.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 到了21世纪，罐藏作为食物保存方法的主导地位已被冷冻取代。通过降温来保持食物新鲜，是一种古老的做法。有关冰窖的最早记载来自伊朗西北部，可追溯到公元前1700年；冰窖是一种墙壁厚实、半埋于地下的建筑。16世纪初，在意大利，人们把水与化学物质混合，使其冰点降至-18摄氏度。几个世纪后，冷冻鱼类和其他货物用船从澳大利亚运往英国。然而，现代冷冻食品产业是由美国人 Clarence Birdseye 于20世纪20年代开创的。Birdseye 在加拿大北极地区与因纽特人一同捕鱼时观察到，快速冷冻会形成更小的冰晶，因而对食物造成的损害较小——这一发现出乎他的意料。尽管如此，冷冻食品需求的大幅增长，是随着冰柜进入普通家庭而出现的。与罐藏食品相比，冷冻食品的优势包括：其风味和质地往往与新鲜食品完全相同，而且冷冻可用于保存种类繁多的食物。

source.text: A survivor’s story

translation.text: 幸存者的故事

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One native bird in New Zealand that has managed to survive the introduction of non-native species
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 新西兰一种在外来物种引入后仍成功存活下来的本土鸟类

source.text: One native bird in New Zealand that has managed to survive the introduction of non-native species

translation.text: 新西兰一种在外来物种引入后仍成功存活下来的本土鸟类

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As an island country with a fauna dominated by birds, New Zealand was once home to an owl species which is now extinct, the laughing owl, named for its distinctive cry. This bird was widespread throughout the islands when European settlers arrived in the middle of the 19th century and it remained in good numbers for some years thereafter. Where other native birds suffered from predation by the Polynesian rat, the laughing owl turned the tables and adapted its diet to include the rodent. It was also capable of catching and killing the other New Zealand owl, the morepork, and even larger birds, such as the weka. However, the laughing owl was wiped out around the beginning of the 20th century, its demise caused by specimen collectors, habitat changes, and non-native predators including cats and stoats. Surprisingly, it is the smaller owl, the morepork, that has managed to survive until this day.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 新西兰是一个岛屿国家，动物群以鸟类为主。这里曾生活着一种如今已经灭绝的猫头鹰——笑鸮，它因独特的叫声而得名。19世纪中叶欧洲移民到来时，笑鸮广泛分布在新西兰各岛，此后数年里数量依然不少。其他本土鸟类遭到波利尼西亚鼠捕食时，笑鸮却反过来把这种啮齿动物纳入了自己的食谱。它还能捕杀新西兰另一种猫头鹰——新西兰鹰鸮（morepork），甚至能捕杀体型更大的鸟类，如 weka。然而，到了20世纪初前后，笑鸮彻底灭绝；标本收藏者、栖息地变化，以及猫和白鼬等外来捕食者共同导致了它的消亡。令人意外的是，反倒是体型较小的新西兰鹰鸮一直存活到了今天。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Speckled dark brown, with yellow eyes and long tails, they are around 29 centimetres long from head to tail and 175 grams in weight. Moreporks have fringes on the edge of their feathers, so they can fly almost silently and not alert potential prey. They have acute hearing and their large eyes are very sensitive to light.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Moreporks nest in tree hollows, in clumps of plants, or in cavities among rocks and roots. In the wild, moreporks usually start nesting in October, although two specimens have been recorded nesting in mid-winter, possibly stimulated by an ample food supply. The female lays up to three white eggs, which she incubates for 20 to 30 days. During this time, she rarely hunts, and the male brings food to her.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: By day, moreporks sleep in roosts. By night, they hunt a variety of animals – mainly large invertebrates including scarab and huhu beetles, moths, caterpillars and spiders. They also take small birds and mice. They can find suitable food in pine forest as well as native forest. A morepork uses its sharp talons to catch or stun its prey, which it then carries away in its bill. Moreporks are clever hunters, and birds such as robins, grey warblers and fantails can end up as their prey. In the day, these small birds sometimes mob drowsy moreporks and chase them away from their roosts; they force the sleepy predators to search for a more peaceful spot.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Moreporks have proved to be ungracious hosts. Scientists trying to establish a population of plovers on Motuora Island in New Zealand’s Hauraki Gulf were mystified as to why only two birds survived out of the 75 placed there. The culprits turned out to be five pairs of moreporks that ate or chased away the new arrivals.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 事实证明，新西兰鹰鸮并不是好客的主人。科学家曾试图在新西兰豪拉基湾的莫图奥拉岛建立一个鸻鸟种群，却不明白为何放到岛上的75只鸟中只有2只存活。后来发现，罪魁祸首是岛上的5对新西兰鹰鸮：它们不是吃掉了这些新来者，就是把它们赶走了。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Although moreporks are still considered to be relatively common, it is likely that numbers are in gradual decline due to predation and loss of habitat. As the female is a hole-nester, she is vulnerable to predators such as stoats and possums during the breeding season, and eggs and chicks will also be at risk from rats. The use of pesticides is another possible threat to the owls, though not a direct one. As moreporks are at the top of the food chain, they could be affected by an accumulative poison by consuming prey that has ingested poison.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The New Zealand Department of Conservation is taking steps to ensure the preservation of New Zealand’s only native owl. The department is involved in measuring the population of moreporks and has put transmitters on a number of birds to determine survival and mortality. As well as being New Zealand’s only native owl, the morepork has symbolic and spiritual importance, so in monitoring the birds it is hoped that the morepork will continue to survive and thrive.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: At dusk, the melancholy sound of the morepork can be heard in forests and parks as it calls to other moreporks and claims territory. Its Māori name (ruru) echoes its two-part cry. In the tradition of the Māori people of New Zealand, the morepork, or ruru, was often seen as a careful guardian. A number of sayings referred to the bird’s alertness. As a bird of the night, it was associated with the spirit world. Moreporks were believed to act as messengers to the gods in the heavens, flying along spiritual paths in the sky. They were the mediums used to communicate with the gods. The occasional high, piercing call of the morepork signified bad news, but the lower-pitched and more common “ruru” call heralded good news.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 黄昏时分，森林和公园里会响起新西兰鹰鸮忧郁的叫声；它借此呼唤同类并宣示领地。它的毛利语名称 ruru，正是在模仿它分成两节的叫声。在新西兰毛利人的传统中，新西兰鹰鸮又称 ruru，常被视为谨慎的守护者。许多谚语都会提到这种鸟的警觉。它作为夜行鸟类，也与灵界联系在一起。人们相信，新西兰鹰鸮会沿着天空中的灵性路径飞行，担任向天上诸神传递消息的使者，是人与诸神沟通的媒介。它偶尔发出的高亢尖厉叫声预示坏消息，而音调较低、也更常听到的“ruru”叫声则预示好消息。

source.text: Ahead of its time

translation.text: 超越时代的发现

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A chance discovery in New Zealand has challenged the country’s recorded history.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 新西兰的一次偶然发现，对该国有文字记载的历史提出了挑战。

source.text: A chance discovery in New Zealand has challenged the country’s recorded history.

translation.text: 新西兰的一次偶然发现，对该国有文字记载的历史提出了挑战。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One October afternoon, a young New Zealander, Sam Tobin, called his dogs and went for a walk down to the nearby Ruamahanga River. Having been very high for days, the river had at last fallen, and Tobin was eager to see what changes the floods had brought. The family farm borders the river, and a four-metre-high flood bank testifies to its natural tendency to flood.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 10月的一天下午，新西兰青年 Sam Tobin 叫上自己的几条狗，朝附近的鲁阿马汉加河（Ruamahanga River）走去。河水连续多日处于高位，终于退了下去；Tobin 很想看看洪水给周围带来了哪些变化。他家的农场紧邻河流，一道高4米的防洪堤说明这里天生容易发生洪水。

source.text: The family farm borders the river, and a four-metre-high flood bank testifies to its natural tendency to flood.

translation.text: 他家的农场紧邻河流，一道高4米的防洪堤说明这里天生容易发生洪水。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Tobin stepped out onto a broad shoulder of river sand, where he noticed what he initially took to be a whitish rock, lit by the sun. Then, getting closer, he realised it was a bone. Such a thing was not uncommon in these parts - he had often come home with fragments, or even whole skeletons, of cows and sheep. But as he scraped aside a stone he realised that it was a human bone, something quite new in his experience. As he picked it up, he saw it was a skull, discoloured with age.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 托宾走上一大片河边沙洲，看到一个被阳光照亮的白色物体，起初以为那是一块岩石。走近后，他才发现那是一块骨头。在这一带，发现骨头并不稀奇——他以前经常带着牛羊的骨头碎片，甚至整副骨架回家。然而，当他把一块石头拨到一旁时，却意识到这是一块人骨，这是他从未遇到过的。拿起来一看，他发现那是一颗因年代久远而变色的头骨。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Tobin replaced the skull and hurried home to tell his mother what the river had delivered to their doorstep. It would prove to be a spectacular find, setting in motion an investigation by some of the country’s most respected specialists, and ultimately challenging our most firmly held assertions about the human settlement of New Zealand.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The police were immediately called, but despite a thorough search they could find nothing that might shed light on the identity of the Ruamahanga skull, or the circumstances of its sudden appearance. The skull was then taken north to be examined by forensic pathologist Dr Fetvis at Auckland Hospital. Despite being hampered by its damaged and incomplete condition - the jawbone and lower left portion of the cranium were missing - Dr Fetvis determined that the skull was that of a female. He’d then consulted with a colleague, Dr Koelmeyer, who believed that the deterioration of the bone placed the time of death ‘before living memory’ and, most significantly as it would turn out, the skull appeared to be European in origin.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Of course, a skull of this age wasn’t particularly unusual in New Zealand. blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Two centuries were to pass before the first recorded European females arrived in New Zealand, both having escaped from prison in Australia. Kathleen Hagerty and Charlotte Edgar are known to have reached the country in 1806. How then do we account for the Ruamahanga skull, which appears to be about 100 years older than that? It is impossible to say with certainty, but the most likely explanation is that a Spanish or Portuguese trading ship was washed onto these wild shores as a result of a shipwreck and a woman got ashore. Implausible, perhaps, but the Ruamahanga skull, today resting in the Wellington Museum, could be the kind of concrete evidence that demands such a drastic re-evaluation of history.

source.text: Ambergris

translation.text: 龙涎香

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: What is it and where does it come from?

source.text: What is it and where does it come from?

translation.text: 它是什么，又来自哪里？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In the ancient world, the waxy grey substance we now refer to as ambergris was highly prized for its medicinal properties, and was widely used as a spice, which was believed to be an aphrodisiac when added to food or wine. Ambergris itself is pleasantly aromatic, especially when warmed, and it was also highly valued as a fixing agent in the making of perfume, since it enabled a scent to retain its fragrance for much longer than might otherwise have been possible. Most ambergris was found in the form of lumps floating on the surface of the sea, or washed up on the shores of tropical and temperate oceans. At one time, ambergris was worth its weight in gold, but there was much confusion about its origins.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在古代，人们十分珍视如今称为龙涎香（ambergris）的灰色蜡状物质，认为它具有药用价值。它还被广泛用作香料；人们相信，把它加入食物或酒中可以催情。龙涎香本身带有宜人的香气，加热后尤其如此。它在制作香水时也被视为珍贵的定香剂，因为它能使香味留存的时间比原本可能达到的更长。人们发现的龙涎香大多呈块状，漂浮在海面上，或被冲上热带和温带海域的岸边。龙涎香一度价值堪比同等重量的黄金，但当时人们对它的来源有许多误解。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Ambergris was known to the Arabs as ‘ambar’ and was originally called amber in the West in the Middle Ages. This eventually led to further confusion in the popular mind between ambergris and true amber, the mineral known to mineralogists as succinite, which is actually fossilised tree resin, and generally yellow in colour. Both substances were rare and costly, and both were associated with the sea, largely because for Europeans the most common source of amber was the shores of the Baltic. In Chapter 92 of Moby Dick, the American writer Herman Melville pours scorn on those who believed the two substances to be the same: ‘Though the word ambergris is but the French compound for grey amber, yet the two substances are quite distinct. For amber, though at times found on the sea-coast, is also dug up in some far-inland soils, whereas ambergris is never found except upon the sea. Besides, amber is a hard, transparent, brittle, odourless substance, used for mouth-pieces to pipes, for beads and ornaments; but ambergris is soft, waxy, and so highly fragrant that it is largely used in perfumery.’

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Moby Dick was published in 1851, by which time the mystery of the origins of ambergris had been resolved by the scientific community. In 1783, the botanist Joseph Banks, who had accompanied Captain James Cook on his voyages of discovery in the Pacific, presented a paper to the Royal Society of London by the German physician Dr Franz Xavier Schwediawer in which it was conclusively proved that ambergris came from sperm whales. In this, he was confirming an observation made in the 13ᵗʰ century by the great Venetian traveller Marco Polo who, while on the island of Socotra in the Indian Ocean, had witnessed a sperm whale vomiting up ambergris. But whereas Marco Polo imagined that the whale had swallowed the lump in the depths of the sea, Schwediawer showed that the origin of the material was inside the whale itself.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 《白鲸》出版于1851年；到那时，科学界已经解开龙涎香来源之谜。1783年，曾随詹姆斯·库克船长在太平洋进行探索航行的植物学家 Joseph Banks，向伦敦皇家学会（Royal Society of London）提交了一篇由德国医生 Franz Xavier Schwediawer 博士撰写的论文。论文确凿证明龙涎香来自抹香鲸。施韦迪亚韦尔由此证实了13世纪威尼斯著名旅行家马可·波罗的一项观察：马可·波罗在印度洋索科特拉岛时，曾亲眼看见一头抹香鲸吐出龙涎香。不过，马可·波罗以为鲸是在深海中吞下了那团物质，Schwediawer 则表明，它其实产生于鲸的体内。

translation.text: 施韦迪亚韦尔由此证实了13世纪威尼斯著名旅行家马可·波罗的一项观察：马可·波罗在印度洋索科特拉岛时，曾亲眼看见一头抹香鲸吐出龙涎香。

source.text: But whereas Marco Polo imagined that the whale had swallowed the lump in the depths of the sea, Schwediawer showed that the origin of the material was inside the whale itself.

translation.text: 不过，马可·波罗以为鲸是在深海中吞下了那团物质，Schwediawer 则表明，它其实产生于鲸的体内。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The sperm whale is the largest of the odontocetes, or toothed whales. Males can grow up to 20 metres in length. Melville described the sperm whale as ‘the king of whales’, and his novel Moby Dick is based on the pursuit of one such creature. Sperm whales are renowned for their ability to dive to great depths, possibly as far as 3 000 metres below the surface, and for remaining underwater for periods of two hours or more in pursuit of their favourite prey, the giant squid.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 抹香鲸是齿鲸类中体型最大的物种，雄性体长可达20米。梅尔维尔称抹香鲸为“鲸中之王”，他的小说《白鲸》正是围绕追捕这样一头鲸展开的。抹香鲸以深潜能力著称，可能潜至海面以下3,000米，并能在水下停留2小时或更久，追捕它们最喜爱的猎物——大王乌贼。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It is from the problems the whales have in digesting the beaks of such creatures that ambergris has its origins. The beak is sharp and irritates the whale’s lower intestine, which responds by producing a black, foul-smelling liquid. It is not clear to scientists whether this secretion should be considered a normal response by the whale’s digestive system or a pathological one, but from time to time large quantities of the liquid are vomited up by the whale. Once outside the whale’s body and exposed to air, the substance hardens, acquiring the waxy, greyish and pleasantly aromatic characteristics of ambergris. Often the beaks of squid are still found embedded in lumps of ambergris, some of which can weigh several hundred kilograms. Melville took some delight in contrasting the origins of ambergris with the high value placed upon it by refined society: ‘Who would think, then, that such fine ladies and gentlemen should regale themselves with an essence found in the inglorious bowels of a sick whale!’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 龙涎香的形成，源于抹香鲸难以消化这类生物的喙。乌贼的喙十分锋利，会刺激鲸的下段肠道；肠道随即产生一种黑色、恶臭的液体。科学家尚不清楚，这种分泌究竟应视为鲸消化系统的正常反应，还是一种病理反应；但鲸会不时吐出大量这种液体。物质离开鲸体并接触空气后会变硬，逐渐具有龙涎香那种蜡质、灰白且气味宜人的特征。人们常能在龙涎香块中发现仍嵌在里面的乌贼喙，有些香块重达数百千克。梅尔维尔颇为得意地把龙涎香的来源与上流社会赋予它的高价值作了对比：“那么，谁能想到，这些优雅的淑女绅士竟会享用一种取自病鲸那不光彩的肠腹之中的香精！”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Sperm whales were ruthlessly pursued by commercial whalers in the 19ᵗʰ and 20ᵗʰ centuries. In 1963-64 alone, almost 30 000 individuals were killed, and only the imposition of a ban on the hunting of sperm whales in 1984 saved the species from extinction. Ambergris was by far the most valuable product to be extracted during the processing of the whales’ carcasses, and over 90 per cent of the annual worldwide total was acquired in this way, as a by-product of commercial whaling. However, even before the ban on hunting sperm whales was imposed, the 1972 Marine Mammal Protection Act had prohibited trade in ambergris. Just as petroleum and plastic products were replacing other natural products of whaling, so ambergris was supplanted in the making of perfume by other materials, some natural and some synthetic in origin. Nevertheless, it is possible that, as sperm-whale populations recover to their former numbers in the wild, so the sight of lumps of ambergris washed ashore along the tide-line will once again become a familiar one to beach-combers the world over.

headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 文字发展中的重要一步

source.text: An important language development

translation.text: 文字发展中的重要一步

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Cuneiform, the world’s first known system of handwriting, originated some 6,000 years ago in Sumer in what is now southern Iraq. It was most often inscribed on palm-sized, rectangular clay tablets measuring several centimetres across, although occasionally larger tablets or cylinders were used. Clay was an excellent medium for writing. Other surfaces which have been employed—for example, parchment, papyrus and paper—are not long-lasting and are easily destroyed by fire and water. But clay has proved to be resistant to those particular kinds of damage.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 楔形文字是目前所知世界上最早的手写文字体系，约6,000年前起源于苏美尔，也就是今天的伊拉克南部。它通常刻写在手掌大小的长方形泥板上，泥板宽度为数厘米；不过，人们偶尔也会使用更大的泥板或圆柱体。黏土是极佳的书写介质。羊皮纸、纸莎草纸和纸张等其他曾被用于书写的材料不耐久，也很容易被火和水毁坏；但事实证明，黏土能够抵御这些特定类型的破坏。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The word ‘cuneiform’ actually refers to the marks or signs inscribed in the clay. The original cuneiform signs consisted of a series of lines—triangular, vertical, diagonal, and horizontal. Sumerian writers would impress these lines into the wet clay with a stylus—a long, thin, pointed instrument which looked somewhat like a pen. Oddly, the signs were often almost too small to see with the naked eye. Cuneiform signs were used for the writing of at least a dozen languages. This is similar to how the Latin alphabet is used today for writing English, French, Spanish and German, for example.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: “楔形文字”这个名称实际上指的是刻在黏土上的笔画或符号。最初的楔形符号由一系列三角形、竖直、斜向和水平线条组成。苏美尔书写者会用一种细长而尖、外形有点像笔的书写工具，把这些线条压进湿润的黏土中。奇怪的是，这些符号往往小得几乎无法用肉眼看清。楔形符号至少被用来书写12种语言。这类似于今天人们使用拉丁字母书写英语、法语、西班牙语和德语等语言。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Before the development of cuneiform, tokens were used by the Sumerians to record certain information. For example, they might take small stones and use them as tokens or representations of something else, like a goat. A number of tokens, then, might mean a herd of goats. These tokens might then be placed in a cloth container and provided to a buyer as a receipt for a transaction, perhaps five tokens for five animals. It was not that different from what we do today when we buy some bread and the clerk gives us back a piece of paper with numbers on it to confirm the exchange.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在楔形文字形成之前，苏美尔人使用小物件来记录某些信息。例如，他们可能取一些小石子，把它们当作代表其他事物的记数物，比如一只山羊。若干枚记数物就可能代表一群山羊。随后，这些记数物会被放进布袋，交给买方作为交易凭证；例如，5枚记数物代表5只动物。这与今天买面包时店员交给我们一张写有数字、用于确认交易的纸条并没有太大不同。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: By the 4th century BCE, the Sumerians had adapted this system to a form of writing. They began putting tokens in a container resembling an envelope, one made of clay instead of cloth. They then stamped the outside to indicate the number and type of tokens inside. A person could then ‘read’ what was stamped on the container and know what was inside.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 到了公元前4世纪，苏美尔人已将这一体系改造成一种书写形式。他们开始把记数物装进一个类似信封的容器中，只不过这个容器由黏土而非布制成。然后，他们会在容器外面压印标记，说明里面记数物的数量和种类。这样一来，人们只需“阅读”容器上的印记，就能知道里面装了什么。

source.text: By the 4th century BCE, the Sumerians had adapted this system to a form of writing.

translation.text: 然后，他们会在容器外面压印标记，说明里面记数物的数量和种类。

source.text: A person could then ‘read’ what was stamped on the container and know what was inside.

translation.text: 这样一来，人们只需“阅读”容器上的印记，就能知道里面装了什么。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Gradually, Sumerians developed symbols for words. When first developed, each symbol looked like the concrete thing it represented. For example, an image which resembled the drawing of a sheep meant just that. Then another level of abstraction was introduced when symbols were developed for intangible ideas such as ‘female’ or ‘hot’ or ‘God’. Cuneiform, in other words, evolved from a way used primarily to track and store information into a way to represent the world symbolically. Over the centuries, the marks became ever more abstract, finally evolving into signs that looked nothing like what they referred to, just as the letters ‘h-o-u-s-e’ have no visual connection to the place we live in. At this last stage in the evolution of cuneiform, the signs took the form of triangles, which became common cuneiform signs.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 苏美尔人逐渐发展出表示词语的符号。最初出现时，每个符号都像它所代表的具体事物。例如，一个看起来像羊的图形就表示羊。后来，人们又进一步抽象，发展出表示“女性”“热”或“神”等无形概念的符号。换言之，楔形文字从一种主要用于追踪和保存信息的方法，演变成了用符号表示世界的方法。几个世纪间，这些笔画变得越来越抽象，最终演变成与所指事物毫无相似之处的符号，就像 h-o-u-s-e 这几个字母在外形上与我们居住的房屋没有任何联系一样。在楔形文字演变的最后阶段，这些符号呈三角形，成为常见的楔形符号。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As the marks became more abstract, the system became more efficient because there were fewer marks for a ‘reader’ to learn. But cuneiform also became more complex because society itself was becoming more complex, so there were more ideas and concepts that needed to be expressed. However, most linguists and historians agree cuneiform developed primarily as a tool for accounting. Of the cuneiform tablets that have been discovered, excavated and translated, about 75 percent contain this type of practical information, rather than artistic or imaginative work.

source.text: But cuneiform also became more complex because society itself was becoming more complex, so there were more ideas and concepts that needed to be expressed.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Cuneiform writing was used for thousands of years, but it eventually ceased to be used in everyday life. In fact, it died out and remained unintelligible for almost 2,000 years. In the late 19th century, a British army officer, Henry Rawlinson, discovered cuneiform inscriptions which had been carved into the surface of rocks in the Behistun Mountains in what is present-day Iran. Rawlinson made impressions of the marks on large pieces of paper as he balanced dangerously on the surrounding rocks.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Rawlinson took his copies home to Britain and studied them for years to determine what each line stood for, and what each group of symbols meant. He found that, in the writing on those particular rocks, every word was repeated three times in three languages: Old Persian, Elamite and Babylonian. Since the meanings in these languages were already known to linguists, he could thus translate the cuneiform. Eventually, he fully decoded the cuneiform marks and discovered that they described the life of Darius, a king of the Persian Empire in the 5th century BCE.

source.text: Australia’s Airborne Dentists

translation.text: 澳大利亚的飞行牙医

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Australians living or travelling in rural and remote areas can face particular difficulties when they need medical care. Hundreds of kilometres from major cities and many hours by road from the closest hospital or clinic, some rural Australians do not have easy access to doctors, nurses and dentists. Organisations such as the Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS) have been established to bring health services to outback Australian communities. The RFDS provides free medical care to people who live, work or travel in remote and regional parts of Australia. This non-profit organisation is the oldest and largest airborne health service of its kind in the world, and since 1928 it has used small aircraft to send doctors and nurses to some of Australia’s most far-away communities.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在澳大利亚乡村和偏远地区生活或旅行的人需要医疗服务时，可能会面临特殊困难。有些乡村居民距大城市数百千米，乘车前往最近的医院或诊所也要花很多小时，因此很难获得医生、护士和牙医的服务。皇家飞行医生服务机构（Royal Flying Doctor Service，RFDS）等组织由此成立，把医疗服务带到澳大利亚内陆偏远社区。RFDS为在澳大利亚偏远及区域性地区生活、工作或旅行的人提供免费医疗。这家非营利组织是世界上同类空中医疗服务中历史最悠久、规模最大的一家；自1928年以来，它一直使用小型飞机把医生和护士送往澳大利亚一些最偏远的社区。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In recent years, the RFDS has also started to fly dentists to regional Australia. As well as offering mobile dental clinics, the RFDS offers a range of preventative and educational services. Looking after the teeth of people in remote areas presents special challenges. These include providing care to disparate communities with no established dental facilities, and dealing with higher incidences of other diseases which are linked to, or caused by poor dental health.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 近年来，RFDS也开始用飞机把牙医送往澳大利亚各地区。除了提供流动牙科诊所外，RFDS还提供一系列预防和教育服务。照顾偏远地区居民的牙齿会遇到一些特殊挑战，包括为分散各地、没有固定牙科设施的社区提供诊疗，以及应对当地更为多发的其他疾病；这些疾病与口腔健康不良有关，或由此引起。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: People in remote areas have very infrequent visits by health staff. RFDS dentists might only visit a community once every few months, or sometimes once per year. Because of infrequent dentist visits, patients in these areas often need to put up with their dental problems before they can get treatment. Consequently, people in remote areas are more likely to have tooth decay (the blackening and deterioration of teeth) and develop gum and other mouth diseases.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 偏远地区很少有医务人员到访。RFDS牙医可能隔几个月才到一个社区一次，有时甚至一年才来一次。由于牙医来得不频繁，这些地区的患者往往要忍受一段时间的牙齿问题，才能得到治疗。因此，偏远地区居民更容易出现龋齿（牙齿变黑和受损），也更容易患牙龈疾病和其他口腔疾病。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In some locations that the RFDS visits, there are no suitable dental facilities, so dentists have to bring everything with them. This includes drills, dentists’ chairs, portable X-ray machines, and computers for keeping track of patients’ treatments. Equipment can weigh up to 100 kilograms, and since the small planes that transport dentists have limited space, dentists cannot always bring everything that they need.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: While dentists in town or city centres can specialise in certain types of treatment, RFDS dentists need to be ‘all-rounders’. They need to be able to do all kinds of dental procedures, as they don’t have the ability to refer patients to more specialised dentists. Even with their broad experience, there are some services that are particularly challenging for RFDS dentists. For example, dentures (or artificial teeth) can be very difficult to provide, as they need to be the right shape and size for the patient, and this requires many visits over a long period of time. As a result, it is not practical to make dentures available.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 城镇或市中心的牙医可以专攻某些治疗项目，RFDS牙医却必须成为“多面手”。他们要能完成各种牙科操作，因为无法把患者转诊给专业程度更高的牙医。即使他们经验广泛，有些服务对RFDS牙医来说仍然格外困难。例如，假牙很难配制，因为必须符合患者口腔的形状和大小，而这需要患者在很长一段时间内多次就诊。因此，向患者提供假牙并不现实。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Some chronic illnesses are more common in remote communities than in the rest of Australia. These illnesses can in turn lead to a lowered resistance to infection, including gum and other oral infections. As a result, people in outback Australian communities are more likely to experience oral health problems than city folk, and this poses extra challenges for both the dentists and the doctors of the RFDS.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 有些慢性病在偏远社区比澳大利亚其他地区更常见。这些疾病又可能降低人体抵抗感染的能力，包括抵抗牙龈及其他口腔感染。因此，与城市居民相比，澳大利亚内陆偏远社区的居民更容易遇到口腔健康问题，这也给RFDS的牙医和医生带来额外挑战。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Because there aren’t a lot of dental services in remote areas, people living in these areas also receive less education about good dental hygiene than their city counterparts do. Australians in very remote communities might not be aware of things that people in cities take for granted, such as the importance of daily tooth brushing. Also, basic dental hygiene items such as toothpaste and toothbrushes can be more expensive in outback areas. Many people are on low incomes, meaning they have extra difficulty affording these products. If this is the case, the RFDS supplies these.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 偏远地区牙科服务不多，因此当地居民获得的良好口腔卫生教育也少于城市居民。极偏远社区的澳大利亚人可能不了解一些城市居民认为理所当然的事情，例如每天刷牙的重要性。此外，牙膏和牙刷等基本口腔清洁用品在内陆偏远地区可能更贵。许多人收入较低，更难负担这些用品。遇到这种情况，RFDS就会提供这些用品。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As well as treating patients, RFDS dentists try to focus on preventative oral health and educate their patients on good oral hygiene, such as tooth brushing and flossing. The RFDS also provides mouthguards for young sports players. Playing contact sports, such as rugby league or Australian rules football, can damage young people’s teeth, so mouthguards provide protection which prevents accidental injuries.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 除了治疗患者，RFDS牙医还努力重视口腔疾病的预防，并向患者讲解良好的口腔卫生习惯，如刷牙和使用牙线。RFDS也为参加体育运动的年轻人提供护齿套。橄榄球联赛或澳式足球等接触性运动可能损伤年轻人的牙齿，护齿套则能提供保护，防止意外受伤。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Adding fluoride to water supplies has been proven to reduce the incidence of tooth decay in many parts of the world. City dwellers in Australia use water supplies that have been fluoridated, and their rates of tooth decay are lower because of this. In remote areas, it is not practical to fluoridate drinking water supplies, and so people living in these areas are more subject to tooth decay. As a result, it is particularly important that people living in areas without fluoridated water pay special attention to regular brushing of their teeth with fluoridated toothpaste.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 事实证明，在供水中添加氟化物可以降低世界许多地区的龋齿发生率。澳大利亚城市居民使用经过氟化处理的供水，因此龋齿发生率较低。偏远地区很难对饮用水进行氟化处理，所以当地居民更容易患龋齿。因此，生活在非氟化供水地区的人尤其需要注意，经常使用含氟牙膏刷牙。

headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 澳大利亚的甘蔗蟾蜍难题

source.text: Australia’s cane toad problem

translation.text: 澳大利亚的甘蔗蟾蜍难题

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: How a toad introduced in Australia to control pests has itself become a pest
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 一种为防治害虫而引入澳大利亚的蟾蜍，后来如何反而成了害兽

source.text: How a toad introduced in Australia to control pests has itself become a pest

translation.text: 一种为防治害虫而引入澳大利亚的蟾蜍，后来如何反而成了害兽

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In the north of Australia there are many sugar cane plantations, which early in the 20th century were being damaged by a particular pest. This was a species of beetle whose larvae, the infant form of the beetle, lived underground in the soil in the sugar cane fields. The sugar cane plants were weakened or died because their roots were eaten by the larvae. This had serious economic consequences for sugar cane farmers. Modern pesticides were not developed until the 1940s, so farmers had to use what was available at the time. Chemicals like arsenic and copper were used, but these were not only expensive but also stayed in the environment and were poisonous to people, plants and animals. It was generally acknowledged by government, farmers and scientists that cheaper and safer methods of pest control had to be found.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 澳大利亚北部有许多甘蔗种植园，20世纪初曾遭一种特定害虫破坏。这是一种甲虫，它的幼体生活在甘蔗地的地下土壤中。幼虫啃食甘蔗根部，使甘蔗长势衰弱甚至死亡，给蔗农造成了严重经济损失。现代农药直到20世纪40年代才问世，因此农民只能使用当时已有的手段。人们使用砷、铜等化学物质，但这些物质不仅昂贵，还会残留在环境中，对人、植物和动物都有毒害。政府、农民和科学家普遍承认，必须找到更便宜、更安全的害虫防治方法。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A promising replacement for copper and arsenic was the use of biological control. Farmers already used some forms of biological pest control in the form of predatory and parasitic wasps and flies, insect-eating birds, and plants from different regions or countries to control pests. Common practice was to release these introduced agents into new environments, the expectation being that they would destroy resident pests. Some species of toad already had successful records as agents of biological control in gardens. For example, in 19th-century France toads were sold to gardeners at markets in Paris to eat insect pests in their gardens. In the early 20th century French sugar cane farmers first took giant toads from South America to control pests in their Caribbean sugar cane plantations. Although there is no evidence that these toads did help to control pests, sugar cane scientists then carried some of these toads from Jamaica and Barbados to Puerto Rico and from there to Hawaii.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 生物防治被视为取代铜和砷的一种很有希望的方法。当时，农民已经采用某些生物防治手段，例如利用捕食性和寄生性蜂类与蝇类、食虫鸟类，以及从其他地区或国家引进的植物来控制害虫。常见做法是把这些外来防治生物放入新环境，期待它们消灭当地害虫。有些蟾蜍在花园中作为生物防治生物，已经有过成功记录。例如，19世纪的法国，巴黎市场上有人向园丁出售蟾蜍，让它们吃掉花园里的害虫。20世纪初，法国蔗农首次把南美洲的巨型蟾蜍带到加勒比地区的甘蔗种植园防治害虫。虽然没有证据表明这些蟾蜍确实有助于控制害虫，甘蔗研究人员随后仍把其中一些从牙买加和巴巴多斯带到波多黎各，再从那里带到夏威夷。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The idea of biological control of pests was not new to Australia. For example, in 1926 there had been a highly successful prevention of the increase of the exotic prickly-pear cactus by the introduction of a moth from Argentina. This success added strength to the argument that biological control was the answer to the sugar cane industry’s pest problems. Accordingly, in the early 1930s a decision was taken to introduce the giant South American toads, which in Australia are now commonly called cane toads, into Australian sugar cane plantations.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 用生物方法防治害虫，对澳大利亚并不新鲜。例如，1926年，人们从阿根廷引进一种蛾，成功阻止了外来仙人掌梨继续蔓延。这一成功进一步支持了这样的观点：生物防治就是解决甘蔗产业害虫问题的办法。因此，20世纪30年代初，人们决定把南美洲的巨型蟾蜍引入澳大利亚甘蔗种植园；如今，这种蟾蜍在澳大利亚通常被称为甘蔗蟾蜍。

source.text: The idea of biological control of pests was not new to Australia.

translation.text: 用生物方法防治害虫，对澳大利亚并不新鲜。

source.text: Accordingly, in the early 1930s a decision was taken to introduce the giant South American toads, which in Australia are now commonly called cane toads, into Australian sugar cane plantations.

translation.text: 因此，20世纪30年代初，人们决定把南美洲的巨型蟾蜍引入澳大利亚甘蔗种植园；如今，这种蟾蜍在澳大利亚通常被称为甘蔗蟾蜍。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In 1935, an Australian entomologist brought 101 cane toads from Hawaii and released them in sugar cane plantations in the north of Australia. However, over the following years it became clear that the cane toads were a failure. There was a fatal flaw in the plan to use them as a form of biological control. This was that earthbound cane toads were expected to eat the mostly flying adult beetles in order to eliminate the soil-dwelling beetle larvae that ate the roots of the cane sugar plants. This, of course, cane toads could not do.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 1935年，一名澳大利亚昆虫学家从夏威夷带回101只甘蔗蟾蜍，把它们放入澳大利亚北部的甘蔗种植园。然而，随后几年里，人们逐渐看清，甘蔗蟾蜍并没有发挥作用。把它们作为生物防治手段的计划存在一个致命缺陷：人们指望只能在地面活动的甘蔗蟾蜍吃掉大多会飞的成年甲虫，从而消灭那些生活在土中、啃食甘蔗根部的甲虫幼虫。甘蔗蟾蜍当然做不到这一点。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Prior to their introduction in Australia, there had been very few opponents and only one made his views public. He was a retired former Chief Entomologist from the state government of New South Wales named Walter Froggatt. He forecast that cane toads might become as great a pest in Australia as rabbits. However, Froggatt’s peers rebuked him and eminent scientists branded his views ‘decidedly pessimistic’. It is estimated that today as many as a hundred million cane toads form a toxic infestation which is slowly spreading throughout the land.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在把甘蔗蟾蜍引入澳大利亚之前，反对者寥寥无几，公开表达反对意见的只有一人。他叫 Walter Froggatt，曾任新南威尔士州政府首席昆虫学家，当时已经退休。他预言，甘蔗蟾蜍在澳大利亚可能会变成与兔子同样严重的害兽。然而，同行斥责了 Froggatt，知名科学家还把他的观点称为“明显过于悲观”。据估计，如今甘蔗蟾蜍可能多达1亿只，形成一片有毒的入侵种群，并在澳大利亚各地缓慢扩散。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Cane toads are large, heavily built amphibians. Average-sized adults are 10-15 cm long and weigh more than a kilo. They have large swellings on each shoulder from which they squirt poison when they are threatened. This venom contains 14 different chemicals, but they do not appear to be harmful to humans as no-one has died in Australia from cane toad poison. Until recently there was no understanding of the toxicity of cane toad poison, but it is now clear that freshwater crocodiles, goannas (large lizards) and dingoes (wild dogs) have died after eating cane toads. Cane toads compete with native Australian fauna for food, and eat the eggs and young of ground-nesting birds. As their numbers increase, they are taking over more and more of the land where native Australian fauna live.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 甘蔗蟾蜍是体型庞大、身躯粗壮的两栖动物。普通成年个体长10至15厘米，体重超过1千克。它们两侧肩部各有一个巨大的隆起，受到威胁时会从中喷出毒液。毒液含有14种不同的化学物质，不过这些物质似乎不会伤害人类，因为澳大利亚尚未有人死于甘蔗蟾蜍毒液。直到不久前，人们仍不了解这种毒液有多强；如今已经清楚，淡水鳄、巨蜥和澳洲野犬都曾因吃下甘蔗蟾蜍而死亡。甘蔗蟾蜍会与澳大利亚本土动物争夺食物，也会吃掉地面筑巢鸟类的蛋和幼鸟。随着数量增长，它们正占据越来越多原本属于澳大利亚本土动物的栖息地。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The lesson that can be learned from the introduction of cane toads is important. It is wrong to think that such an awful biological event could not be repeated. In this instance, the catalyst was the overwhelming consensus of support for introducing cane toads to Australia. The error was that there was little or no testing of these biological agents before they were introduced to see what unplanned effects they might have on the environment.

passages.title: Book review: Triumph of the City

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Book review: Triumph of the City

source.text: Book review: Triumph of the City

translation.text: 书评：《城市的胜利》

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Triumph of the City, by Edward Glaeser, is a thrilling and very readable hymn of praise to an invention so vast and so effective that it is generally taken for granted. More than half the global population already live in urban areas and, every month, five million more flood into the cities of the developed and developing worlds. The crowds and poverty of some of these modern cities may horrify us. They shouldn’t, says Glaeser; they are signs of growth, energy and aspiration. Cities are our best and brightest hope.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Edward Glaeser 的《城市的胜利》精彩刺激、十分易读，是一曲献给某项发明的热情赞歌；这项发明规模如此庞大、成效如此显著，以至于人们通常把它视为理所当然。全球已有一半以上的人口生活在城市地区，而发达国家和发展中国家的城市每月还会再涌入500万人。有些现代城市的拥挤和贫困景象或许令我们震惊。Glaeser 说，其实不必如此，因为这些都是发展、活力和追求的标志。城市是我们最好、也最光明的希望。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This idea has had more than two hundred years of resistance. Not long after the Industrial Revolution began in Britain, the Romantic poets turned away from the smoke and factories of their cities to celebrate the air and light of untouched nature. In 19th-century America, the writer Henry David Thoreau retreated to the wilderness of Walden Pond to live the solitary, simple life, and convinced generations of Americans that cities were bad and nature was good.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: They had, Glaeser admits, a point. The early industrial cities were dirty, since they lacked efficient waste-disposal systems, and disease spread rapidly among the population. But more importantly they were profitable, and there were enormous commercial incentives to make them work, as well as political ones. Their transformation could be achieved at a stroke: in the second half of the 19th century, the French Emperor Napoleon III gave Baron Haussmann unrestricted power to turn the slum-infested city of Paris into one of the wonders and delights of the modern world. Or the transformation could be done by trial and error. Glaeser gives a brilliant account of the stop-start progression of New York to its late 20th-century position as the cultural and economic centre of the world. Either way, Paris, New York and other cities developed because they were truly effective markets of ideas and innovation.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 格莱泽承认，他们的看法确有道理。早期工业城市缺乏高效的废物处理系统，因此肮脏不堪，疾病也在人群中迅速传播。但更重要的是，这些城市能够带来利润；无论从商业还是政治角度，都有巨大的动力让它们有效运转。改造可以一举完成：19世纪下半叶，法国皇帝拿破仑三世赋予奥斯曼男爵不受限制的权力，把贫民窟遍布的巴黎变成现代世界的奇观和乐土之一。改造也可以靠反复试错完成。格莱泽精彩讲述了纽约走走停停的发展过程，以及它如何在20世纪后期成为世界文化与经济中心。无论采取哪种方式，巴黎、纽约等城市之所以能够发展，都因为它们是真正高效的思想与创新市场。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: For these and many other reasons, we should not be so upset by the spectacle of urban poverty. The poor flock to cities in the hope of becoming richer (which, by and large, they do). They also reinvigorate the economy of the city. It is folly to drive them away by forcing property prices to soar with unreasonable planning regulations. Instead, cities should build more houses and thereby hold property prices in check.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It can go wrong, of course. In Glaeser’s view, this is primarily because municipal authorities fail to understand the principal virtues of their cities. The heart of Paris, as many Parisians say, is turning into a museum because of the desire to preserve Baron Haussmann’s 19th-century boulevards. Glaeser defends their preservation, but argues that in the 1950s the French made a mistake in establishing a huge high-rise commercial development — La Défense — on the outskirts of the city. Far better, he says, to have turned the central area of Montparnasse into a new commercial district. This would have revitalised much of the city centre without destroying its fabric. In India, Mumbai could save itself from ever-more inefficient sprawl over the surrounding area simply by relaxing the rules presently imposed on the height of new constructions.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 城市当然也可能走上歧途。格莱泽认为，主要原因是市政当局没有理解自己城市最重要的优点。许多巴黎人说，由于人们希望保存奥斯曼男爵修建的19世纪林荫大道，巴黎市中心正在变成一座博物馆。格莱泽支持保护这些大道，但他认为，法国人在20世纪50年代犯了一个错误：把大型高层商业区拉德芳斯建在城市外围。他说，更好的做法本应是把市中心的蒙帕纳斯地区改造成新的商业区。这样既能使市中心大部分地区恢复活力，又不会破坏其原有格局。在印度，孟买只需放宽目前对新建筑高度的限制，就能摆脱向周边地区不断蔓延、效率越来越低的局面。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In America, it is the suburbs that have proved to be the real disaster. Glaeser is repentant on this subject himself. He moved to the suburbs when he had children. His entirely legitimate excuse is that the government made him (and millions like him) do it. By under-taxing petrol and imposing tight planning restrictions on inner cities that drove up the cost of property, it made flight to the suburbs more or less inevitable for the middle classes.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在美国，真正酿成灾难的是郊区。格莱泽本人在这一点上也有所悔悟。他有了孩子后搬到了郊区。他给出的理由完全站得住脚：是政府迫使他以及数百万和他一样的人这样做。政府对汽油征税过低，又在内城区实行严格的规划限制，推高房产成本，使中产阶级逃往郊区几乎成为必然。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This is a disaster because nothing is more inefficient than a suburb. Suburbanites mingle less, and lose the face-to-face contact that makes being an urbanite so much more creative. Moreover, houses are costlier to heat and cool than flats, and suburbanites drive thousands more miles per year than city dwellers. Every aspect of life involves more consumption. This leads to the strongest and newest argument in favour of cities — they are good for the environment. To live in the country or the suburbs is to have a vastly larger carbon footprint than any urbanite.

source.text: Building a castle

translation.text: 建造一座城堡

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Guédelon is no ordinary building site. There is no rumble of diggers or shriek of circular saws. All is peaceful and quiet, save for the continual tapping of the small army of stonemasons, the quacking of the ducks or the occasional crow of the cockerel. Slowly but surely, a brand new medieval castle is rising from the woods of Guédelon, Yonne, home to the Burgundy vineyards in the heart of France. The year is 1229—that is, for the purposes of this project: to build a prince’s château fort using only the techniques and tools of the 13th century.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 盖德隆绝不是普通的建筑工地。这里听不到挖掘机的轰鸣，也没有圆锯刺耳的尖啸。四周宁静安详，只有一小队石匠持续不断的敲击声、鸭子的嘎嘎声，或偶尔响起的公鸡啼鸣。在法国腹地、勃艮第葡萄园所在地约讷省的盖德隆树林中，一座崭新的中世纪城堡正缓慢而稳步地拔地而起。这里的年份是1229年——至少对这个项目而言是如此：人们要只用13世纪的技术和工具，为一位亲王建造一座设防城堡。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: ‘The project has four main aims,’ explains Maryline Martin, managing director for Guédelon. ‘The first is experimental archaeology – to try and verify all the theories, based on documents of the time. There’s also a social aim, because this region is very poor, with high unemployment: so it provides jobs. Then there’s tourism: the project couldn’t work without visitors because a lot of money is needed to pay people working here and to run the site. And finally, we want to open experimental archaeology to everybody – because in France, history and architecture are still very much oriented to academics.’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: “这个项目有四个主要目标，”盖德隆总经理 Maryline Martin 解释说，“第一是实验考古学——尝试验证依据当时文献提出的所有理论。项目也有社会目标，因为这个地区非常贫困，失业率很高，所以它能提供就业机会。接下来是旅游业：没有游客，项目就无法运转，因为支付这里工人的工资和维持工地运行需要大量资金。最后，我们希望让每个人都能接触实验考古学——因为在法国，历史和建筑仍然在很大程度上以学术界为中心。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The idea for the project emerged about five years ago. It was the brainchild of Michel Guyot, who bought and renovated the nearby castle of Saint-Fargeau, which was built and rebuilt between the 10th and 18th centuries. Beneath his castle were the original foundations of the 13th-century building. Guyot thought it would be fun to construct a château to the same plans, but this proved too big to attempt. So Jacques Moulin, managing director for the local historical monuments, drew up plans for a smaller castle that would still be ambitious, but realistic. Five months later, having managed to get together 600,000 Euros in funding, they began looking for a site that would provide all the materials they needed: stone, water, sand, wood, iron and clay. They found it at Guédelon.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这个项目的构想大约在5年前出现，最初由 Michel Guyot 提出。他买下并翻修了附近的圣法尔若城堡；这座城堡从10世纪到18世纪历经建造与重建。在他的城堡下面，还保留着13世纪原建筑的地基。Guyot 觉得，照同一套图纸再建一座城堡会很有趣，但实践证明工程规模太大，无法尝试。因此，当地历史古迹部门的负责人 Jacques Moulin 为一座较小的城堡绘制了图纸，使项目既雄心勃勃，又切实可行。5个月后，他们成功筹得60万欧元，开始寻找一处能够提供所需全部材料的地点，包括石头、水、沙、木材、铁和黏土。他们在盖德隆找到了这样的地方。

translation.text: 因此，当地历史古迹部门的负责人 Jacques Moulin 为一座较小的城堡绘制了图纸，使项目既雄心勃勃，又切实可行。

source.text: Five months later, having managed to get together 600,000 Euros in funding, they began looking for a site that would provide all the materials they needed: stone, water, sand, wood, iron and clay.

translation.text: 5个月后，他们成功筹得60万欧元，开始寻找一处能够提供所需全部材料的地点，包括石头、水、沙、木材、铁和黏土。

source.text: They found it at Guédelon.

translation.text: 他们在盖德隆找到了这样的地方。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The only major cheat so far was early on when a mechanical earthmover was brought in to raise the castle floor. Archaeologists know how it was done in the 13th century: by backbreaking, tedious work. ‘To do it by hand would have added ten years to the project,’ says Franck, one of the site’s guides. It’s still a long, painstaking task. Next to the beginnings of the east wall is the quarry, where masons extract the ferruginous limestone to build the thick castle walls. They bore lines of holes into the rocks and then they hammer metal wedges into them until the rock splits along the line. It is then hewn into bricks, and cemented together with a mortar of chalk, sand and quicklime. Quicklime is made by heating limestone to 800°C – done off-site because of the poisonous gases that come from the process. Little wonder that 13th-century lime-burners had a life expectancy of only 25–30 years. ‘The bricks are then laid horizontally for the first metre of the wall, and vertically thereafter,’ says Franck, ‘because if there was a shock from, say, a catapult, and the stones were all laid in the same way, the shockwave would shatter the wall.’

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The scientists and craftspeople alike are learning on the job, as they don’t know exactly why or how things were done as the historical evidence suggests. One such discovery concerns the significance of the marks that masons carved into each finished stone. It was thought that these probably had superstitious meaning, but experience and archaeological research reveals three very practical uses: to establish how much each mason should be paid; to keep track of who made what, in case of any problems; and to specify where the stone should be placed in the castle reconstruction.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 科学家和工匠都在工作中边做边学，因为历史证据所反映的许多做法，具体为何采用、又如何实施，他们并不完全清楚。其中一项发现涉及石匠刻在每块成品石料上的记号有何意义。人们过去认为，这些记号可能带有迷信含义；但实际经验和考古研究揭示了3种非常实际的用途：确定每名石匠应得多少报酬；记录每件石料由谁制作，以便出现问题时追查；以及标明石料应当放在重建城堡的哪个位置。

passages.title: Caral: an ancient South American city

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Caral: an ancient South American city
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 卡拉尔（Caral）：一座南美洲古城

source.text: Caral: an ancient South American city

translation.text: 卡拉尔（Caral）：一座南美洲古城

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Huge earth and rock mounds rise out of the desert of the Supe Valley near the coast of Peru in South America. These immense mounds appear simply to be part of the geographical landscape in this arid region squeezed between the Pacific Ocean and the Andes mountains. But looks deceive. These are actually human-made pyramids. Strong evidence indicates they are the remains of a city known as Caral that flourished nearly 5,000 years ago. If true, it would be the oldest known urban center in the Americas and among the most ancient in the world.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 南美洲秘鲁海岸附近的苏佩河谷（Supe Valley）沙漠中，耸立着巨大的土石丘。这片干旱地区夹在太平洋与安第斯山脉之间，这些庞大土丘看起来不过是当地地貌的一部分。然而，眼见未必为实：它们其实是人工建造的金字塔。有力证据表明，这些土丘是一座名为卡拉尔的城市遗迹，近5,000年前曾繁荣一时。如果这一判断属实，卡拉尔将是目前所知美洲最古老的城市中心，也是世界上最古老的城市之一。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Research undertaken by Peruvian archaeologist Ruth Shady suggests that the 150-acre complex of pyramids, plazas and residential buildings was a thriving metropolis when Egypt’s great pyramids were still being built. Though discovered in 1905, for years Caral attracted little attention, largely because archaeologists believed the structures were fairly recent. But the monumental scale of the pyramids had long interested Shady, who began excavations at the site in 1996, about 22 kilometers from the coast and 190 kilometers north of Peru’s capital city of Lima.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 秘鲁考古学家 Ruth Shady 的研究表明，这座占地150英亩、由金字塔、广场和住宅建筑组成的建筑群，在埃及大金字塔仍在修建时已经是一座繁荣都市。卡拉尔虽于1905年被发现，却多年没有引起多少关注，主要因为考古学家认为这些建筑年代并不久远。但金字塔宏大的规模早已引起 Shady 的兴趣；1996年，她在距海岸约22千米、秘鲁首都利马以北190千米的遗址开始发掘。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Shady and her crew searched for broken remains of the pots and containers that most such sites contain. Not finding any only made her more excited; it meant Caral could be what archaeologists term pre-ceramic, that is, existing before the advent in the area of pot-firing techniques. Shady’s team undertook the task of excavating Piramide Mayor, the largest of the pyramids. After carefully clearing away many hundreds of years’ worth of rubble and sand, they identified staircases, walls covered with remnants of colored woven bags and brickwork. In the foundations, they found the remains of grass-like reeds woven into bags. The original workers, she surmised, must have filled these bags with stones from a nearby quarry and laid them atop one another inside retaining walls, gradually giving rise to the pyramid’s immense structure. Shady had samples of the reeds subjected to radiocarbon dating and found that the reeds were 4,600 years old. This evidence indicated that Caral was, in fact, more than 1,000 years older than what had previously been thought to be the oldest urban center in the Americas.

source.text: Shady had samples of the reeds subjected to radiocarbon dating and found that the reeds were 4,600 years old.

translation.text: 她将芦苇样本送去进行放射性碳测年，结果显示芦苇已有4,600年历史。

source.text: This evidence indicated that Caral was, in fact, more than 1,000 years older than what had previously been thought to be the oldest urban center in the Americas.

translation.text: 这项证据表明，卡拉尔实际上比此前被视为美洲最古老城市中心的遗址还要早1,000多年。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: What amazed archaeologists was not just the age, but the complexity and scope of Caral. Piramide Mayor alone covers an area nearly the size of four football fields and is 18 meters tall. A nine-meter-wide staircase rises from a circular plaza at the foot of the pyramid, passing over three terraced levels until it reaches the top. Thousands of manual laborers would have been needed to build such a project, not counting the many architects, craftsmen, and managers. Shady’s team found the remains of a large amphitheater, containing almost 70 musical instruments made of bird and deer bones. Clearly, music played an important role in Caral’s society. Around the perimeter of Caral are a series of smaller mounds and various buildings. These indicate a hierarchy of living arrangements: large, well-kept rooms atop pyramids for the elite, ground-level quarters for craftsmen, and shabbier outlying dwellings for workers.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 令考古学家惊叹的不只是卡拉尔的年代，还有它的复杂程度和规模。仅主金字塔的占地面积就接近4个足球场，高18米。一道宽9米的阶梯从金字塔脚下的圆形广场向上延伸，越过3层台地，直达顶部。建成这样的工程需要数千名体力劳动者，还不包括众多建筑师、工匠和管理者。沙迪的团队发现一座大型圆形剧场的遗迹，里面有近70件用鸟骨和鹿骨制成的乐器。显然，音乐在卡拉尔社会中发挥着重要作用。卡拉尔外围分布着一系列较小的土丘和各种建筑。这些建筑反映出居住安排的等级差异：精英住在金字塔顶部宽敞而维护良好的房间里，工匠住在地面层的居所，劳动者则住在外围较为破旧的房屋中。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But why had Caral been built in the first place? Her excavations convinced Shady that Caral once served as a trade center for the region, which extends from the rainforests of the Amazon to the high forests of the Andes. Shady found evidence of a rich trading environment, including seeds of the cocoa bush and necklaces of shells, neither of which was native to the immediate Caral area. This environment gave rise to people who did not take part in the production of food, allowing them to become priests and planners, builders and designers. Thus occupational specialization, elemental to an urban society, emerged.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 但卡拉尔最初为什么会建在这里？发掘工作使沙迪相信，卡拉尔曾是这一地区的贸易中心，贸易范围从亚马孙雨林一直延伸到安第斯山脉的高地森林。她发现了当地贸易环境繁荣的证据，包括可可灌木的种子和贝壳项链；两者都不是卡拉尔附近地区的本地物产。这种环境催生了一批不参与食物生产的人，使他们可以成为祭司、规划者、建造者和设计者。于是，城市社会的一项基本要素——职业分工——出现了。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But what sustained such a trading center and drew travelers to it? Was it food? Shady and her team found the bones of small edible fish, which must have come from the Pacific coast to the west, in the excavations. But they also found evidence of squash, sweet potatoes and beans having been grown locally. Shady theorized that Caral’s early farmers diverted the area’s rivers into canals, which still cross the Supe Valley today, to irrigate their fields. But because she found no traces of maize, which can be traded or stored and used in times of crop failure, she concluded that Caral’s trade leverage was not based on stockpiling food supplies.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 但是什么支撑着这样一个贸易中心，又吸引旅行者来到这里？是食物吗？沙迪及其团队在发掘中发现了可食用小鱼的骨头，这些鱼一定来自西面的太平洋海岸。他们也发现证据，表明当地种植过南瓜、甘薯和豆类。沙迪推测，卡拉尔早期农民把当地河水引入至今仍穿过苏佩河谷的运河，用来灌溉农田。不过，她没有发现玉米的痕迹；玉米既可以交易和储存，也能在作物歉收时食用。因此，她断定卡拉尔的贸易优势并非建立在囤积食物之上。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It was evidence of another crop in the excavations that gave Shady the best clue to Caral’s success. In nearly every excavated building, her team discovered evidence of cotton—seeds, fibers and textiles. Her theory fell into place when a large fishing net made of those fibers, unearthed in an unrelated dig on Peru’s coast, turned out to be as old as Caral. “The farmers of Caral grew the cotton that the fishermen needed to make their nets,” Shady speculates. “And the fishermen gave them shellfish and dried fish in exchange for these nets.” In essence, the people of Caral enabled fishermen to work with larger and more effective nets, which made the resources of the sea more readily available, and the fishermen probably used dried squash grown by the Caral people as flotation devices for their nets.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 发掘中另一种作物的证据，为沙迪理解卡拉尔的成功提供了最佳线索。她的团队几乎在每座发掘出的建筑中都发现了棉花的证据，包括种子、纤维和纺织物。在秘鲁海岸另一处毫不相关的发掘中，人们出土了一张由这种纤维制成的大渔网；结果发现，它的年代与卡拉尔相同，沙迪的理论由此完整起来。“卡拉尔的农民种植棉花，供渔民制作渔网，”沙迪推测，“渔民则用贝类和鱼干交换这些渔网。”从根本上说，卡拉尔人使渔民能够使用更大、更有效的渔网，从而更容易获取海洋资源；渔民还可能把卡拉尔人种植并晒干的南瓜用作渔网浮子。

source.text: Carnivorous plants

translation.text: 食肉植物

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: They attract insects and then eat their flesh. Is that any way for a plant to behave?
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 它们引来昆虫，再吃掉昆虫的身体。植物真该这样做吗？

source.text: They attract insects and then eat their flesh.

translation.text: 它们引来昆虫，再吃掉昆虫的身体。

source.text: Is that any way for a plant to behave?

translation.text: 植物真该这样做吗？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The naturalist and author of On the Origin of Species, Charles Darwin, was fascinated by carnivorous plants. In 1860, soon after he came across his first carnivorous plant — the sundew, Drosera — he wrote, ‘I care more about Drosera than the origin of all the species in the world.’ He spent months running experiments on the plants. He dropped flies and bits of meat on their leaves and watched them slowly fold their sticky tentacles over their prey. He thought it incredible that brushing a leaf with a single strand of human hair was enough to bring about a response. Yet sundews, he observed, ignored raindrops. To react to such a false alarm, he reasoned, would obviously be a great evil to the plant. This was no accident. This was adaptation.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 博物学家、《物种起源》（On the Origin of Species）的作者查尔斯·达尔文对食肉植物十分着迷。1860年，他刚刚遇到自己的第一种食肉植物——茅膏菜（Drosera）不久便写道：“与世界上一切物种的起源相比，我更关心茅膏菜。”他花了数月时间对这种植物进行实验，把苍蝇和肉块放到叶片上，观察叶片怎样慢慢合拢黏性触手，将猎物包住。他认为，仅用一根人的头发轻扫叶片就足以引起反应，实在不可思议。然而，他观察到茅膏菜会忽略雨滴。他推断，如果对这种误报作出反应，显然会给植物带来很大损害。这并非偶然，而是一种适应。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Darwin expanded his studies from sundews to other species in his book Insectivorous Plants. He was amazed at the quickness and power of the Venus flytrap. He showed that when one of its leaves snapped shut, it formed itself into a temporary ‘stomach’, secreting enzymes that could dissolve the prey. He noted that a leaf took more than a week to reopen after closing, and reasoned that the interlocking spines along the margin of the leaf allowed tiny insects to escape, saving the plant the expense of digesting an insufficient meal.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 达尔文在《食虫植物》一书中把研究从茅膏菜扩展到其他物种。他惊叹于捕蝇草动作之迅速、力量之强。他证明，捕蝇草的一片叶子猛然合拢后，会形成一个临时的“胃”，分泌能够溶解猎物的酶。他注意到，叶片闭合后要过一周多才会重新张开，并推断叶缘相互交错的尖刺能让微小昆虫逃脱，使植物不必为消化一顿分量不足的食物付出代价。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Today, biologists using 21st-century tools to study cells and DNA are beginning to understand how these plants hunt, eat, and digest — and how these strange adaptations came about in the first place. Alexander Volkov, a plant physiologist at Oakwood University in Alabama, believes he has figured out the Venus flytrap’s secret. ‘This,’ Volkov declares, ‘is an electrical plant.’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 如今，生物学家借助21世纪的工具研究细胞和DNA，开始了解这些植物如何捕猎、进食和消化，以及这些奇特的适应最初是怎样形成的。美国阿拉巴马州奥克伍德大学的植物生理学家 Alexander Volkov 认为，自己已经解开了捕蝇草的秘密。Volkov 断言：“这是一种依靠电信号活动的植物。”

source.text: Today, biologists using 21st-century tools to study cells and DNA are beginning to understand how these plants hunt, eat, and digest — and how these strange adaptations came about in the first place.

translation.text: 如今，生物学家借助21世纪的工具研究细胞和DNA，开始了解这些植物如何捕猎、进食和消化，以及这些奇特的适应最初是怎样形成的。

source.text: Alexander Volkov, a plant physiologist at Oakwood University in Alabama, believes he has figured out the Venus flytrap’s secret.

translation.text: 美国阿拉巴马州奥克伍德大学的植物生理学家 Alexander Volkov 认为，自己已经解开了捕蝇草的秘密。

source.text: ‘This,’ Volkov declares, ‘is an electrical plant.’

translation.text: Volkov 断言：“这是一种依靠电信号活动的植物。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: When an insect brushes against a hair on the leaf of a Venus flytrap, the movement sets off an electric charge. The charge builds up inside the tissue of the leaf but is not enough to stimulate the snap, which keeps the Venus flytrap from reacting to false alarms, such as raindrops. An insect, however, is likely to brush a second hair, adding enough electric charge for the leaf to close.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 昆虫碰到捕蝇草叶片上的一根触毛时，这一动作会引发电荷。电荷在叶片组织内部逐渐积累，但尚不足以促使叶片猛然闭合，因此捕蝇草不会对雨滴等误报作出反应。不过，昆虫很可能再碰到第二根触毛，使电荷增加到足以让叶片闭合的程度。

source.text: When an insect brushes against a hair on the leaf of a Venus flytrap, the movement sets off an electric charge.

source.text: The charge builds up inside the tissue of the leaf but is not enough to stimulate the snap, which keeps the Venus flytrap from reacting to false alarms, such as raindrops.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Volkov’s experiments reveal that the electric charge travels down fluid-filled tunnels in a leaf, which opens up pores in cell membranes. Water rushes from the cells on the inside of the leaf to those on the outside, causing the leaf to rapidly flip in shape from convex to concave, like a soft contact lens. As the leaves flip, they snap together, trapping an insect inside.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The bladderwort plant has an equally sophisticated way of setting its underwater trap. It pumps water out of tiny air sacs or bladders, lowering the pressure inside. When a water flea or some other small creature swims past, it bends hairs on the bladder, causing a flap to spring apart. The low pressure sucks water in, carrying the creature along with it. In one five-hundredth of a second, the flap swings shut again. The cells in the bladder then begin to pump water out again, creating a new vacuum. Many other species of carnivorous plants act like living flypaper, catching animals on sticky tentacles. Pitcher plants use yet another strategy, growing long tube-shaped leaves into which insects fall. Some of the largest have pitchers up to 30cm deep and can consume whole frogs unlucky enough to fall into them. Sophisticated chemistry helps make the pitcher a death trap.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Nicholas Gotelli, of the University of Vermont, is trying to figure out what evolutionary forces pushed these plants towards meat. Carnivorous plants clearly benefit from eating animals; when scientists feed pitcher plants extra bugs, the plants get bigger. But the benefits of eating flesh are not the ones you might expect. Carnivorous animals, like ourselves, use the carbon in protein and the fat in meat to build muscles and store energy. Carnivorous plants, however, take nitrogen and phosphorus from the flesh in order to build light-harvesting enzymes. Eating animals, in other words, lets carnivorous plants do what all plants do: grow by taking energy directly from the sun.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Unfortunately, they do a really bad job of it. That’s because they have to use a lot of energy to make the equipment they need to catch animals — the enzymes, the pumps, the sticky tentacles, and so on. A pitcher or a flytrap is not very good at photosynthesis because, unlike plants with ordinary leaves, it does not have flat solar panels that can absorb lots of sunlight. Gotelli suspects that only under special conditions are the benefits of being carnivorous greater than the costs. The poor soil of bogs and swamps, where many carnivorous plants grow, offers little nitrogen and phosphorus, so carnivorous plants enjoy an advantage there over ‘conventional’ plants. Also, bogs are often flooded with sunshine, so even an inefficient carnivorous plant can carry out enough photosynthesis to survive. ‘They’re stuck, and they’re making the best of it,’ says Aaron Ellison of Harvard University.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Unfortunately, the adaptations that enable carnivorous plants to survive in harsh habitats also make them extremely sensitive to environmental changes. Chemical fertilizers used in agriculture and pollution from power plants are adding extra nitrogen to many bogs in North America. Carnivorous plants are so finely adapted to low levels of nitrogen that this extra fertilizer is overloading their systems. Humans also threaten carnivorous plants in other ways. The black market trade in exotic carnivorous plants is strong, but even if this can be prevented, carnivorous plants will continue to suffer from other dangers. Their habitat is disappearing, to be replaced by shopping centers and houses. The suppression of wildfires by government agencies allows other plants to grow quickly and outcompete the Venus flytraps. Good news, perhaps, for flies. But a loss for all who delight in the inventiveness of evolution.

source.text: Deep sea discovery

translation.text: 深海发现

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Recent research has provided new insights into how fish communicate.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 近期研究让人们对鱼类如何交流有了新的认识。

source.text: Recent research has provided new insights into how fish communicate.

translation.text: 近期研究让人们对鱼类如何交流有了新的认识。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Nico Michiels is an ecologist from the University of Tübingen in Germany who spends part of each year in Egypt, where he dives in the Red Sea, observing fish life and gathering data on its coral reefs. In September 2007 he decided to find out how far red light could penetrate the ocean depths. Seawater absorbs different colours at different depths, and as an experienced diver, Michiels was aware that red light is extinguished not far below the surface whereas blue-green light penetrates deeper. To find out the depth at which red disappeared in this particular ocean, however, he attached a special plastic filter to his dive mask, which was designed to block out all colours except red. Then he began to descend. In theory, once he reached about 15 metres, he should have been plunged into darkness. Instead, something totally unexpected happened. Sure enough, 20 metres down it was as dark as night. ‘All the fish disappeared. With no light from the surface, they were effectively black and had become invisible,’ he says. ‘But it didn’t stay black for long. Then I saw a group of goby fish with bright red eyes lit up against the background. After that, red spots began to show up all over the reef.’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Nico Michiels 是德国蒂宾根大学的生态学家，每年会有一段时间住在埃及。他在那里潜入红海，观察鱼类生活，并收集珊瑚礁数据。2007年9月，他决定查明红光能深入海洋多远。海水会在不同深度吸收不同颜色的光；作为经验丰富的潜水员，Michiels 知道，红光在离海面不远处便会消失，而蓝绿光可以深入更远。不过，为了确定红光在这片海域消失的具体深度，他在潜水面镜上装了一块特制塑料滤片，只允许红光通过，阻挡其他所有颜色，然后开始下潜。按理论计算，他到约15米深处后应当陷入黑暗。然而，完全出乎意料的事情发生了。果然，在20米深处，周围黑得如同夜晚。“所有鱼都消失了。没有海面光线照射，它们实际上都变成黑色，看不见了，”他说，“但这种漆黑没有持续多久。接着，我看到一群虾虎鱼，鲜红的眼睛在背景中亮了起来。之后，整片珊瑚礁上开始到处出现红色斑点。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Even with the red filter removed, Michiels could pick them out without much trouble once his eyes grew accustomed to the gloom. It seems strange that no diver or researcher had spotted all this red before, but as Michiels points out, no one saw it because no one expected to see it. On that one dive, Michiels discovered three fish species with prominent red markings, and has found many others since.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But how can fish appear red where there’s no red light? Ordinary red pigments* look red because they reflect red light while absorbing all other wavelengths. At 20 metres down, there had to be some other explanation for the red Michiels was seeing. He suspected fluorescence. Fluorescent pigments behave differently from ordinary ones: they receive incoming light of one wavelength, for example blue, and emit light of a longer wavelength, in this case red. On the reef in the Red Sea during daytime, the most likely explanation was that the predominantly blue and green wavelengths at depth triggered the emission of fluorescent red in the fish.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 但在没有红光的地方，鱼怎么会呈现红色？普通红色色素*之所以看起来是红色，是因为它们反射红光，同时吸收其他所有波长的光。在20米深处，米希尔斯看到的红色必定另有解释。他怀疑这是荧光。荧光色素与普通色素的作用方式不同：它们接收某一波长的入射光，例如蓝光，再发出波长更长的光，在这里就是红光。白天的红海珊瑚礁深处以蓝光和绿光为主，最可能的解释是，这些波长触发了鱼体发出红色荧光。

source.text: But how can fish appear red where there’s no red light?

translation.text: 但在没有红光的地方，鱼怎么会呈现红色？

source.text: Ordinary red pigments* look red because they reflect red light while absorbing all other wavelengths.

translation.text: 普通红色色素*之所以看起来是红色，是因为它们反射红光，同时吸收其他所有波长的光。

source.text: At 20 metres down, there had to be some other explanation for the red Michiels was seeing.

translation.text: 在20米深处，米希尔斯看到的红色必定另有解释。

source.text: He suspected fluorescence.

translation.text: 他怀疑这是荧光。

source.text: Fluorescent pigments behave differently from ordinary ones: they receive incoming light of one wavelength, for example blue, and emit light of a longer wavelength, in this case red.

translation.text: 荧光色素与普通色素的作用方式不同：它们接收某一波长的入射光，例如蓝光，再发出波长更长的光，在这里就是红光。

source.text: On the reef in the Red Sea during daytime, the most likely explanation was that the predominantly blue and green wavelengths at depth triggered the emission of fluorescent red in the fish.

translation.text: 白天的红海珊瑚礁深处以蓝光和绿光为主，最可能的解释是，这些波长触发了鱼体发出红色荧光。

blocks.translationNormalizedText: *色素：使某种事物呈现特定颜色的物质。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: With only a week left in Egypt, and lacking the equipment to confirm that the fish were fluorescent, Michiels photographed as many of them as he could. Then, once back in Germany, he bought an assortment of tropical fish and installed them in his lab. Here he confirmed that the fish did indeed fluoresce. In most of the fish he looked at, the fluorescence could be traced to specialised pigment cells that lie in the skin beneath the scales. These cells contain ‘guanine crystals’, which scatter light to give fish their silvery sheen. However, Michiels says they are still not sure exactly what is fluorescing. ‘It’s not the crystals themselves. It’s probably a fluorescent protein built into the crystals, and we have a suspicion that it might be made by bacteria.’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 米希尔斯在埃及只剩一周时间，而且没有设备确认这些鱼是否会发出荧光，于是尽可能多地给它们拍照。回到德国后，他买来各种热带鱼，养在实验室中，并在那里证实这些鱼确实会发出荧光。在他观察的大多数鱼中，荧光都可以追溯到鳞片下方皮肤中的特殊色素细胞。这些细胞含有“鸟嘌呤晶体”，晶体会散射光线，使鱼体呈现银色光泽。不过，米希尔斯说，他们仍不确定究竟是什么物质在发出荧光。“不是晶体本身。很可能是一种嵌在晶体中的荧光蛋白；我们怀疑它可能由细菌制造。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Intrigued, Michiels began a systematic search for red fluorescence in reef fish. He and his colleagues, Nils Anthes and Dennis Sprenger, have identified some 50 species with red fluorescence. The most common markings tend to be on the body towards the head and to a lesser extent around the eyes, and then the fins. To Michiels, the distribution of these markings is one of the strongest indications that red fluorescence has a very particular function: communication with other members of the species. According to several recent studies, a whole range of animals employ fluorescence as a natural highlighter to boost the visibility of body parts they use to signal, for example to ward off enemies. In reef fish, the red tends to be confined to parts of the body used to signal, suggesting these markings serve a similar function. But instead of highlighting an existing colour, the fluorescence gives the fish a colour that otherwise wouldn’t exist. For example, fish commonly use eye rings to signal that they are present and their direction of gaze, and Michiels suspects that red-eyed gobies use signals to indicate their location and keep their group together.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这一现象引起了米希尔斯的兴趣，他开始系统寻找珊瑚礁鱼类身上的红色荧光。他与同事 Nils Anthes 和 Dennis Sprenger 已经确认约有50个物种会发出红色荧光。最常见的斑纹往往位于身体靠近头部的部位，眼睛周围相对少一些，鳍上也有。米希尔斯认为，这些斑纹的分布是最有力的迹象之一，表明红色荧光具有一种非常明确的功能：与同种其他个体交流。近期多项研究显示，许多动物把荧光当作天然的“荧光标记”，提高用于传递信号的身体部位的可见度，例如借此吓退敌人。珊瑚礁鱼类的红色往往只出现在用于传递信号的身体部位，说明这些斑纹可能发挥类似作用。不过，荧光不是让已有颜色更加显眼，而是赋予鱼一种原本不会存在的颜色。例如，鱼类通常用眼圈来表示自己的存在以及视线方向；米希尔斯怀疑，红眼虾虎鱼会用这些信号标明自己的位置，并让群体保持在一起。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Michiels suspects red fluorescence has another important role for some reef fish: helping them blend in. During his first dive with the red filter, he noticed corals glow a dark but faint red too. Against this irregular red background, a fish that glows red all over would be hard to distinguish. More compelling for Michiels is the case of the scorpionfish, which lies perfectly still until food swims past, which it then sucks in.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Yet if red plays any part in a fish’s life, then it must be able to see it. Fish that live in a world dominated by blue-green light are assumed to have eyes tuned to those wavelengths, and most marine fish that have been studied are thought incapable of seeing red. One exception is the seahorse, whose eyes are sensitive to red. As for the other fish, it remains to be seen.

source.text: Dust and the American West

translation.text: 尘土与美国西部

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Images of deserts in the United States show dusty, barren landscapes, but the land may not always have been this way. Ever since settlers moved west across the US, there has been dust, clouds of it, everywhere. It was part of the landscape, or so it seemed to them. But there were no records of the landscape of the West until the settlers arrived. Now, evidence is starting to emerge which suggests that before the settlers, there was very little dust.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 美国沙漠的图像展现出尘土飞扬、寸草不生的景观，但这里或许并非一直如此。自从定居者横跨美国向西迁移，尘土便随处可见，甚至漫天成云。在他们看来，尘土似乎就是当地景观的一部分。然而，定居者到来前，没有人记录过西部的景观。如今，逐渐出现的证据表明，在定居者到来以前，那里的尘土其实非常少。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The evidence comes from the San Juan Mountains of southwest Colorado, downwind of Arizona and New Mexico. There, Jason Neff, a geochemist from the University of Colorado, has been analyzing sediments, the sand, stones and mud, laid down over the past 5,000 years. Atmospheric dust was minimal throughout those five millennia until the mid-19th century, he says, but then, ‘from about 1860 to 1900, dust deposition rates shot up.’
