translation.text: 英国武装部队负责军械的皇家军械部门，用石墨为炮弹模具制作内衬；这样一来，英国生产炮弹的速度比欧洲对手更快，成本也更低。

source.text: In addition to its value to the armed forces, the government quickly realised the commercial potential of the graphite at Borrowdale, and assumed control of all the mines there during the sixteenth century.

translation.text: 除了对军队的重要性，政府也很快意识到 Borrowdale 石墨的商业潜力，于16世纪接管了当地所有矿井。

source.text: Armed guards accompanied the precious graphite all the way down to the metal foundries by the naval shipyards in the south of England.

translation.text: 武装守卫一路护送珍贵的石墨，把它运往英格兰南部海军造船厂附近的金属铸造厂。

source.text: The graphite was so valuable that the locals, who called it wad, started to steal it.

translation.text: 石墨价值极高，当地人把它称为 wad，并开始偷取。

source.text: As a deterrent, an act of Parliament in 1752 made this offence punishable by time in prison.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The Italians originally invented the wooden casing to hold a thin rod of plumbago firmly in place for ease of writing. Italian craftsmen hollowed out two small sections of cedar wood, into one of which they laid the lead. They then glued the other section over the top and left the two halves to set. When dry, the whole apparatus formed what today we know as a pencil. The Germans took this technique and developed it further by applying mass-production techniques to pencils. At the same time Nicolas-Jacques Conté, a French officer in Napoleon Bonaparte’s army during the late 1700s, developed a method of mixing powdered graphite and clay together for firing in a kiln. Adding more clay to the mixture helped make the pencil harder, sharper, and more precise in its mark. More graphite helped make a pencil mark that was softer, thicker and darker.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The pencil has turned out to be a remarkably resilient and valuable tool whose use has survived well into our high-tech times, as a well-known story shows. It is sometimes said that the American space programme spent millions of dollars to invent a pen capable of writing in the zero gravity of space. The Russians, by contrast, simply equipped their astronauts with good old-fashioned pencils that never let them down. It should be pointed out though, that the popular myth about Americans overlooking the practical advantages of pencils in zero gravity is merely fiction. In actual fact, both American and Russian astronauts were equipped with pencils in their respective countries’ first space flights. A private company later developed pens for writing in zero gravity. In fact, astronauts of every nation now use pens. But no matter — pencils remain in use in every classroom, every planning, building and drawing office, and in every art studio in the world. And there is nothing to suggest that we are likely to invent anything better than graphite to use in our pencils.

source.text: The History of the Pencil

translation.text: 铅笔的历史

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Pencils have existed for millennia. It is known that the ancient Egyptians, Greeks and Romans all used small pieces of metal as writing instruments, and that 14th-century European artists made pale grey drawings with thin rods of lead, silver or zinc. It is, however, generally accepted that the history of the modern pencil began in the 16th century, in the hilly, rural county of Cumberland in north-west England.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 铅笔形式的书写工具已存在数千年。人们知道，古埃及人、古希腊人和古罗马人都曾用小块金属书写；14世纪的欧洲艺术家则用铅、银或锌制成的细棒画出浅灰色图画。不过，人们普遍认为，现代铅笔的历史始于16世纪英格兰西北部多山的乡村郡——坎伯兰。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Some time before 1565, an enormous deposit of the soft, dark grey mineral now known as graphite was discovered in the Borrowdale district of the county. Then, as now, Cumberland was a farming area, and the locals found the mineral useful for marking their sheep so they could identify the ones that belonged to them. It was thought to be a form of lead, and so was referred to as plumbago, a term deriving from the Latin name for that element. However, the mineral was later identified as a form of carbon, and in 1789 the German geologist Abraham Gottlob Werner renamed it graphite, a word based on the ancient Greek grapho, meaning ‘draw’ or ‘write’.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The graphite found at Borrowdale was extremely dense and it could easily be sawn into sticks to be used for marking, writing or drawing. But because graphite is also soft, it requires some form of encasement around it, and so the sticks were initially wrapped in string for stability and ease of use. The news of the usefulness of these early pencils spread far and wide, attracting the attention of artists throughout Europe.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Although deposits of graphite existed in other parts of the world, they were not of the same exceptional purity and quality as Borrowdale graphite, and had to be crushed to a powder to get rid of the impurities. England therefore continued to enjoy a monopoly on the production of pencils until a method of reconstituting the graphite powder could be found. English pencils continued to be made with sticks cut from pure Borrowdale graphite into the 1860s, after which the design was modified. The town of Keswick, close to the Cumberland graphite find, still manufactures pencils today, the factory also being the location of the Cumberland pencil museum.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Experimentation in pencil production was widespread across Europe during the 16th and 17th centuries. Around 1560, an Italian couple named Simonio and Lyndiana Bernacotti made what are probably the first blueprints for the modern, wood-encased pencil. Their concept involved the hollowing out of a stick of juniper wood, and placing a stick of graphite inside. Shortly thereafter, a superior technique to that of the Bernacottis was adopted: two wooden halves were carved, a graphite stick inserted, and the halves then glued together — essentially the same method in use to this day.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Today, pencils are manufactured around the world, using graphite from a number of sources. Most manufacturers use a mix of graphite and clay as the core of their pencils. Each of these substances is ground into a fine powder, which goes on to be cleaned in order to remove any impurities. After the two types of powders have been dried, they are mixed together using water. The amount of clay added to the mixture depends on how hard the pencil is intended to be — higher proportions of clay will make the pencil harder — and the amount of time spent grinding the mixture determines the quality of the core. The graphite-clay mixture is then shaped into long sticks, and after drying these are heated in a kiln to 1,200°C. In the next step in the process, the graphite-clay sticks are immersed in melted wax, which is absorbed into the mixture and helps to make it write more smoothly. In the next stage, the manufacturers use thin planks of cedar wood or juniper wood. Several long parallel grooves are cut into the planks, and the graphite-clay sticks are inserted into these. A second plank which has been prepared in the same way is then glued on top. The whole assembly is then cut into separate pencils. The outside may then be varnished, retaining the natural colour of the wood, or painted in different colours.

source.text: The Importance of Business Cards

translation.text: 名片的重要性

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: The exchange of business cards is as close to a universal ritual as you can find in the business world.
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 在商业世界中，交换名片几乎是你能见到的最普遍的礼仪。

source.text: The exchange of business cards is as close to a universal ritual as you can find in the business world.

translation.text: 在商业世界中，交换名片几乎是你能见到的最普遍的礼仪。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The ritual may be universal, but the details of business cards and how they are swapped vary across countries. Americans throw their cards casually across a table; the Japanese make the exchange of cards a formal ceremony. While there are cards that are discreet and understated, others are crammed full of details and titles. Some businesspeople hand out 24-carat gold cards, and there are kindergarten children who have cards with not only their own contact details, but also with the job descriptions of their parents and even grandparents. This practice has become so common in parts of New York, for example, that the use of such cards is now prohibited by some of these institutions.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这种礼仪或许遍及世界，但名片的具体样式和交换方式因国家而异。美国人会随手把名片扔到桌子对面；日本人则把交换名片当作正式仪式。有些名片低调朴素，另一些却塞满各种资料和头衔。有些商务人士递出24K金名片；还有些幼儿园儿童的名片不仅印着自己的联系方式，甚至列出父母乃至祖父母的职业。例如，在纽约部分地区，这种做法已经十分普遍，以至于一些幼儿园如今禁止使用此类名片。

translation.text: 例如，在纽约部分地区，这种做法已经十分普遍，以至于一些幼儿园如今禁止使用此类名片。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Cards have been around a long time in one form or another. The Chinese invented calling cards in the 15th century to give people notice that they intended to pay them a visit, but these were for social purposes only. Then, in the 17th century, European businesspeople invented a new type of card to act as miniature advertisements, signalling the advent of the business card. In today’s world, business cards can cause people to have strong emotional reactions. According to one experienced company director, very few things can provoke more heated discussion at a board meeting than the composition of the company’s business cards.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 各种形式的卡片已经存在很久。15世纪，中国人发明了拜访卡，用来提前通知别人自己打算登门，不过这种卡片只用于社交。到了17世纪，欧洲商人发明了一种充当微型广告的新卡片，预示着商业名片的出现。在今天的世界里，名片会引发强烈的情绪反应。一位经验丰富的公司董事表示，在董事会上，很少有什么事情比公司名片的内容和设计更能引发激烈讨论。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Lots of companies try to promote themselves by altering the form of the card. Employees at one famous toy company give out little plastic figures with their contact details stamped on them. One fast-food company has business cards which are shaped like a portion of French fries. A Canadian divorce lawyer once gave out cards that could be torn in two – one half for each of the spouses. For many business commentators, such gimmicky business cards prove that the use of a physical business card is nearly at an end. After all, why bother exchanging bits of thick paper at all when you can simply swap electronic versions by smartphone?
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 许多公司试图通过改变名片的形式来宣传自己。一家知名玩具公司的员工会分发小塑料人偶，上面印有联系方式；一家快餐公司的名片做成一份炸薯条的形状；一名加拿大离婚律师曾分发可以撕成两半的名片，夫妻双方各拿一半。在许多商业评论者看来，这类花哨名片证明，实体名片的时代已接近尾声。毕竟，既然可以直接用智能手机交换电子名片，何必还要交换厚纸片呢？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: However, one can just as well argue the opposite: that business cards are here to stay, and, in a business world full of meetings and correspondence, it is more important than ever that your card is unique. Attempts to reinvent business cards for the digital age have not been successful. Even at the latest technology conferences, people still greet each other by handing out little rectangles made from paper rather than using a digital alternative.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，人们同样可以提出相反的观点：名片不会消失；在一个充满会议和通信往来的商业世界中，让自己的名片与众不同反而比以往任何时候都更重要。为数字时代重新设计名片的尝试并未成功。即使在最新的科技会议上，人们见面时仍会递出纸制小长方片，而不是使用数字替代品。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: To understand business cards, it is necessary to understand how business works. That business cards are thriving in a digital age is a forceful reminder that there is much about business that is timeless. According to Kate Jones, a business lecturer, there is one eternal and inescapable issue. Her 2006 study of more than 200 business executives in North America found that trust was the key element for running a successful business. It is vital to be able to look someone in the eye and decide what sort of person they are. In this way, you can transform acquaintanceships into relationships. A good proportion of business life will always be about building social connections – having dinner or playing sport with clients and colleagues – and while computers can deal with administrative tasks, it is still human beings that have to focus on the emotional.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 要理解名片，就必须理解商业如何运作。名片在数字时代依然兴盛，有力地提醒我们：商业中有许多东西不会随时代改变。商业讲师 Kate Jones 表示，有一个永恒而无法回避的问题。她在2006年调查了北美200多名企业高管，发现信任是成功经营企业的关键。能够直视一个人的眼睛，判断对方是什么样的人，至关重要。这样才能把泛泛之交转变为真正的关系。商业生活中总有很大一部分在于建立社会联系，例如与客户和同事共进晚餐或一起运动。计算机可以处理行政事务，但情感层面仍必须由人来关注。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The rapid advance of globalisation means that this relationship-building process is becoming ever more demanding. Managers have to put more effort in when dealing with international counterparts, especially when there is not a common language, which is so often the case these days. A recent UK survey showed that chief executives of global organisations now routinely spend three out of every four weeks on international travel. It is in these situations that business cards are doubly useful, as they are a quick way of establishing connections. Cards can also remind you that you have actually met someone in a face-to-face meeting rather than just searched for them on the Internet. Looking through piles of different cards can enhance your memory in ways that simply looking through uniform electronic lists would never do.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Janet McIntyre is a leading expert on business cards in today’s world. She maintains that as companies become more complex, cards are essential in determining the exact status of every contact you meet in multinational corporations. Janet also explains how exchanging business cards can be an effective way of initiating a conversation, because it gives people a ritual to follow when they first meet a new business contact.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Janet McIntyre 是当今名片研究领域的一位权威专家。她认为，随着公司结构越来越复杂，名片对于确定你在跨国公司遇到的每一位联系人究竟处于什么职位和层级，十分重要。Janet 还解释说，交换名片是开启谈话的有效方式，因为它让人们首次见到新的商业联系人时，有一套礼仪可以遵循。

source.text: Janet McIntyre is a leading expert on business cards in today’s world.

translation.text: Janet McIntyre 是当今名片研究领域的一位权威专家。

source.text: She maintains that as companies become more complex, cards are essential in determining the exact status of every contact you meet in multinational corporations.

translation.text: 她认为，随着公司结构越来越复杂，名片对于确定你在跨国公司遇到的每一位联系人究竟处于什么职位和层级，十分重要。

source.text: Janet also explains how exchanging business cards can be an effective way of initiating a conversation, because it gives people a ritual to follow when they first meet a new business contact.

translation.text: Janet 还解释说，交换名片是开启谈话的有效方式，因为它让人们首次见到新的商业联系人时，有一套礼仪可以遵循。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The business world is obsessed with the idea of creating and inventing new things that will change the way we do everything, and this does lead to progress. But there are lots of things that do not need to be changed and, in Janet McIntyre’s view, tradition also has an equally valuable role to play. Therefore the practice of exchanging business cards is likely to continue in the business world.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 商业世界痴迷于创造和发明新事物，希望它们改变我们做一切事情的方式，而这确实会带来进步。不过，许多事物其实不需要改变；在 Janet McIntyre 看来，传统也能发挥同样宝贵的作用。因此，交换名片的做法很可能会继续存在于商业世界中。

source.text: The last man who knew everything

translation.text: 最后一个无所不知的人

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In the 21st century, it would be quite impossible for even the most learned man to know everything. However, as recently as the 18th century, there were those whose knowledge encompassed most of the information available at that time.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在21世纪，即使学识最渊博的人也绝不可能知晓一切。然而，就在并不久远的18世纪，仍有人掌握了当时几乎所有可获得的信息。

source.text: However, as recently as the 18th century, there were those whose knowledge encompassed most of the information available at that time.

translation.text: 然而，就在并不久远的18世纪，仍有人掌握了当时几乎所有可获得的信息。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This is a review of a biography of one such man.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 本文评介的，正是这样一个人的传记。

source.text: This is a review of a biography of one such man.

translation.text: 本文评介的，正是这样一个人的传记。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Thomas Young (1773–1829) contributed 63 articles to the great British encyclopaedia, Encyclopaedia Britannica, including 46 biographical entries (mostly on scientists and classical scholars) and substantial essays on ‘Bridge’ (a card game), ‘Egypt’, ‘Languages’ and ‘Tides’. Was someone who could write authoritatively about so many subjects a genius, or a dilettante? In an ambitious biography, Andrew Robinson argues that Young is a good contender to be described as “the last man who knew everything”. Young has competition, however: the phrase, which Robinson uses as the title of his biography of Young, also serves as the subtitle of two other recent biographies – Leonard Warren’s 1998 life of palaeontologist Joseph Leidy (1823–1891) and Paula Findlen’s 2004 book on Athanasius Kircher (1602–1680).
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Thomas Young（1773—1829）为英国大型百科全书《大英百科全书》撰写了63篇条目，其中包括46篇人物传记——大多介绍科学家和古典学者——以及有关“桥牌”（一种纸牌游戏）、“埃及”、“语言”和“潮汐”的长篇文章。一个能够权威论述如此多主题的人，究竟是天才，还是涉猎广却不够深入的业余爱好者？Andrew Robinson 在一部雄心勃勃的传记中主张，Young 很有资格被称为“最后一个无所不知的人”。不过，Young 也有竞争者：Robinson 把这句话用作 Young 传记的标题，而最近另外两部传记也用它作副标题——一本是 Leonard Warren 于1998年出版的古生物学家 Joseph Leidy（1823—1891）传记，另一本是 Paula Findlen 于2004年出版的 Athanasius Kircher（1602—1680）传记。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Young, of course, did more than write encyclopaedia entries. He presented his first paper, on the human eye, to the prestigious academic institution, the Royal Society of London, at the age of 20 and was elected a Fellow of the Society shortly afterwards. In the paper, which sought to explain how the eye focuses on objects at varying distances, Young hypothesised that this was achieved by changes in the shape of the lens. He also theorised that light travels in waves and believed that, to be able to see in colour, there must be three receptors in the eye corresponding to the three principal colours (red, green and violet) to which the retina could respond. All these hypotheses were subsequently proved correct.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 当然，Young 所做的远不只是撰写百科全书条目。20岁时，他向享有盛誉的学术机构伦敦皇家学会（Royal Society of London）提交了自己的第一篇论文，主题是人眼；不久后，他当选为学会会员。这篇论文试图解释眼睛如何聚焦不同距离的物体，Young 推测这是通过晶状体形状的变化实现的。他还提出光以波的形式传播，并认为，要看见颜色，眼中必定有三种分别对应三种主要颜色——红、绿、紫——的感受器，视网膜能够对这些颜色作出反应。这些假说后来全都得到证实。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Later in his life, when he was in his forties, Young was instrumental in cracking the code that unlocked the unknown script on the Rosetta Stone, a tablet found in Egypt by the Napoleonic army in 1799. The stone has text in three alphabets: Greek, Egyptian hieroglyphs and another script that was originally unrecognisable. The unrecognisable script is now known as demotic and, as Young deduced, is directly related to Egyptian hieroglyphs. His initial work on this appeared in the Britannica entry ‘Egypt’. In another entry, Young coined the term ‘Indo-European’ to describe the family of languages spoken throughout most of Europe and northern India. These works are landmark achievements for a man who was a child prodigy but who, unlike many remarkable children, did not fade into obscurity as an adult.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 后来，Young 四十多岁时，在破解罗塞塔石碑未知文字的工作中发挥了关键作用。这块石碑由拿破仑军队于1799年在埃及发现，其文字采用三套书写系统：希腊文、埃及象形文字，以及另一种起初无法辨认的文字。后一种文字如今称为世俗体；正如 Young 所推断的，它与埃及象形文字有直接关系。他最初的研究成果出现在《大英百科全书》的“埃及”条目中。在另一篇条目里，Young 创造了“印欧语系”一词，用来描述通行于欧洲大部分地区和印度北部的一组语言。这些成果是里程碑式的成就。Young 从小就是神童，但与许多出色的孩子不同，他成年后并未沉寂无闻。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Born in 1773 in Somerset, England, Young lived with his maternal grandfather from an early age. He devoured books from the age of two and excelled at Latin, Greek, mathematics and natural philosophy (the 18th-century term for science). After leaving school, he was greatly encouraged by Richard Brocklesby, a physician and Fellow of the Royal Society. Following Brocklesby’s lead, Young decided to pursue a career in medicine. He studied in London and then moved on to more formal education in Edinburgh, Göttingen and Cambridge. After completing his medical training at the University of Cambridge in 1808, Young set up practice as a physician in London and, a few years later, was appointed physician at St George’s Hospital.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Young 于1773年出生在英格兰萨默塞特郡，很小就与外祖父一起生活。他从两岁起便如饥似渴地读书，在拉丁语、希腊语、数学和自然哲学——18世纪对科学的称呼——方面表现出色。离开学校后，医生兼皇家学会会员 Richard Brocklesby 给了他很大鼓励。Young 追随 Brocklesby 的道路，决定从医。他先在伦敦学习，之后又前往爱丁堡、哥廷根和剑桥接受更正规的教育。1808年，他在剑桥大学完成医学训练，随后在伦敦开业行医；几年后，他被任命为圣乔治医院的医生。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Young’s skill as a physician, however, did not equal his talent as a scholar of natural philosophy or linguistics. In 1801, he had been appointed to a professorship of natural philosophy at the Royal Institution, where he delivered as many as 60 lectures a year. His opinions were sought by civic and national authorities on matters such as the introduction of gas lighting to London streets and methods of ship construction. From 1819, he was Superintendent of the Nautical Almanac and Secretary to the Board of Longitude. Between 1816 and 1825, he contributed many entries to the Encyclopaedia Britannica, and throughout his career he authored numerous other essays, papers and books.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，Young 作为医生的本领，不及他研究自然哲学或语言学的才华。1801年，他获聘担任皇家研究院自然哲学教授，每年讲授多达60场课程。市政和国家部门会就伦敦街道引入煤气照明、船舶建造方法等问题征求他的意见。1819年起，他担任《航海年鉴》主管和经度委员会秘书。1816至1825年间，他为《大英百科全书》撰写了许多条目；在整个职业生涯中，他还创作了大量文章、论文和书籍。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Young is a perfect subject for a biography – perfect, but daunting. Few men contributed so much to so many technical fields. Robinson’s aim is to introduce non-scientists to Young’s work and life. He succeeds, providing clear expositions of the technical material (especially that on optics and Egyptian hieroglyphs). Some readers of this book will, like Robinson, find Young’s accomplishments impressive; others will see him, as some historians have, as a dilettante. Yet despite the rich material presented in this book, readers will not end up knowing Young personally. We catch glimpses of a playful Young, doodling Greek and Latin phrases in his notes on medical lectures and translating the verses that a young lady had written on the walls of a summerhouse into Greek elegiacs. Young was introduced into elite society, attended the theatre and learned to dance and play the flute. In addition, he was an accomplished horseman. However, his personal life looks pale next to his vibrant career and studies.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Young 是传记的绝佳主人公——绝佳，却也让人望而生畏。很少有人能在如此众多的技术领域作出这么多贡献。Robinson 的目标是向非科学专业的读者介绍 Young 的工作和一生。他做到了，对技术材料作出了清楚说明，尤其是光学和埃及象形文字方面的内容。本书的一些读者会像 Robinson 一样，认为 Young 的成就令人钦佩；另一些人则会像某些历史学家那样，把他视为涉猎虽广却不够深入的业余爱好者。然而，尽管书中材料丰富，读者最终仍无法真正了解 Young 本人。我们偶尔看到他顽皮的一面：他会在医学讲义笔记上随手写下希腊语和拉丁语短句，还会把一位年轻女子写在凉亭墙上的诗句译成希腊挽歌体。Young 进入上流社会，去剧院看戏，学习跳舞和吹长笛。他还是一名技艺娴熟的骑手。不过，与他充满活力的事业和研究相比，他的个人生活显得黯淡。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Young married Eliza Maxwell in 1804, and according to Robinson, “their marriage was happy and she appreciated his work”. Almost all we know about her is that she sustained her husband through some acrimonious disputes about optics and that she worried about money when his medical career was slow to take off. Little evidence survives concerning the complexities of Young’s relationships with his mother and father, and Robinson does not credit them with shaping Young’s extraordinary mind. Despite the lack of personal detail, anyone interested in what it means to be a genius should read this book.

source.text: The Origins of Weather Forecasting

translation.text: 天气预报的起源

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The world’s first public weather forecast appeared in The Times newspaper over 150 years ago: the beginning of a service that gives everyone something to comment on
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 150多年前，世界上第一份面向公众的天气预报刊登在《泰晤士报》（The Times）上；一项人人都有话可说的服务由此诞生。

source.text: The world’s first public weather forecast appeared in The Times newspaper over 150 years ago: the beginning of a service that gives everyone something to comment on

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The pioneering forecast on August 1, 1861, was introduced with a deceptively simple heading: ‘General weather probable during next two days.’ But those few words started an ongoing controversy that still continues today - after all, everyone remembers the forecasts that go wrong, but rarely the ones that are right.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 1861年8月1日，这份开创性的预报以一个看似简单的标题登场：“未来两天可能出现的总体天气状况。”然而，短短几个词引发了一场延续至今的争议——毕竟，人们总会记住预报出错的时候，却很少记得它预测准确的时候。

source.text: But those few words started an ongoing controversy that still continues today - after all, everyone remembers the forecasts that go wrong, but rarely the ones that are right.

translation.text: 然而，短短几个词引发了一场延续至今的争议——毕竟，人们总会记住预报出错的时候，却很少记得它预测准确的时候。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The first forecast was the idea of Admiral Robert FitzRoy, head of the newly founded Meteorological Department, and one of Britain’s greatest but least-known heroes. It was a brave undertaking, because in those days predicting the weather had gained a reputation similar to astrology or fortune-telling. The few people who attempted it had become a national joke when their forecasts inevitably went wrong.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 第一份天气预报是新成立的气象部门负责人 Robert FitzRoy 海军上将提出的。他是英国最伟大却最鲜为人知的英雄之一。这是一项勇敢的尝试，因为在当时，预测天气的名声和占星或算命差不多。少数尝试过的人，常因预报免不了出错而沦为全国笑柄。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: FitzRoy was different, though. His background was faultless, most famously his captaining of the ship HMS Beagle on Charles Darwin’s voyage around the world, which eventually led to the publication of Darwin’s well-known book On the Origin of Species. When FitzRoy retired from active service as an admiral in Britain’s navy, he was looking for a new direction. He subsequently secured a job as chief statistician at the Meteorological Department, part of the Board of Trade. Parliament had voted to set up and fund the Meteorological Department on June 30, 1854, to chart the safest sailing routes across the Atlantic Ocean. However, the British Government was not impressed with the idea of collecting weather reports and establishing a weather forecast, and the suggestion by one Member of Parliament for this was met with laughter from the other MPs.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，FitzRoy 不同。他的履历无可挑剔，其中最著名的经历，是担任“小猎犬号”（HMS Beagle）船长，参与达尔文（Charles Darwin）的环球航行；这次航行最终促成达尔文的名著《物种起源》（On the Origin of Species）出版。FitzRoy 以英国海军上将身份退出现役后，正在寻找新的发展方向。后来，他获得气象部门首席统计师一职；该部门隶属贸易委员会。1854年6月30日，议会投票决定成立气象部门并提供资金，以绘制横渡大西洋的最安全航线。然而，英国政府对收集天气报告和建立天气预报并不感兴趣；一名议员提出相关建议时，其他议员都报以笑声。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: FitzRoy was given a staff of three clerks in a small office in London, but he soon grew bored with the tedium of transcribing thousands of ships’ reports. Instead, he focused on a much more pressing issue - the huge loss of life at sea from storms. This problem came to a head in 1859, when gale-force winds sank the ship named Royal Charter, with the loss of 430 lives, within sight of the shore. Even in those days when ships regularly sank in storms, the loss of the Royal Charter was considered a national tragedy. FitzRoy stirred up feelings even further when he wrote a letter to The Times newspaper explaining that the storm had been entirely predictable.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: FitzRoy 在伦敦一间小办公室里得到三名文员协助，但他很快厌倦了抄录成千上万份船舶报告的枯燥工作。于是，他转而关注一个紧迫得多的问题：风暴造成大量海上人员死亡。1859年，这个问题达到顶点。烈风在离岸边仍清晰可见的地方击沉了 Royal Charter 号，造成430人死亡。即使在那个船只经常因风暴沉没的年代，Royal Charter 号的灾难仍被视为全国性悲剧。FitzRoy 随后致信《泰晤士报》，说明这场风暴完全可以预测，进一步激起了公众情绪。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: That same year, a total of 1,645 lives were lost off the British coast, and FitzRoy wrote repeatedly to The Times pushing for a storm-warning service for shipping. This was just the right moment for a national forecasting service. Knowledge of the weather was improving, barometer readings gave warning of approaching storms, and the invention of the electric telegraph and Morse code in 1844 gave instant communication for the first time.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: So in February 1861, FitzRoy pressed ahead with a storm-warning service. Previously, weather reports had been unreliable, but FitzRoy’s innovation was to issue ships with standardised instruments which allowed for accurate weather reports. At exactly the same time each day the information was sent to him by telegraph, and he was able to draw up more detailed weather maps. The approach of an incoming storm could be recognised, and from London, FitzRoy could telegraph warnings to ports on the coast, where an ingenious system of flags was hoisted up high for passing ships to read. This represented the biggest advance in shipping safety after the introduction of the lifeboat, and in subsequent years the number of lives lost around Britain fell by about a third. FitzRoy became a hero to the fishing and maritime fleets.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 于是，1861年2月，FitzRoy 推动建立风暴预警服务。过去的天气报告并不可靠，而 FitzRoy 的创新是为船只配备标准化仪器，从而取得准确的天气报告。每天在完全相同的时间，各地通过电报把信息传给他，他也因此能够绘制更详细的天气图。人们可以识别正在逼近的风暴；FitzRoy 从伦敦用电报把警报发给沿海港口，那里会升起一套巧妙设计的旗帜，让过往船只读取。这是救生艇问世后航运安全领域最大的进步。此后几年，英国周边海域的死亡人数下降了约三分之一。FitzRoy 成为渔船队和海运船队心目中的英雄。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Encouraged by his storm-warning success, FitzRoy then started a public weather forecasting service. As he had a close connection with The Times, this newspaper introduced his daily forecast in August 1861. It attracted huge attention, including from Queen Victoria, who regularly sent messengers to FitzRoy’s office to get a forecast for the sea crossing over the Solent to an island which she liked to visit off the south coast of England. He was also popular with ordinary fishermen, who were happy not to be out at sea in bad weather. The owners of fishing vessels, however, were not supportive of FitzRoy’s forecasts, which often caused delays for them when bad weather was forecast.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Nevertheless, weather forecasting at that time was very difficult, and one mistake could result in much bad publicity. It wasn’t long before some forecasts turned out wrong, and the letters pages of The Times were full of heated correspondence. It is indisputable that FitzRoy was way ahead of his time, but it is only in recent years that he has been recognised as a towering figure in meteorology, with the honour of an area of sea being given his name in the shipping forecast (a radio broadcast of weather reports for the seas around Britain). His extraordinary determination to get forecasting established cost him dearly though, and he died prematurely. But his legacy lives on, because late in his life he published a book about weather forecasting which was recognised by other scientists to be well ahead of its time.

source.text: The Pyramid of Cestius

translation.text: 塞斯提乌斯金字塔

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A 2,000-year-old pyramid in the city of Rome has been restored by archaeologists.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 考古学家修复了罗马城内一座有2,000年历史的金字塔。

source.text: A 2,000-year-old pyramid in the city of Rome has been restored by archaeologists.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Though Rome draws tourists from around the world to its many impressive sites, one notable monument there has never attracted nearly as much interest: the Pyramid of Cestius. But why would there be a pyramid in Italy? After the Roman conquest of Egypt in 30 B.C., Egyptian architectural style became the fashion in Rome.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 罗马众多令人赞叹的景点吸引着世界各地的游客，但当地一座引人注目的古迹从未获得同等程度的关注：塞斯提乌斯金字塔。不过，意大利为什么会有金字塔？公元前30年罗马征服埃及后，埃及建筑风格在罗马流行起来。

source.text: Though Rome draws tourists from around the world to its many impressive sites, one notable monument there has never attracted nearly as much interest: the Pyramid of Cestius.

translation.text: 罗马众多令人赞叹的景点吸引着世界各地的游客，但当地一座引人注目的古迹从未获得同等程度的关注：塞斯提乌斯金字塔。

source.text: But why would there be a pyramid in Italy?

translation.text: 不过，意大利为什么会有金字塔？

source.text: After the Roman conquest of Egypt in 30 B.C., Egyptian architectural style became the fashion in Rome.

translation.text: 公元前30年罗马征服埃及后，埃及建筑风格在罗马流行起来。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Though obelisks and other monuments inspired by Egypt’s great pyramids sprang up around the city, only two actual pyramids are known to have been built. The only one left standing, the Pyramid of Cestius, was designed as the burial pyramid for a Roman politician named Caius Cestius, who ordered that the building work be completed within a period of 330 days. Construction took place at some point between 18 B.C. and 12 B.C. Cestius’ pyramid had a layer of white Carrara marble on the outside, and was constructed from brick held together by a basic kind of cement on the inside. One of the things that strikes you when you look at the pyramid is how steep it is, so that the shape of Cestius’ pyramid is quite unlike that of typical Egyptian ones. This is a difference that could have been the result of inaccurate information sent back to Rome by soldiers who saw the pyramids in person in Egypt. Alternatively, Roman builders could have drawn inspiration from the pyramids in Nubia, a region located in what is today northern Sudan and southern Egypt.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 方尖碑和其他受埃及大金字塔启发的建筑在城中纷纷出现，但已知真正建成的金字塔只有两座。唯一保存至今的塞斯提乌斯金字塔，是罗马政治家 Caius Cestius 的墓葬金字塔；他下令必须在330天内完成工程。金字塔建于公元前18年至公元前12年之间的某个时期。它外层覆盖白色卡拉拉大理石，内部由砖块砌成，并以一种简单的水泥黏合。看到这座金字塔时，最引人注意的一点是它坡度很陡，因此外形与典型的埃及金字塔大不相同。这种差异可能源于亲眼见过埃及金字塔的士兵传回罗马的信息不准确。另一种可能是，罗马建筑者从努比亚金字塔获得了灵感；努比亚位于今天的苏丹北部和埃及南部。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: At the time of its construction, since there was a strict Roman law prohibiting the placement of tombs within the city itself, the Pyramid of Cestius would have stood in the countryside. Rome grew enormously during the next two centuries, and, by the 3rd century A.D., the pyramid would have been surrounded by buildings. We also know that in the 3rd century A.D., the Pyramid of Cestius was hidden behind a high wall on the orders of Emperor Aurelian; this probably helped it survive throughout the centuries to come, even as other ancient monuments disappeared. By the Middle Ages, the pyramid was covered in vegetation and thick dirt, and popular myth had developed that it might be a tomb for one of the twin brothers Romulus and Remus, who were regarded as the men who had established the city of Rome. Cestius’ actual tomb within the pyramid and the inscription identifying the pyramid as his weren’t rediscovered until the 1660s, when the pyramid underwent restoration. During excavations, when trees and plants were cleared away, two marble bases were found in front of the pyramid, as well as fragments of bronze statues that had once stood on them, on either side of the pyramid. The people employed to excavate the pyramid did not find the urn that would have contained Cestius’ remains, but they did come across a tunnel. It was quite possible, therefore, that robbers had at some earlier time removed the contents of the tomb. But while some of the features of Cestius’ tomb no longer exist, at least the pyramid itself has survived.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 金字塔建造时，罗马法律严格禁止把坟墓设在城内，因此塞斯提乌斯金字塔当时应当坐落在乡间。此后两个世纪，罗马大幅扩张；到公元3世纪，金字塔周围应该已经布满建筑。我们还知道，公元3世纪，奥勒良皇帝下令在塞斯提乌斯金字塔前筑起高墙，把它遮在后面。即使其他古代建筑相继消失，这道墙很可能帮助金字塔在随后数个世纪里保存下来。到中世纪，金字塔被植被和厚厚的泥土覆盖，民间还流传一种说法，认为它可能是孪生兄弟 Romulus 和 Remus 中一人的坟墓；这两人被视为罗马城的建立者。直到17世纪60年代金字塔修复时，内部真正属于塞斯提乌斯的墓室以及表明金字塔主人身份的铭文才重新被发现。发掘期间，树木和植物被清除，人们在金字塔前方发现两座大理石基座，还发现了曾立在基座上的青铜雕像碎片；这些雕像原本分立于金字塔两侧。参与发掘的人没有找到本应盛放塞斯提乌斯遗骸的骨灰瓮，却发现了一条隧道。因此，很可能曾有盗墓者在更早时候取走墓中物品。塞斯提乌斯墓葬的某些部分虽然已不存在，至少金字塔本身保留了下来。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Today, the foundations of Cestius’ pyramid rest below street level near an intersection with heavy traffic, so that passing tourists and residents could easily fail to notice its full height of 119 feet. Across the intersection is the Piramide station, located on Line B of the Rome Metro. In 2011, the Japanese clothing-company entrepreneur Yuzo Yagi, president of Yagi Tsusho Ltd, announced his intention to help the Italian government pay for an ambitious renovation of the Pyramid of Cestius. ‘It’s an act of gratitude,’ he later told journalists. ‘Our company has grown thanks to Italy.’ Work began at the site shortly after Yagi signed an official agreement with the Special Superintendency for the Archaeological Heritage of Rome, and was completed ahead of schedule thanks to his 2-million-euro contribution.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 如今，塞斯提乌斯金字塔的地基位于街面以下，旁边是车流繁忙的十字路口，因此路过的游客和居民很容易忽略它119英尺的完整高度。路口对面是罗马地铁B线的 Piramide 站。2011年，日本服装企业家、Yagi Tsusho Ltd 总裁 Yuzo Yagi 宣布，打算帮助意大利政府承担修缮塞斯提乌斯金字塔这一宏大工程的费用。他后来告诉记者：“这是一种感恩之举。我们公司因意大利而发展壮大。”Yagi 与罗马考古遗产特别监管局签署正式协议后不久，现场工程便启动。由于他捐助了200万欧元，工程提前完工。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As archaeologist Leonardo Guarnieri explained to journalists, officials are now conducting tours of the newly renovated pyramid twice a month by reservation. Visitors who take advantage of the tour can make their way through a narrow corridor in order to enter the burial chamber itself. It is within these walls that they can admire the frescoes: watercolour paintings typical of the time. In the chamber, it is possible to make out four frescoes of the winged Roman goddess of war, Victoria, a figure from Roman legend, as well as a series of vases, the type that would have been used for special rituals and purification purposes. We know from the writings of earlier visitors that there used to be more here, but the majority have disappeared over time. Only one problem remains now that the restoration is complete. The white exterior of the Pyramid of Cestius will have to be cleaned every few months to remove the layer of urban pollution. A team of free-climbers will be employed to do the job, in order to avoid placing builders’ scaffolding around the newly welcoming monument.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 考古学家 Leonardo Guarnieri 向记者解释说，如今有关部门每月两次带领预约游客参观刚修复的金字塔。参加参观的人可以穿过一条狭窄走廊，进入墓室内部。在这里，他们可以欣赏湿壁画，也就是当时典型的水彩画。墓室中可以辨认出四幅带翼的罗马战争女神 Victoria 的壁画；她是罗马传说中的人物。这里还有一系列花瓶，是当时特殊仪式和净化活动会使用的类型。早期访客的文字告诉我们，这里过去曾有更多装饰，但大部分已随时间消失。修复完成后，如今只剩下一个问题：塞斯提乌斯金字塔的白色外墙每隔几个月就必须清洗，以去除城市污染形成的污层。为避免在这座刚重新开放迎客的古迹周围搭设施工脚手架，人们将雇用一队徒手攀爬者完成清洁。

passages.title: The Rise and Fall of Detective Stories

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: The Rise and Fall of Detective Stories

source.text: The Rise and Fall of Detective Stories

translation.text: 侦探小说的兴衰

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Detective stories became hugely popular in the 19th and 20th centuries. William D. Rubinstein looks at why social changes eventually led to their downfall.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 侦探小说在19和20世纪极受欢迎。 William D. Rubinstein 探讨了社会变化为何最终导致这种小说走向衰落。

source.text: Detective stories became hugely popular in the 19th and 20th centuries.

translation.text: 侦探小说在19和20世纪极受欢迎。

source.text: William D. Rubinstein looks at why social changes eventually led to their downfall.

translation.text: William D. Rubinstein 探讨了社会变化为何最终导致这种小说走向衰落。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The detective story is normally said to have begun in the fertile brain of the great American writer Edgar Allan Poe (1809–49), especially in his stories featuring the detective C. Auguste Dupin. From 1859, Dupin had a counterpart in Monsieur Lecoq, created by the French author Emile Gaboriau. Despite these American and French origins, it was to Britain that detective fiction migrated, where it took root and flourished, becoming a characteristically British genre.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 人们通常认为，侦探小说诞生于美国大作家 Edgar Allan Poe（1809—1849）富于创造力的头脑，尤其是他那些以侦探 C. Auguste Dupin 为主角的故事。1859年起，Dupin 在法国作家 Emile Gaboriau 创作的 Monsieur Lecoq 身上有了一个对应人物。尽管侦探小说起源于美国和法国，它后来却转移到英国，在那里扎根、繁荣，并成为一种具有鲜明英国特色的文学类型。

translation.text: 尽管侦探小说起源于美国和法国，它后来却转移到英国，在那里扎根、繁荣，并成为一种具有鲜明英国特色的文学类型。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This transition occurred because of one author and his great detective. The most famous of all fictional detectives, Sherlock Holmes, was introduced by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle in A Study in Scarlet, first published in 1887, and later became the subject of four novels and 56 short stories. Nearly all of the Holmes stories are narrated by his friend Dr Watson. Watson is constantly amazed and stupefied by Holmes’s genius, but despite years of working with him, Watson is never able to produce these brilliant insights himself. Holmes is memorably eccentric, with a range of endearing and less endearing habits. He is a brilliant private detective, categorically better than the plodding and mediocre officials of Scotland Yard, who constantly turn to him when they are baffled. This in itself is pure fiction: in real life there were never any brilliant private detectives to whom Scotland Yard turned when they failed, and the Yard’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) had a remarkable clear-up rate and was highly competent.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这一转变由一位作家和他笔下的一位伟大侦探促成。所有虚构侦探中最著名的福尔摩斯（Sherlock Holmes），由 Arthur Conan Doyle 爵士在1887年首次出版的《血字的研究》（A Study in Scarlet）中推出，后来又成为4部长篇小说和56篇短篇小说的主角。几乎所有福尔摩斯故事都由他的朋友华生医生叙述。华生不断为福尔摩斯的天才感到惊讶和震撼，但即使与他共事多年，华生自己始终无法作出这些精彩推断。福尔摩斯的古怪个性令人难忘，他有许多惹人喜爱或不那么讨喜的习惯。他是一名才华横溢的私人侦探，显然胜过苏格兰场那些行动迟缓、能力平平的官员；这些官员一遇到无法破解的案件，就不断向他求助。不过，这一点本身纯属虚构：现实中从来没有哪位杰出私人侦探，会在苏格兰场失败时受其求助；苏格兰场刑事调查部（Criminal Investigation Department，CID）的破案率其实十分出色，办案能力也很强。

source.text: This transition occurred because of one author and his great detective.

translation.text: 这一转变由一位作家和他笔下的一位伟大侦探促成。

source.text: The most famous of all fictional detectives, Sherlock Holmes, was introduced by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle in A Study in Scarlet, first published in 1887, and later became the subject of four novels and 56 short stories.

translation.text: 所有虚构侦探中最著名的福尔摩斯（Sherlock Holmes），由 Arthur Conan Doyle 爵士在1887年首次出版的《血字的研究》（A Study in Scarlet）中推出，后来又成为4部长篇小说和56篇短篇小说的主角。

source.text: Nearly all of the Holmes stories are narrated by his friend Dr Watson.

translation.text: 几乎所有福尔摩斯故事都由他的朋友华生医生叙述。

source.text: Watson is constantly amazed and stupefied by Holmes’s genius, but despite years of working with him, Watson is never able to produce these brilliant insights himself.

translation.text: 华生不断为福尔摩斯的天才感到惊讶和震撼，但即使与他共事多年，华生自己始终无法作出这些精彩推断。

source.text: Holmes is memorably eccentric, with a range of endearing and less endearing habits.

translation.text: 福尔摩斯的古怪个性令人难忘，他有许多惹人喜爱或不那么讨喜的习惯。

source.text: He is a brilliant private detective, categorically better than the plodding and mediocre officials of Scotland Yard, who constantly turn to him when they are baffled.

translation.text: 他是一名才华横溢的私人侦探，显然胜过苏格兰场那些行动迟缓、能力平平的官员；这些官员一遇到无法破解的案件，就不断向他求助。

source.text: This in itself is pure fiction: in real life there were never any brilliant private detectives to whom Scotland Yard turned when they failed, and the Yard’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) had a remarkable clear-up rate and was highly competent.

translation.text: 不过，这一点本身纯属虚构：现实中从来没有哪位杰出私人侦探，会在苏格兰场失败时受其求助；苏格兰场刑事调查部（Criminal Investigation Department，CID）的破案率其实十分出色，办案能力也很强。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Most of the Holmes stories are set among the higher levels of 19th-century British society, a world inhabited by professional men, retired army officers and country gentlemen, as well as members of royalty and cabinet ministers. Few take place among the working classes or the very poor, whereas in fact much crime was a product of the poverty and gangs in London’s underworld.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 大多数福尔摩斯故事发生在19世纪英国社会的上层，那个世界里生活着专业人士、退役军官和乡绅，也有王室成员和内阁大臣。很少有故事发生在工人阶级或赤贫人群中；然而事实上，许多犯罪都源自伦敦底层社会的贫困和帮派。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In the 20th century detective stories became increasingly popular. Reading these stories was one of the characteristic aspects of the British middle classes in the ‘golden age’ of British detective fiction—the 1920s and 30s. Their emphasis on rationality, the inevitable triumph of justice, and the existence of an unofficial super-detective tells us much about the society of the time. So, too, do the stock characters and unstated prejudices in these works: country folk and domestic servants were almost always depicted as unintelligent, and women were often depicted in a simplistic, two-dimensional way, although a few female detective writers would present female characters in a more realistic manner.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 到了20世纪，侦探小说越来越受欢迎。在英国侦探小说的“黄金时代”——20世纪20和30年代——阅读这类故事是英国中产阶级生活的一项典型特征。这些作品强调理性、正义必然获胜，以及体制外超级侦探的存在，充分反映了当时的社会。作品中那些固定类型的人物和没有明说的偏见也同样说明问题：乡下人和家仆几乎总被描写成不聪明的人，女性形象也常常简单而扁平；不过，少数女性侦探小说作家会更真实地呈现女性角色。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Most of the well-known British authors of ‘golden age’ detective stories were drawn from the middle classes, like their audience. Conan Doyle was a doctor who turned to writing fiction while he awaited his patients; Freeman Wills Crofts was a railway engineer in Northern Ireland; Gilbert Keith Chesterton and Anthony Berkeley were journalists; Cecil Street a career army officer. Apart from a few superstars such as Agatha Christie, financial rewards for these interwar authors were rather meagre; a few hundred pounds per book—a useful income, but nothing princely.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: US writers such as Rex Stout and Ellery Queen attempted to recreate the ‘golden age’ of British detective fiction. For the most part their books were mere imitations of the British models, although they were seldom wholly successful. But in the 1920s and 1930s, America also saw the rise of the ‘hard-boiled’ genre and its detective type: the tough private cop who appeared in the works of Dashiell Hammett and Raymond Chandler. Apart from the violence that appeared throughout their works, Hammett’s and Chandler’s novels were often marked by a political agenda that sought to expose the inequality they saw at the heart of American life. Britain had no real parallel either to their outlook on the world or (until much later) to their violence, but upheld the belief that the authorities should punish criminals regardless of their circumstances.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Rex Stout 和 Ellery Queen 等美国作家曾试图重现英国侦探小说的“黄金时代”。他们的作品大体上只是模仿英国范本，而且很少能够完全成功。不过，20世纪20和30年代的美国也见证了“硬汉派”类型及其侦探形象的兴起：Dashiell Hammett 和 Raymond Chandler 作品中那种强硬的私人侦探。Hammett 和 Chandler 的小说除了处处可见暴力，还往往带有政治意图，试图揭示他们认为处于美国生活核心的不平等。英国无论在世界观上，还是在暴力描写上——后者直到很久以后才出现——都没有真正与他们相对应的作品；英国作品仍坚持一种信念，即不论罪犯身处何种境况，当局都应惩罚他们。

It seemed that writers had simply run out of ingenious plots and puzzles for their detectives to solve. The best-known crime fiction writers, such as P. D. James, eschewed private detectives for police inspectors, and straightforward puzzles for stories that were full of unexpected twists.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Today the detective story no longer exists in Britain, at least in its old form. Arguably this mirrors the transformation of that society as a whole. The belief that scientific developments were invariably beneficial possibly reached its height during the period when the classic detective story flourished, as did the belief in putting rationality at the heart of Britain’s education system. And finally, the central belief that evil-doers would inevitably get their just deserts through the incorruptibility of the judicial system was replaced by a questioning of some of the procedures and decisions associated with that system.

source.text: The Slow Food Organization

translation.text: 慢食组织

source.text: Taking time with food

translation.text: 花时间好好对待食物

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Slow Food began when Carlo Petrini, an Italian journalist, was dismayed by the opening of a fast food restaurant on the famous Piazza di Spagna in Rome. He decided it was time to celebrate the fast-disappearing virtues of the slow production, preparation and eating of food. What he had in mind when he began the Slow Food organization were local foods which were prepared in their traditional manner and eaten at leisurely meals with family and friends. Slow Food is the antithesis of everything fast food stands for, and it is now a thriving international organization with members in 45 countries, a successful publishing operation and a biannual trade show. In addition, Slow Food has launched a project called the ‘Ark of Taste’ and a concept called ‘virtuous globalization’.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 意大利记者 Carlo Petrini 得知罗马著名的西班牙广场开了一家快餐店，深感失望，慢食运动由此诞生。他认为，是时候赞颂那些正在迅速消失的优点了：缓慢地生产、准备和享用食物。他创办慢食组织时，心中所想的是以传统方式烹制的本地食物，以及与家人朋友从容共享的餐食。慢食与快餐所代表的一切完全相反。如今，它已成为蓬勃发展的国际组织，在45个国家拥有成员，出版业务经营成功，还每两年举办一次贸易展。此外，慢食组织还推出了名为“味觉方舟”的项目和“良性全球化”这一理念。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The Ark of Taste is the catalog of endangered food plant and animal species that Slow Food has resolved to protect against the rising global tide of fast food. Some examples of the biodiversity promoted by the Ark of Taste include Iroquois white corn and the Narragansett turkey, both of which are old, or heritage, foods in North America. Biodiversity is a term commonly associated with discussions of threats to wild species, but according to Slow Food the biodiversity of the domesticated species people have depended on for centuries is no less important. For example, when the latest patented hybrid variety of plant proves unable to withstand fungal or bacterial disease, plant breeders will need the disease-resistant genes which can be obtained from heritage plant varieties. If Iroquois white corn had fallen out of production, as it very nearly did two decades ago due to the commercial launch of a new hybrid corn, irreplaceable and possibly crucial sets of corn genes would have been lost forever.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: “味觉方舟”收录了濒危食用植物和动物物种，慢食组织决心保护它们，使其免受全球快餐浪潮不断高涨的冲击。该项目所推广的生物多样性包括易洛魁白玉米和纳拉甘西特火鸡；两者都是北美历史悠久的传统食物。人们谈论野生物种所受威胁时经常使用“生物多样性”一词，但慢食组织认为，人类数百年来所依赖的驯化物种，其多样性同样重要。例如，最新的专利杂交植物品种若被证明无法抵抗真菌或细菌疾病，育种人员就会需要传统植物品种中能够抗病的基因。20年前，易洛魁白玉米因为一种新杂交玉米上市，几乎退出生产；如果它当时真的消失，一些不可替代而且可能至关重要的玉米基因就会永远丧失。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: For some time, plant-saver groups have been preserving heritage plant varieties, but Slow Food takes that project a step further. The movement understands that all the food and plant species in its Ark of Taste carry not only information about genetic traits but they also embody a set of social practices, and in some cases even a way of life of previous generations. Slow Food teaches that when a variety of food or breed of animal disappears, something greater also disappears: a specific, irreplaceable mode of life that a particular people have devised for living in a particular part of the Earth. An example of this is the Iroquois white corn. By working to find new markets for this ancient variety of corn, Slow Food is ensuring a source of income for the Native Americans who grow, roast, and grind this corn and, at the same time, helping to preserve the specific cookery and religious uses that the corn has been selected to support over hundreds of years.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 一段时间以来，植物保护团体一直在保存传统植物品种，但慢食运动把这项工作又向前推进了一步。该运动认识到，“味觉方舟”中的所有食物和植物物种不仅携带着遗传特征的信息，还体现了一整套社会实践，有时甚至承载着前几代人的生活方式。慢食组织告诉人们，一种食物品种或动物品种消失时，随之消失的还有更重要的东西：某一特定族群为在地球上某个特定地区生活而形成的、无法替代的独特生活方式。易洛魁白玉米就是一例。慢食组织努力为这种古老玉米寻找新市场，既确保种植、烘烤和研磨这种玉米的美洲原住民获得收入，也帮助保存以这种历经数百年选育的玉米为基础的特定烹饪方法和宗教用途。

source.text: For some time, plant-saver groups have been preserving heritage plant varieties, but Slow Food takes that project a step further.

translation.text: 一段时间以来，植物保护团体一直在保存传统植物品种，但慢食运动把这项工作又向前推进了一步。

source.text: The movement understands that all the food and plant species in its Ark of Taste carry not only information about genetic traits but they also embody a set of social practices, and in some cases even a way of life of previous generations.

translation.text: 该运动认识到，“味觉方舟”中的所有食物和植物物种不仅携带着遗传特征的信息，还体现了一整套社会实践，有时甚至承载着前几代人的生活方式。

source.text: Slow Food teaches that when a variety of food or breed of animal disappears, something greater also disappears: a specific, irreplaceable mode of life that a particular people have devised for living in a particular part of the Earth.

translation.text: 慢食组织告诉人们，一种食物品种或动物品种消失时，随之消失的还有更重要的东西：某一特定族群为在地球上某个特定地区生活而形成的、无法替代的独特生活方式。

source.text: An example of this is the Iroquois white corn.

translation.text: 易洛魁白玉米就是一例。

source.text: By working to find new markets for this ancient variety of corn, Slow Food is ensuring a source of income for the Native Americans who grow, roast, and grind this corn and, at the same time, helping to preserve the specific cookery and religious uses that the corn has been selected to support over hundreds of years.

translation.text: 慢食组织努力为这种古老玉米寻找新市场，既确保种植、烘烤和研磨这种玉米的美洲原住民获得收入，也帮助保存以这种历经数百年选育的玉米为基础的特定烹饪方法和宗教用途。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Slow Food has moved away from the traditional locations for preserving rare animal and plant species. For example, instead of zoos for rare animals and botanic gardens for rare plants, Slow Food maintains that its plants and animals are best preserved on the dishes and plates of discerning customers. To this end, Slow Food has introduced the concept of virtuous globalization, which recognizes that the best way to ensure a safe future for distinctive local products and practices is to find a global market for them. In this way, local producers will be able to continue producing the food which for many years has been a defining factor of their cultural identity. The characteristics of the virtuous globalization of Slow Foods show how different the concept is from the globalization of fast foods. Whereas global fast food companies aim to sell food that has an unchanging taste wherever in the world it is eaten, the taste of a recognized Slow Food is unique to that food. Another aspect is the quantities sold of these two types of food. In the case of fast food, these are enormous, but the quantities of Slow Food products which are available for selling are limited, due to the rarity of the plants or animals. The customers of virtuous globalization Slow Foods are affluent people who value novelty and are undeterred by the costs, which are high when compared to fast food.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Some years ago, a network of farmers in the USA volunteered to take part in a national Slow Food project. The project was for the farmers to raise a total of 5,000 turkeys from eggs which had been selected from four varieties of endangered turkey. The farmers had to begin by hatching the eggs they had been supplied with, then raising the young turkeys to adults. They were promised a guaranteed price per pound for the adult turkeys. The object of the enterprise was to raise heritage turkeys for the North American holiday of Thanksgiving. Although chefs in some restaurants where the turkeys were on the menu complained that the Slow Food turkeys were smaller than industrially produced turkeys, the distinctive flavors were very well received by consumers. By the following year, the world population of these turkeys had nearly doubled.

source.text: The Tuatara of New Zealand

translation.text: 新西兰楔齿蜥

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Tuatara are lizard-like reptiles found only in New Zealand. They are representative of ancient life forms. Tuatara are the sole surviving members of an ancient lineage of reptiles called Sphenodontia, which is over 250 million years old. Because tuatara still resemble fossils of reptiles that lived during the age of dinosaurs, they are often called “living fossils”. Now only two species survive in New Zealand. One is the Brothers Island tuatara which, until recent re-introductions to sanctuaries (safe places for wildlife), survived only on North Brother Island. The other species is the common tuatara, which inhabits many other offshore islands. Although the two species appear similar, they have genetic differences. Tuatara bones have been found in many parts of New Zealand; where dated, they are usually a few hundred to 5,000 years old. It is not known whether these bones belong to the two living species or to others that are now extinct.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 楔齿蜥（tuatara）是一种外形似蜥蜴的爬行动物，仅见于新西兰，是远古生命形态的代表。它们是古老爬行动物谱系喙头目唯一存活至今的成员，这一谱系已有2.5亿多年历史。楔齿蜥仍与恐龙时代爬行动物的化石相似，因此常被称为“活化石”。如今，新西兰只剩两个物种。一种是兄弟岛楔齿蜥；在近年被重新引入保护区之前，它只在北兄弟岛（North Brother Island）存活。另一种是普通楔齿蜥，栖息在其他许多近海岛屿。两个物种外表相似，却存在遗传差异。新西兰许多地方都发现过楔齿蜥骨骼；凡是经过测年的，通常已有数百年至5,000年历史。目前尚不清楚，这些骨骼属于现存的两个物种，还是属于如今已经灭绝的其他物种。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Many anatomical features distinguish tuatara from other living reptiles—for example, they have a distinctive pattern of openings in the skull, a unique type of haemoglobin in the blood, and males have no external reproductive organ. Adults range from 30 to 75 centimetres in length and weigh between 250 and 1,200 grams. Males are larger than females and have more developed spines in the crest along the neck, back and tail.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The male tuatara courts the female by approaching her with a proud walk. Tuatara mate in late summer, and the female usually lays 6–10 eggs the following spring in a shallow ground-level nest. She may guard the nest for a few nights, then return to her underground burrow. The eggs incubate for about a year, so hatchlings emerge just as new eggs are being laid the next season. Evidence indicates that the sex of hatchlings is determined by both genetic and environmental factors: warmer eggs are more likely to produce males, while cooler eggs tend to produce females. The hatchlings receive no parental care and must find their own food.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 雄性楔齿蜥会昂首阔步地接近雌性，以此求偶。楔齿蜥在夏末交配，雌性通常于翌年春天在地面浅巢中产下6至10枚卵。它可能守巢几晚，然后返回地下洞穴。卵需要孵化约1年，因此上一季的幼体破壳时，下一季的新卵刚好开始产下。证据显示，幼体的性别由遗传和环境因素共同决定：温度较高的卵更可能孵出雄性，温度较低的卵则往往孵出雌性。幼体得不到亲代照料，必须自己寻找食物。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Tuatara live a long time, reaching reproductive maturity at about 15 years and breeding for many decades. Their maximum lifespan is uncertain, but many individuals have lived to 80 years while still looking vigorous and healthy. Tuatara live in underground burrows and are more active at night, though they bask in the sun by day. Both sexes are territorial; males aggressively defend their range by posturing and, if necessary, fighting. Their teeth are their chief weapons, and a bite can cause serious injury. Tuatara are carnivorous, feeding on invertebrates, lizards and the baby seabirds with which they often share burrows.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Tuatara were once widespread and abundant on the New Zealand mainland, but when Polynesian settlers arrived (about 1250–1300 AD) they brought Pacific rats, which killed tuatara. By the time of European settlement in the 1840s, tuatara were almost extinct on the mainland. Some islands provided temporary refuges, but these too were eventually invaded by rats and other mammalian predators.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Legal protection was granted to tuatara and their islands in 1895, yet the reptiles continued to decline. Since then, active conservation management has reversed the trend, and new populations have been established on predator-free islands. In the mid-1980s the New Zealand Wildlife Service (now the Department of Conservation) developed methods to eradicate rats from islands. Rats have since been removed from almost all tuatara islands, making these habitats safe for many threatened native species. Conservationists have also collected eggs for incubation, bred tuatara in captivity, and relocated them to rat-free islands off the Northland coast and to Stephens Island in Cook Strait—areas never invaded by rats and largely free of other mammalian predators. Two additional predator-free islands now host tuatara, raising the total to 37. Many more introductions are planned for islands and mainland reserves cleared of predators.

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: New research reassesses the nature and importance of smell
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 新研究重新评估嗅觉的本质和重要性

source.text: New research reassesses the nature and importance of smell

translation.text: 新研究重新评估嗅觉的本质和重要性

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Traditionally, smell has not been at the forefront of sensory research, pushed aside in favour of the seemingly more vital senses of vision and hearing. There has been a strong belief that people, especially compared to other mammals, are not that influenced by smells.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 传统上，嗅觉并未处于感官研究的前沿；由于视觉和听觉似乎更为重要，嗅觉一直被放在次要位置。长期以来，一种观念十分盛行：气味对人的影响并没有那么大，尤其是与其他哺乳动物相比。

source.text: Traditionally, smell has not been at the forefront of sensory research, pushed aside in favour of the seemingly more vital senses of vision and hearing.

translation.text: 传统上，嗅觉并未处于感官研究的前沿；由于视觉和听觉似乎更为重要，嗅觉一直被放在次要位置。

source.text: There has been a strong belief that people, especially compared to other mammals, are not that influenced by smells.

translation.text: 长期以来，一种观念十分盛行：气味对人的影响并没有那么大，尤其是与其他哺乳动物相比。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One of the first to assert the relative unimportance of the human sense of smell was Pierre Paul Broca, an influential 19th-century anatomist. After comparing the proportion of the brain devoted to smell in different animals, he suggested that mammals can be classed into two broad groups: macrosmatic mammals, such as dogs, have a finely tuned sense of smell which they rely on to perceive the world, while marine mammals and primates, including humans, are microsmatic – the organ with which they smell is small and functionally redundant.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 19世纪颇具影响力的解剖学家 Pierre Paul Broca，是最早主张人类嗅觉相对不重要的人之一。他比较了不同动物大脑中负责嗅觉的部分所占比例，提出哺乳动物大致可分为两类：狗等嗅觉发达型哺乳动物拥有十分敏锐的嗅觉，并依靠它感知世界；海洋哺乳动物和包括人类在内的灵长类则属于嗅觉不发达型，其嗅觉器官较小，在功能上也属多余。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: That idea seemed to fit with more recent studies in genetics, which found that the majority of mammals have about one thousand different types of smell receptor. Most of these aren’t present in humans, who only possess four hundred or so different types.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这一观点似乎与较新的遗传学研究相符。研究发现，大多数哺乳动物约有1,000种不同的嗅觉受体；其中大部分在人类身上并不存在，人类只拥有约400种。

source.text: That idea seemed to fit with more recent studies in genetics, which found that the majority of mammals have about one thousand different types of smell receptor.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Yet these findings may have been misleading. Brain scans show that more of the human brain is devoted to smell processing than Broca’s anatomical studies suggested. And although we may have fewer types of receptor than other mammals, research has shown that the human nose and brain are unusually well connected, with each group of receptors linking to many more neural regions than is the case in other animals. That should give us a good ability to process incoming scents.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 然而，这些发现可能具有误导性。脑部扫描显示，人脑中用于处理气味的部分比布罗卡的解剖研究所表明的更多。虽然我们的受体种类可能少于其他哺乳动物，但研究发现，人类鼻腔与大脑之间的连接异常发达；每组受体所连接的神经区域远多于其他动物。这应当使我们具备良好的气味信息处理能力。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Once researchers began looking, they found the nose to be far more sensitive than its reputation suggested. One study, for example, found that we can pick out a particular substance even when heavily diluted. In fact, a person can smell just one drop of a chemical in a large swimming pool.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: What’s more, with the latest findings, it is becoming clear that the brain’s smelling centres are intimately linked to its system for controlling emotion, fear and memory. That suggests a link between smell and the way we think. One Dutch academic, for example, found that when the smell of orange, seawater or peppermint was pumped through a nightclub, those inside partied harder – they danced more, laughed more, and even thought the music was better than when there was no added scent.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 此外，最新研究逐渐清楚表明，大脑中的嗅觉中枢与控制情绪、恐惧和记忆的系统紧密相连。这说明嗅觉与我们的思维方式存在联系。例如，一名荷兰学者发现，夜总会中散发橙子、海水或薄荷的气味后，里面的人玩得更尽兴：他们跳舞更多、笑得更多，甚至觉得音乐比没有添加气味时更好听。

source.text: What’s more, with the latest findings, it is becoming clear that the brain’s smelling centres are intimately linked to its system for controlling emotion, fear and memory.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Other work has found that scent can influence our cognitive skills. A study found that when men were subjected to a novel smell – either good or bad – during a task used to test decision-making skills, they performed significantly worse than normal. The researchers concluded that the scent stimulated brain areas connected with emotion, making their decisions emotional rather than rational.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 其他研究发现，气味能够影响我们的认知能力。一项研究用某项任务测试决策能力时，让男性接触一种陌生气味，无论好闻还是难闻，他们的表现都明显低于正常水平。研究人员得出结论：气味刺激了大脑中与情绪有关的区域，使他们的决定受到情绪而非理性支配。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The surprising thing about such studies is that up to 95% of subjects altered their behaviour, despite only 5% of them being aware of the introduced smells that they were facing. The question, then, is why do we pay so little conscious attention to our noses unless we smell something really strong?

translation.text: 此类研究令人意外的一点是，多达95%的受试者改变了行为，但只有5%意识到自己接触了人为加入的气味。

source.text: The question, then, is why do we pay so little conscious attention to our noses unless we smell something really strong?

translation.text: 那么问题来了：除非闻到特别浓烈的气味，我们为什么很少有意识地关注自己的鼻子？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One vital factor is that our noses just aren’t equipped to locate the source of an odour. This makes the sense of smell fundamentally different to vision or hearing, which are built to identify sights and sounds with precision. Apparently, we become aware of something when the brain focuses on a single location, after which it picks out the details, like a familiar face, from the scene. With smell, though, the brain does not focus in the same way, and so is not able to make us aware of the details relating to one particular area. It’s for this reason that we can only ever pick out around four smells from a complex mixture.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 一个关键因素是，我们的鼻子并不具备确定气味来源位置的能力。这使嗅觉与视觉或听觉存在根本区别；视觉和听觉天生能够精确确定所见和所闻的位置。看来，只有当大脑把注意力集中到一个位置时，我们才会意识到某种事物；之后，大脑再从整个场景中辨认出细节，例如一张熟悉的面孔。处理气味时，大脑却不会以同样方式聚焦，因此无法让我们意识到某一特定区域里的气味细节。正因为如此，我们从复杂的混合气味中最多只能辨认出约4种气味。

translation.text: 看来，只有当大脑把注意力集中到一个位置时，我们才会意识到某种事物；之后，大脑再从整个场景中辨认出细节，例如一张熟悉的面孔。

source.text: With smell, though, the brain does not focus in the same way, and so is not able to make us aware of the details relating to one particular area.

translation.text: 处理气味时，大脑却不会以同样方式聚焦，因此无法让我们意识到某一特定区域里的气味细节。

source.text: It’s for this reason that we can only ever pick out around four smells from a complex mixture.

translation.text: 正因为如此，我们从复杂的混合气味中最多只能辨认出约4种气味。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Nevertheless, we all have the capacity to train our sense of smell, but it needs to be worked at. Master perfumers, for instance, learn to recognise, name and imagine an extraordinary range of smells through years of practice. This is accompanied by a significant reorganisation of the olfactory areas in the brain that helps them to process the scents more efficiently.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 尽管如此，我们所有人都有训练嗅觉的能力，只是需要付出努力。例如，调香大师经过多年练习，学会识别、命名并想象种类多得惊人的气味。与此同时，他们大脑中的嗅觉区域也会发生显著重组，帮助他们更高效地处理气味。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Smells are also especially good memory evokers, but it’s actually a myth that odours trigger more complete memories than other stimuli. These memories are neither more accurate nor more detailed, but they are unique in that they are more emotional. This isn’t surprising when you consider that both emotion and smell are processed by the same areas of the brain, and there is a strong link between emotion and memory.

source.text: The Whale Goes to Court

translation.text: 鲸鱼走上法庭

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A remarkable legal drama in the U.S.A.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 美国一场非同寻常的法律争论

source.text: A remarkable legal drama in the U.S.A.

translation.text: 美国一场非同寻常的法律争论

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In 1818 a whale became the subject of a controversial court case in New York City. The case involved an old law requiring those who sold fish oil to pay a fee in order to have their barrels inspected by city officials, and certified. However, an oil merchant named Samuel Judd refused to pay the inspection fee on three barrels of oil, claiming that no inspection was necessary because it was whale oil, and whales were not fish. The state disagreed, and so a date was set for a court to decide not a point of law, but the answer to a more fundamental question: is a whale a fish?
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 1818年，一头鲸成为纽约市一桩争议性案件的焦点。案件涉及一项旧法律：出售鱼油的人必须缴费，让市政府官员检查油桶并出具证明。然而，名叫 Samuel Judd 的油商拒绝为3桶油支付检查费。他声称，这些油是鲸油，而鲸不是鱼，因此无需检查。州政府不同意，于是法院定期开庭，要裁决的并非某项法律问题，而是一个更根本问题的答案：鲸是鱼吗？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As simple as that question may appear today, the answer was far from obvious in the early nineteenth century. Indeed, the public debate in New York sparked off by the trial was sensational. At stake was nothing less than what most regarded as the order of nature. According to the commonly accepted scheme of things, if an animal was not a beast or a bird, it was a fish, regardless of whether it breathed air or suckled its young. For as long as anyone could remember, all non-human creatures had been organised according to the categories of birds, beasts and fish. For the average person the answer seemed perfectly obvious: whales swam in the sea and therefore they were fish.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这个问题今天看起来或许很简单，但19世纪初，答案远没有那么明显。事实上，这场审判在纽约引发的公众争论轰动一时。大多数人所理解的自然秩序本身都受到了挑战。按照普遍接受的分类方式，一种动物如果不是走兽或鸟类，就是鱼，无论它是否呼吸空气、是否给幼崽哺乳。在人们的记忆所及范围内，所有非人类生物一直都被归入鸟、兽、鱼这3类。对普通人而言，答案似乎再明显不过：鲸在海里游，所以鲸就是鱼。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Against this traditional framework stood the new Linnaean system of classification, which sought to introduce more scientific values into the classification of living things. Barely half a century old in 1818, the Linnaean system controversially classified whales as mammals because they shared two mammalian characteristics: they were warm-blooded and breathed air.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 与这一传统框架对立的，是新的林奈分类体系；它试图把更科学的标准引入生物分类。1818年时，林奈体系问世还不到半个世纪，却颇具争议地把鲸归为哺乳动物，因为鲸具有两项哺乳动物特征：体温恒定，并且呼吸空气。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: So the trial began in December 1818. Judd’s defence lawyers chose as their star witness one of New York’s most prominent figures, the congressman Samuel Mitchill. Referred to as a ‘living encyclopaedia’ and a ‘walking library’, Mitchill was a renowned natural history lecturer at the college of Physicians and Surgeons who liked to dare his students to test his knowledge of the natural world. ‘Show me the fin, and I will name the fish,’ he boasted. Scientifically, it was an open-and-shut case, and Judd’s defence lawyers believed they only had to do one simple thing to win the trial: insist that it be decided by biology alone. Mitchill seemed fully qualified for this role.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 审判于1818年12月开始。贾德的辩护律师选择纽约最著名的人物之一、国会议员 Samuel Mitchill 担任王牌证人。Mitchill 被称为“活百科全书”和“行走的图书馆”，是医学院一位著名的自然史讲师，喜欢让学生出题考验他对自然界的了解。“给我看一片鳍，我就能说出是什么鱼，”他夸口道。从科学角度看，这是一桩结论显而易见的案件。贾德的辩护律师认为，要赢得审判只需做一件简单的事：坚持完全依据生物学作出裁决。Mitchill 似乎完全有资格承担这一角色。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But this is where the case becomes interesting, and is the reason why the trial of the whale is not some dusty nineteenth-century obscurity. For rather than debate Mitchill on his area of expertise, lawyers for the New York City fish-oil inspectors chose a different tack. Lead counsel William Sampson turned the trial into a contest between scientific learning and common sense, by asking plain-spoken whalers to make their case before the jury.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 但案件正是从这里变得有趣，这也解释了为什么鲸鱼审判并非一桩尘封于19世纪、无人问津的小事。代表纽约市鱼油检查员的律师没有选择在米切尔的专业领域与他辩论，而是改变策略。首席律师 William Sampson 让言辞朴实的捕鲸者在陪审团面前陈述观点，把审判变成了科学知识与常识之间的较量。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The crux of Sampson’s case was the trial’s implication with regard to humans, should Judd be found not guilty. Sampson told jury members that if they accepted Mitchill’s testimony on whales, they were obliged to accept a lower place for their own kind in the natural order. As a result, Mitchill’s day in court did not go smoothly, not least because he was forced to acknowledge serious disputes among his peers regarding exactly how to classify biological organisms. Sampson then took aim at Mitchill himself and what he represented: privileged aristocrats from the scientific community who had lost touch with reality. The smooth-talking Sampson then claimed Mitchill’s beliefs had their origin in Europe – something he rightly judged would infuriate the citizens of always-independent New York. This revolutionary new thinking Sampson claimed, was something that honest working New Yorkers could do without. No longer was this a case about barrels of oil but the proper place of scientific knowledge in the U.S.A.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Sampson 陈述的核心，是如果贾德被判无罪，这场审判对人类会产生何种含义。他告诉陪审员，如果接受米切尔有关鲸的证词，他们就必须接受人类在自然秩序中的地位更低。因此，米切尔出庭作证并不顺利，尤其是因为他被迫承认，同行对生物究竟该如何分类存在严重分歧。接着，Sampson 把矛头指向米切尔本人以及他所代表的群体：科学界享有特权、脱离现实的贵族。能言善辩的 Sampson 随后宣称，米切尔的观念源自欧洲；他正确判断，这会激怒一向崇尚独立的纽约市民。Sampson 声称，诚实勤劳的纽约人根本不需要这种革命性新思想。案件争论的对象不再是几桶油，而是科学知识在美国应当处于什么位置。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Ultimately, what won the case for Samuel Judd were not Mitchill’s scientific arguments, but testimony from a different sphere altogether. In New York’s markets, the merchants implicitly understood that whale oil and fish oil were not the same: whale oil could be used as a fuel for lamps because it could be burned without giving off smoke; fish oil, on the other hand, was nasty, impure stuff used primarily in tanning leather. In the end it was this testimony that led to Judd’s victory.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 最终，帮助 Samuel Judd 胜诉的不是米切尔的科学论证，而是来自完全不同领域的证词。纽约市场中的商人心照不宣地明白，鲸油和鱼油并不相同：鲸油燃烧时不冒烟，因此可用作灯油；鱼油则是肮脏而不纯的东西，主要用于鞣制皮革。最终，正是这些证词让 Judd 赢得了案件。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The trial of the whale still has relevance today, when the court of public opinion remains easily swayed by sceptics. The 1818 trial was really about this question: who gets to decide on the place of the natural world in the human world – scientific experts or public opinion? Whether the issue today is the effects of human activity on the climate of this planet, or one of many other contemporary topics, the legacy of Judd’s case continues to be of relevance.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Izon is a New Zealand company specialising in nanoscience – the study of atoms, molecules and other very small pieces of matter.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Izon是一家专门从事纳米科学的新西兰公司；纳米科学研究原子、分子和其他极微小的物质单元。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The new US headquarters of Izon are situated in Cambridge, Massachusetts, one of the most important global centres of scientific research and technology. Half the other offices in the building Izon shares have scientific names like Stemgent, or the word ‘pharmaceutical’ in the name. In the past three years, Izon has expanded to 17 times its previous size. It’s done so selling only one product that it’s been developing since 2004, the qNano. This is an adjustable tool for the measurement and analysis of tiny particles in scientific research, which comes with a $27,000 price tag. Izon’s success results from the fact that the qNano machine provides precise measurements, while similar machines of the same price only offer averaging techniques. In effect, researchers using the qNano are able to gather information about very small things, and it has many possible applications from drug delivery analysis through to environmental research.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Kristoffer Bolen is Izon’s US head of sales. Alongside his full-time role with the company, he’s just finished the fifth semester of six for his High-Tech Master of Business Administration at Northeastern University, which will be his second master’s degree, alongside a Master of Science. These soon-to-be twin master’s degrees provide Bolen with the perfect combination of skills for his job, which depends on him being able to manage the sales process and also comprehend in depth a very complicated piece of technology. When a customer buys a qNano device, an Izon representative will fly anywhere in America to train them how to use the instrument. blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The Izon story started 8 years ago in New Zealand. Hans van der Voorn was aimless, having sold his own company, and was looking for something more taxing to set his mind to. Van der Voorn was introduced to three scientists with an idea that involved simply a small plastic membrane with a tiny adjustable hole to measure a range of very small particles. Initially he put up an investment of $1.5 million to move the process forward to the development of a prototype, and this led to the founding of Izon and the production of the qNano. Van der Voorn believes that the worlds of science and business sometimes don’t understand each other very well. However, he thinks that engineering can be a bridge between the two, and his long experience in that field has been crucial to the company’s success. He soon realised that Izon was going to need people on the ground overseas if it was going to grow, so the US office was opened. For now Izon trades in the US as a foreign company, so avoids the high level of compliance that comes with being an American-registered company. But he sees that one day soon this will change, as Izon’s current position disallows it from entering into partnerships locally.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Marketing the qNano is complicated. Izon needs scientists both to buy and advertise the product. The science world may seem like a big playing field, but it’s actually a small group. As a result, the critical part of the company’s marketing is articles that clients publish describing work they have performed with the qNano. So for Izon the sale isn’t enough in itself; it also has a stake in how customers are using the qNano. That’s where Yaniv Gaynor comes in. As development and training manager, he’s involved throughout the sales process and manages most of the customer’s post-sale experience. The sales process is new for Gaynor, who shifted cities and switched from a role as teacher at the University of Minnesota to his first private sector role with Izon. ‘It’s tricky, it’s challenging, and it’s not in my comfort zone,’ he concedes. But nine out of ten times, if there’s an unhappy customer, he’s able to turn their experience around. And there’s another part to this, because sitting with customers as they learn about the qNano, Gaynor gets to see how they are using the product. ‘People ask very good questions, and these are great triggers for future development,’ he says.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: qNano的营销工作很复杂。Izon既需要科学家购买产品，也需要他们宣传产品。科学界看似范围很大，实际上圈子很小。因此，公司营销最关键的一环，是客户发表文章，介绍自己使用qNano开展的工作。对Izon而言，仅仅完成销售还不够；客户如何使用qNano也与公司利益相关。这正是 Yaniv Gaynor 发挥作用的地方。作为开发与培训经理，他参与整个销售流程，并负责客户售后体验中的大部分工作。销售对 Gaynor 而言是一个新领域；他搬到另一座城市，辞去明尼苏达大学教师一职，加入Izon，第一次进入私营部门工作。“这很棘手，也很有挑战性，不是我熟悉的领域，”他承认。不过，遇到不满意的客户时，十次中有九次，他都能扭转局面，让客户的体验由差转好。此外还有另一层收获：陪伴客户了解qNano时，Gaynor 能看到他们如何使用产品。“人们会提出非常好的问题，而这些问题正是推动未来开发的绝佳触发点，”他说。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: ‘Our business is selling research tools,’ van der Voorn says. But he knows that the application range of this tool is wide. For instance, Izon is engaged in a project with Harvard University, looking for a particular type of particle of blood that is a symptom of the medical condition of thrombosis. If in the future they can identify this particle, they can design a simple test for it. This would make it easier for doctors to diagnose thrombosis. Another planned development is eventually to shift the US base to more spacious offices on the other side of town. With larger headquarters, the company will be able to bring clients into the Izon building for training with its product, rather than travelling to them, which will hopefully result in an even closer relationship between the company and its customers.
