source.text: Tunnelling under the Thames

translation.text: 在泰晤士河下开凿隧道

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The first tunnel ever to be built under a major river was the tunnel under London’s River Thames
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 世界上第一条建在大河下方的隧道，是伦敦泰晤士河下的隧道

source.text: The first tunnel ever to be built under a major river was the tunnel under London’s River Thames

translation.text: 世界上第一条建在大河下方的隧道，是伦敦泰晤士河下的隧道

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: At the beginning of the 19th century, the port of London was the busiest in the world. Cargoes that had travelled thousands of miles and survived all the hazards of the sea were unloaded on the banks of the Thames, only for their owners to discover that the most frustrating portion of their journey lay ahead. Consignments intended for the southern parts of Britain had to be lifted onto horse carts, pulled through the docks and across London Bridge, built in the 12th century and as impractical as its early date implies. By 1820, London Bridge had become the centre of the world’s largest traffic jam.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 19世纪初，伦敦港是世界上最繁忙的港口。货物经过数千英里的旅程，躲过海上的种种危险，在泰晤士河岸卸下；货主随后却发现，最令人沮丧的一段路程还在前面。运往英国南部的货物必须装上马车，穿过码头，再经伦敦桥过河。这座桥建于12世纪，其不便程度也与悠久年代相称。到1820年，伦敦桥已经成为世界最大交通堵塞的中心。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It was an intolerable situation, and it was clear that if private enterprise could build another crossing closer to the docks, there would be good money to be made in tolls paid by users. Another bridge was out of the question, as this would deny sailing ships access to the city centre, and ambitious men turned their thoughts to tunnelling beneath the Thames instead. This was not such an obvious idea as it might appear. Although increasing demand for coal had meant a great many tunnels had been dug in mines in Britain, working methods remained primitive. Tunnels were dug by men with simple tools, by candlelight. However, in 1807, a group of businessmen got themselves up as the Thames Archway Company. Their ambition was to tunnel below the Thames, but there was little to guide them as there had been no previous attempt to do this. Their chief engineer was Richard Trevithick, designer of the world’s first high-pressure steam engine. His men made progress at the beginning, but then things began to go disastrously wrong, with muddy soil pouring into the tunnel. Eventually the Thames Archway Company had had enough. Its funds were exhausted, Trevithick was sick from exposure to the river water, and its efforts had proved only that a passage under the river exceeded the limits of contemporary mining technology.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: At that time, the only machines used in mines were pumps. It took a man of genius to recognise that a different sort of machine was needed, a machine that could prevent the roof and walls of a tunnel from collapsing. This man was Marc Brunel, a Frenchman who had become one of the most prominent engineers in Britain. Not long after the failure of the Thames Archway Company, Brunel saw a rotten piece of wood lying on the river bank. Examining the wood through a magnifying glass, he observed it was infested with something that looked like a worm. Brunel realised that as it tunnelled through the wood, it would push chewed wood into its mouth and digest it, then excrete a hard substance that lined the new tunnel. Brunel realised that the worm’s digging technique could be adapted to produce a new way of tunnelling. His realisation led him to invent a device that has been used in one form or another in most major tunnels built since: the tunnelling shield. It consisted of a series of iron frames that could be pressed against the tunnel face and supported on a set of horizontal wooden planks that would prevent the face from collapsing. It was a complex machine and not easy to use, but it seemed that it would protect the miners. Brunel’s team examined earth samples taken from beneath the riverbed, and subsequently decided to dig the tunnel close to the muddy river bottom, where he could expect to find clay. This would be a more solid and safe substance to dig through than the sand that was found deeper down.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Brunel began work on his tunnel in 1825, but the problems of such an operation soon became apparent. Although the shield itself worked well, water began to drip into the tunnel. This was more of an annoyance than a danger while the pump was working, but this machine proved unreliable and sometimes failed altogether, meaning that floods began to occur with increasing regularity. The miners often had to run for their lives. Even when Brunel’s men were able to work, they complained of frequent headaches, because the air underground was dirty and contaminated due to the lack of an adequate ventilation system. There were other problems too. Illuminating the tunnels was a constant challenge. Lamps gave off only a weak glow, and there were a number of accidents because the miners could not see what they were doing. Lastly, a number of Brunel’s miners walked off the job because they could not tolerate the excessive temperatures that developed in the cramped conditions underground.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 布鲁内尔于1825年开始修建隧道，但这项工程的问题很快显现出来。盾构本身运行良好，水却开始滴进隧道。水泵正常工作时，这更多只是麻烦，而非危险；但水泵并不可靠，有时会彻底停转，洪水因而越来越频繁地涌入。矿工常常不得不逃命。即使能够工作，工人也经常抱怨头痛，因为缺少适当的通风系统，地下空气污浊不堪。工程还有其他问题。隧道照明始终是一项挑战：油灯只能发出微弱光线，矿工看不清自己在做什么，因此发生了多起事故。最后，还有一些矿工直接离职，因为无法忍受地下狭窄环境中形成的过高温度。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Despite all the setbacks, the tunnel finally emerged on the opposite river bank on August 12, 1841. Brunel’s triumph, however, was only partial. The small payment of a penny per person made by the thousands of visitors hardly paid the interest on the government loan he had required to complete the project. As a result, there was never enough funding to make it accessible to horse-drawn vehicles, as intended. Instead, the passageways were filled with souvenir-sellers by day and the homeless at night, before it was finally closed.

source.text: What Lucy Taught Us

translation.text: 露西教会了我们什么

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A scientific finding in east Africa has changed our understanding of how humans have developed
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 东非的一项科学发现，改变了我们对人类发展过程的理解

source.text: A scientific finding in east Africa has changed our understanding of how humans have developed

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: On a Sunday morning in late November 1974, a team of scientists were digging in an isolated spot in the Afar region of Ethiopia. Surveying the area, palaeoanthropologist Donald Johanson spotted a small piece of bone. Straight away, he recognised that it came from the elbow of a human ancestor. And there were plenty more. “As I looked up the slopes to my left, I saw bits of the skull, a chunk of jaw, a couple of vertebrae,” says Johanson.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: At the group’s campsite that night, Johanson played a Beatles song called “Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds”, and, as the feeling was that the skeleton was female due to its size, someone suggested calling it Lucy. The name stuck and Johanson says, “All of a sudden, she became a person. But the morning after the discovery, the discussion was dominated by questions. How old was Lucy when she died? blocks.sourceNormalizedText: For Johanson, it was immediately apparent that Lucy walked upright. That’s because the shape and positioning of her pelvis reflected a fully upright gait. Lucy’s knee and ankle were also preserved and seemed to reflect bipedal walking. Later studies of feet offer even more evidence. As an upright walker, Lucy strengthened the idea that walking was one of the selective pressures driving human evolution forwards. Early humans did not need bigger brains to take defining steps away from apes. Extra brainpower only came over a million years later with the arrival of the species Homo erectus, meaning upright man. Though big brains would clearly be important later, walking remains one of the traits that makes us uniquely human.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: She may have walked like a human, but Lucy spent at least some of her time up in the trees, as chimpanzees and orangutans still do today. It may be that upright walking evolved in the trees, as a way to walk along branches that would otherwise be too flexible. It’s not clear why Lucy left the safety of the trees. It is thought that savannahs were gradually opening up, so trees were spaced further apart. But hunting for food may have been the real reason for heading to the ground, says Chris Stringer of the Natural History Museum in London. In line with this idea, recent evidence suggests that the diet of early humans was changing at that time.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Studies of the remains of food trapped on preserved human teeth indicate that several species, including Lucy’s, were expanding their diet around 3.5 million years ago. Instead of mostly eating fruit from trees, they began to include grasses and possibly meat. This change in diet may have allowed them to range more widely, and to travel around more efficiently in a changing environment. Fossilised crocodile and turtle eggs were found near her skeleton, suggesting that Lucy died while foraging for them in a nearby lake.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: How did early humans process all these new foods? Later species, like Homo erectus, are known to have used simple stone tools, but no tools have ever been found from this far back. However, in 2010 archaeologists uncovered animal bones with scratches that seem to have been made by stone tools. This suggests that Lucy and her relatives used stone tools to eat meat. There have since been heated debates over whether or not the marks were really made by tools. But if they were, it is not surprising, says Fred Spoor of the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in Leipzig, Germany.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 早期人类如何处理所有这些新食物？人们知道，直立人等较晚出现的物种会使用简单石器，但从未发现过年代如此久远的工具。然而，考古学家2010年发掘出一些带有刮痕的动物骨头，这些痕迹似乎由石器留下。这说明露西及其近亲可能使用石器吃肉。此后，关于这些痕迹究竟是否真由工具造成，人们展开了激烈争论。不过，德国莱比锡马克斯·普朗克进化人类学研究所的 Fred Spoor 说，如果确实如此，也并不令人惊讶。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: TF became a retail success in the 1970s when it succeeded in spotting homeware trends and meeting the needs of its then trendy young customers. However, by 2004, the TF stores were failing and a rethink was clearly necessary. Tibal Fisher, TF’s founder and CEO, decided to change its focus under a new brand name, TF’s Nextstage. His aim was to recapture the now ageing customers that had given him his early success and target consumers aged 60+ with devices and gadgets specifically designed to assist them with the problems associated with ageing: mobile phones with screens that were easy to read; kitchen gadgets with comfortable grips; electronic devices that were easy to set and adjust. TF’s market research proved to be very positive, showing strong consumer support for the products.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The team’s customer research efforts are a classic case of missing the subconscious associations at work in consumers’ minds. Tibal and his executives looked only at surface attitudes. Since those attitudes make up a relatively small part of the total consumer response, the executives are clueless about the reason for the poor sales. It’s critical for companies to understand that every customer relates to a brand emotionally, and it’s those emotions that trigger — or block — purchases.

translation.text: 公司必须明白，每位顾客都会在情感上与一个品牌建立联系，而正是这些情感会促成或阻止购买。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: That’s why we’ve focused on using emotional strategies behind branding for a number of years now. A great example is Alli (pronounced ‘ally’), a drug to aid weight loss. The product deals with a highly emotional issue, so in marketing it, we faced the same challenge that the new TF stores are facing: the very thought of buying the product reminds customers that they have problems they feel negatively about. In the case of TF’s Nextstage, the problems are age and infirmity. In the case of Alli, the problems are excessive weight and its consequences. There’s always a risk that consumers’ negative feelings will discourage them from starting or staying on a diet. So, after extensive market research, we took a number of steps to inject emotions into the whole process of using the product.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 因此，多年来，我们一直注重运用品牌背后的情感策略。一个很好的例子是减重辅助药物Alli，读音与“盟友”相同。产品处理的是一个高度情绪化的问题，所以营销时，我们面临与TF新门店相同的挑战：顾客只要想到购买产品，就会想起那些让自己感到消极的问题。对TF’s Nextstage而言，问题是年龄和身体衰弱；对Alli而言，则是体重过重及其后果。消费者的负面情绪始终可能阻止他们开始节食，或使他们无法坚持。因此，经过广泛市场研究，我们采取了多项措施，把情感融入使用产品的整个过程。

Traditional market research is unlikely to uncover ideas like this, so we use a wide variety of techniques. blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This retailer can get back on track by remembering a principle that applies to consumers in general, and those aged 60+ in particular: they’re attracted by brands they associate with the type of people they’d like to be — not the type they really are. That’s why marketing campaigns for surf gear feature surfers, not the city dwellers who will wear the products while doing their shopping.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这家零售商只要记住一项适用于普通消费者、尤其适用于60岁以上消费者的原则，就能回到正轨：人们会被自己联想到理想自我形象的品牌吸引，而不是被联想到真实自我的品牌吸引。正因为如此，冲浪装备的营销活动会展示冲浪者，而不是那些穿着产品出门购物的城市居民。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: I was reminded of this principle a few years ago when we wanted to find out how far we could apply our design philosophy of making things easier to use in order to move from our core business, kitchen tools, into other products. We conducted what are known as focus groups, where participants were asked to look at photos of people and pick those they perceived to be users and non-users of our products. Consistently, they picked people who looked fit as the sort who would use our products, and people who looked old and boring as the sort who wouldn’t. Yet the participants, all owners of our products, looked a lot more like the latter than the former.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 几年前，我们想知道“让物品更易使用”这一设计理念能应用到多大范围，从而把业务从核心的厨房工具扩展到其他产品；当时，我再次想起这项原则。我们开展了所谓的焦点小组研究，让参与者查看一些人物照片，并挑出他们认为会使用和不会使用我们产品的人。他们每次都认为，看起来身体健壮的人会使用我们的产品，而看起来年老乏味的人不会使用。然而，这些参与者全都是我们产品的使用者，他们自己的外表却远比前一类更接近后一类。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Although the needs of elderly users and those with deteriorating vision or dexterity are very much taken into consideration when we develop new designs, we try to offer products that appeal to 20- and 30-year-olds. We believe that referring to these products as helping tools would serve only to harm the brand in our customers’ eyes. That’s why our philosophy of universal design, which involves creating products that are comfortably useable by the largest possible range of people, is never explicitly stated as part of our marketing position.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 我们开发新设计时，会充分考虑老年使用者以及视力或手部灵活性下降者的需求，但仍努力让产品对20多岁和30多岁的人具有吸引力。我们相信，把这些产品称为辅助工具，只会损害顾客心目中的品牌形象。因此，我们从不在营销定位中明确说明自己的“通用设计”理念；这一理念是要创造尽可能让最广泛人群都能舒适使用的产品。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: We’ve found that market research does not need to be very sophisticated. For instance, we have conducted simple surveys in the lobby of our building, offering free products in exchange for people’s opinions. Some may call this unscientific, but we have uncovered great insights this way. Sometimes the most important signals come from an executive’s own instincts. In Tibal Fisher’s case, this could have told him what his surveys and focus groups didn’t: 60-plus-year-olds won’t support a business that expects them to act their age.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 我们发现，市场研究不必非常复杂。例如，我们曾在公司大楼门厅进行简单调查，用免费产品换取人们的意见。有人可能认为这不科学，但我们用这种方法获得了非常深刻的见解。有时，最重要的信号来自高管自己的直觉。对 Tibal Fisher 而言，直觉本可以告诉他调查和焦点小组没有发现的事实：60岁以上的人不会支持一家要求他们表现得符合自己年龄的企业。

passages.title: Wood: A Valuable Resource in New Zealand’s Economy

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Wood: A Valuable Resource in New Zealand’s Economy

source.text: Wood: A Valuable Resource in New Zealand’s Economy

translation.text: 木材：新西兰经济中的宝贵资源

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: During the settlement of New Zealand by European immigrants, natural timbers played a major role. Wood was easily accessible and relatively cheap. A tradition of wooden houses arose, supported by the recognition that they were less likely to collapse suddenly during earthquakes, a not-infrequent event in this part of the world. But in addition to demand from the domestic market, there was also demand for forest products from overseas.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在欧洲移民定居新西兰的过程中，天然木材发挥了重要作用。木材容易取得，而且相对便宜。当地由此形成了建造木屋的传统；人们认识到，地震发生时木屋不太可能突然倒塌，而地震在这个地区并不少见。不过，除国内市场需求外，海外同样需要森林产品。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Early explorers recognised the suitability of the tall, straight trunks of the kauri for constructing sailing vessels. The kauri is a species of coniferous tree found only in small areas of the southern hemisphere. So, from the early 1800s, huge amounts of this type of wood were sold to Australia and the UK for that purpose. For a period, the forestry industry was the country’s major export earner, but the rate of harvest was unsustainable and, by the beginning of the 20th century, indigenous timber exports were rapidly declining.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 早期探险者发现，高大笔直的贝壳杉树干很适合建造帆船。贝壳杉是一种针叶树，仅生长在南半球少数地区。因此，从19世纪初开始，大量这种木材被卖往澳大利亚和英国用于造船。有一段时期，林业是新西兰出口收入的主要来源；但当时的采伐速度无法持续，到20世纪初，本土木材出口已迅速减少。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: From the 1940s, newly established plantations of an imported species of tree called radiata pine supplied timber and other wood products in increasing quantities. By the 1960s, plantation-grown timber was providing most of the country’s sawn-timber needs, especially for construction. Today, less than two percent of timber is cut from indigenous forests, and almost all of that is used for higher-value end uses such as furniture and fittings. As the pine industry developed, it became apparent that this type of wood was also well suited for many uses. It makes excellent pulp*, and is frequently used for posts, poles, furnishings and mouldings, particleboard, fibreboard, and for plywood and ‘engineered’ wood products. Pine by-products are used in the chemical and pharmaceutical industries and residues are consumed for fuel. This amazing versatility has encouraged the development of an integrated forest-products industry which is almost unique in the world.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 从20世纪40年代起，新建的辐射松种植林开始供应越来越多的木材及其他木制品。这种树种是从海外引进的。到20世纪60年代，种植林木材已经满足了新西兰大部分锯材需求，尤其是建筑用材需求。如今，取自本土森林的木材不足2%，而且几乎全部用于家具和装饰配件等价值较高的最终用途。随着松木产业发展，人们发现这种木材也很适合多种用途。它可以制成优质纸浆*，还常用于制作木桩、电杆、家具、装饰线条、刨花板、纤维板、胶合板及“工程木”产品。松木副产品用于化工和制药行业，剩余材料则用作燃料。如此惊人的多用途特性，推动形成了一个综合性林产品产业，而这样的产业在世界上几乎独一无二。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Exporters of wood products have largely targeted the rapidly growing markets of South and East Asia and Australia. Eighty percent of exports by value go to only five markets: Japan, Korea, China, the United States and Australia. The product mix remains heavily biased towards raw materials, with logs, sawn wood, pulp and paper comprising 75 percent of export value. However, finished wood products such as panels and furniture components are exported to more than 50 countries.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 木制品出口商主要瞄准南亚、东亚和澳大利亚快速增长的市场。按出口额计算，80%的产品只销往5个市场：日本、韩国、中国、美国和澳大利亚。出口产品结构仍严重偏向原材料，原木、锯材、纸浆和纸张占出口额的75%。不过，板材和家具部件等木制成品已出口到50多个国家。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In New Zealand itself, the construction industry is the principal user of solid wood products, servicing around 20,000 new-house starts annually. However, the small size of New Zealand’s population (just over four million), plus its small manufacturing and remanufacturing base, limits the forestry industry’s domestic opportunities. For the last few years local wood consumption has been around only four million cubic metres. source.text: A mechanical friend for children

translation.text: 孩子们的机械朋友

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The development of robots that interact socially with people and assist them in everyday life has been an elusive goal of modern science. Despite impressive advances in the mechanical aspects of this problem, producing robots that bond and socialize with people for sustained periods of time has proven difficult. The most successful robots so far have been storytellers, but they have only been able to maintain human interest for a limited time and typically rely on the robot telling stories that change over time. In practice, commercially available robots seldom cross the 10-hour barrier (i.e., individual users tend to spend less than a combined total of 10 hours with the robots before losing interest). This observation is in sharp contrast to the long-term interactions and bonding that commonly develop between humans and their pets.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 开发既能与人进行社会互动、又能在日常生活中帮助人的机器人，一直是现代科学难以实现的目标。尽管这一问题的机械技术方面取得了显著进步，但事实证明，要造出能与人长期建立联系并进行社会交往的机器人仍十分困难。迄今最成功的机器人是会讲故事的机器人，但它们只能在有限时间内维持人的兴趣，而且通常依靠不断更换所讲的故事。实际中，市售机器人很少能跨过10小时这道门槛，也就是说，每位用户与机器人相处的累计时间通常不到10小时便失去兴趣。这与人和宠物之间普遍形成的长期互动与感情纽带形成鲜明对比。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In a recent study, researchers from the Institute for Neural Computation in California introduced a state-of-the-art social robot into a classroom of 18-to-24-month-olds for five months as a way of studying human/robot interactions. The researchers, including Fumihide Tanaka and Javier R. Movellan, introduced a toddler-sized humanoid robot into a classroom at a childhood education center. One of the QRIO series of robots, the 58 cm machine, was originally developed by Sony. ‘Children of toddler age were chosen because they have no preconceived notions of robots,’ according to Tanaka. One of the goals of the study was to establish whether it was possible for social robots to maintain the interest of children beyond the 10-hour barrier.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在最近一项研究中，加州神经计算研究所的研究人员把一个最先进的社交机器人放进由18至24个月大幼儿组成的班级，持续5个月，以此研究人与机器人的互动。包括 Fumihide Tanaka 和 Javier R. Movellan 在内的研究人员，把一个幼儿大小的人形机器人带进一所幼儿教育中心的教室。这个机器人属于QRIO系列，高58厘米，最初由索尼开发。Tanaka 说：“之所以选择学步期幼儿，是因为他们对机器人没有先入之见。”研究目标之一，是确定社交机器人能否在超过10小时后仍保持孩子的兴趣。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The researchers sent instructions to the robot about every two minutes to do things like giggle, dance, sit down, fall down, or walk in a certain direction. The 45 sessions were videotaped, and interactions between toddlers and the robot were later analyzed. The results showed that the quality of those interactions improved steadily over 27 sessions. The interactions deteriorated quickly over the next 15 sessions, when the robot was ordered to behave in a more limited, predictable manner. Finally, the human/robot relations improved in the last three sessions, after the robot had been instructed to display its full range of behaviors.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 研究人员大约每两分钟向机器人发送一次指令，让它咯咯笑、跳舞、坐下、摔倒，或朝某个方向行走。全部45次活动都被录像，随后研究人员分析了幼儿与机器人的互动。结果显示，在前27次活动中，互动质量稳步提高。接下来的15次活动里，机器人被要求以更加有限、可预测的方式行动，互动质量很快下降。最后，研究人员让机器人展现全部行为，在最后3次活动中，人与机器人的关系又有所改善。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: ‘Initially, the children treated the robot very differently from the way they treated each other,’ Tanaka said. ‘Early in the study, some children cried when QRIO fell. But a month into the study, the toddlers helped QRIO stand up by pushing its back or pulling its hands.’ ‘The most important aspect of interaction was touch,’ Tanaka said. ‘At first, the toddlers would touch the robot on its face, but later on they would touch it only on its hands and arms, like they would with other humans. Another robot-like toy named Robby, which resembled QRIO but did not move, was used as a control in the study. While hugging of QRIO increased, hugging of Robby decreased throughout the study. Furthermore, when QRIO lay down on the floor, caretaking behaviors were frequently observed toward QRIO but seldom toward Robby.’

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The study concluded that after 45 days of immersion in a childcare center over a period of five months, long-term bonding and socialization occurred between toddlers and a state-of-the-art social robot. Overall, the interaction between children and the robot improved over time and the children progressively treated it more as a peer than a plaything. ‘To my knowledge, this is the first long-term study of this sort,’ said Ronald Arkin, a roboticist at the Georgia Institute of Technology in the US.

translation.text: 总体而言，孩子与机器人的互动随时间推移不断改善，他们也越来越把它当作同伴，而不是玩具。

source.text: ‘To my knowledge, this is the first long-term study of this sort,’ said Ronald Arkin, a roboticist at the Georgia Institute of Technology in the US.

translation.text: 美国佐治亚理工学院机器人专家 Ronald Arkin 说：“据我所知，这是首项此类长期研究。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Tanaka and Movellan are now developing autonomous robots for the toddler classroom. ‘It could have great potential in educational settings, assisting teachers and enriching the classroom environment,’ Tanaka said. The researchers hope that more advanced versions of robots like QRIO could become personalized tutors to assist teachers in classrooms. A robotic tutor could react on the spot to social cues and approximate social skills like facial expression and eye gaze, they said. ‘It is becoming clear that, to achieve this goal, we are going to endow machines with something similar to emotion, not just traditional forms of intelligence,’ said Movellan.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 田中和莫韦兰目前正在为幼儿班开发自主机器人。田中说：“它在教育环境中可能大有潜力，可以协助教师并丰富课堂环境。”研究人员希望，QRIO这类机器人的更高级版本可以成为个性化辅导老师，在课堂上协助教师。他们说，机器人辅导老师可以根据现场的社交线索作出反应，并模拟面部表情和目光注视等社交技能。莫韦兰说：“越来越明显的是，要实现这一目标，我们必须赋予机器某种类似情感的东西，而不只是传统形式的智能。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Associate Professor David Powers, an expert in artificial intelligence and cognitive science at Flinders University in South Australia, commented, ‘In this study, it is clearly demonstrated that a limited range of robot behaviors, however impressive, is nowhere near as important to human/robot interaction as being able to make appropriate responses from a broad repertoire of behaviors.’ Ronald Arkin was not surprised by the affection demonstrated by the toddlers toward the robot. ‘Humans have a tremendous propensity to bond with artifacts, whether it be a car, a doll, or a robot,’ he said. But he also cautioned that researchers do not yet understand the consequences of increased human/robot interaction. ‘Studying how robots and humans work together can give us insight into whether this is a good thing or a bad thing for society,’ Arkin said. ‘We need to find out what the consequences are of introducing a robot into a cadre of children. How will that enhance, or potentially interfere with, their social development? Do we really understand the long-term impact of having a robot as a childhood friend?’

passages.title: A new look for Talbot Park

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: A new look for Talbot Park
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 塔尔博特公园（Talbot Park）的新面貌

source.text: A new look for Talbot Park

translation.text: 塔尔博特公园（Talbot Park）的新面貌

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Talbot Park, a housing project in Auckland, New Zealand, was once described as a ghetto, troubled by high rates of crime and vandalism. However, it has just been rebuilt at a cost of $48 m and the project reflects some new thinking about urban design.
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 塔尔博特公园是新西兰奥克兰的一处住房项目，过去曾被形容为贫民区，犯罪和蓄意破坏现象十分严重。不过，这里刚刚耗资4800万美元完成重建，项目体现了城市设计方面的一些新理念。

source.text: Talbot Park, a housing project in Auckland, New Zealand, was once described as a ghetto, troubled by high rates of crime and vandalism.

translation.text: 塔尔博特公园是新西兰奥克兰的一处住房项目，过去曾被形容为贫民区，犯罪和蓄意破坏现象十分严重。

source.text: However, it has just been rebuilt at a cost of $48 m and the project reflects some new thinking about urban design.

translation.text: 不过，这里刚刚耗资4800万美元完成重建，项目体现了城市设计方面的一些新理念。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The new Talbot Park is immediately eye-catching because the buildings look quite different to other state-housing projects in Auckland. ‘There is no reason why state housing should look cheap in my view,’ says architect Neil Cotton, one of the design team. ‘In fact, I was anticipating a backlash by those who objected to the quality of what is provided with government money.’ The tidy brick and wood apartments and townhouses would not look out of place in some of the city’s most affluent suburbs, and this is a central theme of the Talbot Park philosophy.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 新的塔尔博特公园格外引人注目，因为这里的建筑看起来与奥克兰其他公营住房项目很不一样。设计团队成员、建筑师 Neil Cotton 说：“在我看来，公营住房没有理由显得廉价。事实上，我当时就预料，那些反对政府花钱提供如此高质量住房的人会强烈反弹。”这些整洁的砖木公寓和联排住宅即使放在奥克兰一些最富裕的郊区也毫不突兀，而这正是塔尔博特公园理念的核心。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Talbot Park is a triangle of government-owned land, which in the early 1960s was developed for state housing built around a linear garden that ran through the middle. Initially, there was a strong sense of neighbourliness. Former residents recall how the garden played a big part in their childhoods — a place where kids came together to play softball, cricket and bullrush. ‘We had respect for our neighbours and addressed them by title — Mr and Mrs so-and-so,’ recalls Georgie Thompson, who grew up there in the 1960s.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 塔尔博特公园是一块三角形的政府用地。20世纪60年代初，这里被开发为公营住宅区，住房环绕着一条贯穿中央的狭长花园而建。最初，居民之间有很强的邻里情谊。昔日居民回忆，这座花园在他们童年时发挥了重要作用，孩子们会聚在那里玩垒球、板球和冲阵游戏。20世纪60年代在此长大的 Georgie Thompson 回忆道：“我们尊重邻居，会用称谓叫他们，比如某某先生、某某太太。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Exactly what went wrong with Talbot Park is unclear. The community began to change in the late 1970s as more immigrants moved in. The new arrivals didn’t always integrate with the community and a ‘them and us’ mentality developed. In the process, standards dropped and the neighbourhood began to look shabbier. The buildings themselves were also deteriorating and becoming run-down, petty crime was on the rise and the garden was considered unsafe. In 2002, Housing New Zealand decided the properties needed upgrading. The question was, how to avoid repeating the mistakes of the past?
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 塔尔博特公园究竟出了什么问题，并不清楚。20世纪70年代末，随着更多移民迁入，社区开始发生变化。新来者并不总能融入社区，居民之间逐渐形成“他们和我们”的对立心态。在这一过程中，整体水准下降，社区也开始显得越来越破旧。建筑本身同样不断老化、失修；轻微犯罪日益增多，花园也被认为不再安全。2002年，新西兰住房局决定必须升级这些房产。问题在于，怎样才能避免重蹈覆辙？

source.text: The question was, how to avoid repeating the mistakes of the past?

translation.text: 问题在于，怎样才能避免重蹈覆辙？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One controversial aspect of the upgrade is that the new development has actually made the density of housing in Talbot Park greater, putting 52 more homes on the same site. Doing this required a fresh approach that can be summed up as ‘mix and match’. The first priority was to mix up the housing by employing a variety of plans by different architects: some of the accommodation is free-standing houses, some semi-detached, some low-level, multi-apartment blocks. By doing this, the development avoids the uniform appearance of so many state-housing projects, which residents complain denies them any sense of individual identity. The next goal was to prevent overspending by using efficient designs to maximise the sense of space from minimum room sizes. There was also a no-frills, industrial approach to kitchens, bathrooms and flooring, to optimise durability and ensure the project did not go over budget. Architecturally, the buildings are relatively conservative: fairly plain houses standing in a small garden. There’s a slight reflection of the traditional Pacific beach house (a fale) but it’s not over-played. ‘It seems to us that low-cost housing is about getting as much amenity as you can for the money,’ says architect Michael Thompson. Another key aspect of the ‘mix and match’ approach is openness: one that not only lets residents see what is going on but also lets them know they are seen. The plan ensures there are no cul-de-sacs or properties hidden from view, that the gardens are not enclosed by trees and that most boundary fences are see-through — a community contained but without walls.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 此次改造中一个有争议之处，是新项目实际上提高了塔尔博特公园的住房密度，在同一块土地上又增加了52套住宅。要做到这一点，就需要一种可以概括为“混合搭配”的新方法。首要任务是采用不同建筑师设计的多种方案，把各种住房混合起来：有独立式住宅，有半独立式住宅，也有低层多户公寓楼。这样一来，项目便避免了许多公营住宅区千篇一律的外观；居民抱怨，这种统一外观会让他们失去任何个体身份感。下一个目标是避免超支，为此，设计力求高效，以最小的房间面积营造最大的空间感。厨房、浴室和地板也采用不加装饰的工业化方案，以尽可能提高耐用性，并确保项目不超出预算。从建筑风格看，这些建筑相对保守：房屋相当朴素，坐落在小花园中。设计稍稍借鉴了传统太平洋海滨住宅（fale），但没有过分强调。建筑师 Michael Thompson 说：“在我们看来，低成本住房就是要用有限的资金获得尽可能多的便利。”这种“混合搭配”方法的另一个关键是开放性：既让居民能看见周围发生的事情，也让他们知道自己同样会被看见。规划确保这里没有死胡同，没有住宅藏在视线之外；花园不被树木围住，大多数边界围栏也都可以透视——这是一个有边界却没有围墙的社区。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The population today is cosmopolitan: 50% Pacific Islanders, 20% Māori, 15% Asian, 10% New Zealand European and the rest composed of immigrants from Russia, Ukraine and Iran. ‘It was important that the buildings were sufficiently flexible to cater for the needs of people from a wide variety of cultural backgrounds,’ explains designer James Lundy.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Despite the quality of the buildings, however, there should be no doubt that Talbot Park and its surrounding suburb of Tāmaki are low socio-economic areas. Of the 5,000 houses there, 55% are state houses, 28% privately owned (compared to about 65% nationally) and 17% private rental. The area has a high density of households with incomes in the $5,000 to $15,000 range and very few with an income over $70,000. That’s in sharp contrast to the more affluent suburbs in Auckland.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Another important part of the new development is what Housing New Zealand calls ‘intensive tenancy management’. Opponents of the project call it social control. ‘The focus is on frequent inspections and setting clear guidelines and boundaries regarding the sort of behaviour we expect from tenants,’ says Graham Bodman, Housing New Zealand’s regional manager. The result is a code of sometimes strict rules: no loud parties after 10 pm; no washing hung over balcony rails; and a requirement to mow lawns and keep the property tidy. The Tenancy Manager walks the site every day, knows everyone by name and deals with problems quickly. ‘It’s all based on the intensification,’ says project manager Stuart Bracey. ‘We acknowledge that if you are going to ask people to live in these quite tightly-packed communities, you have to actually help them to get to know each other by organising morning teas and street barbecues.’ So far it seems to be working and many involved in the project believe Talbot Park represents the way forward for state housing.

source.text: A study of western celebrity

translation.text: 西方名人现象研究

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: In our celebrity-obsessed culture, TV shows, internet blogs, and even newspapers are often full of the latest news, gossip and scandals about current celebrities

source.text: In our celebrity-obsessed culture, TV shows, internet blogs, and even newspapers are often full of the latest news, gossip and scandals about current celebrities

translation.text: 在这个痴迷名人的文化中，电视节目、网络博客，甚至报纸上常常充斥着当下名人的最新消息、流言和丑闻。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It seems that our current society cannot get enough information about the daily lives of celebrities. But how did celebrities become such an important force in our culture? While people have always shared a certain obsession with the fantastic and the famous, the notion of celebrity, as well as the types of people termed ‘celebrities’, has evolved greatly throughout the ages. The word ‘celebrity’ has its roots in the language of the ancient Roman civilization. The word we now know to mean ‘a condition of being famous’ or ‘a famous person’ is derived from the Latin word ‘celeber’, meaning ‘frequented or populous’.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 当今社会似乎永远看不够名人日常生活的信息。但名人是如何在我们的文化中变得如此重要的？尽管人们一直都对奇异事物和著名人物抱有某种迷恋，但“名人”这一概念，以及被称为名人的人物类型，都在各个时代发生了很大变化。“celebrity”一词源自古罗马文明的语言。如今这个表示“成名状态”或“知名人物”的词，来自拉丁语“celeber”，意思是“人来人往的或人口众多的”。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The celebrities of the ancient world were the powerful and awesome deities of Greece and Rome, and the citizens of these civilizations believed in a vast number of immortals who had a direct impact on their lives. It was, therefore, important to know about these figures’ personal lives. This need to know led to the creation of myths, which personalized the gods and involved them in ancient celebrity scandals that thrilled and excited the common people.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 古代世界的名人，是希腊和罗马那些强大而令人敬畏的神灵。这两个文明的居民相信，数量众多的神仙会直接影响他们的生活。因此，了解这些神灵的私生活十分重要。这种求知需要促成了神话的产生；神话把众神人格化，让他们卷入古代的名人丑闻，给普通民众带来刺激和兴奋。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: During ancient times, amateur and professional athletes also began to make an impact on the celebrity culture. Victors in the ancient Olympic Games were treated as heroes and were often elevated to god-like status. In the ancient Roman civilization, gladiators – the equivalent of today’s professional athletes – were also revered by the common people for their heroics and seemingly superhuman strength.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在古代，业余和职业运动员也开始影响名人文化。古代奥运会的获胜者被视为英雄，地位经常被抬高到近似神明的程度。在古罗马文明中，角斗士相当于今天的职业运动员；普通民众同样崇敬他们，因为他们英勇无畏，似乎拥有超人的力量。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As Europe moved into the Dark Ages (the years spanning approximately 400–1300 AD) and a time when athletics and the arts were largely forgotten, monarchs and rulers continued to maintain celebrity status, while religious figures took on newfound fame. The miraculous lives and fascinating deaths of spiritual figures lent excitement to the lives of common people when there was often little else to be excited about, as they faced war, disease and food shortages.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: During the period 1300–1600 AD, or the Renaissance period as it is known, interest in ruling figures faded. As Europe emerged from its long neglect of the arts, there was greater appreciation for portraits, statues and stone carvings. This period of appreciation for the arts lent a sense of celebrity to artists who were noted for their works and their personal achievements. It was a time when artists began to surpass political and religious individuals for supreme celebrity – a trend that would continue into later centuries.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在公元1300至1600年间，也就是人们所说的文艺复兴时期，人们对统治者的兴趣减退了。随着欧洲摆脱长期忽视艺术的状态，人们更加欣赏肖像画、雕像和石雕。这一崇尚艺术的时期，使那些以作品和个人成就闻名的艺术家也拥有了名人光环。艺术家在这一时期开始超越政治和宗教人物，成为最受瞩目的名人，而这一趋势在后来几个世纪中继续延续。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: While the figures of the ancient and early modern civilizations were able to achieve moderate and sometimes lasting celebrity within particular cultures, the global reach of their fame was limited. It was not until the 1700s, when technological advances made publishing commercially viable, that the extent of a person’s fame could spread further. The increase in the availability of the written word was accompanied by a huge rise in the number of common people who could read, allowing a mass audience to find out about celebrities for the first time. Suddenly, the lives of authors, politicians, war heroes, and other celebrities could now be read about in newspapers around the world. These gave ordinary people the opportunity to become intimately knowledgeable about the figures they most admired.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 古代和近代早期文明中的人物，虽然能在特定文化中获得一定程度、乃至有时长久不衰的声名，但他们的名气在全球传播的范围有限。直到18世纪，技术进步使商业出版成为可行之事，个人声名才得以传播得更远。文字资料越来越容易取得，与此同时，普通民众中能够阅读的人数也大幅增加，使大众第一次可以了解名人。作家、政治家、战争英雄及其他名人的生活，突然间都能通过世界各地的报纸为人所知。普通人因而有机会深入了解自己最崇拜的人物。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In the modern era, particularly as radio and film took off in the 1900s, things really began to change. First, radio began to make its way into the average home in the 1920s and 1930s. Professional athletes also began to be regarded as stars, as their games and exploits could be broadcast over the air for an entirely new audience. Then, the rise of television in the 1950s only cemented the premier level of celebrity that film stars, athletes and television actors were beginning to share. This also meant a huge increase in the individual salaries of these celebrities. Even a few animals gained fame through children’s TV shows. The emergence of reality television shows in the late 1990s allowed all kinds of people with little ability to enjoy a short burst of fame on the television screen. All you needed, it seemed, was an attractive appearance. Today, reality television programmers make it possible to be famous not for doing anything in particular, but simply for being, with the audience deciding whether someone deserves to become a celebrity or not. As the meaning of celebrity continues to evolve and redefine itself in a quickly changing world, there is no telling who will become of interest next.

headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 一项由两人开展的蜘蛛丝利用项目，历时4年终于完成。

source.text: A two-man project to use spider silk is achieved after 4 years

translation.text: 一项由两人开展的蜘蛛丝利用项目，历时4年终于完成。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A rare textile made from the silk of more than a million wild spiders has been on display at the American Museum of Natural History in New York City. To produce this golden cloth, 70 people spent four years collecting golden-orb spiders from telephone poles in Madagascar, while another dozen workers carefully extracted about 80 feet of silk filament from each of the arachnids. The resulting 11-foot-by-4-foot textile is the only large piece of cloth made from natural spider silk in the world today.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 一件用100多万只野生蜘蛛的蛛丝制成的稀有织物，曾在纽约市美国自然历史博物馆展出。为了制作这块金色织物，70个人花了4年时间，从马达加斯加的电线杆上收集金色圆网蛛；另有12名工人小心地从每只蜘蛛身上抽取约80英尺长的丝线。最终制成的织物长11英尺、宽4英尺，是当今世界上唯一一块用天然蛛丝制成的大型布料。

source.text: A rare textile made from the silk of more than a million wild spiders has been on display at the American Museum of Natural History in New York City.

translation.text: 一件用100多万只野生蜘蛛的蛛丝制成的稀有织物，曾在纽约市美国自然历史博物馆展出。

source.text: The resulting 11-foot-by-4-foot textile is the only large piece of cloth made from natural spider silk in the world today.

translation.text: 最终制成的织物长11英尺、宽4英尺，是当今世界上唯一一块用天然蛛丝制成的大型布料。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Spider silk is very elastic and strong compared with steel or Kevlar, said textile expert Simon Peers, who co-led the project. Kevlar is a lightweight synthetic fabric, chemically related to nylon, that is used in bullet-proof vests. Kevlar is resistant to wear, tear and heat and has virtually no melting point. But the tensile strength of spider silk is even greater than Kevlar’s aramid filaments and higher than that of high-grade steel. Most importantly, spider silk is extremely lightweight: a strand long enough to circle the Earth would weigh less than 500 grams (18 oz). It is also especially ductile, able to stretch up to 140 percent of its length without breaking and to retain its strength below –40 °C, giving it toughness equal to that of leading commercial fibres.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 共同负责该项目的纺织专家 Simon Peers 说，与钢或凯夫拉相比，蛛丝弹性很大，也很坚韧。凯夫拉是一种轻质合成织物，在化学性质上与尼龙相关，用于制作防弹背心。它耐磨、抗撕裂、耐热，而且几乎没有熔点。但蛛丝的抗拉强度甚至高于凯夫拉的芳纶丝，也高于优质钢。最重要的是，蛛丝极其轻盈：一根足以环绕地球的蛛丝重量不到500克（18盎司）。它的延展性也特别好，在不断裂的情况下可以拉伸至自身长度的140%，并能在低于零下40摄氏度时保持强度，因此其韧性可与领先的商用纤维相当。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Researchers have long been intrigued by the unique properties of spider silk. Unfortunately, spider silk is extremely hard to mass-produce. Unlike silkworms—easy to raise in captivity—spiders have a habit of biting off each other’s heads when housed together. According to Peers, there is intensive research worldwide aimed at replicating spider-silk tensile properties for use in medicine and industry, but no-one has yet reproduced all the qualities of natural silk.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 长期以来，研究人员一直对蛛丝的独特性质着迷。遗憾的是，蛛丝极难大规模生产。蚕很容易人工饲养，而蜘蛛养在一起时却有咬掉彼此脑袋的习性。皮尔斯说，世界各地正在开展大量研究，试图复制蛛丝的抗拉性能，用于医疗和工业领域；但目前还没有人能重现天然蛛丝的全部特性。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Peers conceived the idea of weaving spider silk after reading about French missionary Jacob Paul Camboué, who worked with spiders in Madagascar during the 1880s and 1890s. Camboué built a small hand-driven machine to extract silk from up to 24 spiders at once, without harming them: the spiders were briefly restrained, their silk collected, then released. Peers built a replica of this 24-spider “silking” machine, said co-leader Nicholas Godley. As a test the pair collected about 20 spiders. “When we stuck them in the machine and started turning it, lo and behold, this beautiful gold-coloured silk started coming out,” Godley recalled.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 皮尔斯读到法国传教士 Jacob Paul Camboué 的事迹后，萌生了用蛛丝织布的想法。19世纪80和90年代，Camboué 曾在马达加斯加研究蜘蛛。他制作了一台小型手摇机器，一次最多可以从24只蜘蛛身上抽丝，而且不会伤害它们：蜘蛛只被短暂固定，蛛丝收集完毕后便会被放生。项目另一位负责人 Nicholas Godley 说，皮尔斯仿制了这台可容纳24只蜘蛛的“抽丝”机器。两人收集了约20只蜘蛛进行测试。Godley 回忆道：“我们把它们放进机器，开始转动手柄；看哪，美丽的金色蛛丝真的出来了。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: To make a textile of any significant size, the scale had to increase dramatically. Fourteen thousand spiders yield about an ounce of silk, Godley said, and the finished textile weighs about 2.6 pounds. By the end, handlers had worked with more than one million female golden-orb spiders—abundant in Madagascar and famed for their golden thread. Because the spiders produce silk only in the rainy season, all were collected between October and June. An additional 12 workers used hand-powered machines to extract the silk and twist it into 96-filament yarn. After “silking”, the spiders were released; within a week they regenerate their silk, allowing the same individuals to be used again—“the gift that never stops giving,” said Godley.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 要制成具有一定面积的织物，项目规模就必须大幅扩大。戈德利说，1.4万只蜘蛛只能产出约1盎司蛛丝，而成品织物重约2.6磅。项目结束时，工作人员已经接触过100多万只雌性金色圆网蛛。这种蜘蛛在马达加斯加数量很多，以产出金色丝线闻名。由于蜘蛛只在雨季产丝，所有蜘蛛都是在10月至次年6月期间收集的。另有12名工人使用手摇机器抽丝，并将蛛丝捻成由96根细丝组成的纱线。“抽丝”后，蜘蛛会被放生；它们可在一周内重新生成蛛丝，因此同一只蜘蛛还能再次使用。戈德利称其为“永不停歇的馈赠”。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Spending four years to produce a single piece of cloth is hardly practical for scientists or companies hoping to exploit spider silk in biomedicine or as a Kevlar alternative. Several groups have inserted spider genes into bacteria and even goats to make silk, but results have been only partly successful. One reason is that spider silk begins as a liquid protein produced in a special gland in the abdomen. Using the spinneret, the spider applies force that rearranges the protein’s molecular structure, transforming it into solid fibre. “When we talk about a spider spinning silk, we’re talking about how it applies forces to convert liquid to solid,” explained spider-silk expert Todd Blackledge of the University of Akron, who was not involved in the project. “Every year we get closer to mass production, but we’re not there yet.” For now, we must be content with one extraordinarily beautiful cloth—courtesy of more than a million spiders.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 对于希望把蛛丝用于生物医学或用作凯夫拉替代品的科学家和公司而言，花4年时间只制作一块布显然并不实用。几个研究团队已把蜘蛛基因植入细菌，甚至山羊体内来生产丝，但只取得了部分成功。原因之一在于，蛛丝最初是一种液态蛋白质，由蜘蛛腹部的特殊腺体产生。蜘蛛利用吐丝器施加力量，重新排列蛋白质的分子结构，使其转变为固体纤维。未参与该项目的阿克伦大学蛛丝专家 Todd Blackledge 解释说：“我们谈论蜘蛛吐丝时，谈的就是它如何施加力量，把液体变成固体。我们每年都更接近大规模生产，但目前仍未实现。”眼下，我们只能满足于这一块美得非同寻常的织物——这是100多万只蜘蛛共同带来的成果。

source.text: Antarctic research

translation.text: 南极研究

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Thirteen nations took part in the recent International Polar Year
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 13个国家参加了最近的国际极地年活动。

source.text: Thirteen nations took part in the recent International Polar Year

translation.text: 13个国家参加了最近的国际极地年活动。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: New Zealand’s contribution to International Polar Year was a 52-day voyage by the ship Tangaroa in order to conduct research in Antarctica’s Ross Sea. Lead scientist Mary Livingston emphasises just what a multi-faceted expedition this was, bringing together zoologists, oceanographers, meteorologists and other scientists from the Ministry of Fisheries, the National Institute for Water and Atmospheric Research, the National Museum and various universities, to study life beneath the seas of Antarctica. Competition for berths – the ship can carry 44 people, including 13 crew – was fierce. Voyage leader Stu Hanchet says, ‘We could have filled the science positions four times over … we had so many people requesting a berth … We ended up with a really strong team.’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 新西兰对国际极地年的贡献，是由“坦加罗阿”号开展一次为期52天的航行，前往南极洲罗斯海进行研究。首席科学家 Mary Livingston 强调，这是一支涉及众多领域的考察队。渔业部、国家水与大气研究所、国家博物馆和多所大学的动物学家、海洋学家、气象学家及其他科学家汇聚在一起，研究南极海域水下的生命。船上可载44人，其中包括13名船员，因此争夺船位的竞争十分激烈。航行负责人 Stu Hanchet 说：“申请船位的人实在太多……科学岗位即使增加到4倍也能全部招满……最后我们组建了一支非常强大的团队。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It would be hard to overstate how hostile the Antarctic environment is for scientists. The Tangaroa’s captain, Graham Leachman, explains that the Ross Sea is subject to katabatic winds* that sweep down off the Antarctic continent to create rough seas. Another danger is the possibility of the ship colliding with floating ice. ‘Even though the ship’s officers use all sorts of high-tech equipment … none of it can tell you how thick the ice is,’ says Leachman, ‘and you still can’t beat looking out of the window.’ In the dark, he says, you can’t tell how thick the ice is, but if you can see its colour, it’s possible to estimate. This is why he prefers sailing in summer, when the hours of daylight in these high latitudes are longest, even though this plays tricks with his passengers’ body clocks.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 南极环境对科学家极其恶劣，怎么强调都不为过。“坦加罗阿”号船长 Graham Leachman 解释说，罗斯海会遭遇从南极大陆俯冲而下的下降风*，造成汹涌海况。另一项危险是船只可能与浮冰相撞。Leachman 说：“虽然船上的驾驶员会使用各种高科技设备……但没有一种能告诉你冰有多厚，往窗外看仍是最可靠的方法。”他说，黑暗中无法判断冰层厚度；但只要能看见冰的颜色，就可以作出估计。正因如此，他更喜欢夏季航行，此时这些高纬度地区的白昼最长，尽管长时间日照会扰乱乘客的生物钟。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Analysis of what the expedition found continues, but it’s likely that several new species have been discovered and numerous other secrets revealed about life 3,000 metres below the surface. ‘We have collected huge worms and strange crustaceans,’ says Livingston, ‘but most impressive of all were the starfish that measured more than half a metre across – that’s most abnormal for creatures belonging to this species.’ This phenomenon of Antarctic seas is called ‘gigantism’ – the fact that some species grow to unusually large sizes. Livingston suggests various possible causes for gigantism including the extreme cold, few predators and high levels of oxygen in the seawater, but as yet no final determination can be made. Another interesting discovery was that in some places every inch of the sea floor was covered with life, whereas elsewhere icebergs have scoured out deep scars and ravines in the sea floor as they go by.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: By using deep-sea trawl nets, high-definition cameras and water samplers, the team has revealed that many of the creatures that live at extreme depths have a bizarre appearance. Among them were spotted tunicates, plankton-eating animals that are slender structures that appear to be fashioned from glass. The most fearsome-looking fish was the Southern Ocean daggertooth, a species that is ‘monocyclic’, meaning the fish die after the first spawning. They are also unusual for being capable of shedding their teeth and growing a new set. Another predatory fish brought to the surface was the stareater, an extraordinary species that has an appendage like a piece of cord hanging from its chin. In these deep, dark waters, this glows red and attracts prey to swim within striking distance. Just as impressive and much more beautiful were the basket stars, a species related to starfish that lives on the seabed. The basket stars’ five arms branch out numerous times to form a spectacular fan-like structure which they turn to face into the current so that food is brought into their embrace.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But whatever exciting discoveries were made, everyday life onboard ship in the Ross Sea is unrelenting. Most people share a cabin with one other person – they’re allocated so that as one person begins their 12 hours off duty, the other occupant is starting work on deck. The fresh food runs out in a few days and after that most provisions are frozen, canned or dried. Expedition general manager Fred Smits recognises that the cook has an essential role in ensuring the well-being of those onboard. ‘When you are at sea for so long,’ he says, ‘you think a lot about your next meal.’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，无论取得了多么令人兴奋的发现，在罗斯海的船上，日常生活都十分辛苦，毫无喘息。大多数人会与另一个人共用船舱；人员这样安排，是为了让一个人开始12小时休息时，另一位同舱者正好到甲板上开工。新鲜食物几天后就会吃完，此后的大部分食物都是冷冻、罐装或干制品。考察队总经理 Fred Smits 明白，厨师对保障船上人员的身心状态至关重要。他说：“长时间待在海上时，你会常常想着下一顿饭。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Perhaps most controversially, one of the precious berths on the Tangaroa was taken up by cameraman Max Quinn, who filmed a documentary about the voyage. Quinn’s inclusion wasn’t welcomed at first. ‘Scientists by nature,’ Livingston says, ‘tend to be camera-shy and quiet. They’re not into having cameras there, so it was difficult getting everyone’s permission and agreement.’ But in the end Quinn fitted in very well. ‘The trick,’ he says, ‘is to mostly film the scientists at work, in their professional roles … rather than eating their breakfast.’ He knows when not to intrude. The documentary is a window on a trip few people get to make and also a peek into what research really looks like. ‘Science,’ says Livingston, ‘is intrepid, more so than people realise. It’s not necessarily examining dry samples in the laboratory, but can also mean braving the elements on deck. That’s what the documentary captures, the sense of real people with real lives.’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 或许最具争议的是，“坦加罗阿”号一个宝贵的船位给了摄影师 Max Quinn，他拍摄了一部有关此次航行的纪录片。起初，人们并不欢迎 Quinn 加入。利文斯顿说：“科学家天性往往不愿面对镜头，而且性格安静。他们不喜欢旁边有摄像机，所以很难取得每个人的许可和同意。”但 Quinn 最终很好地融入了团队。他说：“诀窍是主要拍摄科学家工作时的专业状态……而不是他们吃早餐的样子。”他知道何时不应打扰别人。这部纪录片为人们打开了一扇窗，让他们看到一段很少有人能亲身经历的旅程，也一窥真实的研究是什么样子。利文斯顿说：“科学工作勇于冒险，远超人们的想象。它未必是在实验室里检查干燥样本，也可能意味着在甲板上直面恶劣天气。纪录片捕捉到的正是这一点——真实的人过着真实生活的感觉。”

source.text: Australia’s camouflaged creatures

translation.text: 澳大利亚的伪装动物

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Many species of animal in Australia protect themselves by using camouflage — a way of ‘hiding’ by blending into the surroundings.
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 澳大利亚许多动物物种利用伪装来保护自己，也就是通过融入周围环境来“隐藏”自己。

source.text: Many species of animal in Australia protect themselves by using camouflage — a way of ‘hiding’ by blending into the surroundings.

translation.text: 澳大利亚许多动物物种利用伪装来保护自己，也就是通过融入周围环境来“隐藏”自己。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Most species use camouflage to some extent. If they are convincing, they survive to pass their genes on to future generations. After generations of natural selection, animals can develop astonishingly complex camouflage techniques, manipulating shape, colour and movement. ‘The principle of camouflage is to make it economically unviable for a predator to pursue a particular species of prey,’ explains Professor Mark Elgar of the University of Melbourne. ‘Camouflage increases the search time and, as a consequence, the predator will simply target another species, either because it doesn’t see the camouflaged individual or it just finds something more obvious to do.’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 大多数物种都会在一定程度上利用伪装。只要伪装足够逼真，它们就能生存下来，并把基因传给后代。经过一代代自然选择，动物可以发展出极为复杂的伪装技巧，灵活运用体形、颜色和动作。墨尔本大学的 Mark Elgar 教授解释说：“伪装的原则，是让捕食者觉得追逐某一种猎物得不偿失。伪装会延长搜寻时间，因此捕食者会直接转向另一物种：要么因为它看不到伪装起来的个体，要么只是因为它发现了更显眼的目标。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The easiest way for an animal to disguise itself is to be invisible in its surroundings. To that end, stick and leaf insects have evolved complex camouflage to hide themselves from predators. Many have the texture of sticks or dry leaves, while others imitate living foliage, even the veins in a leaf. Some insects develop blemishes to match the spots caused by disease. A convincing appearance only works if its owner also acts the part, so during the day the creature using this type of camouflage keeps motionless, or sways like a dead leaf in the breeze. If disturbed, it falls to the ground and stays still. Entomologist Paul Zborowski, who has spent decades photographing inconspicuous creatures, rates the desert insects of Central Australia as the most convincingly disguised creatures he’s seen. ‘It’s an incredibly old habitat, so the creatures have had a long time to adapt,’ Zborowski explains. Most of them behave like stones and don’t move all day, feeding only at night.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 动物隐藏自己最简单的办法，就是让自己在周围环境中仿佛不存在。为此，竹节虫和叶䗛进化出了复杂的伪装，以躲避捕食者。许多种类具有枯枝或干叶般的质感，另一些则模仿鲜活的叶片，甚至连叶脉也惟妙惟肖。有些昆虫还会长出斑痕，以模拟植物因疾病形成的斑点。逼真的外表只有配上相应的动作才有效，因此，采用这类伪装的生物白天会一动不动，或像枯叶一样随风摇摆。一旦受到惊扰，它便掉到地上，保持静止。昆虫学家 Paul Zborowski 数十年来一直拍摄不起眼的生物；在他见过的动物中，澳大利亚中部的沙漠昆虫伪装得最逼真。Zborowski 解释说：“这片栖息地极为古老，因此那里的生物有很长时间来适应环境。”其中大多数像石头一样，整天不动，只在夜间进食。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A tawny frogmouth sitting motionless on a stump also illustrates the importance of pairing a persuasive costume with behaviour. Professor Gisela Kaplan of the University of New England in Australia says the frogmouth’s skill at camouflaging is learned behaviour. While adopting a pose may be a reflex of the bird, and can be observed in a hatchling’s first week, the ability to choose a backdrop which matches its colouration does not develop for 4–6 months. When the chicks land, they are usually highly conspicuous, and their parents try to signal to them to move to a safe location.

translation.text: 澳大利亚新英格兰大学的 Gisela Kaplan 教授说，蟆口鸱的伪装本领是后天学会的。

source.text: While adopting a pose may be a reflex of the bird, and can be observed in a hatchling’s first week, the ability to choose a backdrop which matches its colouration does not develop for 4–6 months.

translation.text: 摆出特定姿势或许是这种鸟的反射行为，雏鸟出生第一周便可观察到；但选择与自身颜色相配背景的能力，要到4至6个月后才会形成。

source.text: When the chicks land, they are usually highly conspicuous, and their parents try to signal to them to move to a safe location.

translation.text: 雏鸟落地时通常十分显眼，亲鸟会设法发出信号，让它们转移到安全地点。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Fixed camouflage is only good against a relatively unchanging environment, so some animals, such as the cuttlefish, have evolved an adaptable disguise. The cuttlefish can almost instantly change its colour, pattern and texture to match its surroundings, using specialised cells and muscles. On Queensland’s reefs, scientists have been studying another ocean dweller that uses colour change, although not to blend into the surroundings. Dr Karen Cheney, from the University of Queensland, says the bluestriped fangblenny alters its colouration to mimic other species of fish, allowing it to travel with them and benefit from safety in numbers.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 固定不变的伪装只适用于相对稳定的环境，因此乌贼等一些动物进化出了可以调整的伪装。乌贼利用特殊细胞和肌肉，几乎能在瞬间改变颜色、花纹和表面质感，使自己与周围环境相配。在昆士兰的珊瑚礁上，科学家一直在研究另一种会变色的海洋生物，不过它变色并不是为了融入环境。昆士兰大学的 Karen Cheney 博士说，蓝纹尖牙鳚会改变体色来模仿其他鱼类，从而与它们一起游动，并借助群体优势提高安全性。

It darts out from the safety of the wrasse’s cleaning station to nip at unsuspecting fish passing by, but it doesn’t attack those coming to be cleaned.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The most famous form of mimicry, however, is for defence, not attack. Batesian mimicry refers to animals that gain protection from predators by imitating a dangerous organism, often using conspicuous colours. The nineteenth-century naturalist Henry Bates first suggested this camouflage technique after noticing that several Amazonian butterfly species looked the same. The technique was later called after him.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，最著名的拟态形式是用于防御，而不是攻击。贝氏拟态是指动物通过模仿危险生物来获得保护，免受捕食者攻击；这种模仿常会采用醒目的颜色。19世纪博物学家 Henry Bates 注意到亚马孙地区有几种蝴蝶外形相同，因而首次提出这种伪装技巧。后来，这种技巧便以他的名字命名。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In Australian waters, the harmless harlequin snake eel sports the same black and white bandings as the highly toxic yellow-lipped sea krait, ensuring no predator will attack. However, the success of Batesian mimicry depends on the ratio of mimics to originals. If a predator encounters too many that are edible, it will just assume none of the animals with those markings are dangerous, explains Martyn Robinson, an educational naturalist with the Australian Museum.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In Queensland’s tablelands, the chameleon gecko has another way of making predators hesitate. Its body is brown, but its tail is banded in black and white. Robinson explains that if attacked, the chameleon gecko will drop off its tail, which will wriggle around on the ground. Many lizards do this, but in the case of the chameleon gecko the tail bones actually rub against one another, so it squeaks. ‘The predator is, of course, thoroughly absorbed by this black-and-white-striped, wriggling, squeaking thing on the ground, and the gecko can sneak away,’ Robinson says. It’s a one-time-only trick: the regrown tail is brown, the same as the gecko’s body.

source.text: Biomimicry

translation.text: 仿生学

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Velcro, now commonly used instead of buttons and zippers, is probably the most famous example of ‘biomimicry’, where technologists turn to nature for inspiration. In 1948, scientist Georges de Mestral was walking through long grass when he noticed that dozens of seeds had attached themselves to his trousers. Under a microscope, de Mestral noted the hook-and-loop system the seed cases used to stick so firmly, and was inspired.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 如今常被用来替代纽扣和拉链的魔术贴（Velcro），可能是“仿生学”最著名的例子；在仿生学中，技术人员会向大自然寻求灵感。1948年，科学家 Georges de Mestral 走过一片高草地时，发现数十颗种子粘在了自己的裤子上。de Mestral 在显微镜下观察到，种子外壳利用钩与环组成的结构牢牢附着在物体上，并由此获得灵感。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: US biologist Janine Benyus wrote a book on the subject called Biomimicry: Innovation Inspired by Nature. Published in 1997, the book set off the current wave of technology modelled on nature. According to Benyus, our ancestors were practised in the art of biomimicry. ‘I think it’s an old impulse for humans to take their cues from other organisms,’ she says, referring to African tribes that found edible plants by observing the dining habits of chimpanzees. But lately we’ve become more focused on what we can make ourselves. Benyus thinks our drift away from nature started with the advent of agriculture: ‘When we broke free from the challenges of hunting and gathering and learnt to stock our cupboards, we fooled ourselves into believing that we didn’t need other organisms at all,’ she says.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 美国生物学家 Janine Benyus 写过一本有关这一主题的书，名为《仿生学：受自然启发的创新》。该书于1997年出版，引发了当前这股模仿自然的技术浪潮。Benyus 认为，我们的祖先早已熟练掌握仿生之道。她说：“我认为，人类向其他生物寻求启示，是一种由来已久的本能。”她以非洲部落为例：他们通过观察黑猩猩的进食习惯来寻找可食用植物。然而近来，我们越来越专注于自己能够制造什么。Benyus 认为，人类逐渐疏离自然始于农业出现之时。她说：“当我们摆脱狩猎采集的种种挑战，学会在橱柜里储存食物后，我们便误以为自己根本不再需要其他生物。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The scientific, industrial, petrochemical and genetic engineering revolutions have repeatedly reinforced the idea that we are liberated from biological constraints. In recent years, however, the illusion that we are independent of nature has been shattered by the spectre of global warming and the looming end to fossil fuel supplies. Since few of us would be willing to forgo the products and services we’ve grown accustomed to – food, water, shelter, the conveniences that modern technology brings – the challenge is to meet the complex demands of civilisation within the bounds of sustainability. ‘Nature has learnt to fly, live in the depths of the ocean and craft miracle materials,’ writes Benyus. ‘Living creatures have done everything we want to do, without guzzling fossil fuel or polluting the planet. What better models could there be?’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 科学革命、工业革命、石油化工革命和基因工程革命，一再强化了这样一种观念：我们已经摆脱生物条件的限制。然而近年来，全球变暖的阴影和化石燃料供应即将枯竭的前景，打破了人类可以独立于自然的幻想。我们中很少有人愿意放弃已经习惯的产品和服务——食物、水、住所，以及现代技术带来的便利。因此，当前的挑战是在可持续发展的范围内满足文明社会的复杂需求。Benyus 写道：“大自然已经学会飞行、生活在海洋深处，并制造神奇的材料。生物已经做到了我们想做的一切，却不用大量消耗化石燃料，也不会污染地球。还有比它们更好的范本吗？”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: There are no better models, according to Tim Finnigan, a marine engineer at the University of Sydney. In his quest to harness the world’s waves and tides for renewable energy more efficiently, Finnigan has taken his cues from aquatic life. With their streamlined bodies and stiff, high tail fins, sharks convert up to 90 per cent of their body energy into forward thrust. Inspired by such efficient hydrodynamics, but turning the theory on its head, Finnigan designed his tidal stream generator: an 18-metre-long biomimetic shark tail with a fin spanning 15 metres. ‘Rather than have a body moving through a stationary fluid, we have fluid that’s moving past a stationary body,’ says Finnigan.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: While conventional architects were designing buildings dependent on expensive air conditioning systems, when Mick Pearce tried to do the same, he struck a problem. ‘We were building office blocks for a client in Zimbabwe and we ran out of funds. So we looked for ways to make a building without traditional air conditioning.’ One day, driving through the grasslands, he saw a large mound created by termites, the ant-like insect common in Africa. He noticed that air entering at the base of the mound was mixed with water drawn from subterranean levels by the termites, causing evaporative cooling. Pearce wanted to reproduce this principle but he needed an alternative system, and in his building massive fans were employed at the base of the structure to lower the temperature of the circulating air. Pearce’s termite-inspired cooling system cut energy use to 10 per cent of a similar air-conditioned building.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use energy from the sun to convert water and carbon dioxide into carbohydrates and oxygen. Plants can manage it with humbling ease. But, as the 40 researchers from 11 institutes who have collaborated to form the Australian Artificial Photosynthesis Network have realised, it is very complex. However, there is one aspect working in our favour. In nature, environmental variables like temperature, carbon dioxide and light availability limit the rate of photosynthesis. In a laboratory these variables can be optimized. ‘We don’t have to cope with drought or frost. We can work with a highly controlled, specified set of conditions,’ says Tom Collings, the group’s spokesman.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 光合作用是绿色植物利用太阳能，把水和二氧化碳转化为碳水化合物和氧气的过程。植物完成这一过程轻而易举，令人自叹不如。然而，由11家机构的40名研究人员合作组成的澳大利亚人工光合作用网络已经认识到，这一过程非常复杂。不过，有一个方面对我们有利。在自然环境中，温度、二氧化碳和光照条件等环境变量会限制光合作用的速度；在实验室里，这些变量可以得到优化。该团队的发言人 Tom Collings 说：“我们不必应对干旱或霜冻，可以在一套受到高度控制、明确规定的条件下开展工作。”

source.text: Biophilic Design

translation.text: 亲生物设计

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Biophilic design, a movement related to green architecture, has gained much momentum within the building community in recent years. The premise of biophilic design is to avoid or minimise harmful impacts on the natural environment and, equally importantly, to provide and restore beneficial contacts between people and nature in the built environment.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 亲生物设计是一场与绿色建筑相关的运动，近年来在建筑界发展势头强劲。亲生物设计的基本理念，是避免或尽量减少对自然环境的有害影响；同样重要的是，要在人工建成的环境中，让人与自然建立或恢复有益的接触。

source.text: Biophilic design, a movement related to green architecture, has gained much momentum within the building community in recent years.

translation.text: 亲生物设计是一场与绿色建筑相关的运动，近年来在建筑界发展势头强劲。

source.text: The premise of biophilic design is to avoid or minimise harmful impacts on the natural environment and, equally importantly, to provide and restore beneficial contacts between people and nature in the built environment.

translation.text: 亲生物设计的基本理念，是避免或尽量减少对自然环境的有害影响；同样重要的是，要在人工建成的环境中，让人与自然建立或恢复有益的接触。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: People have a psychologically developed need to commune with nature, but this has frequently been neglected. All too often, architects put creative originality before the needs of the people who must live and work in their futuristic constructions, with scant regard for emotional as well as practical considerations. Biophilic design does not advocate tree houses or cave-dwelling, but it does provide nature-based features that maximise human functioning and health. Though not technically a biophilic design, Fallingwater—the stunning house in rural Pennsylvania designed in the 1930s by Frank Lloyd Wright—arguably speaks to the human soul far more than the box-like blocks of flats designed by his contemporary Le Corbusier.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 人类在心理上形成了亲近自然的需求，但这一需求经常受到忽视。建筑师往往把创作上的独创性置于居住和工作在其未来主义建筑中的人们的需求之上，很少顾及情感和实际两方面的考量。亲生物设计并不主张住树屋或洞穴，而是提供以自然为基础的元素，最大限度地改善人的机能和健康。流水别墅（Fallingwater）严格来说并非亲生物设计；这座令人赞叹的住宅位于宾夕法尼亚州乡间，由 Frank Lloyd Wright 于20世纪30年代设计。可以说，与其同时代人 Le Corbusier 设计的盒子般公寓楼相比，它更能触动人的心灵。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In the modern world, much of our built environment obstructs the age-old connection between humans and nature. The rate of technological progress far exceeds the rate of psychological evolution, leaving us ill-equipped to cope with our lifestyles, which in turn leads to increased stress. Because biophilia attempts to integrate basic and current needs, it can alleviate the difficulties caused by the brain’s constant efforts to function in a modern environment it has not yet evolved to handle. For example, one crucial element of the natural landscape for human health is sunlight. We are evolutionarily programmed to respond positively to sunny areas over dark or overcast ones and sense that they will foster restoration, improve emotional well-being and promote health.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在现代世界中，大量人工建成的环境阻隔了人与自然之间古老的联系。技术进步的速度远远超过心理进化的速度，使我们缺乏应对自身生活方式的能力，进而造成更大压力。亲生物理念试图把人的基本需求与当下需求结合起来，因此可以缓解大脑在尚未进化到足以适应的现代环境中不断努力运作所带来的困难。例如，自然景观中对人类健康至关重要的一个因素是阳光。进化使我们天生更喜欢阳光充足的地方，而不是阴暗或阴云密布之处；我们会感觉前者有助于恢复身心、改善情绪健康并促进身体健康。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Because of its tremendous impact on human psychology, biophilic design plays a vital role in healthcare and its delivery. The current healthcare system contains many flaws, especially in its physical spaces. Hospitals, clinics and offices are high-stress environments for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals alike. One well-known study looked at the impact of nature on patients after surgery. One group had a view of a tree; the others had a window looking onto a brick wall. The first group had shorter hospital stays, received fewer negative comments from nurses, required fewer analgesics and had slightly fewer post-operative complications.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 亲生物设计对人的心理有巨大影响，因此在医疗保健及其服务提供中发挥着重要作用。当前的医疗体系存在许多缺陷，物理空间方面尤其如此。对患者、访客和医护人员来说，医院、诊所和诊室都是压力很大的环境。一项著名研究考察了自然景观对术后患者的影响。一组患者能看见一棵树，另一组患者的窗外则是一堵砖墙。第一组住院时间更短，护士对他们的负面评价更少，所需止痛药更少，术后并发症也略少。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As a consequence of this and other studies, nature and nature-based design have been integrated into the physical design of many hospitals. For example, Dartmouth-Hitchcock Medical Center (DHMC) in New Hampshire boasts an atrium design illuminating the entire facility. Natural elements also permeate the building, including wood, stone and numerous live plants. While DHMC was built to incorporate these qualities, other hospitals have had biophilic features added to existing structures. The application of biophilic concepts to hospital interiors has increased substantially as administrators have witnessed patients’ positive responses to nature.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这项研究和其他研究促使自然元素及以自然为基础的设计融入许多医院的空间设计。例如，新罕布什尔州的达特茅斯—希区柯克医疗中心（Dartmouth-Hitchcock Medical Center，DHMC）拥有一个能让整座设施充满光线的中庭。木材、石材和大量活体植物等自然元素也遍布楼内。DHMC 从建造之初就纳入了这些特点，另一些医院则在既有建筑中增添亲生物元素。管理人员亲眼看到患者对自然的积极反应后，亲生物理念在医院室内设计中的应用大幅增加。

source.text: The application of biophilic concepts to hospital interiors has increased substantially as administrators have witnessed patients’ positive responses to nature.

translation.text: 管理人员亲眼看到患者对自然的积极反应后，亲生物理念在医院室内设计中的应用大幅增加。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Many existing buildings contain biophilic elements, but only a few have been built with the specific idea of biophilic design in mind. One such building is the Adam Joseph Lewis Center for Environmental Studies at Oberlin College in Ohio. The director of Oberlin’s Environmental Studies Program, David Orr, explained that the building’s goals were “to create not just a place for classes but rather a building that would help to redefine the relationship between humankind and the environment—one that would expand our sense of ecological possibilities”. The Lewis Center is sustainable in a broader sense than in the typical application of the word. It harnesses solar power, utilises both active and passive air systems, and monitors the weather to adapt to conditions. The Centre’s “Living Machine” treats wastewater by combining traditional wastewater technology with wetland ecosystems’ purification processes, producing water that can be used in the toilets and for irrigation. In their design, Orr and his team of architects engineered a healthy and comfortable space for students while ensuring the surrounding environment was undamaged.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Another example is the University of Guelph-Humber building in Ontario, Canada. It contains a centrally located bio-wall, vertically spanning the building. The wall is covered in dense foliage which not only connects people to nature on the inside of the building, but also functions as a new filtration-system prototype. The wall purifies the air and has the potential to fulfil the building’s fresh-air-intake requirements. These examples prove that the built environment need not interfere with biological human needs to commune with nature, nor with existing ecological systems.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 另一个例子是加拿大安大略省的圭尔夫—汉伯大学大楼。楼内中央设有一面纵向贯穿建筑的生态墙。墙面覆盖着茂密植物，不仅让建筑内部的人与自然相连，还充当一种新型过滤系统的原型。这面墙能够净化空气，并有可能满足整栋建筑的新鲜空气进气需求。这些实例证明，人工建成的环境不必妨碍人类亲近自然的生物需求，也不必干扰现有生态系统。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Ancient architects built for their cultures, which were almost always more in touch with the earth than Western society is today. They mimicked nature’s forms, producing magnificent structures that still awe us—though biophilic design is a novel concept, they certainly employed some of its recommendations. Today we can add another layer to this tradition and ensure maximal benefit for our planet and ourselves.

source.text: Bird Migration

translation.text: 鸟类迁徙

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Birds are highly mobile and among the swiftest of living creatures. Flight gives them the power to move in any direction for as long as they have the energy to keep going. They are equipped with lightweight, hollow bones, a finely-tuned navigation system and an ingenious heat-conserving design that allows them to face life in the harshest of climates. Their respiratory systems have to perform efficiently during sustained flights at altitude, so they have evolved a system of extracting air from their lungs that far exceeds that of any other animal. These features enable birds to come and go with the seasons. On the way, they face constant danger and a daily requirement to find food, water and a safe place to rest. So why do millions of birds migrate rather than stay in one place?
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 鸟类的活动能力极强，也是速度最快的生物之一。只要还有能量继续前进，飞行就使它们能够朝任何方向移动。鸟类有轻盈的中空骨骼、调校精细的导航系统和巧妙的保温结构，因而能够在最严酷的气候中生存。它们在高空持续飞行时，呼吸系统必须高效运作，因此进化出一套从肺部抽取空气的系统，其效率远超任何其他动物。这些特征使鸟类能够随季节来去迁移。途中，它们时刻面临危险，每天还必须找到食物、水和安全的休息地。那么，为什么数以百万计的鸟会选择迁徙，而不是留在一个地方？

source.text: So why do millions of birds migrate rather than stay in one place?

translation.text: 那么，为什么数以百万计的鸟会选择迁徙，而不是留在一个地方？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Most of the explanation revolves around food. In temperate and arctic regions of the northern hemisphere, food is abundant during a short growing season. Migration evolved as a way for birds to exploit resources that are seasonally abundant and, equally important, to go elsewhere when the resources become scarce or harsh weather arrives. Many species can tolerate cold temperatures if food is plentiful but when food is not available they must migrate.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 大部分原因都与食物有关。在北半球温带和北极地区，食物会在短暂的生长季中大量出现。迁徙行为由此进化而来，使鸟类能够利用季节性丰富的资源；同样重要的是，当资源变得匮乏或恶劣天气来临时，它们可以前往别处。许多物种在食物充足时能够忍受低温，但一旦找不到食物，就必须迁徙。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: While this simple explanation for why birds migrate is essentially true, intriguing questions remain. One puzzling fact is that many birds journey much further than would be necessary to find food and good weather. Another apparent conundrum involves the huge migrations performed by arctic birds and mudflat-probing shore birds that breed close to polar regions. In general, the further north a migrant species breeds, the further south it spends the winter. Yet, en route to a final destination in southern latitudes, all these individuals overfly areas of seemingly suitable habitat spanning two hemispheres. Such compulsive journeys probably evolved over time and in response to fluctuations in weather but we do not really know.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But just how do birds reach their destination and, more to the point, how do young birds migrate over vast distances without parental assistance? Very few adults migrate accompanied by their offspring and youngsters may have little or no inkling of their parents' appearance. Cuckoos are famous for depositing their eggs in the nests of other birds that unwittingly serve as foster-parents. Astonishing as this piece of evolutionary behaviour is, it is even more remarkable to consider that, once grown, the young cuckoo makes its own way to ancestral wintering grounds in the tropics before returning single-handedly to northern Europe to seek out a mate among its own kind.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，鸟究竟如何抵达目的地？更关键的是，幼鸟没有亲鸟帮助，怎样能迁徙如此遥远的距离？极少有成年鸟带着后代迁徙，幼鸟甚至可能对父母的外形所知甚少或一无所知。杜鹃会把卵产在其他鸟的巢中，让毫不知情的鸟充当养父母，这一点十分著名。这种进化行为已经令人惊叹，但更不可思议的是，小杜鹃长大后会独自前往祖先在热带的越冬地，随后又独自返回北欧，在同类中寻找配偶。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As we continue to study bird migration, its mystery is better understood but also compounded. Mounting evidence has confirmed that birds use the sun and stars to obtain compass directions but true navigation requires an awareness of position and time, especially when lost. Experiments have shown that, after being taken thousands of miles over an unfamiliar landmass, birds are still capable of returning rapidly to nest sites. Such phenomenal powers are the product of computing a number of sophisticated cues including an innate map of the night sky and the pull of the Earth's magnetic field. How the birds use their 'instruments' remains unknown, but one thing is clear – they see the world with a sensory perception superior to ours. Most small birds migrate at night and take their direction from the position of the setting sun. However, as well as seeing the sun go down, they also seem to see the plane of polarised light it causes. This calibrates their compass. Travelling at night provides other benefits: the danger of meeting predators as well as the risk of dehydration due to flying for long periods in warm sunlit skies is reduced. Furthermore, at night the air structure is cool and smooth and conducive to sustained, stable flight.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 随着我们不断研究鸟类迁徙，人们对其中的奥秘了解得更多，但同时也发现它更加复杂。越来越多的证据已经证实，鸟类利用太阳和星辰获取罗盘方向；但真正的导航还要求它们了解自己的位置和时间，尤其是在迷失方向时。实验表明，即使被带到数千英里外一片陌生的陆地上，鸟类仍能迅速返回筑巢地点。这种非凡能力来自对多种复杂线索的综合计算，其中包括与生俱来的夜空地图和地球磁场的牵引力。鸟类究竟如何使用这些“仪器”仍是未知，但有一点很清楚：它们感知世界的能力胜过我们。大多数小型鸟类在夜间迁徙，并根据落日的位置确定方向。不过，它们似乎不仅能看到太阳落下，还能看见由此形成的偏振光平面，从而校准自己的罗盘。夜间飞行还有其他好处：遇到捕食者的危险较小，也能降低长时间在温暖、阳光充足的天空中飞行所造成的脱水风险。此外，夜间空气凉爽平稳，有利于长时间稳定飞行。
