source.text: How well do people concentrate?

translation.text: 人们的专注力有多强？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: When you read do you also listen to music? Do you talk to friends or colleagues at the office? As you are reading online, are you also emailing or instant-messaging? Since the 1990s, virtually all of us have spent part of our day multitasking – that is, either switching from one task to another or juggling two or more things at the same time. Although doing many things at once can be a way of making tasks fun and energizing, according to author Thomas Lehman, ‘You sacrifice focus when you do this. Multitasking is shifting focus from one task to another in rapid succession. It gives the illusion that you’re simultaneously tasking, but you’re not really. You can only shift back and forth. It’s like playing tennis with three balls.’ Of course, it depends on what you’re doing. For some people, listening to music while working actually makes them more imaginative because they are using their brains for different cognitive functions. But we’re all familiar with what Lehman calls ‘email voice’, when someone you’re talking to on the phone suddenly appears not to be fully engaged with the conversation.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 阅读时，你也会听音乐吗？在办公室里，你会和朋友或同事说话吗？在线阅读的同时，你还会收发电子邮件或即时消息吗？自20世纪90年代以来，我们几乎每个人每天都会花一部分时间处理多项任务，也就是在不同任务之间切换，或同时应付两件乃至更多事情。作家 Thomas Lehman 指出，虽然同时做许多事情能让任务变得有趣，使人更有干劲，但“这样做会牺牲专注力。所谓多任务处理，是在不同任务之间快速转移注意力。它让你以为自己在同时做几件事，其实并非如此。你只能来回切换，就像同时用三个球打网球一样”。当然，这也取决于你在做什么。对有些人来说，工作时听音乐确实能增强想象力，因为大脑动用的是不同的认知功能。不过，我们都熟悉 Lehman 所说的“邮件腔”——与你通电话的人突然显得没有全心投入谈话。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But today, as we feel required to do more and more things in a shorter period of time, researchers are trying to figure out how the brain changes attention from one subject to another. Earl Miller, professor of neuroscience at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, explains that humans have a very large prefrontal cortex, which is the part of the brain that helps us switch and prioritize tasks. In humans, he says, this area is about one-third of the entire cortex, while in dogs and cats, it is four or five percent and in monkeys about 15 percent. ‘With the growth of the prefrontal cortex, animals become more flexible in their behavior,’ according to Miller. We can do a couple of things at the same time if they are routine, but once they demand more cognitive processing, even the human brain has ‘a severe bottleneck’. Miller conducted studies where electrodes were attached to the heads of people to monitor them while performing different tasks. He found that ‘when there’re lots of visual stimulants out there in front of you, only one or two objects tend to activate your neurons, indicating that you’re really only focusing on one or two items at a time.’

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Although we may be advised to focus on one thing at a time, the real world doesn’t work that way. We are constantly interrupted. Gloria Mark, professor of informatics at the University of California, has studied this using people in offices as subjects. blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Psychiatrist Edward Hallowell has termed the effects of multitasking ‘attention deficit trait’, which he attributes entirely to the environment. ‘Our minds fill with noise – brain activity with little significance – and the brain gradually loses its capacity to attend fully to anything.’ Desperately trying to keep up with a multitude of jobs, we ‘feel a constant low level of panic and guilt.’ But Hallowell says that despite our belief that we cannot control this overload, we can. ‘We need to create boundaries,’ he says. That means devices like cellphones being banned at meetings. It means training yourself not to look at your computer every 20 seconds.

source.text: Insect Decision-Making

translation.text: 昆虫的决策

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It has long been held that decisions made collectively by large groups of people are more likely to turn out to be accurate than decisions made by individuals. The idea goes back to the ‘jury theorem’ of Nicolas de Condorcet, an 18th-century French philosopher who was one of the first to apply mathematics to the social sciences. Condorcet’s theory describes collective decisions, outlining how democratic decisions tend to outperform dictatorial ones. If, for example, each member of a jury has only partial information, the majority decision is more likely to be correct than a decision arrived at by a single juror. Moreover, the probability of a correct decision increases with the size of the jury.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 长期以来，人们一直认为，由一大群人共同作出的决定，比个人作出的决定更有可能是准确的。这一观点可追溯至18世纪法国哲学家 Nicolas de Condorcet 提出的“陪审团定理”；他是最早将数学应用于社会科学的人之一。Condorcet 的理论描述了集体决策，并阐明民主决策往往优于独裁决策。例如，如果陪审团的每名成员都只掌握部分信息，那么多数人的决定比单个陪审员作出的决定更可能正确。此外，正确决策的概率会随着陪审团规模的扩大而提高。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Now it is becoming clear that group decisions are also extremely valuable for the success of social animals, such as ants, bees, birds and dolphins. Bees make collective decisions, and they do it rather well, according to Christian List of the London School of Economics, who has studied group decision-making in humans and animals. Researchers led by Dr List looked at colonies once the original colony reached a certain size. The queen goes off with about two-thirds of the worker bees to live in a new home or nest, leaving a daughter queen in the old nest with the remaining workers. Among the bees that depart are some that have searched for and found some new nest sites, and reported back using a characteristic body movement known as a ‘waggle dance’ to indicate to the other bees the suitable places they have located. The longer the dance, the better the site. After a while, other bees start to visit the sites signalled by their companions to see for themselves and, on their return, also perform more waggle dances. The process eventually leads to a consensus on the best site and the breakaway swarm migrates. The decision is remarkably reliable, with the bees choosing the best site even when there are only small differences between alternative sites.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 如今越来越清楚的是，群体决策对蚂蚁、蜜蜂、鸟类和海豚等社会性动物能否成功生存也极为重要。伦敦政治经济学院的 Christian List 研究过人类和动物的群体决策；据他说，蜜蜂会共同作出决定，而且做得相当好。List 博士带领研究人员观察了蜂群达到一定规模后的情况。蜂王会带着约三分之二的工蜂离开，前往新居或新巢，并把一只子代蜂王和其余工蜂留在旧巢。离开的蜜蜂中，有些已经搜寻并找到数个新巢址；它们回来后会用一种称为“摇摆舞”的特有身体动作报告发现，以此向其他蜜蜂指示合适的地点。舞跳得越久，说明地点越好。过一阵子，其他蜜蜂开始亲自前往同伴所指示的地点察看，回来后也会跳更多摇摆舞。这个过程最终使蜂群就最佳地点达成共识，分出的蜂群随后迁往那里。这种决策非常可靠，即使备选地点之间只有细微差别，蜜蜂也能选出最佳地点。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But exactly how do bees reach such a robust consensus? To find out, Dr List and his colleagues used a computer-generated model of the decision-making process. By experimenting with it, they found that, when bees in the model were very good at finding nesting sites but did not share their information, this dramatically slowed down the migration, leaving the swarm homeless and vulnerable. Conversely, bees in the model blindly followed the waggle dances of others without first checking. The researchers concluded that the ability of bees to identify successfully and quickly the best site depends on both the bees’ interdependence in communicating the whereabouts of the best site, and their independence in confirming this information for themselves.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 但蜜蜂究竟如何达成如此稳固的共识？为了找出答案，List 博士及其同事使用了一个由计算机生成的决策过程模型。通过对模型进行试验，他们发现，当模型中的蜜蜂很善于寻找巢址，却不共享信息时，迁徙速度会大幅减慢，使蜂群无家可归且容易受到伤害。相反，在另一种情况下，模型中的蜜蜂没有先行核查，就盲目跟随其他蜜蜂的摇摆舞。研究人员得出结论：蜜蜂能否成功而迅速地找出最佳地点，既取决于它们相互依靠、交流最佳地点的位置，也取决于它们独立地亲自核实这一信息。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Another situation in which collective decisions are taken occurs when animals are either isolated from crucial sources of information or dominated by other members of the group. Jose Halloy of the Free University of Brussels in Belgium used robotic cockroaches to subvert the behaviour of living cockroaches and control their decision-making process. In his experiment, the artificial bugs were introduced to the live ones and soon became sufficiently socially integrated that they were perceived by the real cockroaches as equals. By manipulating the robots, which were in the minority, Halloy was able to persuade the living cockroaches to choose an inappropriate shelter—even one which they had rejected before being infiltrated by the robots.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The way insects put into effect collective decisions can be complex and as important as the decisions themselves. At the University of Bristol, in the UK, Nigel Franks and his colleagues studied how a species of ant establishes a new nest. Franks and his associates reported how the insects reduce the problems associated with making a necessarily swift choice. If the ants’ existing nest becomes suddenly threatened, the insects choose certain ants to act as scouts to find a new nest. How quickly they accomplish the transfer to a new home depends not only on how soon the best available site is found, but also on how quickly the migration there can be achieved.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Once the suitable new nest is identified, the chosen ants begin to lead others, which have made it to the new site or which may simply be in the vicinity, back to the original threatened nest. source.text: Intelligent behaviour in birds

translation.text: 鸟类的智能行为

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Many people are aware of the intelligence of chimpanzees and other mammals. However, birds also demonstrate intelligent behaviour.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 许多人知道黑猩猩和其他哺乳动物很聪明。不过，鸟类也会展现智能行为。

source.text: Many people are aware of the intelligence of chimpanzees and other mammals.

translation.text: 许多人知道黑猩猩和其他哺乳动物很聪明。

source.text: However, birds also demonstrate intelligent behaviour.

translation.text: 不过，鸟类也会展现智能行为。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: For centuries, many scholars maintained that humans were the only intelligent organisms on Earth. Many traits were considered to be exclusively human examples of acumen – for example, language, tool use, deception, and awareness of self and others. However, exciting new research on a number of animals, particularly birds, has called into question the uniqueness of these traits, forcing us to reconsider this opinion. In 1964, people were amazed when naturalist Jane Goodall first discovered chimpanzees making and using tools. But ornithologists, people who study birds, were not overly surprised. Almost 20 years earlier, a renowned ornithologist had shown that tool use was commonplace in populations of woodpecker finches residing on the Galápagos Islands. These tiny birds routinely used twigs to extract grubs from under bark.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 几个世纪以来，许多学者一直坚称，人类是地球上唯一具有智能的生物。语言、使用工具、欺骗，以及认识自己和他人等许多特征，都曾被视为人类才有的才智表现。然而，针对多种动物，尤其是鸟类开展的令人振奋的新研究，对这些特征是否为人类独有提出了质疑，迫使我们重新审视这一看法。1964年，博物学家 Jane Goodall 首次发现黑猩猩会制作并使用工具，令世人大为惊讶。但研究鸟类的鸟类学家并没有特别吃惊。早在近20年前，一位著名鸟类学家就已证明，生活在加拉帕戈斯群岛的啄木鸟雀种群普遍会使用工具。这些小鸟经常用细枝从树皮下掏出蛴螬。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Since then, the catalogue of tool-using animals has grown. At least three Australian bird species make tools similar to those of the woodpecker finch, and when white-winged choughs come across shellfish, they have been known to use rocks as hammers to crack open the recalcitrant shells. Other birds show a more sophisticated level of insight. For example, black kites have been reported dropping bait into lakes to bring fish to the surface of the water, thereby making them easier to catch. A kite may also pick up a smouldering stick from an area recently burned by a bushfire and drop the stick on a patch of unburned grass. The bird then feasts on the small animals that flee from the subsequent fire.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 此后，会使用工具的动物名单不断增加。澳大利亚至少有三种鸟会制作与啄木鸟雀所用工具相似的工具；人们还发现，白翅山鸦遇到贝类时，会把石头当作锤子，敲开难以破开的外壳。其他鸟类展现出更高层次的洞察力。例如，据报道，黑鸢会把诱饵投入湖中，引鱼游到水面，从而更容易捕捉。黑鸢还可能从刚遭林火焚烧的区域捡起一根仍在阴燃的树枝，把它扔到一片尚未燃烧的草地上。随后，它便以逃离新起火势的小动物为食。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Most tool-using behaviours are a means of extracting food, which may provide a clue as to how the mental abilities needed for tool use evolved. The predominant explanation is based on the proverb that ‘necessity is the mother of invention’. Essentially, brain tissue is energetically expensive, so animals should have evolved only the intellectual capabilities required to overcome the challenges they face in their environment. Consider a hypothetical duck grazing on a seemingly endless supply of grass. Being particularly intelligent will not help the duck eat more grass. In contrast, other species, such as birds of prey, live in a more challenging environment, where food may be distributed erratically, hidden from view or highly mobile. The food itself may be quite intelligent. So, if there are not enough resources to feed all individuals, then only the smartest in each generation will live and reproduce.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 大多数使用工具的行为都是获取食物的手段，这或许能提示我们：使用工具所需的心智能力是如何演化出来的。主流解释以“需要是发明之母”这句谚语为基础。简言之，脑组织耗能很高，因此动物应当只演化出克服自身环境挑战所需的智力。不妨设想一只鸭子，在看似取之不尽的草地上吃草。格外聪明并不能帮助它吃到更多草。相比之下，猛禽等其他物种生活在更具挑战的环境中，那里的食物可能分布不定、藏而不露，或移动速度极快，猎物本身也可能相当聪明。因此，如果资源不足以养活所有个体，那么每一代中只有最聪明的个体才能存活并繁殖。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: New Caledonian crows boast many different tools in their toolkit. They use a hooked tool made by removing all but one of the side branches from a twig. They fashion serrated rakes (using their beaks as scissors) from stiff, leathery pandanus leaves. They also make probes by modifying their own moulted feathers. Each tool is used in slightly different ways to pull grubs from deep within tree trunks. The crows carry their favourite tool from one foraging site to the next. They also store their tools for later reuse in a secure place on their perch. Problem-solving abilities have traditionally been thought to be beyond the reach of animals. Nevertheless, birds are coming up with innovative solutions all the time. Recently, New Caledonian crows were observed moulding a piece of wire, something they had never seen before, into a hook and then using it to retrieve food.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 新喀里多尼亚乌鸦的“工具箱”里有许多不同工具。它们会把细枝上除一根侧枝外的其余侧枝全部去掉，制成带钩工具；会用喙充当剪刀，将坚韧如革的露兜树叶制成锯齿耙；还会改造自己脱落的羽毛，做成探针。每种工具的用法略有不同，都是为了从树干深处掏出蛴螬。乌鸦会把最喜欢的工具从一个觅食点带到下一个，还会把工具存放在栖木上的安全位置，留待日后再用。传统上，人们认为动物不具备解决问题的能力。尽管如此，鸟类一直在想出创新办法。最近，人们观察到新喀里多尼亚乌鸦把一段从未见过的金属丝弯成钩子，再用它取出食物。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Literally hundreds of such reports have accumulated in back copies of scientific journals. Recently, a team of biologists from McGill University in Canada collated them and compared the frequency and size of innovations with the size of the birds’ forebrain (the brain area responsible for higher-order information processing) relative to the hindbrain. The team uncovered a clear relationship: birds with relatively large forebrains are able to invent fresh solutions to ecological challenges, and to exploit the discoveries and inventions of others, more often than birds with relatively small forebrains.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: What better way to exercise a political brain than to be deceitful! Perhaps the best example of deception among birds comes from the white-winged choughs. Choughs are cooperative breeders – that is, they form a communal group consisting of one breeding pair and up to 15 non-breeding ‘helpers’. However, because young choughs have so little enthusiasm for foraging, or gathering food, they are often too hungry to help. And because it is socially unacceptable to be part of a group and provide little help, young choughs often act deceptively. For example, when an adult is watching, a young chough will place some food in the mouth of a hungry chick but not release it. Instead, it waits until the adult departs and then eats the food itself. A chough can also help the group by preening the chicks. Interestingly, it is more likely to preen the chicks if another bird can see it do so. A chough that has been sitting totally still on the nest while the rest of the group is foraging out of sight will comically spring up and frantically start to preen the chicks as soon as some of its group members come into view. It is likely that these young choughs are only motivated to help when others are watching because they are concerned about their social status. Choughs need other choughs to like them, as they cannot breed without them.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It all began in 1958 with a phone call from Louis Engel, a banker at Merrill Lynch, a US-based financial management company, who wanted to know how investors in shares had performed relative to investors in other assets such as low-risk investments with guaranteed returns. ‘I don’t know, but if you gave me $50,000 I could find out,’ replied Jim Lorie, a dean at the University of Chicago’s business school. Louis Engel soon agreed to provide the funding, and more. The result, in 1960, was the launch of the University’s Center for Research in Security Prices. Half a century later CRSP (pronounced ‘crisp’) data are everywhere. They provided the foundation of at least one-third of all empirical research in finance over the past 40 years, according to a presentation at a symposium held this month. They probably influenced much of the rest.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 一切始于1958年的一通电话。美国金融管理公司美林的银行家 Louis Engel 想知道，与投资有回报保障的低风险资产等其他资产的人相比，股票投资者的表现如何。芝加哥大学商学院院长 Jim Lorie 回答：“我不知道，但如果你给我5万美元，我就能查明。”Louis Engel 很快同意提供这笔资金，而且还不止这些。于是，1960年，该校成立了证券价格研究中心。半个世纪后，CRSP的数据无处不在。CRSP读作“crisp”。据本月一场研讨会上的报告称，过去40年至少三分之一的金融实证研究都以这些数据为基础，而其余研究很可能也大多受到它们影响。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Getting the CRSP data together was a tough process in what were then the early days of computers. Up to three million pieces of information on all the shares traded on the New York Stock Exchange between 1926 and 1960 were transferred from paper in the exchange’s archive to magnetic tape. A lot of time was spent adjusting prices to take account of complexities in the market. Lorie and his co-researcher, Lawrence Fisher, chose January 1926 as the start date because they wanted the data to span at least one complete business cycle from boom to bust, or vice versa.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在当时计算机尚处于早期发展阶段的情况下，汇集CRSP数据是一个艰难的过程。纽约证券交易所档案中，1926年至1960年所有交易股票的资料多达300万项，它们从纸张转录到磁带上。研究人员还花费大量时间调整价格，以计入市场中的种种复杂因素。Lorie 和共同研究者 Lawrence Fisher 选择1926年1月作为起始日期，是因为他们希望数据至少涵盖一个从繁荣到萧条，或反向变化的完整商业周期。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: When these two economists published the first study based on the CRSP data in 1964, they reported that the annual compound return on the shares over the entire 35-year period was (depending on the tax status of the investor) between 6.8% and 9%. Acknowledging that good data on the performance of other assets were not available, the study claimed that the rate of return on shares was ‘substantially higher than for alternative investment media’, providing the first empirical support for the still-popular idea that shares outperform other investments over the long run. Fisher and Lorie also observed that many people chose to invest in assets with lower returns because they were cautious by nature and were concerned about the risk of loss inherent in investing in the stock market. Economists today call the amount of extra return that investors need to compensate them for this additional risk the ‘equity risk premium’, although they differ greatly on how big investors should expect it to be.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 1964年，这两位经济学家发表第一项以CRSP数据为基础的研究时报告称，在完整的35年期间，股票的年复合收益率介于6.8%至9%之间，具体取决于投资者的税务状况。研究承认，当时没有关于其他资产表现的优质数据，但仍声称股票收益率“远高于其他投资工具”，从而首次以实证证据支持了如今依然流行的观点：从长期看，股票的表现优于其他投资。Fisher 和 Lorie 还观察到，许多人天性谨慎，担心投资股市固有的亏损风险，因而选择收益较低的资产。如今，经济学家把投资者为补偿这项额外风险而要求获得的额外收益称为“股权风险溢价”，不过对于投资者应预期它有多大，他们的看法差异很大。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: After Fisher and Lorie’s 1964 report there was no stopping the love affair between financial economists and the data that studying these numbers produced. Myron Scholes, now a Nobel laureate, became director of CRSP in 1974, and ensured the database was both kept up to date and made readily available to academic economists everywhere. In turn, this resource became ever more useful as computing power became more affordable. The CRSP database has since been expanded to include a full range of different types of investments. It has been replicated across the world.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Fisher 和 Lorie 的1964年报告发表后，金融经济学家开始对分析这些数字所能得到的数据着迷，此后这股研究热情一发不可收拾。后来获得诺贝尔奖的 Myron Scholes 于1974年出任CRSP主任，并确保数据库不断更新，也方便世界各地的学术经济学家使用。随着计算成本下降，这项资源也变得越来越有用。此后，CRSP数据库已扩展到涵盖各种投资类型，世界各地也建立了类似的数据库。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One of the earliest uses of CRSP data was by Eugene Fama, an economist at the University of Chicago, to support his ‘efficient-market hypothesis’. He found that over a lengthy period share prices tended to rise and fall randomly, without showing much of a pattern. Markets are efficient, he said, because all relevant information is reflected in share prices at any given moment, meaning there are no predictable movements in prices for smart investors to exploit. Fama did concede that there was some evidence of temporary short-term predictability in share prices, however. That stipulation has resulted in a vast number of papers based on discovering such ‘variations’ through data mining. In theory, such anomalies are potentially lucrative for investors, but as believers in efficient markets observe with satisfaction, it seems that no sooner are such anomalies discovered and reported in journals than they typically disappear.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: CRSP数据最早的用途之一，是芝加哥大学经济学家 Eugene Fama 用它来支持自己的“有效市场假说”。他发现，在很长一段时期内，股票价格往往随机涨跌，几乎不呈现固定规律。他说，市场之所以有效，是因为任何时刻的股价都反映了所有相关信息，这意味着不存在可供聪明投资者利用的、能够预测的价格走势。不过，Fama 确实承认，有些证据表明股价在短期内暂时具有可预测性。这项限定引出了大量论文，它们通过数据挖掘来发现这类“变动规律”。理论上，这类异常现象可能让投资者获利；但令有效市场的信奉者满意的是，此类异常似乎通常刚被发现并在期刊上报道，便会消失。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: However, the sheer volume of material means that financial economists are becoming increasingly specialised, which may have costs as well as benefits. Some economists worry that much of this statistical analysis is creating some interference that drowns out serious thinking about the big questions, such as why the financial system nearly collapsed in 2008 and how a repeat can be avoided. Robert Shiller, an economist at Yale University and a long-time sceptic about the efficient-market hypothesis, feels that with the creation of the CRSP database economists suddenly believed that finance had become scientific. According to Shiller, conventional ideas about investing and financial markets – and about their vulnerabilities – seemed out of date to the new empiricists. He worries that academic departments are full of economists who are so specialised in data analysis that they fail to see and understand the whole. They get a sense of authority from work that contains lots of data. To have seen the 2008 global financial crisis coming, he argues, it would have been better to ‘go back to old-fashioned readings of history, studying institutions and laws. We should have talked to grandpa.’

source.text: Jellyfish – The Dominant Species

translation.text: 水母：占据主导的物种

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Jellyfish have become the curse of beach holidays, permeating every ocean on the globe, thriving in the Arctic and the tropics. In an ever-changing world where other species struggle to endure, jellyfish populations are on the rise. To the untrained eye, these creatures drift aimlessly on the oceans’ currents and appear benign. In addition, they lack sharp claws, piercing teeth or even a brain. Despite this, they are armed with an amazing arsenal of weapons, especially the stinging power of their tentacles. As a result, jellyfish are among the most-feared, least-understood creatures in the seas.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 水母已经成为海滨度假的祸患。它们遍布全球每一片海洋，从北极到热带都能繁盛生长。在这个不断变化、其他物种艰难求生的世界里，水母数量却在上升。 在没有受过训练的人看来，这些生物随洋流漫无目的地漂浮，似乎并无危害。况且，它们既没有锋利的爪子、尖锐的牙齿，甚至连大脑都没有。尽管如此，它们却配备了一整套惊人的武器，尤其是触手的蜇刺能力。因此，水母既是海洋中最令人畏惧的生物之一，也是最不为人了解的生物之一。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: According to Dr Monty Graham, a jellyfish scientist at the University of South Alabama, US, ‘Jellyfish are a pretty good group of animals to track coastal ecosystems. When you start to see jellyfish numbers grow, that usually indicates a stressed system.’ While populations appear to be down this year, Dr Graham sees ‘a statistically solid increase’ over the longer term. This increase first gained attention in the 1980s when a huge number of jellyfish, Atlantic Ocean natives named Mnemiopsis leidyi, devastated the Black Sea, an ecosystem already weakened by overfishing of anchovies. Scientists believe that this species of jellyfish came in on the bottom of a ship and then rapidly multiplied, feeding on anchovy eggs and the plankton that young fish rely on.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 美国南阿拉巴马大学水母科学家 Monty Graham 博士说：“水母是追踪沿海生态系统状况的一类很好的动物。当你开始看到水母数量增加时，通常说明这个系统正承受压力。”虽然今年水母数量似乎有所下降，但从更长时期来看，Graham 博士看到了“统计学上可靠的增长”。 这种增长最早在20世纪80年代引起关注。当时，大量名为 Mnemiopsis leidyi、原产大西洋的栉水母重创了黑海，而过度捕捞鳀鱼早已削弱了当地生态系统。科学家认为，这种栉水母随船底进入黑海，随后迅速繁殖，以鳀鱼卵和幼鱼赖以为生的浮游生物为食。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Dense jellyfish aggregations can be a natural feature of healthy ocean ecosystems, but a clear picture is now emerging of more severe and frequent jellyfish outbreaks worldwide. Dr Anthony Richardson, from the University of Queensland, Australia, explains that once jellyfish gain a foothold, if conditions are right, they can establish a massive population at the expense of other ocean life. The problem is that parts of the ocean might switch from being dominated by fish to being dominated by jellyfish.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 水母密集聚集本来可以是健康海洋生态系统的自然特征，但如今一幅清晰的图景正在显现：世界各地水母暴发的严重程度和频率都在上升。澳大利亚昆士兰大学的 Anthony Richardson 博士解释说，一旦水母站稳脚跟，只要条件适宜，它们就能以牺牲其他海洋生物为代价，建立起庞大种群。问题在于，部分海域可能从由鱼类占主导，转变为由水母占主导。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A study done by Richardson and his colleagues explores the causes behind jellyfish infestation, and the need for swift, decisive action to stem the jellyfish takeover. Jellyfish outbreaks are linked directly to human actions, including overfishing, the input of fertilizer and sewage into the ocean, and climate change. Overfishing has removed fish from marine ecosystems at astounding rates. According to Richardson, this has made it possible for jellyfish to take their place. ‘This is because small fish appear to keep jellyfish in check by predation (on jellyfish when they are very small) and competition (when feeding). So, once we remove fish, jellyfish can proliferate.’ Eutrophication is another human-caused change in the ocean that has likely contributed to jellyfish explosions. Eutrophication is an increase in nitrogen and phosphorus in the ocean, largely caused by fertilizer and waste run-off. This leads to algae blooms, which lower oxygen in the marine ecosystem, creating so-called ‘dead zones’, which have been increasing dramatically around the world. According to Richardson, these low-oxygen waters give jellyfish the advantage. ‘Fish avoid low-oxygen waters but jellyfish, having lower oxygen demands, not only survive but can thrive in these conditions as there is less predation and competition from fish.’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Richardson 及其同事开展的一项研究，探讨了水母泛滥背后的原因，以及迅速采取果断行动遏制水母接管海洋的必要性。水母暴发与人类活动直接相关，包括过度捕捞、化肥和污水排入海洋，以及气候变化。 过度捕捞正以惊人的速度把鱼类从海洋生态系统中清除。Richardson 说，这使水母有可能取代鱼类的位置。“这是因为小鱼似乎会通过捕食和竞争来抑制水母：水母很小时，小鱼会捕食它们；进食时，两者会相互竞争。所以，一旦我们把鱼类清除，水母就会大量繁殖。” 富营养化是人类造成的另一种海洋变化，很可能也助长了水母数量激增。富营养化是指海洋中氮和磷增加，主要由化肥和废弃物流失所致。它会造成藻华，降低海洋生态系统中的含氧量，形成所谓的“死亡区”；世界各地的这类区域正在急剧增加。Richardson 说，这些低氧水域让水母占据优势。“鱼类会避开低氧水域，水母所需氧气较少，却不仅能够存活，还能在这种环境中繁盛，因为来自鱼类的捕食和竞争都减少了。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Once jellyfish appear en masse in an ecosystem, they can make it very difficult for fish to stage a comeback. By feeding on fish, the jellyfish successfully prevent fish from returning to their normal population numbers, says Richardson. ‘One can thus think of two alternate states with each being stable: one dominated by fish and the other by jellyfish. Unfortunately, where there is a jellyfish-dominated state then this does not support the nutritional needs of other fish, marine mammals, and seabirds.’ In other words, an ecosystem that loses fish also loses the species that depend on fish for survival. This state has been defined as a ‘monoculture of jellyfish’, an apt analogy since the situation shares similarities with other monocultures. When the rich biodiversity of tropical forests is replaced by plantations growing a single species of tree, an area of rich variety becomes a desert in terms of biodiversity, as do ocean ecosystems when jellyfish become the dominant species. One result of large jellyfish populations is the economic effect it has had on the fishing industry. In the Gulf of Mexico, shrimp fishermen are struggling with a jellyfish boom that fills nets, causing them to break and resulting in millions of dollars in losses.

translation.text: 热带森林丰富的生物多样性若被只种植单一树种的种植园取代，一个物种丰富的地区便会沦为生物多样性意义上的荒漠；水母成为主导物种时，海洋生态系统也会如此。

source.text: One result of large jellyfish populations is the economic effect it has had on the fishing industry.

translation.text: 水母种群庞大造成的一个后果，是给渔业带来经济影响。

source.text: In the Gulf of Mexico, shrimp fishermen are struggling with a jellyfish boom that fills nets, causing them to break and resulting in millions of dollars in losses.

translation.text: 在墨西哥湾，虾类渔民正为水母激增而苦恼：水母塞满渔网，导致渔网破裂，造成数百万美元损失。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Experts say that a greater understanding of jellyfish, including their ideal water temperature and feeding habits, is necessary to determine with certainty what is causing the recent massive invasion and to come up with ways to combat it. Due to the difficulty of turning ecosystems around once jellyfish have become dominant, Richardson and his colleagues propose focusing on ‘prevention rather than cure’. They recommend a halt to overfishing small fish that are vital to keeping jellyfish in check, reducing the amount of fertilizer and sewage running off into the oceans, and finally, if possible, confronting climate change.

source.text: Keeping the water away

translation.text: 让洪水远离

source.text: New approaches to flood control

translation.text: 防洪新方法

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Recently, winter floods on the rivers of central Europe have been among the worst for 600 to 700 years, and dams and dykes (protective sea walls) have failed to solve the problem. Traditionally, river engineers have tried to get rid of the water quickly, draining it off the land and down to the sea in rivers reengineered as high-performance drains. But however high they build the artificial riverbanks, the floods keep coming back. And when they come, they seem to be worse than ever.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 近来，中欧河流的冬季洪水达到600至700年来最严重的程度之一，水坝和防护性堤坝都未能解决问题。传统上，河流工程师设法迅速排走洪水：让水离开陆地，并通过改造成高效排水渠的河道流入大海。然而，无论人工河岸筑得多高，洪水都会卷土重来；而且每次来袭，似乎都比以往更严重。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Engineers are now turning to a different plan: to sap the water’s destructive strength by dispersing it into fields, forgotten lakes and flood plains. They are reviving river bends and marshes to curb the flow, and even plugging city drains to encourage floodwater to use other means to go underground. Back in the days when rivers took a winding path to the sea, floodwaters lost force and volume while meandering across flood plains and inland deltas, but today the water tends to have a direct passage to the sea. This means that, when it rains in the uplands, the water comes down all at once.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 如今，工程师转而采用另一种方案：把水分散到田野、被遗忘的湖泊和洪泛平原中，削弱其破坏力。他们正在恢复河流弯道和沼泽，以减缓水流，甚至堵住城市排水管，让洪水通过其他途径渗入地下。过去，河流蜿蜒入海，洪水迂回穿过洪泛平原和内陆三角洲时，会失去力量并减少水量；如今，水流往往直达大海。这意味着高地一下雨，水就会同时倾泻而下。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Worse, when the flood plains are closed off, the river’s flow downstream becomes more violent and uncontrollable; by turning complex river systems into the simple mechanics of a water pipe, engineers have often created danger where they promised safety. The Rhine, Europe’s most engineered river, is a good example. For a long time engineers have erased its backwaters and cut it off from its plain. The aim was partly to improve navigation, and partly to speed floodwaters out of the Alps and down to the North Sea. Now, when it rains in the Alps, the peak flows from several branches of the Rhine coincide where once they arrived separately, and with four-fifths of the Lower Rhine’s flood plain barricaded off, the waters rise. The result is more frequent flooding and greater damage. The same thing has happened in the US on the Mississippi River, which drains the world’s second-largest river catchment into the Gulf of Mexico. Despite some $7 billion spent over the last century on levees (embankments), the situation is growing worse.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 更糟的是，洪泛平原一旦被隔绝，河流下游的水势就会变得更加猛烈而失控。工程师把复杂的河流系统变成水管般简单的机械通道，常常在承诺安全之处反而制造了危险。欧洲受人工改造最多的河流莱茵河就是一个典型例子。长期以来，工程师不断消除它的回水区，并切断它与洪泛平原的联系；目的部分是改善航运，部分是让洪水更快流出阿尔卑斯山，奔向北海。如今，阿尔卑斯山一下雨，莱茵河数条支流的洪峰会在同一时间汇合，而过去它们是先后抵达的；再加上下莱茵河五分之四的洪泛平原被堤坝隔离，水位便会上涨，结果是洪水更频繁、破坏更严重。同样的情况也发生在美国密西西比河。它把世界第二大河流集水区的水排入墨西哥湾；尽管过去一个世纪投入约70亿美元修建防洪堤，情况仍在恶化。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Specialists in water control now say that a new approach is needed — one which takes the whole landscape into consideration. To help keep London’s feet dry, the UK Environment Agency is reflooding 10 square kilometres of the ancient flood plain of the River Thames outside Oxford. Nearer to London, it has spent £100 million creating new wetlands and a relief channel across 16 kilometres of flood plain. Similar ideas are being tested in Austria, in one of Europe’s largest river restorations to date. The engineers calculate that the restored flood plain of the Drava River can now store up to 10 million cubic metres of floodwater, and slow down storm surges coming out of the Alps by more than an hour, protecting towns not only in Austria, but as far downstream as Slovenia and Croatia.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 如今，水利专家表示，需要一种把整个地貌纳入考虑的新方法。为帮助伦敦免遭水患，英国环境署正让牛津城外泰晤士河古老洪泛平原中的10平方公里区域重新蓄水。在更靠近伦敦的地方，该署投入1亿英镑，在16公里长的洪泛平原上建造新的湿地和分洪河道。奥地利也在试验类似构想，实施欧洲迄今规模最大的河流修复工程之一。工程师计算得出，修复后的德拉瓦河洪泛平原如今最多可储存1,000万立方米洪水，并使来自阿尔卑斯山的暴雨洪峰延迟一个多小时，不仅保护奥地利的城镇，也保护下游远至斯洛文尼亚和克罗地亚的城镇。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The Dutch, for whom preventing floods is a matter of survival, have gone furthest. This nation, built largely on drained marshes and seabed, has had several severe shocks in the last two decades, when very large numbers of people have had to be evacuated. Since that time, the Dutch have broken one of their most enduring national stereotypes by allowing engineers to punch holes in dykes. They plan to return up to a sixth of the country to its former waterlogged state in order to better protect the rest.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 对荷兰人来说，防洪关乎生存，因此他们走得最远。这个国家大部分建在排干的沼泽和海床上，过去20年里曾遭受数次严重冲击，大量居民不得不撤离。自那以后，荷兰人打破了本国一种根深蒂固的典型形象，允许工程师在堤坝上开洞。他们计划让全国最多六分之一的土地恢复到从前的水涝状态，以便更好地保护其余地区。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Water use in cities also needs to change. At the moment, cities seem to create floods; they are concreted and paved so that rains flow quickly into rivers. A new breed of ‘soft engineers’ wants cities to be porous; Berlin is one place where this is being done. Tough new rules for new developments mean that drains will be prevented from becoming overloaded after heavy rains. Architects of new urban buildings are diverting rainwater from the roofs for use in toilets and the irrigation of roof gardens, while water falling onto the ground is collected in ponds, or passes underground through porous paving. One high-tech urban development can store a sixth of its annual rainfall, and reuse most of the rest.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 城市用水方式也需要改变。目前，城市似乎会制造洪水：地面由混凝土和铺装材料覆盖，雨水因而迅速流入河流。新一代“软工程师”希望城市能够透水，柏林便是正在实践这一构想的地方。针对新开发项目的严格新规意味着，暴雨过后排水系统不会再超负荷。新建城市建筑的设计师把屋顶雨水引去冲洗厕所、灌溉屋顶花园；落到地面的水则汇入池塘，或穿过透水铺装渗入地下。一个高科技城市开发区可以储存其全年降雨量的六分之一，并重新利用其余雨水中的大部分。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Could this be expanded to protect a whole city? The test case could be Los Angeles. With non-porous surfaces covering 70% of the city, drainage is a huge challenge. Billions of dollars have been spent digging huge drains and concreting riverbeds, but many communities still flood regularly. Meanwhile, this desert city ships water from hundreds of kilometres away to fill its taps and swimming pool. Los Angeles has recently launched a new scheme to utilise floodwater in the Sun Valley section of the city. The plan is to catch the rain that falls on thousands of driveways, parking lots and rooftops in the valley. Trees will soak up water from parking lots; houses and public buildings will capture roof water to irrigate gardens and parks, and road drains will empty into old gravel pits to recharge the city’s underground water reserves. Result: less flooding and more water for the city. It may sound expensive, until we realise how much is spent trying to drain cities and protect areas from flooding, and how little this method achieves.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这种做法能否扩大到保护整座城市？洛杉矶可能成为试验案例。城市70%的面积由不透水表面覆盖，排水是一项巨大挑战。人们已经花费数十亿美元开挖巨型排水渠，并用混凝土铺设河床，但许多社区仍经常发生洪灾。与此同时，这座沙漠城市从数百公里外调水，供水龙头和游泳池使用。最近，洛杉矶启动了一项新计划，要在市内太阳谷地区利用洪水。计划将收集谷地数千条车道、停车场和屋顶上的降雨。树木会吸收停车场的积水；住宅和公共建筑将收集屋顶雨水来灌溉花园和公园；道路排水管则会把水排入废弃砾石坑，补充城市地下水储备。结果是洪灾减少，城市可用水增加。这个方案听来或许昂贵，但只要想到为了给城市排水、防止各地受淹，人们投入了多少钱，而这种传统方法成效又多么有限，就不会这样认为了。

translation.text: 树木会吸收停车场的积水；住宅和公共建筑将收集屋顶雨水来灌溉花园和公园；道路排水管则会把水排入废弃砾石坑，补充城市地下水储备。

source.text: Result: less flooding and more water for the city.

translation.text: 结果是洪灾减少，城市可用水增加。

source.text: It may sound expensive, until we realise how much is spent trying to drain cities and protect areas from flooding, and how little this method achieves.

translation.text: 这个方案听来或许昂贵，但只要想到为了给城市排水、防止各地受淹，人们投入了多少钱，而这种传统方法成效又多么有限，就不会这样认为了。

source.text: How an ancient building material is influencing modern construction

translation.text: 一种古代建筑材料如何影响现代建造业

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In a quest to make concrete more durable and sustainable, an international team of geologists and engineers has found inspiration in the concrete used by the ancient Romans. The chemical secrets of Roman concrete have been uncovered in samples taken from a concrete Roman breakwater. A breakwater is a barrier that is built out into the sea to protect coasts and harbors from the force of waves. This particular breakwater has spent the last 2,000 years submerged in seawater. The international team of researchers that collected the samples was led by Paulo Monteiro, a professor of civil and environmental engineering at the University of California, Berkeley. Analysis of samples from the ancient underwater site in Pozzuoli Bay near Naples in Italy pinpointed why the best Roman concrete was superior to most modern concrete.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 为了制造更耐久、更可持续的混凝土，一支由地质学家和工程师组成的国际团队从古罗马人使用的混凝土中获得了灵感。研究人员从一座罗马混凝土防波堤采集样本，揭开了罗马混凝土的化学奥秘。防波堤是一道伸入海中、保护海岸和港口免受海浪冲击的屏障。这座防波堤已经在海水中浸泡了2,000年。采集样本的国际研究团队由加州大学伯克利分校土木与环境工程教授 Paulo Monteiro 带领。通过分析意大利那不勒斯附近波佐利湾古代水下遗址的样本，团队明确了最佳罗马混凝土优于大多数现代混凝土的原因。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Concrete was the Roman Empire’s construction material of choice. It was used in land monuments such as the Pantheon in Rome, as well as in underwater and partially underwater coastal and harbor structures. Monteiro and his team were particularly interested in how the coastal and harbor structures endured the unforgiving saltwater environment. Chemical analysis of Roman concrete showed that it differs from the modern kind in several ways. One is the content of the cement that binds the material in the concrete. The most commonly used cement in recent decades has been Portland cement. Portland cement is a compound of calcium, silicates, and hydrates (C-S-H). However, analysis of Roman concrete shows that it contains a significantly different cement. Roman cement contains aluminum, which is not found in Portland cement, and less silicon than is found in Portland cement. The resulting calcium-aluminum-silicate-hydrate (C-A-S-H) is an exceptionally stable cement.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 混凝土是罗马帝国首选的建筑材料。它既用于罗马万神殿等陆上纪念建筑，也用于水下或部分位于水下的海岸和港口设施。Monteiro 及其团队特别想知道，这些海岸和港口设施如何经受住严酷的海水环境。化学分析表明，罗马混凝土与现代混凝土在几个方面有所不同，其中之一是黏合混凝土中各种材料的水泥成分。近几十年来最常用的是波特兰水泥，它是一种由钙、硅酸盐和水合物组成的化合物，即C-S-H。然而，对罗马混凝土的分析表明，它所含的水泥明显不同。罗马水泥含有波特兰水泥没有的铝，而且含硅量低于波特兰水泥，由此形成的钙铝硅酸盐水合物，即C-A-S-H，是一种极为稳定的水泥。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The recipe for the contents of Roman concrete was first described around 30 BC by Vitruvius, an engineer for the Roman Emperor Augustus. Volcanic ash was one of the ingredients, and it is now understood that this is crucial, as it is volcanic ash that contains the aluminum that ultimately gives Roman concrete its great durability. The Romans devised an efficient method of making concrete for coastal structures. They combined volcanic ash with lime, which added the calcium to the mix. This was then packed, together with stones and chunks of rock, into wooden molds, which were then immersed in seawater. The seawater instantly triggered a hot chemical reaction. The lime was hydrated by the seawater, which means that it incorporated water molecules into its structure, and reacted with the volcanic ash to cement the whole mixture together. This reaction formed the concrete that was used to build some of the most enduring structures in Western civilization.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 公元前30年前后，罗马皇帝奥古斯都的工程师维特鲁威首次记述了罗马混凝土的配方。火山灰是其中一种原料；如今人们知道，这一点至关重要，因为火山灰中含有铝，而铝最终赋予罗马混凝土极强的耐久性。罗马人设计了一种高效制造海岸设施混凝土的方法。他们把火山灰与石灰混合，由石灰向混合物中添加钙；再把混合物连同石块和岩石碎块装进木模，浸入海水。海水会立刻触发炽热的化学反应。海水使石灰水合，也就是让石灰把水分子纳入自身结构；石灰随后与火山灰反应，把整个混合物胶结在一起。这个反应形成的混凝土，被用于建造西方文明中一些最为经久不衰的设施。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: According to Marie Jackson, a member of the research team, Roman concrete is one of the most durable construction materials on the planet, and that was no accident. Shipping was the lifeline of political, economic, and military stability for the Roman Empire, so constructing harbors that would last was critical. ‘Over time, the Romans used less and less concrete.’ ‘As the Roman Empire declined, and shipping declined, the need for the seawater concrete declined,’ said Jackson. ‘You could also argue that the original structures were built so well that, once they were in place, they didn’t need to be replaced,’ she added.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 研究团队成员 Marie Jackson 说，罗马混凝土是地球上最耐久的建筑材料之一，而这并非偶然。航运是维系罗马帝国政治、经济和军事稳定的生命线，因此建造经久耐用的港口至关重要。Jackson 说：“随着时间推移，罗马人使用的混凝土越来越少。罗马帝国衰落、航运减少后，对海水混凝土的需求也随之下降。”她补充说：“你也可以认为，最初的设施建得实在太好，一经建成便无须更换。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Producing Roman concrete also left a smaller carbon footprint than its modern counterpart. ‘It’s not that modern concrete isn’t good—it’s so good we use 19 billion tons of it a year,’ says Monteiro. ‘The problem is that manufacturing Portland cement accounts for seven percent of the carbon dioxide that industry puts into the air.’ Portland cement holds most modern concrete together. However, making Portland cement releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere from burning fuel in order to heat a mix of limestone and clays to 1,450 degrees Celsius. The production of Roman concrete, however, was much cleaner, as less heat was needed. A temperature that was a third lower than that required for making Portland cement was sufficient for making Roman concrete.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 生产罗马混凝土所留下的碳足迹也小于现代混凝土。Monteiro 说：“并不是现代混凝土不好；它太好用了，所以我们每年要使用190亿吨。问题在于，制造波特兰水泥产生的二氧化碳占工业排放到空气中的二氧化碳总量的7%。”大多数现代混凝土都靠波特兰水泥黏合。然而，制造波特兰水泥时，需要燃烧燃料，把石灰石和黏土的混合物加热到1,450摄氏度，这会向大气释放二氧化碳。相比之下，生产罗马混凝土要清洁得多，因为所需热量较少；比制造波特兰水泥所需温度低三分之一，就足以制造罗马混凝土。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Some modern concrete no longer contains Portland cement; instead, fly ash is used, which causes fewer greenhouse gas emissions. Fly ash is a waste product from burning coal, and the researchers are investigating whether volcanic ash would be a good, large-volume replacement in countries that cannot access fly ash easily. ‘There is not enough fly ash in this world to replace half of the Portland cement being used,’ said Monteiro. ‘Many countries don’t have fly ash, so the idea is to find alternative local materials that will work, including the kind of volcanic ash that Romans used. Using these alternatives could replace 40 percent of the world’s demand for Portland cement.’

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Cutting greenhouse gas emissions is one powerful incentive for finding a better way to provide the concrete the world needs; another is the need for stronger, longer-lasting buildings, bridges, and other structures. ‘In the middle 20th century, concrete structures were designed to last 50 years, and a lot of them are on borrowed time,’ Monteiro says. ‘Now we design buildings to last 100 to 120 years.’ Yet Roman harbor installations have survived 2,000 years of chemical attack from seawater and wave action. Stronger, longer-lasting modern concrete may be the legacy of a deeper understanding of how the Romans made their incomparable concrete.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 减少温室气体排放，是寻找更好方式来供应全球所需混凝土的一项强大动力；另一项动力，则是建造更坚固、更长寿的楼宇、桥梁和其他设施。Monteiro 说：“20世纪中叶，混凝土结构的设计寿命是50年，其中许多如今都在勉强超期服役。现在，我们把建筑的设计寿命定为100至120年。”然而，罗马港口设施经受海水化学侵蚀和海浪冲击已有2,000年。更深入地理解罗马人如何制造出无与伦比的混凝土，或许会为后世留下更坚固、更耐久的现代混凝土。

source.text: What led to the disappearance of the giant mammals?

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Although it’s hard to imagine in this age of urban sprawl and automobiles, North America once belonged to huge, elephant-like mammoths, camels, bear-sized beavers and other giant beasts, collectively known as ‘megafauna’. Some 11,000 years ago, however, these large-bodied mammals—about 70 species in all—disappeared. Their demise coincided roughly with the arrival of humans on the continent and dramatic climate change—factors that have inspired several theories about the die-off. blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The third explanation for what brought on this North American extinction does not involve human beings. Instead, its proponents blame the loss on the climate. The Pleistocene epoch in question witnessed considerable climate instability, explains Russell W. Graham of the Denver Museum of Nature and Science. As a result, their regular habitats disappeared, and species that had once formed communities split apart. For some animals, this brought opportunity. For much of the megafauna, however, the increasingly uniform terrain left them with shrinking geographical ranges—a death sentence for large animals, which need correspondingly large ranges. Although these creatures managed to maintain viable populations through most of the Pleistocene period, the final major climate fluctuation pushed them over the edge, Graham says.

translation.text: 脑中音乐

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Scientists investigate ‘earworms’, the music we can’t get out of our heads
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 科学家研究挥之不去的音乐——“耳虫”

source.text: Scientists investigate ‘earworms’, the music we can’t get out of our heads

translation.text: 科学家研究挥之不去的音乐——“耳虫”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Ever had a song stuck in your head, playing on an endless loop? Scientists call them ‘involuntary musical images’, or ‘earworms’, and a wave of new research is shining light on why they occur and what can be learned from them. Some neuroscientists and cognitive psychologists are studying earworms to explore the mysteries of memory and the part of the brain that is beyond our conscious control. ‘The idea that we have full control over our thought processes is an illusion,’ says psychologist Lauren Stewart, who founded the master’s program in music, mind and brain at Goldsmiths, University of London, UK, where recent research has taken place. Researchers haven’t been able to watch what happens in the brain when earworms occur, because they happen unpredictably. Much of what is known about them comes from surveys, questionnaires, diaries and lab experiments.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 你是否遇到过一首歌卡在脑中，无休止地循环播放？科学家称之为“不自主音乐意象”，也叫“耳虫”。一系列新研究正在揭示它们为何出现，以及我们可以从中了解到什么。有些神经科学家和认知心理学家正在研究耳虫，以探索记忆的奥秘，以及大脑中不受意识控制的部分。心理学家 Lauren Stewart 说：“我们以为自己能完全控制思维过程，其实这是一种错觉。”她在英国伦敦大学金匠学院创办了“音乐、心智与大脑”硕士项目，近期研究也在那里进行。研究人员还无法直接观察耳虫出现时大脑中发生了什么，因为它们来得无法预测。现有的大部分相关知识都来自调查、问卷、日记和实验室实验。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A Goldsmiths study published in the journal Memory and Cognition this year showed that the singing we hear in our heads tends to be true to actual recordings. Researchers had 17 volunteers tap to the beat of any earworm they heard during a four-day period while a device attached to their wrist recorded their movements. The tapping tempos were within 10% of the tempos of the original recordings. Another Goldsmiths study, published this year in Consciousness and Cognition, found that people who report hearing earworms often, and find them most intrusive, have slightly different brain structures, with more gray matter in areas associated with processing emotions.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 金匠学院今年在《记忆与认知》期刊发表的一项研究显示，我们脑中听到的歌声往往忠实于实际录音。研究人员让17名志愿者在4天内每当听到耳虫，就按其节拍敲击；绑在他们手腕上的设备会记录动作。敲击速度与原始录音的速度相差不超过10%。金匠学院今年在《意识与认知》发表的另一项研究发现，那些自称经常听到耳虫、并认为耳虫最具侵扰性的人，大脑结构略有不同：与处理情绪有关的区域中，灰质更多。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Studies also show that the music in our heads often starts playing during times of ‘low cognitive load’, such as while showering, getting dressed, walking, or doing chores. Dr Stewart likens earworms to ‘sonic screen savers’ that keep the mind entertained while it is otherwise unoccupied. She and her colleagues tested that theory by having volunteers listen to songs and giving them various tasks afterwards. The volunteers who sat idly for the next five minutes were the most likely to report hearing the music in their heads. Dr Stewart observed that the more challenging the activity, the less likely the volunteers were to hear the music. Diary studies also show songs tend to match people’s moods and therefore they are not random. If you are energized and upbeat, an earworm that occurs is likely to be uptempo too.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Researchers say they can’t pinpoint a spot in the brain where earworms live. Imaging studies by Andrea Halpern at Bucknell University, in Lewisburg, USA, have shown that deliberately imagining music and actually listening to music activate many of the same neurological networks. Dr Halpern’s earlier studies showed that when subjects listened to the first few notes of familiar music, areas in the right frontal and superior temporal portions of the brain became activated, along with the supplementary motor area at the top, which is typically involved in remembering sequences. When the same subjects listened to unfamiliar music and were asked to recall it, there was activity in the left frontal portions of the brain instead.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One factor that makes some songs stick might be repetition. ‘Repetition leads to familiarity which leads to anticipation, which is satisfied by hearing the song,’ says John Seabrook, author of The Song Machine: Inside the Hit Factory, about how producers pump pop songs full of aural ‘hooks’, the punchy melodic phrases designed to target the brain and leave it wanting more. The researchers are comparing the melodic structure of 100 often mentioned songs with 100 similarly popular songs that weren’t cited as earworms, to assess the difference. Songs with earworm potential appear to share certain features: a repeating pattern of ups and downs in pitch, and irregular musical intervals.

source.text: Multi-tasking and the brain

translation.text: 多任务处理与大脑

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Do you think you're a master of multi-tasking? Think again. Unless you are one of the three percent of super-taskers in the population, research shows that your brain isn't capable of paying close attention to more than one complex task at a time. Researchers who study attention say that effective multi-tasking is beyond most of us. Psychiatrist Edward M Hallowell even describes multi-tasking as 'a mythical activity in which people believe they can perform two or more tasks simultaneously as effectively as they can perform one'.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It is true that you can check your email while eating your lunch, or listen to music while walking. But innate activities like walking, chewing, and breathing do not require you to pay attention, whereas activities such as reading, tapping out a text message, or driving a car do require attention. Why is paying attention to two things at once difficult? 'The brain can perform simultaneous tasks, but attention has capacity limitations,' says Associate Professor Paul E Dux, a cognitive neuroscientist at the University of Queensland in Australia. When you do only one thing at a time, you're better at that task than when you're doing multiple things concurrently. Take the classic multi-tasking scenario of talking on a mobile phone while driving - an ill-advised activity that many people believe they have mastered. When David Strayer, Professor of Psychology at the University of Utah in the US, and his team observed 56,000 drivers as they approached an intersection, the majority of drivers who were talking on their phone failed to stop in accordance with traffic laws. And it did not matter if the driver was using a handheld or hands-free device. Even with both eyes on the road and both hands on the wheel, drivers' performance was impaired. Strayer's research shows that performance deteriorates drastically when attention is split between tasks: more mistakes are made and it takes longer to complete each activity.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The prefrontal cortex is the brain region responsible for choosing what to pay attention to, and for coordinating inputs from other brain areas. By scanning the prefrontal cortex of people while they multi-tasked, scientists at the French Institute of Health and Medical Research in Paris (INSERM) found that when people focused on a single thing, the right and left sides of the prefrontal cortex work together. But when people attempt to perform two things at once, the sides work independently. blocks.sourceNormalizedText: To the question of whether there is a difference between the sexes, Koechlin's imaging studies uncovered no differences in the ability to switch between tasks in the prefrontal cortices of men or women. But other researchers studying real life scenarios such as finding lost keys, believe there might be some truth to the claim that women are superior multi-taskers. Women have a much better strategy for finding the keys, whereas men tend to jump to it and be far less organised and thorough. 'It's as if they don't stop to reflect and plan for a moment,' says Professor Keith Laws from the University of Hertfordshire in England. But while the ability to develop strategies for coping with the numerous tasks in everyday life could give women an advantage, 'nobody can juggle two, never mind three, "complex" tasks at the same time.'

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: However, David Strayer's research uncovered that some rare people possess extraordinary multi-tasking ability. These so-called 'super-taskers' exhibit different patterns of brain activity when multi-tasking compared to ordinary people: they show less activity in the prefrontal cortex during multi-tasking, suggesting their brains are functioning with a high level of efficiency. Strayer thinks that pilots of high-performance aircraft, high-end chefs who can cook several meals at the same time to perfection, and elite doctors in hospital emergency rooms might all be more likely to be super-taskers. 'All other things being equal, we suspect that super-taskers will rise to a top position in any occupation that places a high demand on juggling various tasks that demand attention at the same time.'

passages.title: Nanotechnology: the science of the very small

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Nanotechnology: the science of the very small
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 纳米技术：研究微小尺度的科学

source.text: Nanotechnology: the science of the very small

translation.text: 纳米技术：研究微小尺度的科学

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Nanoscience and nanotechnology have become very fashionable in recent times. Their prominence has inspired science fiction and raised a lot of hope and hype about the possibilities. But what exactly is nanotechnology? Most definitions agree that it is the manufacture of structures that measure up to 100 nanometres (nm). The diameter of an atom is typically only two or three tenths of a nanometre while that of the human hair is around 100,000 nm. Essentially, we are now able to build new structures from atoms and molecules as if we were using the bricks of a children’s construction toy.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 近来，纳米科学和纳米技术变得十分时髦。它们备受瞩目，激发了科幻创作，也让人们对各种可能性既满怀希望，又大肆炒作。但纳米技术究竟是什么？大多数定义都认同，它是制造尺寸不超过100纳米的结构。一枚原子的直径通常只有零点二或零点三纳米，而人类头发的直径约为100,000纳米。从本质上说，我们如今能够用原子和分子建造新结构，就像使用儿童拼搭玩具的积木一样。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Most of the electronic consumer goods that we use today contain components that measure less than 100 nm. The lasers in our CD and DVD players make use of the properties of semiconductor layers that are just a few atoms in thickness, so we clearly are in the nanotechnology age. There are many other everyday items that we take for granted that have nanoparticles in them. One of these is sunscreen. In the 1990s there were safety issues with many of the sunscreen products available, so scientists at Oxford University set about finding a solution. The product they developed uses nanoparticles of titanium dioxide that are doped with the element manganese. This product is almost transparent to the eye when spread on the skin, and it is effective for much longer than many of the traditional preparations. In this case, we see an example of nanotechnology providing a solution to an existing problem rather than opening up new product areas.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 我们今天使用的大多数消费电子产品，都含有尺寸小于100纳米的元件。CD和DVD播放机中的激光器利用了只有几个原子厚的半导体层所具有的性质，因此我们显然已经身处纳米技术时代。许多习以为常的日常用品中也含有纳米颗粒，防晒霜便是其中之一。20世纪90年代，市面上许多防晒产品存在安全问题，于是牛津大学的科学家开始寻找解决方案。他们研发的产品使用掺入锰元素的二氧化钛纳米颗粒。这种产品涂在皮肤上时，肉眼看起来几乎透明，有效时间也比许多传统制剂长得多。这个例子表明，纳米技术是在解决现有问题，而不是开辟新的产品领域。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The technique of using nanotechnology to adapt existing products can also be applied to garments, upholstery, paint, and plastics to improve their longevity. Bearing this in mind, it is interesting to ask whether nanotechnology can help with some of the world’s major current issues. The recent growth in climate change awareness calls a range of things into question. Can we use energy more effectively? Can we reduce the carbon dioxide in the atmosphere? Can we use and purify water more effectively? Can health care be improved? Nanotechnology may very well provide the solutions. There are few times in history when the application of science to improving the human condition has been so apparent.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: We are already making new types of solar cells and batteries by using our newfound ability to manipulate matter at the atomic and molecular scale. If we can capture some of the huge quantities of energy that arrive at the Earth’s surface from the Sun, and store it effectively, we can reduce the need for fossil fuel-based power stations. We are already using nanoparticles and nanoporous materials to capture harmful greenhouse gases, and we may possibly convert some of them back into fuel. There are, however, many technical problems involved, and it will be another decade or so before some of these ideas are deployed.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 我们已经利用新近获得的、在原子和分子尺度操控物质的能力，制造新型太阳能电池和蓄电池。如果能够捕获抵达地球表面的部分巨量太阳能，并加以有效储存，我们就能减少对化石燃料发电站的需求。我们已经在利用纳米颗粒和纳米多孔材料捕获有害温室气体，或许还能把其中一部分重新转化为燃料。不过，这涉及许多技术难题，其中一些构想还要约十年才能投入应用。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Water purification is increasingly challenging and many believe that water, which we take for granted, is going to become more valuable than oil. Currently we do not use water efficiently, and many industrial and food processes leave contamination in water that is potentially toxic and difficult to remove. Nanofiltration may provide the solution to these problems, and may also offer new routes to the desalination of brackish water and groundwater in some parts of the world.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Food production and processing are becoming more important as the world’s population increases. There are concerns that potentially harmful nano-products might enter the body via the gut. Such concerns are being addressed, but it is even more important to ask questions about how nanotechnology might increase the nutritious yield of food and be adapted to help preserve and package food. There is already evidence to show that it might also be helpful in the primary production of raw food materials, by way of better delivery of pesticides in the field and better extraction of protein and carbohydrates.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 随着世界人口增加，食品生产和加工变得愈发重要。人们担心，具有潜在危害的纳米产品可能会经由肠道进入人体。这些担忧正在得到应对，但更重要的是研究纳米技术能否提高食品的营养产出，以及能否经过调整来帮助保存和包装食品。已有证据显示，它还可能有助于食品原料的初级生产，方法包括在农田中更有效地施用农药，以及更有效地提取蛋白质和碳水化合物。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Healthcare is an area where the application of nanotechnology is already exceeding the expectations of ten years ago. We are now at the threshold of a new subject, ‘theranostics’, whereby nanoparticles will first deliver the diagnostic information to the clinician and then, using the same particle, deliver a form of therapy.

passages.title: New filter promises clean water for millions

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: New filter promises clean water for millions
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 新型过滤器有望为数百万人提供洁净水

source.text: New filter promises clean water for millions

translation.text: 新型过滤器有望为数百万人提供洁净水

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: An ingenious invention is set to bring clean water to developing countries, and while the science may be cutting edge, the materials are extremely down to earth.
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 一项巧妙发明即将为发展中国家带来洁净水；其科学原理或许十分前沿，所用材料却极为朴实。

source.text: An ingenious invention is set to bring clean water to developing countries, and while the science may be cutting edge, the materials are extremely down to earth.

translation.text: 一项巧妙发明即将为发展中国家带来洁净水；其科学原理或许十分前沿，所用材料却极为朴实。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A handful of clay, yesterday’s coffee grounds and some cow manure are the ingredients that could bring clean, safe drinking water to many developing countries. The simple new technology, developed by Australian National University (ANU) materials scientist and potter Tony Flynn, allows water filters to be made from commonly available materials and fired (or baked) using cow manure as the source of heat, without the need for a kiln (an oven for baking or drying pottery). The filters have been tested and shown to remove common pathogens (disease-producing organisms) including E. coli.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 一把黏土、昨天剩下的咖啡渣和一些牛粪，就是可能为许多发展中国家带来清洁、安全饮用水的原料。这项简易新技术由澳大利亚国立大学的材料科学家兼陶艺家 Tony Flynn 开发，该校英文简称为ANU。它让人们能够用随处可得的材料制造净水器，并以牛粪为热源烧制，无须使用烧制或烘干陶器的窑炉。测试表明，这些净水器能够清除包括大肠杆菌在内的常见病原体，即致病生物。

source.text: A handful of clay, yesterday’s coffee grounds and some cow manure are the ingredients that could bring clean, safe drinking water to many developing countries.

translation.text: 一把黏土、昨天剩下的咖啡渣和一些牛粪，就是可能为许多发展中国家带来清洁、安全饮用水的原料。

source.text: The simple new technology, developed by Australian National University (ANU) materials scientist and potter Tony Flynn, allows water filters to be made from commonly available materials and fired (or baked) using cow manure as the source of heat, without the need for a kiln (an oven for baking or drying pottery).

translation.text: 这项简易新技术由澳大利亚国立大学的材料科学家兼陶艺家 Tony Flynn 开发，该校英文简称为ANU。它让人们能够用随处可得的材料制造净水器，并以牛粪为热源烧制，无须使用烧制或烘干陶器的窑炉。

source.text: The filters have been tested and shown to remove common pathogens (disease-producing organisms) including E. coli.

translation.text: 测试表明，这些净水器能够清除包括大肠杆菌在内的常见病原体，即致病生物。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The invention was born out of a project involving the Manatuto community in East Timor. A charity operating there wanted to help set up a small industrial site manufacturing water filters, but initial research found the local clay to be too fine — a problem solved by the addition of organic material. While the problems of producing a working ceramic filter in East Timor were overcome, the solution was kiln-based and particular to that community’s materials and couldn’t be applied elsewhere. Flynn’s technique for manure firing, with no requirement for a kiln, has made this zero-technology approach available anywhere it is needed.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这项发明源于一个涉及东帝汶马纳图托社区的项目。在当地开展工作的一家慈善机构想帮助设立一个制造净水器的小型工业场所，但初步研究发现，当地黏土颗粒太细；加入有机材料解决了这个问题。虽然在东帝汶制造可用陶瓷过滤器的难题得以克服，但解决方案依赖窑炉，而且只适合该社区的材料，无法用于其他地方。Flynn 使用牛粪烧制的技术不需要窑炉，使这种“零技术”方法可以在任何有需要的地方使用。

source.text: The invention was born out of a project involving the Manatuto community in East Timor.

translation.text: 这项发明源于一个涉及东帝汶马纳图托社区的项目。

source.text: A charity operating there wanted to help set up a small industrial site manufacturing water filters, but initial research found the local clay to be too fine — a problem solved by the addition of organic material.

source.text: While the problems of producing a working ceramic filter in East Timor were overcome, the solution was kiln-based and particular to that community’s materials and couldn’t be applied elsewhere.

translation.text: 虽然在东帝汶制造可用陶瓷过滤器的难题得以克服，但解决方案依赖窑炉，而且只适合该社区的材料，无法用于其他地方。

source.text: Flynn’s technique for manure firing, with no requirement for a kiln, has made this zero-technology approach available anywhere it is needed.

translation.text: Flynn 使用牛粪烧制的技术不需要窑炉，使这种“零技术”方法可以在任何有需要的地方使用。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Other commercial clay filters do exist, but, even if available, with prices starting at US$5 each, they are often outside the budgets of most people in the developing world. Unlike other water filtering devices, Flynn’s filters are inexpensive and simple to produce. Take a handful of clay, mix it with a handful of organic material such as used tea leaves, coffee grounds or rice hulls, add water in a sufficient quantity to make a stiff mixture and form a cylindrical pot that has one end closed, then dry it in the sun. According to Flynn, used coffee grounds have given the best results to date. The walls of the filter can be measured using the width of an adult finger as the standard. Next, surround the pots with straw, put them in a mound of cow manure, light the straw and then top up the burning manure as required. The filters are finished in 45 to 60 minutes.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 市面上确实还有其他黏土净水器，但即使能够买到，每个起价5美元，往往也超出发展中世界大多数人的承受范围。Flynn 的净水器与其他净水装置不同，价格低廉，制作简单。取一把黏土，加入一把用过的茶叶、咖啡渣或稻壳等有机材料，再加足量的水，和成硬实的混合物；将其塑成一端封闭的圆筒形容器，然后放在阳光下晒干。Flynn 说，迄今用过的咖啡渣效果最佳。过滤器壁厚可以用成年人的手指宽度作为标准。接着，用稻草围住陶罐，把它们放入一堆牛粪中，点燃稻草，再按需要向燃烧的牛粪上补料。过滤器会在45至60分钟内烧制完成。

source.text: Other commercial clay filters do exist, but, even if available, with prices starting at US$5 each, they are often outside the budgets of most people in the developing world.

translation.text: 市面上确实还有其他黏土净水器，但即使能够买到，每个起价5美元，往往也超出发展中世界大多数人的承受范围。

source.text: The filters are finished in 45 to 60 minutes.

translation.text: 过滤器会在45至60分钟内烧制完成。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The properties of cow manure are vital, as the fuel can reach a temperature of 700 degrees in half an hour, and will be up to 950 degrees after another 20 to 30 minutes. The manure makes a good fuel because it is very high in organic material that burns readily and quickly. The manure has to be dry and is best used exactly as found in the field; there is no need to break it up or process it any further. In contrast, a potter’s kiln is an expensive item and can take up to four or five hours to get up to 800 degrees. It needs expensive, scarce fuel, such as gas or wood to heat it, and experience to use it. With no technology, no insulation and nothing other than a pile of cow manure and a match, none of these requirements apply.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 牛粪的特性至关重要：这种燃料可在半小时内达到700摄氏度，再过20至30分钟，温度最高可达950摄氏度。牛粪是优质燃料，因为其中有机物含量很高，能够轻易而迅速地燃烧。牛粪必须干燥，最好直接使用田野里找到的原样牛粪，无须打碎或进一步处理。相比之下，陶窑价格昂贵，升至800摄氏度可能需要四五个小时；它需要用天然气或木材等昂贵而稀缺的燃料加热，操作起来也需要经验。这里不需要技术，不需要隔热材料，除了一堆牛粪和一根火柴什么也不需要，因此上述要求都不适用。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It is also helpful that, like clay and organic material, cow manure is freely available across the developing world. A cow is a natural fuel factory. Manure is a mixture of vegetable materials of different sizes, and cow manure as a fuel is the same wherever it is found.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 还有一点也很有帮助：牛粪与黏土和有机材料一样，在发展中世界各地都可以免费获得。一头牛就是一座天然燃料工厂。牛粪由大小不一的植物性材料混合而成，无论在哪里找到，作为燃料的性质都一样。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Just as using manure as a fuel for domestic use is not a new idea, the fact that liquid can pass through clay objects is something that potters have always known, and clay’s porous nature is something that, as a former ceramics lecturer in the ANU School of Art, Flynn is well aware of. The difference is that, rather than viewing the porous nature of the material as a problem — after all, not many people want a pot that won’t hold water — his filters capitalize on this property.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The filtration process is simple, but effective. The basic principle is that there are passages through the filter that are wide enough for water droplets to pass through, but too narrow for pathogens. Tests with the deadly E. coli bacterium have seen the filters remove 96.4 to 99.8 per cent of the pathogen — well within safe levels. The thickness of the clay container needs to be the same thickness as an adult finger for the process to be effective. If this is the case, using only one filter, a liter of water can be obtained in two hours.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 过滤过程简单，却很有效。基本原理是，过滤器中存在一些通道，宽到足以让水滴通过，却窄到病原体无法穿过。用致命的大肠杆菌进行的测试显示，这些过滤器能清除96.4%至99.8%的病原体，完全达到安全水平。黏土容器必须与成年人的手指一样厚，过滤过程才能有效。在符合这一条件的情况下，只用一个过滤器，两个小时便能获得一升水。

source.text: Tests with the deadly E. coli bacterium have seen the filters remove 96.4 to 99.8 per cent of the pathogen — well within safe levels.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The use of organic material, which burns away leaving cavities after firing, helps produce the structure in which pathogens will become trapped. It overcomes the potential problems of finer clays that may not let water through and also means that cracks are soon halted. source.text: Playing soccer

translation.text: 踢足球

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: There are many differences between playing soccer in the street and joining a youth team in an organized league in the USA
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 在街头踢球，与加入美国正规联赛中的一支青少年球队，存在许多差别

source.text: There are many differences between playing soccer in the street and joining a youth team in an organized league in the USA

translation.text: 在街头踢球，与加入美国正规联赛中的一支青少年球队，存在许多差别

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Street soccer, as its name implies, is an informal variation of the sport, often played on the street, particularly in urban areas. There are many reasons for the widespread popularity of street soccer. Unlike youth soccer, its more formally organized counterpart, no large space is needed, and goal posts, corner markers, and marked lines, associated with the formal game, are typically absent, as are game officials or referees. Another attraction of street soccer is that it is played frequently and competitively, but does not necessarily require standard 11-a-side teams or fixed playing positions. Unlike in youth soccer, inexperienced street soccer players rarely learn from repetitive technical and tactical drills. Instead, they learn from their poor performance in competition, unconscious of the skills they are nonetheless developing, and without older adults or coaches present. Players learn without effort through playing the game, and soon attain an almost natural feeling for the sport.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 顾名思义，街头足球是这种运动的一种非正式变体，常常在街道上进行，尤其是在城区。街头足球广受欢迎的原因很多。与组织更正式的青少年足球不同，它不需要大片场地，正式比赛中的球门柱、角旗和场地标线通常都不存在，比赛官员或裁判也没有。街头足球的另一个吸引力在于，比赛进行得频繁而激烈，却不一定需要标准的11人制球队或固定位置。与青少年足球不同，经验不足的街头球员很少通过反复练习技术和战术来学习。相反，他们会从比赛中的糟糕表现中吸取经验；虽然没有意识到自己正在培养哪些技巧，身边也没有年长者或教练，但他们仍在成长。球员通过踢比赛毫不费力地学习，很快便对这项运动形成一种近乎本能的感觉。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In spite of all these obstacles, which are probably solvable in most instances, there is another sociological explanation of why in many places street soccer doesn’t enjoy the same popularity it once did. In his book How Soccer Explains the World, US writer Franklin Foer observes: But for all the talk of freedom, the 1960s parenting style had a far less relaxed side too. Like the 1960s consumer movement which brought seat belts and airbags to cars, the (youth) soccer movement felt like it could create a set of … regulations that would protect both the child’s body and mind from damage. Soccer leagues like the one I played in as a child handed out ‘participation’ prizes to every player, no matter how few games his (or her) team won. Where most of the world accepts the practice of using your head to hit the ball as an essential element of the game, some (youth) soccer parents have worried over the potential for injury to the brain. An entire industry grew up to manufacture protective headgear. Even though very little medical evidence supports this fear, some youth leagues prohibited heading the ball altogether.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A growing body of people don’t believe street soccer involves a legitimate educational method. They argue that children need to be taught by experts. Youth soccer instruction now begins with four-year-olds, so that they will have an advantage as six-year-olds. This need to get ahead brings with it a fear of falling behind that only expert instruction can prevent. This type of instruction leaves no room for the trial-and-error approach of street soccer.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One of the basic ideas of street soccer is that young players are assigned a particular role by a better player and are expected to play for the good of the team. Such an assignment runs counter to the idea of youth soccer that every child needs to learn every position and will benefit from doing so. In street soccer, you fill the role that you are best able to at a particular time. While this role assignment can change from game to game, the purpose is always the same: to get the best out of each individual at any given moment.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In street soccer, children have to learn patience, to wait their turn, to realize that they are not entitled to make decisions, or even be listened to simply because they show up. Positions of responsibility are earned through competition within the team. Younger players in street soccer must wait to attain those positions. In youth soccer, however, with its overly democratic values, youngsters are guaranteed their time in the spotlight. Whether it’s their turn to be captain, to play a central position or to take a crucial shot, youth soccer players come to believe that hard work and patience aren’t really necessary.

passages.title: Roller coaster: the great fairground attraction

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Roller coaster: the great fairground attraction

source.text: Roller coaster: the great fairground attraction

translation.text: 过山车：游乐场的绝佳项目

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: How they move
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 过山车如何运行

source.text: How they move

translation.text: 过山车如何运行

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Like a passenger train, a roller coaster consists of a series of connected cars that move on a track. But unlike a passenger train, it has no engine or power source of its own. For most of the ride, it is moved only by the forces of inertia and gravity. The only exertion of energy occurs at the very beginning of the ride when the coaster train is pulled up the lift hill.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 过山车与客运列车一样，由一系列相连、沿轨道移动的车厢组成。但它与客运列车不同，自身没有发动机或动力源。在行程的大部分时间里，过山车只在惯性和重力作用下移动。唯一需要消耗能量的阶段出现在行程刚开始时，此时列车会被拉上提升坡。

source.text: Like a passenger train, a roller coaster consists of a series of connected cars that move on a track.

source.text: But unlike a passenger train, it has no engine or power source of its own.

translation.text: 但它与客运列车不同，自身没有发动机或动力源。

source.text: For most of the ride, it is moved only by the forces of inertia and gravity.

translation.text: 在行程的大部分时间里，过山车只在惯性和重力作用下移动。

source.text: The only exertion of energy occurs at the very beginning of the ride when the coaster train is pulled up the lift hill.

translation.text: 唯一需要消耗能量的阶段出现在行程刚开始时，此时列车会被拉上提升坡。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The traditional lifting mechanism is a long length of chain running up the hill under the track. The chain is fastened in a loop, which is wound around a gear at the top of the hill and another one at the bottom. The gear at the bottom of the hill is turned by a motor. This turns the chain so that it continually moves up the hill like a long conveyor belt. The coaster cars grip onto the chain, which simply pulls them to the top. At the summit, the train is released and starts its descent.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 传统提升装置是一条很长的链条，沿斜坡铺设在轨道下方。链条首尾相连形成环路，绕在坡顶和坡底各一个齿轮上。坡底的齿轮由电动机驱动，带动链条像一条长传送带一样持续向坡顶移动。过山车车厢扣住链条，由链条直接拉到顶端。到达坡顶后，列车被释放并开始下行。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The purpose of this initial ascent is to build up a sort of reservoir of potential energy, which simply means that as the coaster gets higher in the air, there is a greater distance gravity can pull it down.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 最初爬坡的目的是积蓄某种势能。简单来说，过山车升到空中越高，重力可以把它向下拉动的距离就越长。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As the train starts coasting down the hill, this potential energy is converted into kinetic energy (energy of motion), and the train speeds up. At the bottom of the hill, this has reached its maximum, and this propels the train up the second hill, again building up the potential-energy level.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 列车开始滑下斜坡时，势能转化为动能，也就是运动的能量，列车随之加速。到达坡底时，动能达到最大值，并推动列车爬上第二个坡，再次提高势能水平。

source.text: At the bottom of the hill, this has reached its maximum, and this propels the train up the second hill, again building up the potential-energy level.

translation.text: 到达坡底时，动能达到最大值，并推动列车爬上第二个坡，再次提高势能水平。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In this way, the course of the track is constantly converting energy from kinetic to potential and back again. This fluctuation in acceleration is what makes roller coasters so much fun. At its most basic level, this is all a roller coaster is – a machine that uses gravity and inertia to send a train along a winding track.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 轨道沿线就这样不断把动能转化为势能，再把势能转回动能。加速度的这种起伏变化，正是过山车如此有趣的原因。从最基本的层面看，过山车就是这样一台机器：它利用重力和惯性，让列车沿蜿蜒曲折的轨道前进。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Coasting through history
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 滑行穿越历史

source.text: Coasting through history

translation.text: 滑行穿越历史

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Roller coasters have a long, fascinating history. Their direct ancestors were ice slides, popular in Russia in the 16th and 17th centuries. They consisted of a long, steep, wooden slide covered in ice. Riders walked up a ladder or set of stairs to the top of the slide, as high as 21 metres up. At the top, they climbed into sleds made of wood or blocks of ice and shot down the slope. At the base, the sleds would crash-land in a sand pile.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 过山车有着悠久而迷人的历史。它的直系祖先是16和17世纪流行于俄罗斯的冰滑道。这种设施由一条长而陡峭、表面覆冰的木制滑道构成。乘客沿梯子或台阶走到滑道顶部，最高可达21米。他们在顶端坐进木制雪橇或冰块制成的雪橇，随后飞驰下坡。到达底部时，雪橇会撞进沙堆停下。
