source.text: The internal body clock

translation.text: 体内生物钟

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Each of our cells has an internal 'clock' which dictates our daily rhythms. But why?
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 我们的每个细胞都有一个内部“时钟”，支配着每日节律。但为什么会这样？

source.text: Each of our cells has an internal 'clock' which dictates our daily rhythms.

translation.text: 我们的每个细胞都有一个内部“时钟”，支配着每日节律。

source.text: But why?

translation.text: 但为什么会这样？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: From buffalo to bacteria, oaks to algae, all life follows the same relentless 24-hour cycle, which is driven by the rising and setting of the Sun. Or is it? Over 250 years ago, a French scientist performed a simple experiment that blew apart the idea that all life on Earth does the bidding of the Sun. Intrigued by the way some flowers open and close their leaves each day, Jean-Jacques de Mairan put a heliotrope in a darkened room and observed the effect. He was expecting the plant, robbed of sunlight, to cease its daily routine. To his astonishment, its leaves continued to open and close as if in response to some invisible timekeeper.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 从水牛到细菌，从橡树到藻类，所有生命都遵循同一个毫不间断的24小时周期，而这个周期由太阳升起和落下驱动。真是这样吗？250多年前，一位法国科学家进行了一项简单实验，彻底打破了地球上一切生命都听命于太阳的观念。Jean-Jacques de Mairan 对一些花朵每天开合叶片的方式很感兴趣，于是把一株天芥菜放进黑暗房间，观察会有什么影响。他原以为，植物失去阳光后会停止每日活动。令他惊讶的是，叶片仍继续开合，仿佛在响应某个看不见的计时器。

translation.text: 真是这样吗？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But what – and where – is this internal timekeeper? And how does it achieve such astonishing regularity? These are the mysteries at the forefront of chronobiology, the study of the effect of time in living organisms. The search for answers is about more than just tying up some scientific loose ends. Internal ‘clocks’ clearly cause a lot of hardship. When an individual’s ‘clock’ is knocked out of synchronization through having to work at night or go on long-haul flights, that person can be left utterly unable to think or act. Yet even when these ‘clocks’ work correctly, the natural rhythms of alertness they generate prove dangerous: traffic accident statistics show two deadly peaks, at 4 a.m. and again twelve hours later when people are at their least alert.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 但这个内部计时器是什么，又在哪里？它如何实现如此惊人的规律性？这些奥秘处在时间生物学研究的最前沿；时间生物学研究时间对生物体的影响。寻找答案不只是为了解决几个尚未收尾的科学问题。内部“时钟”显然会造成许多困扰。一个人因夜间工作或长途飞行而使自己的“时钟”失去同步后，可能会完全无法思考或行动。然而，即使这些“时钟”正常运转，它们产生的自然警觉度节律也可能十分危险：交通事故统计显示有两个致命高峰，一个在凌晨4点，另一个在12小时后，这两个时段都是人们警觉度最低的时候。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: During the 1970s, best-selling books began to emerge claiming such phenomena were manifestations of so-called biorhythms, a set of three cycles governing physical, emotional and intellectual traits. Said to start from the moment of birth and repeat every 23, 28 and 33 days respectively, they were supposed to result in ‘critical days’ when one or more cycles led to sub-optimal performance, with unfortunate consequences.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 20世纪70年代，一些畅销书开始出现，声称这类现象是所谓生物节律的表现。生物节律由3个周期组成，分别支配身体、情绪和智力特征。据说，这些周期从出生时开始，分别每23天、28天和33天重复一次，并会造成“关键日”；在这些日子里，一个或多个周期会使人的表现低于最佳水平，带来不幸后果。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Scientists have since dismissed biorhythms as pseudoscience, insisting the existence of the three cycles has no basis in fact. In 1998, Dr Terence Hines of Pace University, New York State published the most comprehensive study of the claims made for biorhythms, reviewing the results of over 130 investigations. He found that three-quarters of them failed to provide any support for biorhythms. Most of the remainder contained blunders ranging from faulty mathematics to basic errors in statistics, while the handful of positive studies were explicable as flukes.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 此后，科学家认为生物节律属于伪科学，并坚持指出，这3个周期的存在毫无事实依据。1998年，纽约州佩斯大学 Terence Hines 博士发表了对生物节律主张最全面的研究，审查了130多项调查的结果。他发现，其中四分之三没有提供任何支持生物节律的证据。其余研究大多存在错误，从数学计算不当到基本统计错误都有；而少数得出正面结论的研究，也可以用偶然巧合来解释。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But there is no doubting the existence of 24-hour biological cycles – or, rather, ones roughly 24 hours long. Following de Mairan’s pioneering work, other researchers found that when deprived of the cues provided by sunlight, organisms settle down to ‘free-running’ cycles that are close to, but rarely exactly, 24 hours long. In the case of humans, the cycle is typically around 24.5 hours long. This is the so-called ‘circadian’ cycle (from the Latin meaning ‘about a day’), the length of which is generated by the mysterious internal ‘clock’.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，24小时生物周期的存在毋庸置疑；更准确地说，是长度约为24小时的周期。德梅朗完成开创性研究后，其他研究人员发现，生物体失去阳光提供的提示时，会进入接近24小时、却很少恰好为24小时的“自由运行”周期。人类的周期通常约为24.5小时。这就是所谓的“昼夜节律”周期；这个词来自拉丁语，意为“大约一天”，而周期长度由神秘的内部“时钟”产生。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: During the late 1960s, chronobiologists believed they had found the ‘clock’, in the form of the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), a collection of nerves in a region of the brain known as the hypothalamus. Linked to photosensitive cells in the eye, the SCN senses daylight and triggers the release of hormones like melatonin, which keep body functions in synchronization with the time of day. For a few years the SCN was regarded as the ultimate pacemaker – at least in higher organisms such as ourselves. But in 1971, scientists at the California Institute of Technology working with fruit flies found evidence for something truly amazing. Fruit flies appeared to have genes affecting the daily rhythm of their behavior – suggesting that there are ‘clocks’ inside each of their cells. Further evidence for this emerged in 1995, when researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital isolated nerve cells from the SCN, and found they kept up a circadian cycle without help from daylight. Finally in 1997, scientists at Northwestern University, Illinois, found a gene that regulates the daily rhythms of cellular activity in mammals.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 20世纪60年代末，时间生物学家认为自己找到了这个“时钟”，即视交叉上核（SCN）。它是位于大脑下丘脑区域的一组神经。视交叉上核与眼内感光细胞相连，能够感知日光，并触发褪黑素等激素释放，使身体功能与一天中的时间保持同步。有几年时间，视交叉上核被视为最终的节律起搏器，至少对人类这样的高等生物而言如此。但1971年，加州理工学院研究果蝇的科学家发现了某种真正惊人的证据。果蝇似乎拥有影响其每日行为节律的基因，这表明每个细胞内部都有“时钟”。1995年又出现了进一步证据：马萨诸塞总医院的研究人员从视交叉上核分离出神经细胞，发现即使没有日光帮助，这些细胞仍会保持昼夜节律。最后，1997年，伊利诺伊州西北大学的科学家发现了一个调节哺乳动物细胞活动每日节律的基因。

source.text: Finally in 1997, scientists at Northwestern University, Illinois, found a gene that regulates the daily rhythms of cellular activity in mammals.

translation.text: 最后，1997年，伊利诺伊州西北大学的科学家发现了一个调节哺乳动物细胞活动每日节律的基因。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The details of how this gene, known as CLOCK, actually works are still being investigated, but they could culminate in better ways of coping with shift-work and jet-lag. Professor Takahashi, who led the research, says that now that we know that circadian clocks exist throughout our bodies, we will need new strategies and therapeutics to reset all of our cells. But how do all the biochemical ‘clocks’ inside their cells stay in synchronization and why did organisms bother to acquire a link with sunlight? So far, no-one knows, though there are several theories. For example, sunlight might be useful in keeping the myriad cellular ‘clocks’ in lockstep.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In the search for answers, researchers are studying the behavior of a microbe called cyanobacterium. In 2005, a team at Nagoya University, Japan, showed that chemical reactions between three proteins produced by this bacterium ebbed and flowed on a 24-hour cycle. Cyanobacterium is the oldest form of life on Earth, so this suggests that cellular ‘clocks’ have existed for over three billion years. All subsequent organisms have followed suit, says Professor Johnson of Vanderbilt University, Tennessee. ‘Bacteria, fungi, plants and animals all appear to have evolved clock systems independently from each other.’ Quite why is still unknown. But one thing is clear: the daily routine of life is certainly not a modern invention.

passages.title: The Myth of the Eight-hour Sleep

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: The Myth of the Eight-hour Sleep

source.text: The Myth of the Eight-hour Sleep

translation.text: 八小时睡眠的神话

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: We often worry about lying awake in the middle of the night—but it could be good for you. Indications from both science and history suggest that the eight-hour sleep may not be a natural or inborn pattern for humans. In the early 1990s, psychiatrist Thomas Wehr conducted research which implies just that. Wehr kept a group of people in a darkened room for 14 hours a day for a month. It took some time for their sleep to regulate, but by the fourth week the subjects had settled into a very distinct sleeping pattern. First, they slept for four hours, then woke for one or two hours before falling into a second four-hour sleep. Though sleep scientists were impressed by the implications of the study, the idea that we must sleep for eight consecutive hours persists amongst the general public.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 我们常常担心自己半夜醒着，但这或许对你有好处。科学和历史中的迹象都表明，八小时睡眠可能并非人类自然或与生俱来的模式。20世纪90年代初，精神科医生 Thomas Wehr 开展了一项研究，结论正是如此。他让一组人连续一个月每天在黑暗房间里待14小时。他们的睡眠过了一段时间才变得规律，但到第4周，受试者已形成一种非常鲜明的睡眠模式：先睡4小时，再清醒1至2小时，之后又睡4小时。睡眠科学家虽然对这项研究的意义印象深刻，公众却仍普遍坚持认为，我们必须连续睡满8小时。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In 2001, historian Roger Ekirch of Virginia Tech University in the US published a paper drawn from 16 years of research, revealing historical evidence that humans used to sleep in two distinct periods of time each night. Ekirch’s research found more than 500 references to a segmented sleeping pattern—in diaries, court records, medical books and literature, from the ancient Greeks to tribes in Nigeria. Much like Wehr’s findings, these references describe a first sleep which began not long following sunset. Then there was a waking period of one or two hours and after that a second sleep. During the waking period, people could be quite active. They sometimes got up and moved around the house, although most people stayed in bed, and perhaps read or wrote if they had enough money for candles. In many historic accounts, Ekirch found that people used the time that they were awake between periods of sleep to think about and attempt to analyse their dreams.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 2001年，美国弗吉尼亚理工大学历史学家 Roger Ekirch 发表了一篇以16年研究为基础的论文，揭示了人类过去每晚分两个不同时段睡眠的历史证据。Ekirch 从日记、法庭记录、医学书籍和文学作品中发现500多处有关分段睡眠模式的记载，年代和地域从古希腊一直延伸到尼日利亚部落。与韦尔的发现非常相似，这些记载描述，第一段睡眠在日落后不久开始，随后有1至2小时的清醒期，之后才是第二段睡眠。清醒期间，人们可能相当活跃。有时他们会起床在屋内走动，不过大多数人仍躺在床上；如果有钱购买蜡烛，或许还会阅读或写作。Ekirch 在许多历史记录中发现，人们会利用两段睡眠之间醒着的时间，思考并尝试分析自己的梦。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In his book, Evening’s Empire, historian Craig Koslofsky suggests an explanation for this divided sleep pattern in Europe. ‘Associations with night before the 17th century were not good,’ he writes. He goes on to explain that the streets of the cities and towns at night were often populated by thieves or worse. The streets at night consequently scared many people. Even the wealthy, who could afford to light their way, had better things to spend their nights on.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 历史学家 Craig Koslofsky 在《夜晚的帝国》一书中，为欧洲这种分段睡眠模式提出了一种解释。他写道：“17世纪以前，人们对夜晚的联想并不好。”他接着解释，当时城镇的街道夜间常有小偷，甚至更危险的人出没。因此，夜晚的街道令许多人害怕。即使富人有钱照亮道路，也有更好的方式度过夜晚。

source.text: In his book, Evening’s Empire, historian Craig Koslofsky suggests an explanation for this divided sleep pattern in Europe.

translation.text: 历史学家 Craig Koslofsky 在《夜晚的帝国》一书中，为欧洲这种分段睡眠模式提出了一种解释。

source.text: ‘Associations with night before the 17th century were not good,’ he writes.

translation.text: 他写道：“17世纪以前，人们对夜晚的联想并不好。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Ekirch found that references to the first and second sleep started to disappear during the late 17th century. The pattern began to alter first among the upper classes in northern Europe and, over the course of the next 200 years, began changing amongst the rest of Western society. By the 1920s, the idea of a first and second sleep had receded entirely from our social consciousness. Ekirch attributes the initial shift to improvements in street and home lighting.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 埃基尔希发现，有关第一段和第二段睡眠的记载从17世纪末开始消失。睡眠模式最先在北欧上层阶级中发生变化，并在接下来的200年里逐渐影响西方社会其他阶层。到20世纪20年代，第一段和第二段睡眠的观念已从社会意识中彻底消退。埃基尔希把最初的转变归因于街道和家庭照明的改善。

source.text: Ekirch found that references to the first and second sleep started to disappear during the late 17th century.

source.text: The pattern began to alter first among the upper classes in northern Europe and, over the course of the next 200 years, began changing amongst the rest of Western society.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As the night became a time for all kinds of activity, the length of time people slept declined. In 1667, Paris became the first city in the world to light its streets, using wax candles in glass lamps. It was followed by another French city, Lille, in the same year and by Amsterdam in Holland two years later, where a much more efficient oil-powered lamp was developed. London didn’t light its streets until 1684, but by the end of the 17th century, more than 50 of Europe’s major towns and cities were lit at night. Coffee houses emerged as a fashionable phenomenon and many were open virtually around the clock. Going out at night became commonplace, and spending hours lying in bed was considered a waste of time. ‘People were becoming increasingly time-conscious and sensitive to efficiency, certainly before the 19th century,’ says Ekirch. ‘But the Industrial Revolution intensified that attitude considerably.’ Strong evidence of this shifting attitude is contained in a medical journal from 1829 which urged parents to force their children out of the pattern of first and second sleep.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 随着夜晚成为开展各种活动的时间，人们的睡眠时长减少了。1667年，巴黎使用玻璃灯罩内的蜡烛照亮街道，成为世界上第一个这样做的城市。同年，法国另一座城市里尔也开始实行；两年后，荷兰阿姆斯特丹同样开始照明街道，并在那里开发出效率高得多的油灯。伦敦直到1684年才照亮街道，但到17世纪末，欧洲已有50多座主要城镇和城市在夜间亮起灯光。咖啡馆成为一种时髦现象，许多咖啡馆几乎全天候营业。夜间外出变得司空见惯，躺在床上耗费数小时则被视为浪费时间。埃基尔希说：“可以肯定，早在19世纪以前，人们就越来越重视时间、关注效率。但工业革命大大强化了这种态度。”1829年的一份医学期刊有力证明了这种态度转变；该刊敦促父母强迫孩子摆脱第一段和第二段睡眠的模式。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Today, most people seem to have adapted quite well to the eight-hour sleep, but Ekirch believes many sleeping problems may have roots in the human body’s natural preference for divided sleep, as well as in difficulties caused by extended exposure to artificial light in the modern world. This could be the cause of a condition called sleep maintenance insomnia, where people wake during the night and have trouble getting back to sleep. The condition first appears in literature at the end of the 19th century, at the same time as accounts of interrupted sleep disappear.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Sleep psychologist Gregg Jacobs says that the idea that we must sleep for an extended period of time could be damaging if it makes people who wake up in the night anxious, as this anxiety can itself discourage sleep and is likely to affect waking life too. Jacobs suggests that the waking period between sleeps, when people simply rested and relaxed, could have played an important part in the human capacity to regulate stress naturally. Russell Foster, a professor of circadian (body clock) neuroscience at Oxford University in the UK, shares this point of view. ‘Over 30% of the medical problems that doctors are faced with stem directly or indirectly from sleep. But sleep has been ignored in medical training, and there are very few centres where sleep is studied,’ Foster says. He feels this needs to change.

passages.title: The origin and development of applause

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: The origin and development of applause

source.text: The origin and development of applause

translation.text: 掌声的起源与发展

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Whether you clap, cheer or whistle a great public performance, you are following a long tradition.
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 无论你为一场精彩的公开演出鼓掌、欢呼还是吹口哨，你都在沿袭一种历史悠久的传统。

source.text: Whether you clap, cheer or whistle a great public performance, you are following a long tradition.

translation.text: 无论你为一场精彩的公开演出鼓掌、欢呼还是吹口哨，你都在沿袭一种历史悠久的传统。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Scholars aren’t quite sure about the origins of applause, but the form that is still most common, clapping the hands together, was formalized in Western culture during and after performances. During the time of the Roman Republic (509 BC – 27 BC) the common way to end a play was for the chief actor to yell ‘Valete et plaudite!’ (‘Farewell, and applaud!’) thus signaling to the audience that it was time for them to give praise by striking hands and making explosive noise. It’s no surprise, then, that this became a means of crowd manipulation. Rome saw the rise of a professional class of applauders, or ‘people who clapped for their dinner’, hired to infiltrate crowds and manipulate their reaction to performances. Actors would hire a dozen or so people to spread out among their audiences and prolong the applause, or, if they were feeling especially bold, to start ‘spontaneous’ chants and shouts of praise.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 学者们并不十分确定掌声的起源。不过，在西方文化中，如今仍最常见的形式——双手相拍——已成为演出期间及结束后的一种固定惯例。罗马共和国时期（公元前509年—公元前27年），一出戏通常由首席演员高喊“Valete et plaudite!”（“再会，请鼓掌！”）来收场，以此向观众示意：现在是他们双手相击、发出爆裂般声响来表达赞赏的时候了。因此，这种做法后来成为操纵人群的一种手段，也就不足为奇了。在罗马，职业喝彩者这一群体随之兴起；这些人也被称为“靠拍手换饭吃的人”。他们受雇混入观众之中，操纵人们对演出的反应。演员会雇用十二人左右，让他们分散在观众席中，把掌声延续下去；如果演员们格外大胆，还会让这些人发起“自发的”齐声呼喊和赞美声。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The Roman Republic came to an end and was replaced by the Roman Empire (27 BC – 476 AD) where applause became a way for leaders to interact directly with their citizens. One of the chief methods they used to estimate their standing with the people was gauging the greetings they got when they entered the arena. Leaders became astute at reading the volume, the rhythm, and the length of the crowd’s claps for clues about how well they were doing as officials and lawmakers. ‘We should think of it as an ancient type of opinion poll,’ says Greg Aldrete, a professor of history. ‘This is how you gauge the people.’ Roman leaders were gathering data about people by listening to applause.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 罗马共和国走向终结，取而代之的是罗马帝国（公元前27年—公元476年）；在帝国时期，掌声成了统治者与公民直接互动的一种方式。要判断自己在民众中的地位，统治者采用的一项主要方法，就是评估他们进入竞技场时受到的欢迎程度。他们很善于从人群拍手的音量、节奏和持续时间中寻找线索，判断自己作为官员和立法者表现如何。“我们应当把它看作一种古代的民意调查，”历史学教授 Greg Aldrete 说，“这就是你了解民众的方式。”罗马统治者通过聆听掌声来收集有关民众的数据。

source.text: Leaders became astute at reading the volume, the rhythm, and the length of the crowd’s claps for clues about how well they were doing as officials and lawmakers.

translation.text: “我们应当把它看作一种古代的民意调查，”历史学教授 Greg Aldrete 说，“这就是你了解民众的方式。”

source.text: Roman leaders were gathering data about people by listening to applause.

translation.text: 罗马统治者通过聆听掌声来收集有关民众的数据。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Clever leaders of the ancient world researched their rivals, too. Cicero, the Roman lawyer, would send friends to stand around outside the arena, taking notes to see what kind of greeting each official got when he entered, the better to see who was beloved by the people, and who was not. They had a lot of information to assess. ‘Ancient crowds were more interactive than they are today,’ Aldrete points out. ‘There was a lot of back and forth between speakers and crowds. And particularly in the Greco-Roman world, crowds, especially in cities, were really good at communicating messages through rhythmic clapping, sometimes coupled with shouts.’ The coding was, he says, invaluable when assessing an orator’s fortunes.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 古代世界中精明的统治者也会调查自己的对手。罗马律师西塞罗会派朋友守候在竞技场外，做记录，看看每位官员入场时受到怎样的欢迎，从而更好地判断谁受民众爱戴、谁不受爱戴。他们有大量信息需要评估。“古代人群的互动性比今天的人群更强，”Aldrete 指出，“演讲者与人群之间会频繁地相互回应。尤其是在希腊—罗马世界，人群——特别是城市中的人群——非常善于通过有节奏的拍手来传递信息，有时还会配合呼喊。”他说，这种用掌声节奏传递信息的方式，对于判断一位演说家的前景极有价值。

translation.text: 古代世界中精明的统治者也会调查自己的对手。

translation.text: 他们有大量信息需要评估。

translation.text: “古代人群的互动性比今天的人群更强，”Aldrete 指出，“演讲者与人群之间会频繁地相互回应。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Around the first century AD, those systems of applause became more and more elaborate. Applause no longer meant, simply, ‘claps’. While Greco-Roman audiences certainly smacked their palms together the same way we do today, their overall strategies of applause were much more varied than clapping alone. Crowds expressed degrees of approval of the person or persons before them, ranging from claps, to snaps (of the finger and thumb), to waves (of the edge of the toga). The emperor Aurelian decided to replace this gesture by waving a special handkerchief instead, a prop which he then distributed to all Roman citizens, so they would never be without a way to praise him.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 大约到了公元1世纪，这些喝彩方式变得越来越复杂。喝彩不再仅仅意味着“拍手”。虽然希腊—罗马观众的确会像今天的我们一样双掌相击，但他们整套表达赞赏的方式远比单纯拍手丰富多样。人群会以一系列不同动作，表达对面前一人或多人程度不等的赞许：从拍手，到用拇指和另一根手指打响指，再到挥动托加袍的衣边。奥勒良皇帝决定不再挥动托加袍衣边，改为挥动一块特制手帕；随后，他又把这种手帕分发给所有罗马公民，让他们随时都有办法赞颂他。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Although the style of applause may have changed over the centuries, the need to manipulate remained. The 16th-century French poet Jean Daurat is credited with bringing back the Roman practice of hiring professional applauders. In France, this group became known as a ‘claque’. Daurat handed out tickets to his own performances to people who promised to applaud at the end. By the early 1820s, claques had become institutionalized, with an agency in Paris specializing in the distribution of the claqueurs’ services. The historian William B. Cohen describes the intricate price lists agencies of this kind would hand out to potential patrons: polite clapping would cost this many francs, enthusiastic applause would cost this many. The claque also underwent a kind of classification: the rieurs (laughers) would laugh loudly at the jokes; the pleureurs (criers) would feign tears in reaction to performances; the commissaires (officers) would learn a play or a piece of music by heart and then call attention to its best parts. This practice spread to Milan, to Vienna, and to London before falling out of fashion. The claque lost its power once people became aware of its tricks.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 尽管几个世纪以来，喝彩的方式或许发生了变化，但操纵人群的需求依然存在。据认为，16世纪法国诗人 Jean Daurat 重新采用了罗马人雇用职业喝彩者的做法。在法国，这个群体被称为“claque”。Daurat 把自己演出的门票发给那些承诺会在演出结束时鼓掌的人。到了1820年代初，claque 已经制度化，巴黎有一家机构专门安排职业喝彩者（claqueurs）的服务。历史学家 William B. Cohen 描述了此类机构会发给潜在顾客的繁复价目表：礼貌鼓掌收费若干法郎，热烈喝彩又收费若干法郎。claque 内部也出现了某种分类：rieurs（笑者）会在笑话出现时放声大笑；pleureurs（哭泣者）会假装因演出而落泪；commissaires（专员）会把一出戏或一段音乐熟记于心，然后引导人们注意其中最精彩的部分。这种做法传到米兰、维也纳和伦敦，之后逐渐不再流行。人们一旦识破 claque 的伎俩，它便失去了影响力。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: And clapping itself evolved. In the 18th century, symphonies and concerts became more serious, aligning themselves with the reverence and spirituality associated with religious ceremonies. Knowing when to maintain silence, as well as when to clap, became a mark of sophistication, a kind of code for audiences to learn. Applause became a matter of ‘do’ or ‘don’t’, so losing many old shades of meaning. Those changes changed performers, too. Applause became much less of a true dialogue with an audience, especially so with opera, where the singers saw it as part of a basic transaction with the crowd. So by the time the 19th century arrived, applause had become standardized and institutionalized, and had become an expectation rather than the reward it used to be.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 拍手这种行为本身也在演变。18世纪，交响乐和音乐会变得更加严肃，并逐渐与宗教仪式所具有的敬畏感和精神性相契合。懂得何时保持安静、何时鼓掌，成了有修养的标志；这也成了观众需要学习的一套规范。喝彩成了一件只能“做”或“不做”的事，于是失去了过去许多细微含义。这些变化也改变了表演者。掌声在很大程度上不再构成与观众之间真正的对话；在歌剧中尤其如此，歌唱者把掌声视为自己与观众之间基本交换的一部分。因此，到了19世纪，掌声已经标准化并制度化，成了人们意料之中的事，而不再像过去那样是一种奖赏。

source.text: Those changes changed performers, too.

translation.text: 这些变化也改变了表演者。

source.text: Applause became much less of a true dialogue with an audience, especially so with opera, where the singers saw it as part of a basic transaction with the crowd.

translation.text: 掌声在很大程度上不再构成与观众之间真正的对话；在歌剧中尤其如此，歌唱者把掌声视为自己与观众之间基本交换的一部分。

source.text: So by the time the 19th century arrived, applause had become standardized and institutionalized, and had become an expectation rather than the reward it used to be.

translation.text: 因此，到了19世纪，掌声已经标准化并制度化，成了人们意料之中的事，而不再像过去那样是一种奖赏。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In the 21st century we’re reinventing applause, to make it what it used to be: a coded form of communication. More and more the digital world allows us to link and like and share through our devices. By connecting with others in this way, we become part of the performance by participating in it, demonstrating our appreciation by amplifying and extending the show through commenting and praising. Our kind of applause matters more now, in many ways, because it is no longer momentary and short-lived, but is far more permanent instead.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在21世纪，我们正在重新塑造喝彩，使它恢复过去的样子：一种用特定信号传递信息的交流方式。在数字世界中，我们越来越能够借助设备相互连接、点赞和分享。以这种方式与他人建立联系，我们通过参与而成为表演的一部分；我们还借助评论和赞美来放大并延续演出，以此表达欣赏。从许多方面看，我们这种喝彩如今变得更为重要，因为它不再转瞬即逝，而是持久得多。

passages.title: The plan to bring an asteroid to Earth

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: The plan to bring an asteroid to Earth
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 把小行星带到地球的计划

source.text: The plan to bring an asteroid to Earth

translation.text: 把小行星带到地球的计划

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Moving in orbit around our Sun are millions of rocks known as asteroids. Now scientists have plans to capture one.
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 数百万块被称为小行星的岩石正在围绕太阳运行。如今，科学家计划捕获其中一颗。

source.text: Moving in orbit around our Sun are millions of rocks known as asteroids.

translation.text: 数百万块被称为小行星的岩石正在围绕太阳运行。

source.text: Now scientists have plans to capture one.

translation.text: 如今，科学家计划捕获其中一颗。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Send a robot into space, catch an asteroid and bring it back to Earth’s orbit. This, say scientists and engineers at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), could be feasible. A four-day workshop was dedicated to investigating the feasibility of capturing a near-Earth asteroid, bringing it closer to our planet and using it as a base for future manned space-flight missions.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 把机器人送入太空，捕获一颗小行星，再把它带回地球轨道。加州理工学院的科学家和工程师说，这或许可行。一场为期4天的研讨会专门研究这一设想的可行性：捕获一颗近地小行星，把它带到更靠近地球的位置，并将其用作未来载人航天任务的基地。

source.text: Send a robot into space, catch an asteroid and bring it back to Earth’s orbit.

translation.text: 把机器人送入太空，捕获一颗小行星，再把它带回地球轨道。

source.text: This, say scientists and engineers at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), could be feasible.

translation.text: 加州理工学院的科学家和工程师说，这或许可行。

source.text: A four-day workshop was dedicated to investigating the feasibility of capturing a near-Earth asteroid, bringing it closer to our planet and using it as a base for future manned space-flight missions.

translation.text: 一场为期4天的研讨会专门研究这一设想的可行性：捕获一颗近地小行星，把它带到更靠近地球的位置，并将其用作未来载人航天任务的基地。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This is not something the scientists are imagining could be done someday in the future. It is possible with the technology we have today and could be accomplished within a decade. A robotic probe could anchor to an asteroid with simple magnets or grab it with specialised claws. Alternatively, a large spacecraft could use its gravitational field to shift the orbit of a larger asteroid, sending it towards Earth.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 科学家并不是在设想未来某一天也许能做到这件事。利用我们今天拥有的技术，这已经可能实现，而且可以在10年内完成。机器人探测器可以用简单磁铁固定在小行星上，也可以用专用机械爪抓住它。另一种办法是，让大型航天器利用自身引力场改变一颗较大小行星的轨道，把它送向地球。

translation.text: 科学家并不是在设想未来某一天也许能做到这件事。

source.text: It is possible with the technology we have today and could be accomplished within a decade.

translation.text: 利用我们今天拥有的技术，这已经可能实现，而且可以在10年内完成。

translation.text: 机器人探测器可以用简单磁铁固定在小行星上，也可以用专用机械爪抓住它。

source.text: Alternatively, a large spacecraft could use its gravitational field to shift the orbit of a larger asteroid, sending it towards Earth.

translation.text: 另一种办法是，让大型航天器利用自身引力场改变一颗较大小行星的轨道，把它送向地球。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: ‘Once you get over the initial reaction — You want to do what?! — it actually starts to seem like a reasonable idea,’ says engineer John Brophy, who helped organise the workshop. In fact, many of these ideas have been on the drawing board for years as part of NASA’s planetary-defence programme against large space-based objects that might threaten Earth. And there’s no shortage of potential targets: NASA estimates there are 19 500 asteroids at least 100 metres wide within 45 million kilometres of Earth.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 协助组织研讨会的工程师 John Brophy 说：“只要克服最初那种‘你想干什么？！’的反应，这个想法实际上便开始显得合乎情理。”事实上，作为美国国家航空航天局抵御可能威胁地球的大型太空物体的行星防御计划的一部分，其中许多设想已经筹划多年。潜在目标也并不短缺：美国国家航空航天局估计，距离地球4500万公里以内，至少有1.95万颗宽度不小于100米的小行星。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Though rearranging the heavens may seem an excessive undertaking, this US mission has its merits. The US already has plans to send astronauts to a near-Earth asteroid, a mission that would mean confining them in a tiny capsule for three to six months and would involve all the risks of a deep-space voyage. Instead, robots could bring an asteroid close enough for them to get there in just a month.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 重新安排天体的位置也许显得是一项过分庞大的工程，但这项美国任务自有其优点。美国已经计划把宇航员送往一颗近地小行星；这项任务意味着要把他们限制在一个狭小太空舱中3至6个月，还会面临深空航行的全部风险。另一种办法是由机器人把小行星带得足够近，让宇航员只需一个月便能到达。

translation.text: 重新安排天体的位置也许显得是一项过分庞大的工程，但这项美国任务自有其优点。

source.text: Instead, robots could bring an asteroid close enough for them to get there in just a month.

translation.text: 另一种办法是由机器人把小行星带得足够近，让宇航员只需一个月便能到达。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: An asteroid would provide a stationary base from which to launch missions further into space. There are several advantages to this. For one, launching missions carrying materials from Earth requires a lot of power, fuel and, consequently, money, because of our planet’s strong force of gravity. Since this would be far weaker on an asteroid, materials mined there could be more easily taken off the asteroid and shuttled around the solar system.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 小行星可以提供一个固定基地，从那里发射任务，前往更遥远的太空。这有几项优势。首先，由于地球引力强大，从地球发射携带物资的任务需要大量动力和燃料，因而也需要大量资金。小行星上的引力要弱得多，因此在那里开采的材料可以更轻松地运离小行星，再转运到太阳系各处。

source.text: An asteroid would provide a stationary base from which to launch missions further into space.

translation.text: 小行星可以提供一个固定基地，从那里发射任务，前往更遥远的太空。

source.text: There are several advantages to this.

translation.text: 这有几项优势。

source.text: For one, launching missions carrying materials from Earth requires a lot of power, fuel and, consequently, money, because of our planet’s strong force of gravity.

translation.text: 首先，由于地球引力强大，从地球发射携带物资的任务需要大量动力和燃料，因而也需要大量资金。

source.text: Since this would be far weaker on an asteroid, materials mined there could be more easily taken off the asteroid and shuttled around the solar system.

translation.text: 小行星上的引力要弱得多，因此在那里开采的材料可以更轻松地运离小行星，再转运到太阳系各处。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Many asteroids have a lot to offer. Some are rich in metals, which can be mined and used to build space-based habitats, or brought back to Earth. Others are up to one-quarter water, which could be used for life-support or broken down into hydrogen and oxygen to make fuel. Astronomers would also have the chance to get a close-up look at one of the solar system’s earliest relics, generating important scientific data. ‘Executing the asteroid-retrieval plan would help demonstrate and greatly expand mankind’s space-based engineering capabilities,’ says engineer Louis Friedman, another co-organiser of the Caltech workshop. For instance, the mission would teach engineers how to capture an unco-operative target, which could be useful practice for planetary-defence missions in the event of a threat from a meteoroid or comet approaching our planet,’ he adds.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 许多小行星拥有大量可利用资源。有些富含金属，可以开采后用于建造太空居住设施，或运回地球。另一些小行星含水量高达四分之一，这些水既可以用于维持生命，也可以分解成氢和氧来制造燃料。天文学家还将有机会近距离观察太阳系最早期的遗存之一，获取重要科学数据。加州理工学院研讨会的另一位共同组织者、工程师 Louis Friedman 说：“执行小行星回收计划，将有助于展示并大幅提升人类的太空工程能力。”他还说，例如，这项任务可以教会工程师如何捕获一个不配合的目标；如果有流星体或彗星接近地球并构成威胁，这会成为行星防御任务的实用演练。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Former astronaut Rusty Schweickart, co-founder of the B612 Foundation, an organisation dedicated to protecting Earth from asteroid strikes, points out that although it would be technically feasible, shifting such a hefty and substantial target would not be easy: ‘You’re moving the largest mother-lode imaginable,’ he says.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 前宇航员 Rusty Schweickart 是B612基金会的共同创办人，该组织致力于保护地球免遭小行星撞击。他指出，尽管从技术上看此事可行，要移动如此沉重庞大的目标却并不容易。他说：“你要移动的是能够想象到的最大矿藏。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Still, these obstacles only add to the appeal of the project for engineers, who love to go over every potential difficulty in order to solve it. And if the challenges posed by a large asteroid seem too daunting, researchers could always start with a smaller asteroid, perhaps two to ten metres across. Last year, Brophy helped conduct a study to look at the feasibility of bringing a two-metre, 1 000-kilogram asteroid — of which there might conceivably be millions — to the International Space Station. The study suggested the asteroid could be captured robotically in something as simple as a large bag. Of course, such a small object might not have the same emotional impact as a larger target. ‘NASA isn’t going to want to go to something that is smaller than our spaceships,’ says engineer Dan Mazanek from NASA’s Langley Research Center.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，这些障碍只会增加项目对工程师的吸引力，因为他们喜欢逐一研究每一种潜在困难，再设法解决。如果大型小行星带来的挑战显得过于艰巨，研究人员随时可以从较小的小行星入手，也许选择一颗直径2至10米的目标。去年，布罗菲协助开展了一项研究，考察把一颗直径2米、重1000公斤的小行星带到国际空间站是否可行；这样的目标可能有数百万颗。研究表明，机器人或许只需一个大袋子那么简单的装置，就能捕获这颗小行星。当然，这么小的物体可能无法像较大目标那样激动人心。美国国家航空航天局兰利研究中心工程师 Dan Mazanek 说：“美国国家航空航天局不会愿意前往一个比我们的飞船还小的东西。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: No matter the size of the asteroid, these plans would require hefty investments. Even capturing a small asteroid would consume at least a billion dollars. Convincing taxpayers to foot such a bill could be difficult. However, private industry might be interested in getting involved. One possibility would be to push the asteroid into near-Earth orbit and then invite anyone who wants to develop the capabilities to reach and mine the object.

source.text: The Power of Smell

translation.text: 嗅觉的力量

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Research shows that our olfactory sense is more influential than we realise

source.text: Research shows that our olfactory sense is more influential than we realise

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Dogs’ noses are renowned for sensitivity to smells, while human noses are thought to be poor by comparison, yet that might be a misconception. According to recent studies, our noses are in fact acutely sensitive instruments that guide our everyday lives to a surprising extent. Subtle smells can change your mood, behaviour and the choices you make, often without you realising it. Our own odours, meanwhile, indicate emotional states such as fear or sadness to those around us. The big mystery is why we aren’t more aware of our nasal activity. Noses have certainly never been at the forefront of sensory research, and were pushed aside until recently in favour of the seemingly more vital senses of vision and hearing. ‘There has been a lot of prejudice that people are not that influenced by olfactory stimuli, especially compared to other mammals,’ says Lilianne Mujica-Parodi, who studies the neurobiology of human stress at Stony Brook University in New York, in the United States.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 狗鼻子对气味的敏感性广为人知，相比之下，人们认为人类鼻子的嗅觉很差，但这或许是一种误解。近期研究显示，我们的鼻子其实是极其敏锐的感知工具，对日常生活的引导作用大得出人意料。细微的气味能够改变人的情绪、行为和所作选择，而当事人往往毫无察觉。与此同时，我们自身的气味也会向周围的人传达恐惧或悲伤等情绪状态。最大的谜团在于，我们为何没有更清楚地意识到自身的嗅觉活动。鼻子从来都不是感觉研究的重点；直到最近，它还一直让位于视觉和听觉，因为后两者看似更加重要。研究人类压力神经生物学的 Lilianne Mujica-Parodi 任职于美国纽约石溪大学。她说：“人们长期抱有偏见，认为嗅觉刺激对人类的影响没有那么大，尤其是与其他哺乳动物相比时。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One of the first people to assert the relative unimportance of human smelling was Pierre Paul Broca, an influential 19th-century anatomist. After comparing the proportion of the brain devoted to smell in different animals, he suggested that mammals can be classed into two broad groups: macrosmatic mammals, such as dogs, have a finely tuned sense of smell which they rely on to perceive the world, while we, along with other primates and the marine mammals, are microsmatic – we have small olfactory organs that we only rely on to a small extent. That idea seemed to fit with more recent studies which found that the majority of mammals have genes coding for about 1000 different types of smell receptor. Most of these genes aren’t expressed in humans, giving our noses just 400 different types of receptor.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 最早主张人类嗅觉相对不重要的人之一，是19世纪颇具影响力的解剖学家 Pierre Paul Broca。他比较了不同动物大脑中用于嗅觉的部分所占比例，提出哺乳动物大致可以分为两类：狗等嗅觉发达型动物（macrosmatic mammals）拥有十分敏锐的嗅觉，并依靠它感知世界；而人类与其他灵长类动物和海洋哺乳动物一样，属于嗅觉弱化型（microsmatic），嗅觉器官较小，对它的依赖程度也很低。这一观点似乎与较新的研究结果吻合：大多数哺乳动物都有编码约1,000种不同嗅觉受体的基因。人类体内的大部分此类基因并不表达，因此我们的鼻子只有400种不同受体。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Yet these findings may have been misleading. Brain scans now show that more of the brain is devoted to smell processing than Broca’s anatomical studies suggested. And although we may have fewer types of receptor than other mammals, Charles Greer at Yale University in the United States has shown that the human nose and brain are unusually well connected, with each group of receptors linking to many more neural regions than is the case in other animals. That should give us a good ability to process incoming scents. Once researchers began looking, they found the nose to be far more sensitive than its reputation suggested. One study, for example, found that we can detect certain chemicals diluted in water to less than one part per billion. That means that a person can detect just a few drops of a strong smell like ethyl mercaptan in an Olympic-sized pool.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，这些发现可能具有误导性。如今的脑部扫描显示，大脑中用于处理嗅觉的部分比布罗卡的解剖学研究所表明的更多。美国耶鲁大学的 Charles Greer 还证明，尽管人类的受体种类可能少于其他哺乳动物，但人类鼻子与大脑之间的连接异常紧密：每组受体连接的神经区域远多于其他动物。这应当使我们具备良好的气味处理能力。研究人员一旦开始仔细考察，就发现鼻子的敏感程度远远超过其名声所显示的水平。例如，一项研究发现，我们能够检测出水中稀释至十亿分之一以下浓度的某些化学物质。也就是说，在奥运会标准泳池中，只需加入几滴乙硫醇这样气味强烈的物质，人就能察觉。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: ‘We are also exceptionally gifted at telling smells apart, even in the case of two molecules whose only difference is that their structures are mirror images of one another. That is fantastic sensitivity,’ says George Dodd, a perfumer and researcher at the olfaction group of the University of Warwick, in the United Kingdom. What’s more, it’s becoming clear that the brain’s olfactory centres are intimately linked to its limbic system, which is involved in emotion, fear and memory. That suggests a link between smell and the way we think.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The power of smell will be no news to estate agents, who often advocate the smell of baking bread or brewing coffee to promote the sale of a house. But there are more subtle and surprising effects too. When Hendrik Schifferstein and colleagues, from Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands, pumped the smell of orange, seawater or peppermint into a nightclub, the revellers danced more, rated their night as more enjoyable, and even thought the music was better than when there was no added scent. Meanwhile, Rob Holland, of the University of Utrecht in the Netherlands, found that the hint of aroma wafting out of a hidden bucket of citrus-scented cleaner was enough to persuade students in a hostel to clean up after themselves.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 嗅觉的力量对房产经纪人来说并不新鲜，他们常建议用烤面包或煮咖啡的香味来促进房屋销售。不过，气味还有一些更加微妙、出人意料的作用。荷兰代尔夫特理工大学的 Hendrik Schifferstein 及其同事把橙子、海水或薄荷的气味送入一家夜总会，结果欢聚的人们跳舞更多，认为当晚更加愉快，甚至觉得音乐也比没有添加气味时更好。与此同时，荷兰乌得勒支大学的 Rob Holland 发现，一个隐藏水桶中的柑橘香清洁剂散发出的淡淡气味，就足以促使宿舍里的学生自行收拾干净。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Other work has found that scent can influence our cognitive skills. A study by William Overman and colleagues at the University of North Carolina in the United States found that when men were subjected to a novel smell – either good or bad – during a task used to test decision-making skills, they performed significantly worse than normal. The researchers conclude the scent stimulated brain areas connected with emotion, making their decisions emotional rather than rational.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 其他研究发现，气味还会影响认知能力。美国北卡罗来纳大学的 William Overman 及其同事开展了一项研究：男性在进行一项测试决策能力的任务时，如果闻到一种陌生气味，无论好闻还是难闻，表现都会显著低于正常水平。研究人员得出结论，气味刺激了与情绪有关的脑区，使他们的决定偏向感性，而非理性。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Smells are especially good memory evokers, but it is actually a myth that odours trigger more detailed memories than other stimuli. ‘The memory is not more accurate and you don’t remember more details,’ says Yaara Yeshurun at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot, Israel, ‘but it is unique in that it is more emotional.’ This isn’t surprising when you consider that there are certain brain areas dedicated to both emotion and olfaction, such as the amygdala, and there is a strong link between emotion and memory. In 2009, Yeshurun found that the link between a memory and a smell is stronger if the smell is unpleasant rather than pleasant. She also discovered that the very first time we attach a smell to an object, it evokes a much greater response in our brains than for any subsequent encounter with the smell or object, laying down stronger foundations for the memory. That doesn’t happen with any other sense. Since those first encounters with a smell would have happened at a young age, this explains why smells often transport us back to our childhood.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 气味特别容易唤起记忆，但认为气味比其他刺激能触发更详细记忆的说法其实是误区。以色列雷霍沃特魏茨曼科学研究所的 Yaara Yeshurun 说：“记忆并不会更准确，人们也不会想起更多细节；其独特之处在于，它带有更强烈的情绪。”考虑到杏仁核等某些脑区同时参与情绪和嗅觉活动，而且情绪与记忆密切相关，这一点并不奇怪。2009年，Yeshurun 发现，如果气味令人不快，它与记忆之间的联系会比气味宜人时更强。她还发现，我们第一次把某种气味与某个物体联系起来时，大脑产生的反应远大于后来任何一次再次接触这种气味或物体时的反应，因而为记忆打下更牢固的基础。其他任何感官都不会出现这种情况。人们最初接触某种气味时通常年纪尚小，这就解释了为什么气味经常把我们带回童年。

translation.text: 其他任何感官都不会出现这种情况。

source.text: Since those first encounters with a smell would have happened at a young age, this explains why smells often transport us back to our childhood.

translation.text: 人们最初接触某种气味时通常年纪尚小，这就解释了为什么气味经常把我们带回童年。

source.text: The problem of graffiti

translation.text: 涂鸦问题

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Is it art? Or is it a crime?

source.text: Is it art? Or is it a crime?

translation.text: 它是艺术，还是犯罪？

independentReview.reason: 人工逐句复核确认：当前显式分组与语义边界一致，覆盖完整连续，不依赖模糊猜配，原文与译文均未改动。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The term ‘graffiti’ derives from the Italian word graffio meaning ‘scratching’, and can be defined as uninvited markings or writing scratched or applied to objects, built structures, and natural features. It is not a new phenomenon; examples can be found on ancient structures around the world, in some cases predating the Greeks and Romans. In such circumstances, it has acquired invaluable historical and archaeological significance as it provides a social history of life and events at that time. This is not true of more recent graffiti, which has become a pervasive problem particularly over the last 50 years, as a result of the availability of cheap and quick means of mark-making. These include the ubiquitous spray paints.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: “涂鸦”一词源自意大利语 graffio，意为“刮划”，可以定义为：未经邀请，在物品、人工构筑物和自然景观上刻画或添加的标记或文字。涂鸦并非新现象；世界各地的古代建筑上都能找到实例，有些甚至早于古希腊和古罗马时期。在这种情况下，涂鸦具有极其宝贵的历史和考古意义，因为它记录了当时生活和事件的社会史。较近时期的涂鸦却并非如此。尤其在过去50年里，廉价而快捷的留痕工具日益普及，涂鸦因此成为无处不在的问题，其中就包括随处可见的喷漆。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Graffitists, the people who are responsible for creating graffiti, are indiscriminate about the surfaces they choose. Wherever graffiti appears, it is usually considered a priority to remove it as quickly as possible. One reason for this is to prevent ‘copy-cat’ emulation, which can occur rapidly once a clean surface is defaced, and so many companies and councils have a policy of removing graffiti within an hour or two of it being reported. Another reason is that as paints, glues, and inks dry out, they can become increasingly difficult to remove. A more important factor, however, is that graffiti can lead to more serious forms of vandalism and, ultimately, to the deterioration of a neighborhood area, and in this way contributes to a general social decline. For this reason, the police like to be notified of new graffiti incidents. To aid in achieving a successful prosecution, they encourage owners of properties to take photographs of any new graffiti, as there could be other related incidents occurring locally. An incidence pattern can help to identify possible culprits, as can their ‘tag’—the distinctive mark graffitists leave to show the graffiti is their work.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Any proposal to remove graffiti has to be carefully considered because techniques designed for robust or utilitarian surfaces may result in considerable damage to older, more historic buildings. Consequently, as no two sites are the same, there is no one treatment which will be suitable for all situations; each site must be looked at individually. The owners of some graffiti-affected sites may wish to attempt their own treatment, whereas others may prefer to contact a specialist contractor. However, whichever course is decided on, it is important to follow a systematic approach. The first step is to carry out cleaning trials to see which method is suitable for the removal of the graffiti media used, and also which method has the least impact on the site surface. These trials should be carried out on a small unobtrusive area if possible and should always start with the least aggressive cleaning method, usually water, and stop once a successful method has been found.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 任何清除涂鸦的方案都必须慎重考虑，因为针对坚固或实用型表面设计的技术，可能会严重损坏年代较久、更具历史价值的建筑。因此，既然没有两个地点完全相同，也就没有一种处理方法适用于所有情况；每个地点都必须单独考察。有些受涂鸦影响地点的业主可能希望自行处理，另一些则可能更愿意联系专业承包商。然而，无论选择哪一种做法，都应遵循系统化流程。第一步是开展清洁试验，判断哪种方法适合清除所用的涂鸦材料，同时确定哪种方法对现场表面影响最小。如果可能，试验应在一小块不显眼的区域进行，而且始终要从侵蚀性最低的清洁方式开始，通常先用水；一旦找到有效方法，就应停止试验。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Apart from water, a variety of methods can be used to remove graffiti; broadly, these are divided into chemical and mechanical systems. When using either of these systems, care must be taken with regard to protecting both passers-by and the person carrying out the graffiti removal. Chemical preparations are based on dissolving the graffiti media; these solvents can range from mild to potentially dangerous chemical ‘cocktails’. When using chemicals, it is important to wear protective clothing, take measures to minimize any run-off of potentially harmful chemicals, and avoid the drifting of aerial mists. Mechanical systems are often in the form of wire-brushing and grit blasting, which attempt to chip off the graffiti media. Operators of mechanical systems must also wear protective clothing to avoid being hurt by hard airborne particles. This method often leaves marks on a surface.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 除水以外，还有多种方法可以清除涂鸦，大致分为化学系统和机械系统。使用任何一种系统时，都必须注意保护路人和清除涂鸦的操作人员。化学制剂通过溶解涂鸦材料发挥作用；这类溶剂既可能很温和，也可能是具有潜在危险的化学“混合剂”。使用化学品时，必须穿戴防护服，采取措施尽量减少可能有害的化学品流淌外泄，并防止雾状颗粒飘散。机械系统通常采用钢丝刷洗和喷砂，试图把涂鸦材料从表面剥落。机械系统操作人员同样必须穿戴防护服，以免被空气中的坚硬颗粒击伤。这种方法往往会在表面留下痕迹。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Different measures can be adopted to combat a recurring problem of graffiti. It is clear that protection measures will ultimately be more successful and less damaging than multiple removal treatments. Popular places for graffiti are often readily accessible flat surfaces where the graffiti will have an instant impact, but this is not always the case, and graffitists may scale bridges to give their work greater prominence. Possible protection measures may include a combination of floodlighting to illuminate dark areas and surveillance systems such as closed-circuit television. Research has shown that prominently placed cameras can reduce the incidence of graffiti in areas with a recurring problem. Unfortunately, the cost of any of these measures may be too high, and so physical obstacles such as fences, railings, doors, or gates can be introduced to discourage unauthorized access, though in some cases, these obstacles simply provide a new surface for graffiti.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 对于反复出现的涂鸦问题，可以采取不同措施加以应对。显然，与多次清除相比，保护措施最终会更有效，对表面的损害也更小。容易到达、能让涂鸦立刻引人注目的平坦表面，往往是涂鸦的热门地点，但情况并非总是如此；涂鸦者也可能爬上桥梁，让作品更加醒目。可采用的保护措施可能包括泛光照明与监控系统的组合：前者照亮黑暗区域，后者可使用闭路电视等设备。研究表明，在反复发生涂鸦的地区，把摄像头放在显眼位置能够减少涂鸦事件。遗憾的是，这些措施的成本可能过高，因此可以设置围栏、栏杆、门或大门等实体障碍，阻止未经许可的人员进入。不过在某些情况下，这些障碍反而只是为涂鸦提供了新的表面。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Another strategy is to apply a removable anti-graffiti barrier-coating as a form of preventive measure. Although this will not stop graffiti being applied, it will make its removal much easier and usually only involves using water, which reduces the possibility of damage to the site surface. Barrier coatings are usually applied by brush or spray, leaving a thin veneer that essentially serves to isolate the graffiti from the surface. So, although there is no prescription for dealing with every graffiti incident, there are some steps that can be taken to minimize the impact of graffiti and to protect vulnerable surfaces.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 另一种策略是涂上一层可移除的防涂鸦隔离涂层，作为预防措施。虽然它无法阻止人们留下涂鸦，却会使清除工作容易得多，而且通常只需用水，从而降低损坏现场表面的可能性。隔离涂层通常用刷子涂刷或喷涂，形成一层薄膜，实质上把涂鸦与表面隔开。因此，虽然没有适用于每起涂鸦事件的统一处理方案，人们仍可采取一些步骤，尽量减少涂鸦的影响，并保护容易受损的表面。

source.text: The Return of Monkey Life

translation.text: 猴群归来

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Rain-forest trees growing anew on Central American farmland are helping scientists find ways for monkey and agriculture to benefit one another.
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 中美洲农田上重新生长的雨林树木，正帮助科学家寻找让猴类与农业相互受益的方法。

source.text: Rain-forest trees growing anew on Central American farmland are helping scientists find ways for monkey and agriculture to benefit one another.

translation.text: 中美洲农田上重新生长的雨林树木，正帮助科学家寻找让猴类与农业相互受益的方法。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Hacienda La Pacifica, a remote working cattle ranch in Guanacaste Province of northern Costa Rica, has for decades been home to a community of mantled howler monkeys. Other native primates—white-faced capuchin monkeys and spider monkeys—were once common in this area too, but vanished after the Pan-American Highway was built nearby in the 1950s and most of the surrounding land was cleared for cattle-raising. At Hacienda La Pacifica, however, an enlightened ranch owner chose to leave some strips of native trees growing. He used these as windbreaks to protect both cattle and their food crops from dry-season winds. In the process, the farmer unwittingly founded a unique laboratory for the study of monkeys.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: La Pacifica 庄园是哥斯达黎加北部瓜纳卡斯特省一座偏远的经营性养牛场，几十年来一直生活着一个披风吼猴群体。白面卷尾猴和蜘蛛猴等其他本土灵长类动物，过去在这一地区也很常见；但20世纪50年代附近建成泛美公路、周边大部分土地被清理用于养牛后，它们便消失了。不过，La Pacifica 庄园一位开明的农场主选择保留几条生长着本土树木的地带。他把这些树带用作防风林，在旱季的风中保护牛群及其饲料作物。这个过程中，他无意间建立了一座研究猴类的独特实验室。

translation.text: La Pacifica 庄园是哥斯达黎加北部瓜纳卡斯特省一座偏远的经营性养牛场，几十年来一直生活着一个披风吼猴群体。

source.text: Other native primates—white-faced capuchin monkeys and spider monkeys—were once common in this area too, but vanished after the Pan-American Highway was built nearby in the 1950s and most of the surrounding land was cleared for cattle-raising.

translation.text: 白面卷尾猴和蜘蛛猴等其他本土灵长类动物，过去在这一地区也很常见；但20世纪50年代附近建成泛美公路、周边大部分土地被清理用于养牛后，它们便消失了。

source.text: At Hacienda La Pacifica, however, an enlightened ranch owner chose to leave some strips of native trees growing.

translation.text: 不过，La Pacifica 庄园一位开明的农场主选择保留几条生长着本土树木的地带。

source.text: He used these as windbreaks to protect both cattle and their food crops from dry-season winds.

translation.text: 他把这些树带用作防风林，在旱季的风中保护牛群及其饲料作物。

source.text: In the process, the farmer unwittingly founded a unique laboratory for the study of monkeys.

translation.text: 这个过程中，他无意间建立了一座研究猴类的独特实验室。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Ken Glander, a primatologist from Duke University in the USA, is studying La Pacifica’s monkeys in an effort to understand the relationship between howlers and regenerating forests at the edges of grazing lands. Studying such disturbed woodlands is increasingly important because throughout much of the New World Tropics, these are the only forests left. In the 18th century, tropical dry forests once covered most of Central America, but by the 1980s less than two percent remained undisturbed, and less than one percent was protected.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 美国杜克大学灵长类动物学家 Ken Glander 正在研究 La Pacifica 的猴群，希望了解吼猴与牧场边缘再生森林之间的关系。研究这种受过干扰的林地日益重要，因为在新大陆热带地区的许多地方，它们是仅存的森林。18世纪时，热带干旱森林曾覆盖中美洲大部分地区；但到20世纪80年代，保持原状的面积已不足2%，受到保护的面积更不足1%。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Howlers persist at La Pacifica, Glander explains, because they are leaf-eaters. They eat fruit when it is available but, unlike capuchin and spider monkeys, do not depend on large areas of fruiting trees. Glander is particularly interested in howlers’ ability to thrive on leaves loaded with toxins—poisonous substances designed to protect the plants. For leaf-eaters, long-term exposure to a specific plant toxin can increase their ability to neutralise the poisonous substances and absorb the leaf nutrients. Watching generations of howlers at La Pacifica has shown Glander that the monkeys keep their systems primed by sampling a variety of plants and then focusing on a small number of the most nutritious food items. The leaves that grow in regenerating forests, like those at La Pacifica, are actually more howler-friendly than those produced by the centuries-old trees that survive farther south. In younger forests, trees put most of their limited energy into growing wood, leaves and fruit, so they produce much lower levels of toxin than do well-established, old-growth trees.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Glander 解释说，吼猴之所以能在 La Pacifica 延续下来，是因为它们以树叶为食。有水果时，它们也会吃，但与卷尾猴和蜘蛛猴不同，它们不依赖大片结果的树林。Glander 特别关注吼猴靠含有大量毒素的树叶生存的能力；这些有毒物质是植物用来保护自己的。对食叶动物来说，长期接触某种特定植物毒素，可以增强中和有毒物质并吸收叶片养分的能力。Glander 观察了 La Pacifica 数代吼猴，发现它们会取食多种植物，使自身系统保持应对毒素的状态，随后集中食用少数营养最丰富的食物。La Pacifica 这类再生森林中长出的树叶，实际上比南面那些存活了数百年的古树所长树叶更适合吼猴。较年轻森林里的树木把有限能量大多用于生长木质部分、叶片和果实，因此产生的毒素远少于根基稳固的原始林老树。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The value of maturing forests to primates is also a subject of study at Santa Rosa National Park, about 35 miles northwest of La Pacifica. Large areas of Santa Rosa’s forests had at one time been burnt to make space for cattle ranching and coffee farming, thereby devastating local monkey habitat. But in 1971 the government protected the area by designating it a national park, and species of indigenous trees which had been absent for decades began to invade the abandoned pastures. Capuchins were the first to begin using the reborn forests, followed by howlers. Eventually, even spider monkeys, fruit-eaters that need large areas of continuous forest, returned. In the first 28 years following protection of the area, the capuchin population doubled, while the number of howlers increased seven-fold.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 正在成熟的森林对灵长类动物有何价值，也是圣罗莎国家公园的一项研究课题。该公园位于 La Pacifica 西北约35英里处。圣罗莎的大片森林一度遭焚烧，以便为养牛和咖啡种植腾出空间，当地猴类栖息地因此受到毁灭性破坏。但1971年，政府把该地区划为国家公园加以保护；消失数十年的本土树种开始进入废弃牧场。卷尾猴最先开始利用重生的森林，随后是吼猴。最终，就连需要大片连片森林的食果蜘蛛猴也回来了。该地区受到保护后的最初28年里，卷尾猴种群扩大了一倍，吼猴数量则增长到原来的七倍。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Some of the same traits that allow howlers to survive at La Pacifica also explain their population boom in Santa Rosa. Howler reproduction is faster than that of other native monkey species. They give birth for the first time at about 3.5 years of age, compared with seven years for capuchins, and eight or more for spider monkeys. Also, while a female spider monkey will have a baby about once every four years, well-fed howlers can produce an infant every two years. Another factor is diet. Howlers are very adaptable feeders and need only a comparatively small home range. Spider monkeys, on the other hand, need to occupy a huge home range. Also crucial is the fact that the leaves howlers eat hold plenty of water, so the monkeys can survive away from open streams and water-holes. This ability gives them a real advantage over capuchin and spider monkeys, which have suffered during the long, ongoing drought in the area.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 吼猴得以在 La Pacifica 生存的若干特征，也能解释它们的种群为何在圣罗莎迅速扩大。吼猴的繁殖速度比其他本土猴类更快。它们约3.5岁时首次产仔，而卷尾猴要到7岁，蜘蛛猴则要到8岁或更晚。此外，雌性蜘蛛猴大约每4年才产一只幼仔，食物充足的吼猴却能每2年产一只。另一个因素是饮食。吼猴的取食适应性很强，只需相对较小的活动范围；蜘蛛猴则需要极大的活动范围。同样关键的是，吼猴所吃的树叶含有充足水分，因此它们即使远离溪流和水塘也能生存。这项能力让它们比卷尾猴和蜘蛛猴拥有明显优势；后两种猴一直受到当地漫长且仍在持续的干旱影响。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Alejandro Estrada, an ecologist at Estación de Biología Los Tuxtlas in Veracruz, Mexico, has been studying the ecology of a group of howler monkeys that thrive in a habitat totally altered by humans: a cacao plantation in Tabasco State, Mexico. Cacao plants need shade to grow, so 40 years ago the owners of Cholula Cacao Farm planted figs, monkey-pod and other tall trees to form a protective canopy over their crop. The howlers moved in about 25 years ago after nearby forests were cut. This strange habitat seems to support about as many monkeys as would a same-sized patch of wild forest. The howlers eat the leaves and fruit of the shade trees, leaving the valuable cacao pods alone.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 墨西哥韦拉克鲁斯州 Los Tuxtlas 生物学站的生态学家 Alejandro Estrada，一直在研究一群生活在完全由人类改造的栖息地中的吼猴：墨西哥塔巴斯科州的一座可可种植园。可可植株需要遮阴才能生长，因此40年前，Cholula 可可农场的业主种植了无花果树、雨树和其他高大树木，在作物上方形成保护性树冠。附近森林被砍伐后，吼猴于大约25年前迁入。这个奇特栖息地所容纳的猴子数量，似乎与同等面积的野生森林大致相当。吼猴吃遮阴树的叶片和果实，却不碰价值很高的可可豆荚。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Estrada believes the monkeys bring under-appreciated benefits to such plantations, dispersing the seeds of fruits such as fig and other shade trees, and fertilising the soil. Spider monkeys also forage for fruit here, though they need nearby areas of forest to survive in the long term. He hopes that farmers will begin to see the advantages of associating with wild monkeys, which could include potential ecotourism projects. ‘Conservation is usually viewed as a conflict between farming practices and the need to preserve nature,’ Estrada says. ‘We’re moving away from that vision and beginning to consider ways in which commercial activities may become a tool for the conservation of primates in human-modified landscapes.’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Estrada 认为，猴类会给这类种植园带来未获充分认识的好处，包括传播无花果等果树和其他遮阴树的种子，以及给土壤施肥。蜘蛛猴也会来这里觅食水果，不过从长远看，它们需要附近有森林才能生存。他希望农民开始看到与野生猴类共处的益处，其中可能包括潜在的生态旅游项目。Estrada 说：“人们通常把自然保护视为农业生产方式与保护自然需要之间的冲突。我们正在摆脱这种看法，开始思考如何让商业活动成为一种工具，用来保护人类改造景观中的灵长类动物。”

passages.title: The return of the black-footed ferret

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: The return of the black-footed ferret

source.text: The return of the black-footed ferret

translation.text: 黑足鼬归来

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: The rise, fall, and rise of one of North America’s rarest mammals
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 北美洲最稀有哺乳动物之一的兴起、衰落与复兴

source.text: The rise, fall, and rise of one of North America’s rarest mammals

translation.text: 北美洲最稀有哺乳动物之一的兴起、衰落与复兴

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The black-footed ferret (Mustela nigripes) is a small carnivorous mammal, similar in length to a domestic cat, and is the only ferret species native to North America. For at least 100,000 years they lived in an area that extended almost uninterrupted from southern Canada to northern Mexico. But numbers fell dramatically throughout the 19th and 20th centuries, to such an extent that the black-footed ferret was declared ‘possibly extinct’. Then, almost miraculously, it returned from the dead.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 黑足鼬（Mustela nigripes）是一种小型食肉哺乳动物，体长与家猫相近，也是唯一原生于北美洲的鼬种。至少10万年来，它们生活在一片从加拿大南部延伸到墨西哥北部、几乎连成一体的区域。然而，19和20世纪期间，黑足鼬数量急剧下降，以至于被宣布“可能已经灭绝”。随后，它几乎奇迹般地死而复生。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Within the genus Mustela, the ferret belongs to the subgenus Putorius, of which there are only three extant species: the European polecat; the Siberian polecat; and the black-footed ferret. The European polecat lives in open forests and meadows, and is thought to be the ancestor of the domestic ferret. The Siberian polecat looks more similar to the black-footed ferret, and leads a similar life on open grasslands and semi-desert regions across Russia, China and Siberia.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Ferrets probably evolved in Europe between three and four million years ago, and dispersed into North America across an ice-age land bridge at least two million years ago. They then advanced south-eastward to the Great Plains through ice-free passageways. The black-footed ferret’s history in North America is inextricably linked to the creature which became almost its sole prey — the prairie dog. These small rodents are a type of ground squirrel which live in networks of underground tunnels, known as burrows. The black-footed ferret’s short legs and long, slim body make it superbly adapted for life in the burrow systems of its prey.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Spending virtually all their time underground, black-footed ferrets have always been elusive. Ferrets are never mentioned in accounts of the early explorers or pioneers who crossed the Great Plains by wagon train during the early to mid-1800s. They were, however, occasionally listed in records kept by fur companies in the upper Missouri River basin during that period. Black-footed ferrets were not officially recognized by scientists until 1851, when a description and drawing of one featured in a book by the renowned naturalist John James Audubon and Reverend John Bachman. For over two decades, no other specimens were seen, and scientists even began to question their existence. Then, in 1874, a Dr Elliott Coues issued a request for specimens through the popular magazine The American Sportsman, and was soon rewarded. With these he was able to add to Audubon’s description, and confirm the existence of the black-footed ferret.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In the decades that followed, European settlement across North America changed the landscape dramatically, with vast areas being transformed into crop and grazing land. As agriculture and ranching expanded, the black-footed ferret’s main prey, the prairie dog, became a target for extermination, and was eventually eradicated from 98% of its original range. The result was devastating for black-footed ferret populations throughout the continent. Even today, the prairie dog is still trapped and poisoned, because ranchers believe that it competes with livestock for grass — a notion that belies recent research showing that prairie dogs and cattle feed on different plants.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 随后数十年，欧洲移民在北美洲各地定居，极大改变了当地景观，大片土地被改造成农田和牧场。随着农业和畜牧业扩张，黑足鼬的主要猎物草原犬鼠成为根除目标，最终从原分布范围的98%中消失。整个北美洲的黑足鼬种群因此遭受毁灭性打击。即使今天，人们仍在捕捉和毒杀草原犬鼠，因为牧场主认为它会与牲畜争食牧草；然而，近期研究表明，草原犬鼠与牛所吃的植物并不相同，这一结果与上述观念相矛盾。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As late as the 1950s, black-footed ferrets were still thought to occur in low densities throughout most of their historic range. However, by the 1960s, the only known population was a small colony in south-western South Dakota. In 1967, the US Fish and Wildlife Service classified the black-footed ferret as an endangered species, and in 1974 the South Dakota colony disappeared. Finally, in January 1979, the last ferret in a captive-breeding programme died — making the black-footed ferret the first mammal to be declared extinct in the Northern Hemisphere in the 20th century.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But that was not the end of the story. In 1981, a farm dog called Shep carried an odd-looking creature to its owner’s ranch house in Meeteetse, Wyoming. The rancher put the carcass in his fridge and alerted state officials. The dog had found a black-footed ferret — which led to efforts again being made to save the species. An intensive search in the region led to the discovery of a 130-strong population. This wild colony thrived for a while, but disaster struck again and the number of animals was drastically reduced by the disease distemper — probably contracted from domestic dogs. In 1985, in a final bid to save the species, the remaining 18 individuals in the colony were trapped for a new captive-breeding programme. This project was successful, and there are now more than 2,000 black-footed ferrets in captivity across the US and Canada.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A reintroduction programme began in 1991. Before they can be reintroduced into their natural habitat, captive ferrets have to learn to hunt and escape from predators. They are first held in pens on the prairie, where they are fed prairie dog meat. Once the ferrets associate these animals with food, keepers unleash live prey into the pens, and they soon realise that they must hunt or go hungry. Then, to get the ferrets used to living underground, they have to be tempted into the holes with food.

source.text: The Tasmanian Tiger

translation.text: 塔斯马尼亚虎

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The Tasmanian tiger, or thylacine, was a carnivorous marsupial (a meat-eating mammal which carries its young in a pouch). It was given the name ‘tiger’ because it had striped fur, and because it was ferocious. Between 24 million and 15 million years ago, many types of thylacine roamed across Australia, their powerful jaws playing a role in maintaining a balance in the ecosystems of their day. Some species were fox-sized, while others were barely the size of kittens.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 塔斯马尼亚虎又称袋狼，是一种食肉有袋类动物，也就是把幼崽带在育儿袋中的食肉哺乳动物。它因皮毛有条纹、性情凶猛而得名“虎”。2,400万至1,500万年前，许多种袋狼游荡在澳大利亚各地，强有力的颌部在维持当时生态系统平衡方面发挥作用。有些物种像狐狸一样大，另一些却只有小猫般大小。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But when a period of climate change cooled Australia about 12 million years ago, the numbers of these ancient thylacines began to decline. By about 3 million years ago, only one species was left. About 4,000 years ago, these vanished completely from the Australian mainland, so that Tasmania, a large island to the south of Australia, became the last remaining place where thylacines existed. They ruled the island’s animal life unchallenged until Europeans—with sheep, dogs and a great indifference to native flora and fauna—seem to have brought about their extinction. In 1936, the last captive Tasmanian tiger died in Hobart Zoo. Since then, many expeditions have searched for tigers in the Tasmanian bush, but no definitive evidence has been found. Despite this, there are many who keep searching.

source.text: But when a period of climate change cooled Australia about 12 million years ago, the numbers of these ancient thylacines began to decline.

translation.text: 到约300万年前，只剩下一个物种。

source.text: About 4,000 years ago, these vanished completely from the Australian mainland, so that Tasmania, a large island to the south of Australia, became the last remaining place where thylacines existed.

source.text: They ruled the island’s animal life unchallenged until Europeans—with sheep, dogs and a great indifference to native flora and fauna—seem to have brought about their extinction.

translation.text: 袋狼一直毫无对手地主宰岛上的动物世界，直到带着羊和狗、又对本土动植物极为漠视的欧洲人到来；看来正是他们造成了袋狼灭绝。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In 1981, Dutch-born zoologist Hans Naarding was in Tasmania conducting a survey of Latham’s snipe, a species of endangered bird. One night, he saw an animal in the light from the searchlight mounted on his vehicle. He described it as about the size of a large dog, but with slightly sloping hindquarters and a fairly thick tail continuing straight on from its backbone. He said that it had 12 distinct stripes on its back, running down to the point where the tail began. He reported the sighting to the Director of Tasmania’s National Parks. “When the news broke,” said Naarding, “I was besieged by television crews, including four or five from Japan, and others from the United Kingdom, Germany, New Zealand and South America.”

The tiger, as always, had escaped to its lair—a place that many insist exists only in the imagination. So is it out there? Even experts differ in opinion.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Randolph Rose, Associate Professor of Zoology at the University of Tasmania, says that he once dreamed of seeing a thylacine, but is now convinced that his dream will go unfulfilled. The consensus among conservationists is that any animal with a population base of less than 1,000 is headed for extinction within 60 years. “Sixty years ago,” he says, “there was only one thylacine that we know of, and that was in Hobart Zoo. Take it from me, the tiger is gone.” But Dr David Pemberton, curator of zoology at the Tasmanian Museum, states that, despite scientific thinking that a relatively large population is required to sustain a species, “the Florida panther is down to a dozen or so animals, and, while it does have some inbreeding problems, it’s still ticking along! After all, animals can be notoriously elusive. The strange fish known as the coelacanth, with its ‘proto legs,’ was thought to have died out with the dinosaurs 70 million years ago, until a specimen was dragged to the surface in a shark net off the coast of South Africa in 1938.”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Wildlife biologist Nick Mooney has the unenviable task of investigating all so-called sightings of the tiger. source.text: Understanding climate change

translation.text: 理解气候变化

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Could the writings of 18th-century sailors unlock the complexities of today’s climate changes?
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 18世纪水手的文字记录，能否帮助我们解开当今气候变化的复杂问题？

source.text: Could the writings of 18th-century sailors unlock the complexities of today’s climate changes?

translation.text: 18世纪水手的文字记录，能否帮助我们解开当今气候变化的复杂问题？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Are the climatic changes the world is seeing now really unprecedented, or have there been other times when change was just as swift? ‘If we go back to the past and find there really hasn’t been anything like this before, then that strengthens the case that human activity is responsible for the rapid changes we are seeing today,’ says climatologist Dennis Wheeler of the University of Sunderland, UK.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 世界如今正在经历的气候变化真的前所未有，还是过去也有过变化同样迅速的时期？英国桑德兰大学气候学家 Dennis Wheeler 说：“如果我们回顾过去，发现此前确实从未发生过这样的情况，就更能支持这样一种观点：人类活动要为我们今天看到的快速变化负责。”

source.text: Are the climatic changes the world is seeing now really unprecedented, or have there been other times when change was just as swift?

translation.text: 世界如今正在经历的气候变化真的前所未有，还是过去也有过变化同样迅速的时期？

source.text: ‘If we go back to the past and find there really hasn’t been anything like this before, then that strengthens the case that human activity is responsible for the rapid changes we are seeing today,’ says climatologist Dennis Wheeler of the University of Sunderland, UK.

translation.text: 英国桑德兰大学气候学家 Dennis Wheeler 说：“如果我们回顾过去，发现此前确实从未发生过这样的情况，就更能支持这样一种观点：人类活动要为我们今天看到的快速变化负责。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But the past is tricky territory for climatologists. While tree rings and ice cores chart annual changes in climate going back millennia, they cannot show what happened on a month-to-month basis. There are some long-running chronicles of temperature and air pressure over land dating back to the 17th century, but systematic records of air movements over the oceans — which govern most of our weather — were almost non-existent before the mid-19th century, by which time the Industrial Revolution was already well under way, and factory chimneys were pouring carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. In order to establish whether today’s climate changes indeed had any precedent in the past, what Wheeler needed was detailed information from earlier times, and he soon became convinced that the multitude of jottings in old ships’ records could provide just that.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: By the late 17th century, the seafaring nations of Europe had fleets of ships criss-crossing the seas, all keeping meticulous accounts of their voyages, including regular observations of weather conditions. In 1731, it became obligatory for British naval vessels to keep a detailed logbook, and by 1750 the practice was universal. A vast number of such records survive to this day. Despite initial reluctance among climatologists to use these historical documents for scientific research, Wheeler and his team secured funding for a project to sift through two thousand old logbooks. They pored over records of English, Dutch, French and Spanish fleets, with the aim of creating a climatological database for the world’s oceans between 1750 and 1850.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Harder still was interpreting observations on the strength of the wind. It was 1850 before most ships were equipped with accurate instruments to collect climatic data, previous to which officers had to rely on judgement and experience. And, as the numerical Beaufort scale of wind strength did not become official until 1838, most of the logbooks in Wheeler’s archives describe weather conditions using words alone — and often archaic or peculiar ones. A sample of English logs from 1685 to 1700 produced 73 different ways of describing the wind’s force. To everyone’s relief, closer scrutiny showed that many terms were used just once or twice: most log-keepers stuck to a similar set of terms.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 更困难的是解读风力观测记录。直到1850年，大多数船只才配备准确收集气候数据的仪器；此前，军官只能依靠判断和经验。数值化的蒲福风级到1838年才成为正式标准，因此 Wheeler 档案中的大部分航海日志只用文字描述天气状况，而且经常使用古旧或奇特的词语。从1685至1700年的英国日志中抽取一批样本，便出现了73种描述风力的不同方式。令所有人松一口气的是，进一步仔细研究显示，许多说法只使用过一两次；大多数日志记录者采用的词汇体系较为相似。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Having to deal with logs from four nations, from both naval and merchant vessels, made the task of translating archaic terms into hard numbers doubly daunting. Toughest of all was unravelling the terms used aboard trading ships. These had their own complex vocabulary of gales, trade winds, and monsoons, each in several grades, Wheeler discovered. But, by checking sea-miles covered, and cross-checking with the logs of occasional naval escorts, the team eventually worked out which terms meant what. passages.title: Urban Regeneration: an award-winning redevelopment project in Berlin

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Urban Regeneration: an award-winning redevelopment project in Berlin
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 城市再生：柏林一项获奖的再开发工程

source.text: Urban Regeneration: an award-winning redevelopment project in Berlin

translation.text: 城市再生：柏林一项获奖的再开发工程

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Just over a kilometer south of Berlin’s Potsdamer Platz, near the left bank of the Landwehr Canal, an extensive, triangular-shaped area of waste ground once separated the neighbourhoods of Kreuzberg to the east and Schöneberg to the west. Known as Gleisdreieck, meaning ‘triangle of rails’, it was formed by the intersection of different railway lines built in the mid-nineteenth century that entered Berlin from the south. Tracks, sheds and warehouses belonging to three old railway stations – Dresdner Bahnhof (1875-1882), Potsdamer Bahnhof (1838-1944) and Anhalter Bahnhof (1839-1952) – are situated on a raised area some twenty hectares in size, at a height of four metres above the surrounding ground level.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在柏林波茨坦广场以南略多于一公里处，靠近兰德韦尔运河左岸，曾有一大片三角形荒地，把东面的 Kreuzberg 街区与西面的 Schöneberg 街区隔开。这里称为 Gleisdreieck，意为“铁路三角区”，由19世纪中叶修建、从南面进入柏林的多条铁路线相交而成。三座旧火车站——Dresdner Bahnhof（1875—1882）、Potsdamer Bahnhof（1838—1944）和 Anhalter Bahnhof（1839—1952）——所属的铁轨、车棚和仓库，坐落在一片约20公顷的高地上，高出周围地面4米。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As the railway infrastructure gradually ceased to be used, the whole area of Gleisdreieck became increasingly run down and abandoned, to the point of being used as a rubbish tip after 1945. Meanwhile, vegetation took over, turning it into a surprising, natural haven in the middle of built-up areas. The closeness of the wall which divided the city of Berlin between 1961 and 1990 also contributed to the fact that Gleisdreieck was for decades clearly identified as no-man’s-land. Only a station of the same name in Berlin’s underground railway system testified to its existence. Shortly before the fall of the Berlin Wall, however, the German Museum of Technology was established there, attracting large numbers of visitors and giving visibility to the site. More importantly, the unification of the formerly divided city gave the zone more centrality, at which point it became imperative to identify a purpose for it.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 随着铁路基础设施逐渐停用，Gleisdreieck 整片地区日益破败荒废，1945年后甚至被当作垃圾场。与此同时，植被占据了这里，把它变成建筑密集区中央一处出人意料的自然避难所。1961至1990年间分割柏林的围墙离这里很近，也使 Gleisdreieck 数十年来被清楚视为无人区。只有柏林地铁系统中一座同名车站证明它的存在。不过，就在柏林墙倒塌前不久，德国技术博物馆在此成立，吸引大批参观者，让这个地点进入公众视野。更重要的是，原本分裂的城市实现统一后，这一区域变得更为居中；此时，为它确定用途已势在必行。

source.text: The closeness of the wall which divided the city of Berlin between 1961 and 1990 also contributed to the fact that Gleisdreieck was for decades clearly identified as no-man’s-land.

source.text: Only a station of the same name in Berlin’s underground railway system testified to its existence.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: After 2006, the State of Berlin put forward the proposal of converting Gleisdreieck into a large urban park that would integrate the different urban zones which converged there. The decades-long isolation of the site, which had formerly presented a problem, now represented an opportunity for joining the southern area of Potsdamer Platz with Kreuzberg and Schöneberg. The creation of the park would trigger one of the biggest urban expansions inside Berlin, all within a framework of multiple uses and social characteristics. It was necessary to stimulate the development of sixteen new hectares of local amenities that would be capable of integrating different generations and social groups in a sustainable way, and in harmony with nature. Following intense discussion with local proprietors and residents, the need to reconcile these goals with the conservation of railway heritage also emerged.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Once the area had been subjected to a process of undergrowth clearance and decontamination, it was then organized around a combination of existing and added elements. The project as a whole was planned around a large central meadow, intersected from east to west by a concrete footpath, and from north to south by a pair of railway lines. Once a month, a train slowly travels along these lines from its parking shed to the German Museum of Technology. The concrete footpath, which is a continuation of one of the main Kreuzberg boulevards, starts in the east, bridges the four-metre difference in ground level by means of a stairway, and suddenly ends in the west on reaching the underground lines.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这片地区经过清除灌木和污染治理后，依托原有与新增元素的组合重新规划。整个项目围绕一片大型中央草地布局，一条混凝土人行道从东向西穿过草地，两条铁路线则从北向南贯穿。每月一次，一列火车会沿这些铁轨，从停车棚缓慢驶往德国技术博物馆。混凝土人行道是 Kreuzberg 一条主要林荫大道的延伸，从东面开始，通过一段楼梯跨越4米的地面高差，最终在西面抵达地下铁路线时突然结束。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: North of the meadow, there is a large concrete slab with rounded edges. Being south-facing, this functions as a big sunny terrace, full of benches complete with footrests. In the south, the meadow overlooks Yorckstrasse, an underpass crossed by more than fifteen former railway bridges. To the east of the meadow there is quite a dense forest of pre-existing maples, oaks and birches, as well as newly planted trees of the same species. In this area, a couple of large metal frames each hold two swings. The edges of the park are finished with a collection of distinctive, functional spaces, for example a nursery, sports fields, concave surfaces for skateboards, stages for dancing, community gardens, or simply areas covered in gravel obtained from the site itself.
