blocks.sourceNormalizedText: At the end of his book, Nicholson gives his forecast of what will and will not change in the business world. He believes that most people will still prefer more traditional forms of work and throughout their lives will continue to aim at lifelong status advancement. He also maintains that the line between work and home will be less defined, but that people will prefer traditional working patterns if working from home leaves them isolated from their work community. He doubts that the high-tech ideas of virtual companies will ever be very successful because people will still want to meet each other face-to-face. Nicholson describes his ideal organisation in the future: it would be decentralised, with small sub-units; the staff would be from diverse backgrounds and be allowed a high degree of self-determination. New endeavours and creativity would replace systems and rationality. Nicholson acknowledges that there is a long way to go in terms of the translation of his ideas of evolutionary psychology into practical propositions, but he is confident more and more people will come round to his way of thinking.

source.text: Child’s Play in Medieval England

translation.text: 中世纪英格兰的儿童游戏

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Professor Nicholas Orme investigates childhood in the Middle Ages

source.text: Professor Nicholas Orme investigates childhood in the Middle Ages

translation.text: Nicholas Orme 教授考察中世纪的童年生活

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: ‘Play up! Play up! And play the game!’ The ringing chorus of Sir Henry Newbolt’s celebrated cricket poem ‘Vitai Lampada’ (1908) sums up views about play in 19th- and early 20th-century Britain. Children’s play was important, and adults should regulate and direct it. Games promoted endurance, self-discipline and team spirit – qualities needed for the health of society and government. Newbolt was one in a long line of people who thought in this way. The notion that children’s play should be used for educational and social purposes goes back at least to the ancient Greeks and the toys and games of medieval England tell us much about how adults then saw childhood. But they also reveal a good deal about children themselves, and cast light on what has recently become a controversial issue.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: “加油！加油！好好比赛！”Henry Newbolt 爵士的著名板球诗《Vitai Lampada》（1908）中这句响亮的叠句，概括了19世纪及20世纪初英国人对游戏的看法。儿童游戏很重要，成年人应当加以规范和引导。游戏能够培养耐力、自律和团队精神，而这些品质是社会和政府健康运转所需要的。Newbolt 只是众多持这种观点者中的一员。儿童游戏应当服务于教育和社会目的，这种观念至少可以追溯到古希腊；中世纪英格兰的玩具和游戏让我们充分了解当时成年人如何看待童年。不过，它们也揭示了许多儿童自身的情况，并为一个近来颇具争议的问题提供了线索。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Forty years ago, the French historian Philippe Aries argued, in Centuries of Childhood, that childhood in the Middle Ages did not exist in its modern sense. Children were regarded by adults with relatively little affection and followed a way of life not very different from that of their elders. More recent historians have disputed this, pointing to plentiful signs of parental affection and arguing that childhood, by its very nature, must always have been much the same.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In this debate play is crucial. Did adults encourage it? If so, did they see it as recreational (by providing toys, for example) or as educational (making children play in particular ways)? Did children play as their elders told them, or did they invent their own games, away from adults and even against their wishes? These questions can be answered from a rich body of evidence including actual toys of the period, pictures of children’s activities in contemporary manuscripts and literary sources such as religious works and dictionaries. We know not only how medieval English children played but what their elders thought on the subject.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: We know, for example, that adults gave children toys from infancy onwards. In 1398 the writer John Trevisa describes babies playing with ‘a child’s brooch’, an object similar in function to the bright plastic toys given to babies today to bite and handle. William Horman, 16th-century author of a Latin textbook, talks of buying a rattle to stop a baby crying. Indeed, by 1300 it appears there was a toy industry in England. Boys’ toys often took military forms, such as the two metal soldiers of that date, found in London, and made from a mould. Girls had dolls, known before the 17th century as ‘poppets’ or puppets, commercially manufactured, imported and, in 1582, taxed at a halfpenny each. Not that children were by any means dependent on things that were bought for them. Gerald of Wales recalls how he and his brothers built towns, palaces, churches and monasteries from sand at Manorbier Castle in about 1150 (perhaps on the nearby beach).
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 例如，我们知道，成年人从孩子还是婴儿时起就会给他们玩具。1398年，作家 John Trevisa 描述婴儿玩一种“儿童胸针”；它在功能上类似于今天给婴儿啃咬和抓握的鲜艳塑料玩具。16世纪拉丁语教科书作者 William Horman 提到过买拨浪鼓来让婴儿停止哭泣。事实上，到1300年时，英格兰似乎已经出现了玩具产业。男孩的玩具常以军事事物为造型，例如在伦敦发现的两件约于当时用模具铸成的金属士兵玩具。女孩则有玩偶；17世纪以前，这类玩偶称为“poppets”或“puppets”，由商家生产，也从国外进口，并在1582年按每个半便士征税。不过，儿童绝不是只能依靠成年人为他们购买东西。Gerald of Wales 回忆说，约1150年，他和兄弟们曾在曼诺比尔城堡（或许是在附近的海滩上）用沙子建造城镇、宫殿、教堂和修道院。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This willingness of children to take the initiative in play, not just to wait for adults to direct them, is evident in the way they observed the calendar. Medieval life was regulated by light, weather, crops and the Church’s cycle of fasts and festivals. Children shared in the adult round of religious festivals, but had their own observances as well, semi-detached from their elders. In the 1200s, the priest Thomas Docking remarked that in spring a child ‘follows the ploughman; in autumn he accompanies the grape-gatherers’. In 1518, the poet Alexander Barclay records children playing with tops in March, looking for fruit in summer and making footballs by filling pigs’ bladders with dried peas in autumn.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It is clear from this evidence that the relationship between adults and children in medieval society was, in major respects, a modern one. Parents took an indulgent interest in their children, providing them with toys and giving them time to play. Children played in a wide variety of ways – imaginatively, skilfully, athletically and violently – developing their minds, bodies and social skills. Adults tried at times to direct play – partly to keep children in order, partly to give them skills for adult life – but children gravitated to one another and formed a culture of their own. We can answer Aries’s thesis, then, with a resounding ‘No!’. Childhood has always been much the same.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这些证据清楚表明，中世纪社会中成年人和儿童的关系，在主要方面与现代相似。父母怀着宽容宠爱的态度关心孩子，给他们玩具，也给他们游戏的时间。儿童以各种各样的方式玩耍——充满想象、技巧娴熟、富有运动性，有时也很暴力——并在此过程中发展心智、身体和社交技能。成年人有时试图引导游戏，一方面是让儿童守规矩，另一方面是培养他们成年生活所需的技能；但儿童会自然聚在一起，形成自己的文化。因此，我们可以用一声响亮的“不！”回应阿里耶斯的论点。童年一直以来都大体相同。

source.text: Children’s literature studies today

translation.text: 当今的儿童文学研究

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Who studies children’s literature and what is it that they study? The answers to this question are complex and messy, because of the many confounding factors which exist in this field.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 谁在研究儿童文学，他们研究的又是什么？这个问题的答案既复杂又混乱，因为这一领域存在许多相互干扰的因素。

source.text: Who studies children’s literature and what is it that they study?

translation.text: 谁在研究儿童文学，他们研究的又是什么？

source.text: The answers to this question are complex and messy, because of the many confounding factors which exist in this field.

translation.text: 这个问题的答案既复杂又混乱，因为这一领域存在许多相互干扰的因素。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Firstly, unlike literature for adults, children’s literature is not generally written by its own readers. Adults write for children, and thus adult perceptions of what children are and of what they could and should become are woven into the literature.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 首先，儿童文学与成人文学不同，通常并不是由其读者自己创作的。成年人为儿童写作，因此，成年人如何看待儿童、认为儿童能够以及应当成为什么样的人，都会被编织进这些文学作品中。

source.text: Firstly, unlike literature for adults, children’s literature is not generally written by its own readers.

translation.text: 首先，儿童文学与成人文学不同，通常并不是由其读者自己创作的。

source.text: Adults write for children, and thus adult perceptions of what children are and of what they could and should become are woven into the literature.

translation.text: 成年人为儿童写作，因此，成年人如何看待儿童、认为儿童能够以及应当成为什么样的人，都会被编织进这些文学作品中。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Furthermore, some of those who study children’s literature (and those who write certain kinds of children’s books) are less interested in literary values than in the kinds of lessons it can teach- either in terms of creating better children or in terms of serving a particular curriculum. The issue of how a teacher can use a children’s book is often contentious, but even outside the classroom, much material for children is still didactic.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 此外，一些研究儿童文学的人，以及某些类型儿童读物的作者，对文学价值的兴趣，不如对作品能够传授何种道理的兴趣浓厚；他们可能希望作品培养出更好的儿童，也可能希望它服务于某种特定课程。教师应如何使用儿童读物，往往是一个有争议的问题；但即使在课堂之外，大量面向儿童的材料仍带有说教性质。

source.text: Furthermore, some of those who study children’s literature (and those who write certain kinds of children’s books) are less interested in literary values than in the kinds of lessons it can teach- either in terms of creating better children or in terms of serving a particular curriculum.

translation.text: 此外，一些研究儿童文学的人，以及某些类型儿童读物的作者，对文学价值的兴趣，不如对作品能够传授何种道理的兴趣浓厚；他们可能希望作品培养出更好的儿童，也可能希望它服务于某种特定课程。

source.text: The issue of how a teacher can use a children’s book is often contentious, but even outside the classroom, much material for children is still didactic.

translation.text: 教师应如何使用儿童读物，往往是一个有争议的问题；但即使在课堂之外，大量面向儿童的材料仍带有说教性质。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Thirdly, while almost all literature is currently promoted within a strong commercial matrix, children’s literature is often especially targeted for marketing initiatives. This fact means that readers are often recruited with a message that is negligibly literary and significantly oriented to ideas of consumption. Daniel Hade (2002) has raised useful questions about whether children’s experience of reading is altered when their books are part of a larger marketing framework involving the movie, the game, and the toy of a popular children’s book. How children perceive and respond to their stories in this new context is an important question.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 第三，虽然目前几乎所有文学作品都在强大的商业体系中推广，但儿童文学往往尤其成为营销活动的目标。这意味着，吸引读者的信息几乎没有文学色彩，却明显以消费观念为导向。Daniel Hade（2002）提出了一些有益的问题：当儿童读物被纳入一个更大的营销框架，与热门儿童读物衍生的电影、游戏和玩具相连时，儿童的阅读体验是否会发生改变？在这种新语境中，儿童如何理解并回应自己所读的故事，是一个重要问题。

source.text: Thirdly, while almost all literature is currently promoted within a strong commercial matrix, children’s literature is often especially targeted for marketing initiatives.

translation.text: 第三，虽然目前几乎所有文学作品都在强大的商业体系中推广，但儿童文学往往尤其成为营销活动的目标。

source.text: This fact means that readers are often recruited with a message that is negligibly literary and significantly oriented to ideas of consumption.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Young people’s accounts of what and how they read also enable a more sophisticated description of many of the complex processes involved in reading. All descriptions of reading runs the risk of solipsism: i.e. this is how I read so this is what reading is for everyone. Asking other readers how they read, however, reduces that risk. For example, if I am a strong visualizer as I read, I may consider that visualization is a key component of successful reading and I may judge books by their capacity to evoke a vivid visual response. Other readers, however, may help me to realize that not everyone reads with mental pictures. Some readers respond to the patterns of the words, ‘hearing’ them inaudibly like a subliminal radio program. Others respond to the patterns of feelings in the story, responding with an emotional connection. Talking to competent readers, of all ages, provides a better understanding of reading experiences.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Children’s insights are even more important when it comes to understanding the significance of print literature as one aspect of literary culture. Too often adults assume that reading any book at all is a more worthwhile experience than playing a digital game of any kind. A humbler approach would include asking why the game appeals to the player. Many adults will probably never develop the automatic skills to process a game as readily as they can read a book. This does not indicate that a book is better, but that a particular set of skills is absent. Non-players must acknowledge that some fictional universes are thus closed to them, and a logical response would be to find someone who can guide them to the pleasures and challenges of the gaming world. Games need to be judged individually just as books do, and any evaluative framework needs to take this into account.

source.text: Does class size matter?

translation.text: 班级规模重要吗？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Of all the ideas for improving education, few are as simple or attractive as reducing the number of pupils per teacher. Unlike competing proposals for reform, class-size reductions rarely elicit huge outcries or involve structural change. The testing of educators, by contrast, generally arouses the anger of unions. Similarly, establishing special ‘charter’ schools involves privileging some schools over others, with the credits provided usually coming out of the budgets of struggling local schools. With its uncomplicated appeal, class-size reduction in the U.S. has lately gone from being a subject of primary academic interest to a policy juggernaut with over twenty states aiming at decreasing class sizes.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在所有改善教育的构想中，很少有哪一种像减少每名教师所教学生人数那样简单而有吸引力。与其他改革方案不同，缩小班级规模很少引发强烈抗议，也不涉及结构性变革。相比之下，对教育工作者进行考核通常会激起工会的愤怒。同样，设立特殊的“特许学校”意味着让部分学校享有优于其他学校的待遇，而拨给它们的资金通常来自本已举步维艰的当地学校预算。由于这种做法简单易懂、颇具吸引力，缩小班级规模近来在美国已从一个主要由学术界关注的议题，发展成势不可挡的政策潮流；已有20多个州计划减小班级规模。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Do small classes improve school achievement? To answer this, investigators have attempted to analyse existing data, such as records at the U.S. Department of Education. These reveal that there were steep drops in pupil-teacher ratios between 1969 and 1997, but no significant gains in academic performance.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Over the past 35 years, some studies of existing data have produced evidence that smaller classes benefit students, but most of these studies were poorly designed. The exception was the Tennessee study called Project STAR (Student Teacher Achievement Ratio). Frederick Mosteller of Harvard University has called it ‘one of the greatest experiments in education in United States history’.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Students entering kindergarten were randomly assigned to one of three kinds of classes: a small class of 13 to 17 students, a regular-size class of 22 to 26 or a regular-size class with both a teacher and a full-time teacher’s aide.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 刚进入幼儿园的学生被随机分到三类班级之一：13至17人的小班、22至26人的普通规模班级，或同时配有一名教师和一名全职助教的普通规模班级。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The students remained in whatever category they had been assigned to throughout the third grade, after which they joined a regular classroom in the fourth. To ensure that teaching quality did not differ, teachers were randomly assigned to small and regular-size classrooms. Few teachers received any special training for working with small classes, and there were no new curricular materials.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: At the end of STAR, researchers analysed the data. Jeremy Finn of New York University and Charles Achilles of Eastern Michigan University found evidence for ‘an array of benefits of small classes’. They calculated that students in smaller classes were outperforming their counterparts in regular-sized classes by the first grade and that this advantage persisted even after students returned to larger classes. They also found that the effect was stronger for black and Hispanic minority groups – a significant finding for policy-makers.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: STAR项目结束后，研究人员分析了数据。纽约大学的 Jeremy Finn 和东密歇根大学的 Charles Achilles 找到了“小班带来一系列益处”的证据。他们计算发现，到一年级时，小班学生的表现已经优于普通规模班级中的同龄学生；即使学生后来回到更大的班级，这种优势仍然存在。他们还发现，这种效果在黑人和西班牙裔少数群体中更强，对政策制定者而言，这是一项意义重大的发现。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Eric Hanushek of Stanford, however, criticises some of STAR’s key conclusions. He argues that STAR does not prove that gains persist long after students return to regular classes. It was debatable how much later improvement stemmed from other factors, such as a supportive home. Nor does he accept that the benefits accumulate, with participants widening the gap with their peers in larger classes year by year.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The largest public class size reduction programme so far, California’s, stands more as a warning than as worthy of emulation. That state is trying to reduce classes in kindergarten through grade three despite a shortage of teachers that is most acute in low-income areas.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This is exacerbating the disparity in resources available to rich and poor schools in California, because more affluent areas can attract the best teachers. Indeed, some of the extra teachers needed are being recruited from the poorer schools. Researchers found a statistically significant achievement advantage in reading, writing and mathematics for students in classes that had been reduced to 20. What is more, the effect did not vary for students of different backgrounds.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这正加剧加利福尼亚州富裕学校与贫困学校之间的资源差距，因为较富裕地区能够吸引最优秀的教师。事实上，所需的部分新增教师正是从较贫困学校招来的。研究人员发现，班级人数降至20人后，学生在阅读、写作和数学方面取得了具有统计显著性的成绩优势。此外，这种效果并未因学生背景不同而有所变化。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Wisconsin’s Student Achievement Guarantee in Education (SAGE) was a five-year pilot study to do some of the groundwork for a major project. Class sizes were reduced in only 14 schools, but it was noteworthy for targeting schools at which 30% of the students were below poverty level, compared with California’s across-the-board approach. SAGE lowered the average pupil-teacher ratio in kindergarten through third grade to 12–15:1 from 21–25:1. Analysts have studied the results of first-grade students in these schools and similar first-grade students elsewhere and found the results accord with those from STAR.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: STAR and SAGE have made it hard to argue against reducing class sizes. But the California initiative shows that reductions made with too little forethought can yield minuscule gains. Administrators need solid information before they can make sensible policy decisions.

source.text: Flower Power

translation.text: 鲜花的力量

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Why do we give people flowers? To offer condolence to those who are grieving. To celebrate. To woo. To ask for forgiveness. We all know intuitively that there is a universal emotional response. In the US alone, the flower industry is now worth about $5 billion a year, which suggests that, at the very least, they service a compelling human need.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 我们为什么要送花？向悲痛中的人表示慰问，为喜事庆祝，向心仪之人求爱，或请求原谅。我们都凭直觉知道，人类对鲜花有一种普遍的情感反应。仅在美国，花卉产业如今每年产值约50亿美元；这表明，鲜花至少满足了人类一种强烈的需求。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Recent studies at the Department of Psychology at Rutgers State University of New Jersey investigated claims that flowers are unique among living organisms in their ability to induce profound changes in our emotional state. As the first part of their research, the Rutgers team visited 150 women in their homes. Each was presented with a variety of gifts such as flowers, fruit or sweets. The women were unaware that the study was about the effect of the flowers on their emotions. They were told that it was a study about their daily moods, and that they would receive a gift in return for taking part. Following the presentation of the gift, those receiving flowers were assessed as displaying a much more positive mood than those who got other gifts, and this effect lasted for several days. After receiving flowers, they were also more willing to answer questions concerning their social circle and intimate conversations with friends and family. The results suggest that flowers influence our secondary socio-emotional behaviours, as well as having a strong effect on our immediate emotional expression.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 新泽西州罗格斯州立大学心理学系近期开展研究，检验了这样一种说法：在所有生物中，鲜花具有独特能力，能够让我们的情绪状态发生深刻变化。在研究的第一部分，罗格斯团队上门访问了150名女性，分别向她们送上鲜花、水果或糖果等礼物。受访女性并不知道研究考察的是鲜花对情绪的影响。研究人员告诉她们，这项研究关注日常心情，而参与者会获得礼物作为回报。送出礼物后，评估发现，收到鲜花的人表现出的心情远比收到其他礼物的人积极，而且这种效果持续了数天。收到鲜花后，她们也更愿意回答有关社交圈，以及与亲友私密交谈的问题。结果表明，鲜花不仅会强烈影响我们即时的情绪表达，还会影响后续的社会情感行为。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In the second study, the psychologists observed participants being handed single flowers, or alternative gifts, in a constrained and stressful situation – inside an elevator. Contrary to predictions regarding gender differences, both men and women presented with flowers were more likely to smile, to stand closer and to initiate conversation. Several subjects who were given the alternative gift then learnt that flowers were also being handed out, and returned to the elevator and demanded a flower. The scientists used elevators for this study precisely because the most typical behaviour in sparsely occupied elevators is for people to retreat to opposite corners. The subjects who received flowers, however, closed up that space to a considerable extent – indicating that the flowers not only induced a strong positive mood, but brought a significant affiliation among people who had never previously met.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 第二项研究中，心理学家观察参与者在一个空间受限、压力较大的环境——电梯内——收到一枝鲜花或其他礼物时的反应。与关于性别差异的预测相反，收到鲜花的男性和女性都更可能微笑、站得更近并主动交谈。几名收到其他礼物的受试者后来得知现场还在送花，便返回电梯索要鲜花。科学家之所以使用电梯开展研究，正是因为人不多时，电梯内最典型的行为是各自退到相对的角落。然而，收到鲜花的受试者大幅缩短了彼此间的距离。这表明，鲜花不仅带来强烈的积极情绪，还使此前从未见过面的人产生了明显的亲近感。

source.text: The subjects who received flowers, however, closed up that space to a considerable extent – indicating that the flowers not only induced a strong positive mood, but brought a significant affiliation among people who had never previously met.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Various evolutionary hypotheses attempt to explain the remarkably powerful psychological effect of flowers. One is that our aesthetic preferences for fertile locations and growing things stem from prehistory, when these clues in our environment could mean the difference between starvation and survival. We may have become hardwired to respond positively to flowers because for early man, finding them in a particular location predicted future food supplies and possibly a better place to rear children. Yet the flaw in this argument is that the showy flowers which humans seem to find most visually attractive are generally found on those plants which yield no edible products.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 各种进化假说试图解释鲜花为何具有如此强大的心理作用。一种解释认为，我们在审美上偏爱肥沃之地和生长中的事物，这源于史前时代；当时，环境中的这些线索可能意味着挨饿还是生存下来的区别。我们可能已经形成了对鲜花作出积极反应的先天倾向，因为对早期人类而言，在某个地方发现鲜花，预示着未来会有食物供应，而且那里或许更适合养育孩子。然而，这一论点有一个缺陷：人类似乎认为视觉上最吸引人的艳丽花朵，通常生长在不会产出任何可食用物的植物上。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The Rutgers psychologists’ findings show that the various physical attributes of flowers combine to directly affect our emotions through multi-channel interactions. We have evolved preferences for the particular colours, textures, patterned symmetries and specific floral odours which influence our moods. Indeed, previous research has established that popular perfumes, which often have a floral ‘top-note’, will actually reduce depression. The origins of these inclinations may well be as the evolutionary theories suggest: the patterned symmetries of flowers can be detected easily as a recognisable signal within a wide variety of visual arrays, and a response to certain colour tones is important in finding ripe fruit against a leafy background. But, claim the Rutgers team, these preferences have long been separated from their primary evolutionary use, and become rewarding to us more generally. Thus plants with preferred colours, shapes and odours – despite having no other products – would therefore be protected and dispersed.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 罗格斯心理学家的发现表明，鲜花的各种物理特征相互结合，通过多重感官通道的互动直接影响我们的情绪。我们在进化中形成了对特定颜色、质地、规则对称图案和某些花香的偏好，而这些特征会影响心情。事实上，早先研究已经证实，通常带有花香“前调”的流行香水确实会减轻抑郁。这些偏好的起源很可能正如进化理论所说：在纷繁的视觉景象中，花朵规则的对称图案很容易被辨认为一种信号；而要在绿叶背景中找到成熟果实，对某些色调作出反应也十分重要。不过，罗格斯团队认为，这些偏好早已脱离最初的进化用途，并在更广泛的意义上给我们带来愉悦。因此，即使没有其他产物，具有受偏爱颜色、形状和气味的植物仍会受到保护并传播开来。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The Rutgers study suggests that flowers may have actually evolved to exploit their peculiar impact on humans. The team’s theory proposes a plant-human co-evolution, or even domestication, based on the intense emotional rewards that flowers provide. The idea that flowering plants, with no known food or other basic survival value to man, have co-evolved with us by exploiting an emotional niche instead, is very much like the scenario presented for the evolution of dogs. Flowers may be the plant equivalent of ‘companion animals’. If this is true, then there is a very real sense in which, when you next give flowers, they are using you just as much as you are using them.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 罗格斯大学的研究表明，鲜花实际上可能是为了利用自身对人类的特殊影响而进化的。研究团队提出，植物与人类之间存在共同进化，甚至可能存在驯化关系，其基础正是鲜花带来的强烈情感回报。开花植物没有已知的食物价值或其他基本生存价值，却通过利用情感生态位与我们共同进化；这一观点与关于狗的进化情景十分相似。鲜花或许就是植物中的“伴侣动物”。如果这是真的，那么下次你送花时，从一个非常实际的意义上说，鲜花利用你的程度，与你利用它们的程度同样大。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Human beings naturally become attached to places they visit or inhabit and these emotional attachments have become increasingly important in research on recreation sites and activities. Research into this phenomenon is called ‘sense-of-place research’. This research has employed a variety of approaches to gauge people’s feelings toward a place, including surveys and personal interviews, but so far has not used photo-based methods. However, Visitor Employed Photography (VEP), used to capture visitor perceptions of landscape and recreational quality, represents a potential innovation in sense-of-place research.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A ‘place’ is a setting that we give meaning to based on the personal experiences, relationships and feelings we associate with it. A crucial distinction that needs to be made is between the more subjective concept of attachment and the symbolic ‘meanings’ or labels we use to describe the type of place a setting represents. Is, for example, a multiple-use forest area a wilderness? A playground? A workplace? Symbolic meanings are important in that they form the basis of our attachment to a place: we attribute meaning to our settings, and in turn become attached to the meanings (Stedman, 2003). All settings can have multiple meanings depending on how we encounter them. Some researchers suggest that, because meaning emerges through individual experience, for example ‘my camping trip’, place meanings are completely individualistic: a given setting such as a park will contain as many different meanings as there are people using the setting (Meinig, 1979). Others, however, (e.g. Greider & Garkovich, 1994) assert that meanings are based on social categories and therefore are shared by others within these categories. For example, farmers share certain meanings for a plot of land that are distinct from those of real-estate developers or hunters.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: “地方”是一个环境；我们根据与之相连的个人经历、人际关系和感受，赋予这个环境意义。这里必须作出一个关键区分：一边是较为主观的依恋概念，另一边是我们用来描述某个环境所代表地方类型的象征性“意义”或标签。例如，一片具有多种用途的森林地区究竟是荒野、游乐场，还是工作场所？象征性意义十分重要，因为它们构成我们依恋某个地方的基础：我们赋予周围环境意义，继而又依恋这些意义（Stedman，2003）。 所有环境都可能具有多重意义，具体取决于我们如何接触它们。一些研究人员认为，由于意义产生于个人经历，例如“我的露营之旅”，地方意义完全因人而异：公园等特定环境所包含的不同意义，会与使用这个环境的人数一样多（Meinig，1979）。但另一些研究人员，例如Greider和Garkovich（1994），则主张意义建立在社会类别之上，因此会由同一类别中的人共同拥有。例如，农民对一块土地所共有的某些意义，不同于房地产开发商或猎人赋予它的意义。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Clearly, place attachment is built through familiarity with a place over a period of months or even years. Relph (1976) describes sense-of-place attachment as the steady accumulation of events within a setting; this creates ‘home places’. According to this view, those who have participated fully in the life of the home or community, or have accumulated a series of everyday events in a setting, will have the strongest attachment to it. Extended residence in a place tends to make us feel toward it almost as a living thing, affecting our emotions in the same way as a family would (Ryden, 1993). However, Tuan (1977) notes that a sense of place may also develop quite rapidly in ‘chosen places’, where dramatic landscapes and intense experiences can lead to an immediate attachment. Indeed, many settings, especially those that attract visitors, may simultaneously exist as home places and chosen places.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 显然，对地方的依恋，是在数月甚至数年间逐渐熟悉某个地方而形成的。Relph（1976）把地方感中的依恋描述为某个环境中各种事件的不断积累，这会形成“家园之地”。按照这种观点，那些充分参与家园或社区生活，或在某个环境中积累了一系列日常事件的人，会对那里产生最强的依恋。长期居住在一个地方，往往会让我们几乎把它当作有生命的事物来感受；它对我们情绪的影响，就像家人一样（Ryden，1993）。不过，Tuan（1977）指出，在“自选之地”，地方感也可能很快形成；壮阔的景观和强烈的经历可以让人立即产生依恋。 事实上，许多地方，尤其是吸引访客的地方，可能同时既是家园之地，也是自选之地。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Clearly we are dealing with a complex phenomenon and photo-based research methods may help us to understand it better. In VEP, tourists are asked to take photographs. This technique has primarily been used to assess the perceptions of visitors to parks and recreation places. Haywood (1990) describes several benefits of VEP. Photography is an enjoyable, familiar activity to tourists which helps to sharpen observation and identify specific locations that are important. It can give clearer ideas on elements that are liked or disliked and also facilitates comparisons between places.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: However, several methodological issues need to be taken into account. First, who should take the photographs? VEP research typically involves visitors or tourists but, when applied to questions of attachment to a community, this approach has potential pitfalls. Chenoweth (1984) notes that research subjects may take photos that represent only a part of their entire recreational experience. This tendency probably relates to unfamiliarity with the setting. For example, when researchers assign the task of photographing a travel route with which respondents are not familiar, participants may save too many pictures and then use them all up at the end of their visit, even if there is no suitable material. Markwell (1997) noted an opposite tendency in his study of pictures taken on a nature tour: beginnings of excursions were over-represented, due perhaps to the initial novelty of the trip. Furthermore, Haywood (1990) suggests that compressing the photo-taking period into a single day (as he did in his work) may result in an over-representation of tourist icons rather than ordinary places. In contrast, Yamashita (2002), when focusing on local residents’ perceptions of the qualities of the water around them, noted that residents may have more difficulty expressing visual appeal than visitors, precisely because they are insiders and less conscious of aesthetic qualities. When addressing complex attachment to landscape, we would expect, however, that familiarity ought to increase the validity of the items selected to represent sources of attachment. We also expect that photographs taken by local residents will represent a wider range of phenomena than pictures taken by transient visitors.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But how should the photographs be interpreted? source.text: Packaging

translation.text: 包装

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One of the most prominent design issues in pharmacy is that of drug packages and the patient information leaflets (PILs) included in them. Many pharmacists are concerned that current designs are ‘accidents waiting to happen’. The UK government shares this concern and, in 2003, the National Patient Safety Agency created a new role, appointing Colum Lowe, who has 14 years’ experience as a designer in the private sector, as head of design and human factors.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 药房设计中最突出的问题之一，是药品包装及其中所附的患者信息说明书（patient information leaflets，PILs）。许多药剂师担心，当前的设计就像“等着发生的事故”。英国政府也有同样的忧虑，并于2003年在国家患者安全局（National Patient Safety Agency）新设了一个职位，任命拥有14年私营部门设计师经验的 Colum Lowe 担任设计与人为因素主管。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Packaging design in the pharmaceutical industry is handled by either in-house teams or external design agencies. For packaging design of over-the-counter medicines, which do not have to be dispensed by a pharmacist but can be bought directly from a sales assistant, characteristics such as attractiveness and distinguishability are important and so these are usually commissioned from an external design team. The marketing team prepares the initial brief and the designers come up with six or seven designs. Two or three of these are then tested on a consumer group. In contrast, most designs for prescription-only products are created in-house. In some cases, this may simply involve the company’s design team applying the house design and then handing it over to design engineers rather than testing the design on a consumer group. Clearly this process cannot adequately address the needs of the wide variety of patients using medication.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 制药行业的包装设计由内部团队或外部设计机构负责。非处方药无须由药剂师配发，顾客可以直接向售货员购买，因此这类药品的包装设计很看重吸引力和辨识度等特点，通常会委托外部设计团队完成。营销团队先拟定初步的设计要求，设计师再提出六七套方案，随后从中挑选两三套交由消费者小组测试。相比之下，大多数处方药产品的设计都由内部完成。有时，公司设计团队可能只是套用企业统一设计，再交给设计工程师，而不会让消费者小组测试。显然，这套流程无法充分照顾使用药物的各类患者的需要。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Design considerations

source.text: Design considerations

translation.text: 设计考量

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In her book Information Design for Patient Safety, Thea Swayne highlighted a multitude of design problems. For example, drugs that look or sound alike can lead to confusion; small type sizes and even the glare on silver-foil packaging can lead to names or instructions being misread. One such example is a drug that was accidentally injected into a patient through the spine (intrathecally) rather than through the veins (intravenously). Investigations following this tragedy attributed some blame to the poor choice of typescript used on the drug container. Furthermore, according to Swayne, real situations in which medicines are used include a parent giving a cough medicine to a child in the middle of the night; packaging should be designed for moments such as these rather than for the ideal world of a hospital.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Thea Swayne 在《患者安全信息设计》（Information Design for Patient Safety）一书中指出了大量设计问题。例如，外观或读音相似的药品可能造成混淆；字号过小，甚至银箔包装上的反光，都可能让人看错药名或说明。曾有一种药物被误从患者的脊柱注入，即鞘内注射，而不是从静脉注入，即静脉注射。事后对这起悲剧的调查认为，药品容器上的字体选择不当也负有一定责任。此外，Swayne 指出，现实中的用药情境包括家长半夜给孩子服用止咳药；包装设计应当面向这类时刻，而不是面向医院里的理想环境。

source.text: Safety and compliance

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Child protection is another area that gives designers opportunities to improve safety. According to the Child Accident Prevention Trust, 70% of children admitted to hospital with suspected poisoning have swallowed medicines, and although child-resistant lids have helped, they are not yet fully effective. There is scope for improving what is currently available, according to Richard Mawle, a freelance product designer who feels it is not just children who are blocked by child-proof closures. ‘Many child-resistant packs are based on strength but older people may have the same level of strength as a child,’ he explained, and suggested that better designs could rely on cognitive skills (e.g. removing the lid using a three-step process).
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 儿童防护也是设计师有机会提升安全性的一个领域。据儿童意外预防信托基金会称，因疑似中毒入院的儿童中有70%吞服过药物；尽管防儿童开启的瓶盖有所帮助，却仍未能完全奏效。自由产品设计师 Richard Mawle 认为，现有产品仍有改进空间，因为防儿童开启的封口挡住的并不只是儿童。他解释说：“许多防儿童开启的包装依靠的是力气，但老年人的力气可能与儿童相当。”他建议，更好的设计可以依靠认知能力，例如通过三个步骤才能打开盖子。

source.text: Design principles and guidelines

translation.text: 设计原则与指南

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Most designers work according to basic principles; for example, certain print styles are known to be more difficult to read than others. Look-alike boxes present the potential for errors and an obvious solution would be to use colours to highlight a larger dosage of a drug. However, according to Thea Swayne, designating a colour to a particular dosage is not recommended because this could lead to the user not reading the text on a box.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 大多数设计师都会遵循一些基本原则；例如，人们知道某些印刷字体比其他字体更难阅读。外观相似的药盒可能引发差错，一个显而易见的办法是用颜色突出较高剂量的药物。然而，Thea Swayne 认为，不宜给特定剂量指定一种颜色，因为这可能导致使用者不再阅读药盒上的文字。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Design features can provide the basis for lengthy debates. One argument is that if all packaging was white with black lettering, people would have no choice but to read every box carefully. The problem is that trials of drug packaging are few – common signage studies concern road-traffic signs and visual-display units. Although some designers take results from such studies into account, proving that a particular feature is beneficial can be difficult. For example, current UK legislation requires packaging to include the name of the medicine in Braille, but, according to Karel van der Waarde, a design consultant to the pharmaceutical industry, ‘it is not known how much visually impaired patients will benefit nor how much the reading of visually able patients will be impaired’. Van der Waarde is sceptical about current legislation and says that many regulatory authorities do not have the resources to handle packaging information properly. ‘They do not look at the use of packaging in a practical context – they only see one box at a time and not several together as pharmacists would do,’ he said.

source.text: Innovation

translation.text: 创新

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: On a positive note, a recent innovation exhibition revealed several new designs. ‘The popper’ aims to help arthritis sufferers remove tablets from blister packs, and ‘Pluspoint’ is an adrenaline auto-injector (a device that allows diabetics to inject themselves) aimed at overcoming the fact that many patients do not carry their medication due to its prohibitive size. The aim of good design is to try to make things more user-friendly as well as safer. The guidelines in Information Design for Patient Safety are not intended to be legally binding. Rather, the book’s purpose is to create a basic design standard and to stimulate innovation. The challenge for the pharmaceutical industry is to adopt such a standard.

source.text: Insect-inspired robots

translation.text: 仿昆虫机器人

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A recent conference reports on developments in biorobotics
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 近期一场会议报告了仿生机器人技术的发展

source.text: A recent conference reports on developments in biorobotics

translation.text: 近期一场会议报告了仿生机器人技术的发展

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A tiny insect navigates its way across featureless salt-pans. A cockroach successfully works out how to scramble over an obstacle. The mantis shrimp scans its aquatic world through hyperspectral eyes. Using the most basic of equipment and brains tinier than a pin-head, insects constantly solve complex problems of movement, vision and navigation – processing data that would challenge a super-computer. How they do it is driving one of the most exciting new fields of technology – biomimetics and biorobotics, the imitation of insect systems to control man-made machines. Delegates at a recent conference presented some outcomes of their work in this area.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 一只小小的昆虫在毫无明显地标的盐碱地上辨路前行。一只蟑螂成功想出越过障碍的方法。螳螂虾用超光谱眼睛扫视水下世界。昆虫只凭最基本的身体装置和比针头还小的大脑，却不断解决运动、视觉和导航方面的复杂问题，处理的数据甚至会令超级计算机为难。它们究竟如何做到这一点，正在推动一个最令人振奋的新技术领域：仿生学与仿生机器人技术（biomimetics and biorobotics），也就是模仿昆虫系统来控制人造机器。近期一场会议的与会者展示了他们在这一领域取得的部分成果。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Dr Alex Zelinsky suggested that the method by which wasps use landmarks to find their way back to the nest may one day be part of a system for navigating cars that know where to go. A research team led by Dr Zelinsky has shown that a robot can navigate its way among 50 different landmarks by recognising them individually using a panoramic camera. “The inspiration came from biology, where wasps use a practical method turn back and look to orient themselves as they emerge from their nest. By flying to and fro, they look at the wasp nest from different angles and perspectives so they can recognise it again,” he explained. The robot’s panoramic camera logs the surrounding area and its key landmarks, which are then stored in its computer according to how reliable they are as navigational aids. The landmarks are then scaled, from small to large, so that the robot can recognise whether it is getting closer to or further away from them. Their location is built into a map in its mind, which operates at different scales and instructs the robot whether to turn left or right at a particular mark. The technology provides a general way for a machine to navigate an unknown landscape.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Alex Zelinsky 博士提出，黄蜂利用地标寻找归巢路线的方法，将来或许会成为一种汽车导航系统的一部分，让汽车知道该往哪里走。Zelinsky 博士领导的研究团队已经证明，一个机器人可以用全景相机逐一识别50个不同地标，并在其间导航。他解释说：“灵感来自生物界。黄蜂离巢时会采用一种实用方法：转身回望，以确定方向。它们来回飞行，从不同角度和视点观察蜂巢，以便再次认出它。”机器人的全景相机会记录周围区域及其主要地标，再按照这些地标作为导航参照的可靠程度，把它们存入计算机。随后，系统会把地标按从小到大的比例呈现，让机器人判断自己是在接近还是远离地标。各地标的位置被纳入机器人脑中的地图；这张地图会以不同尺度运作，并在特定标记处指示机器人左转还是右转。这项技术为机器在陌生地形中导航提供了一种通用方法。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: For three decades, Professor Ruediger Wehner has journeyed from Switzerland to the Sahara Desert where Cataglyphis, a tiny ant with a brain weighing just 0.1 mg, performs acts of navigational genius when it leaves its nest, forages for food and returns successfully. Cataglyphis uses polarised light, caused when air molecules scatter light, to orient and steer itself. Wehner’s team found that the ant has a set of specialised photoreceptors along the upper rim of its eyes that detect polarised light, while other receptors perform different navigational tasks. As the sun moves, the ant notes its direction each time it leaves the nest and updates its internal compass. Using other eye receptors it stores a snapshot image of landmarks close to the nest entrance in its eyes and compares this with what it sees as it returns. The ant also has a way of measuring distance travelled, while a path integrator periodically informs the ant of its current position relative to its point of departure. Rather than integrate all the information it receives in its brain, the ant actually performs a number of complex calculations in different organs. Like a super-computer, the ant has many separate sub-routines going on simultaneously. Using the ant’s ability to steer by polarised light and to store and reuse landscape images, Wehner and colleagues have built “Sahabot,” a small vehicle that uses polarisers and a CCD camera to store 360° images of its surroundings. It navigates by using polarised sunlight and comparing the current images of landmarks to the ones in its memory.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 三十年来，Ruediger Wehner 教授一次次从瑞士前往撒哈拉沙漠。在那里，一种名为Cataglyphis、脑重仅0.1毫克的小蚂蚁离巢觅食后总能顺利返回，展现出非凡的导航本领。空气分子散射光线会产生偏振光，Cataglyphis便利用这种光来辨别方向并控制行进路线。Wehner 的团队发现，这种蚂蚁眼睛上缘有一组专门探测偏振光的感光细胞，其他感受器则负责不同的导航任务。随着太阳移动，蚂蚁每次离巢都会记下太阳的方向，并更新体内的指南针。它还会用其他眼部感受器，把巢穴入口附近地标的快照储存在眼中，返回时再与眼前所见进行比较。蚂蚁也能测量已经走过的距离，而路径积分器会定期告知它当前相对于出发点的位置。蚂蚁并非在大脑中整合收到的全部信息，而是在不同器官中分别完成多项复杂计算。它就像一台超级计算机，同时运行着许多彼此独立的子程序。Wehner 及其同事利用蚂蚁凭偏振光确定方向、储存并重复利用地貌图像的能力，造出了小型车辆“Sahabot”。它使用偏振片和CCD相机储存周围环境的360度图像，并利用偏振阳光导航，同时把当前地标图像与记忆中的图像进行比较。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Professor Robert Michelson had a different desert challenge – to design a flying robot that can not only navigate but also stay aloft and hover in the thin atmosphere of Mars. Drawing inspiration from insect flight, he has gone beyond nature to devise a completely new concept for a flying machine. The “Entomopter” is a sort of double-ended dragonfly whose wings beat reciprocally. Michelson says that the flapping-wing design gives the craft unusually high lift compared with a fixed-wing flyer, enabling it to fly slowly or hover in the thin Martian air – whereas a fixed-wing craft would have to move at more than 400 km/h and could not stop to explore.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Engineer Roger Quinn and entomologist Professor Roy Ritzmann are taking their inspiration from cockroaches. blocks.sourceNormalizedText: International experts believe there are tremendous opportunities in biorobotics. However, delegates at the conference had differing visions for the future of the science. While some were concerned that the initial applications of biorobotics may be military, others, such as Dr Barbara Webb, predicted swarms of tiny, cheap, insect-like robots as society’s cleaners and collectors. Sonja Kleinlogel hoped the study of the hyperspectral eyes of the mantis shrimp might yield remote sensors that can watch over the environmental health of our oceans. Several delegates were concerned about the ethical implications of biorobotics and urged that close attention be paid to this as the science and technologies develop.

source.text: How watching sport affects the brain

translation.text: 观看体育比赛如何影响大脑

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: At about the same time that the poet Homer invented the epic there, the ancient Greeks started a festival in which men competed in a single race, about 200 metres long. The winner received a branch of wild olives. The Greeks called this celebration the Olympics. Though the ancient sprint remains, today the Olympics are far more than that. Indeed, the Games seem to celebrate the dream of progress as embodied in the human form. That the Games are intoxicating to watch is beyond question. During the Athens Olympics in 2004, 3.4 billion people, half the world, watched them on television. Certainly, being a spectator is a thrilling experience—but why?

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In 1996, three Italian neuroscientists, Giacomo Rizzolatti, Leonardo Fogassi and Vittorio Gallese, examined the premotor cortex of monkeys. They discovered that inside these primate brains there were groups of cells that ‘store vocabularies of motor actions’, just as there are grammars of movement. These networks of cells are the bodily ‘sentences’ we use every day, the ones our brain has chosen to retain and refine. Think, for example, about a golf swing. To those who have only watched the Masters Tournament on TV, golfing seems easy. To the novice, however, the skill of casting a smooth arc with a lopsided metal stick is virtually impossible. This is because most novices swing with their consciousness, using an area of the brain next to the premotor cortex. To the expert, on the other hand, a perfectly balanced stroke is second nature. For him, the motor action has become memorized, and the movements are embedded in the neurons of his premotor cortex. He hits the ball with the tranquility of his perfected autopilot.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 1996年，三位意大利神经科学家 Giacomo Rizzolatti、Leonardo Fogassi 和 Vittorio Gallese 研究了猴子的前运动皮层。他们发现，在这些灵长类动物的大脑中，有一些细胞群会“储存运动动作的词汇”，正如运动也有自己的语法一样。这些细胞网络构成了我们每天使用的身体“句子”，也就是大脑选择保留并不断完善的那些动作。以高尔夫挥杆为例。对于只在电视上看过美国大师赛的人来说，打高尔夫似乎很容易。然而，对新手而言，要用一根形状不对称的金属球杆划出平滑的弧线，几乎是不可能的。这是因为大多数新手会有意识地挥杆，使用的是大脑中邻近前运动皮层的一个区域。相反，对高手来说，完美平衡的一击已经成为本能。对他而言，这个运动动作已经被记住，相关动作嵌入了前运动皮层的神经元中。他在那套已臻完善的“自动驾驶”系统支配下，从容地把球击出。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: These neurons in the premotor cortex, besides explaining why certain athletes seem to possess almost unbelievable levels of skill, have an even more amazing characteristic, one that caused Rizzolatti, Fogassi and Gallese to give them the lofty title ‘mirror neurons’. They note that ‘the main functional characteristic of mirror neurons is that they become active both when the monkey performs a particular action (for example, grasping an object or holding it) and, astonishingly, when it sees another individual performing a similar action’. Humans have an even more elaborate mirror neuron system. These peculiar cells mirror, inside the brain, the outside world: they enable us to internalize the actions of another. In order to be activated, though, these cells require what the scientists call ‘goal-orientated movements’. If we are staring at a photograph, a fixed image of a runner mid-stride, our mirror neurons are totally silent. They only fire when the runner is active: running, moving or sprinting.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 前运动皮层中的这些神经元不仅可以解释为何某些运动员似乎拥有近乎不可思议的高超技能，还有一个更加惊人的特点。正因如此，里佐拉蒂、福加西和加莱塞给它们取了一个响亮的名称：“镜像神经元”。他们指出：“镜像神经元的主要功能特征是，当猴子做出某个特定动作时，例如抓取或拿住物体，它们会变得活跃；令人惊讶的是，当猴子看到另一个个体做出类似动作时，它们也会变得活跃。”人类拥有一套更加复杂的镜像神经元系统。这些奇特的细胞在大脑内部映照外部世界，使我们能够把他人的动作内化。不过，要激活这些细胞，动作必须是科学家所说的“目标导向型动作”。如果我们盯着一张照片，画面中的跑步者定格在迈步途中，我们的镜像神经元会完全沉默。只有跑步者真正活动起来，奔跑、移动或冲刺时，它们才会放电。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: What these electrophysiological studies indicate is that when we watch a golfer or a runner in action, the mirror neurons in our own premotor cortex light up as if we were the ones competing. This phenomenon of neural mirroring was first discovered in 1954, when two French physiologists, Gastaut and Bert, found that the brains of humans vibrate with two distinct wavelengths, alpha and mu. The mu system is involved in neural mirroring. It is active when our bodies are still, and disappears whenever we do something active, like playing a sport or changing the TV channel. The surprising fact is that the mu signal is also quiet when we watch someone else being active, as on TV. These results are the effect of mirror neurons.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这些电生理研究表明，当我们观看高尔夫球手或跑步者运动时，我们自己前运动皮层中的镜像神经元也会活跃起来，仿佛参赛的是我们自己。1954年，两位法国生理学家 Gastaut 和 Bert 发现，人脑会以阿尔法波和缪波这两种不同波长振荡，由此首次发现了这种神经镜像现象。缪波系统参与神经镜像。我们的身体静止时，它处于活跃状态；每当我们做出主动动作，如参加体育活动或切换电视频道时，它便会消失。令人意外的是，当我们看到别人活动时，例如在电视上观看，缪波信号也会沉寂。这些结果正是镜像神经元作用所致。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Rizzolatti, Fogassi and Gallese call the idea of mirror neurons the ‘direct matching hypothesis’. They believe that we only understand the movement of sports stars when we ‘map the visual representation of the observed action onto our motor representation of the same action’. According to this theory, watching an Olympic athlete ‘causes the motor system of the observer to resonate. The ‘motor knowledge’ of the observer is used to understand the observed action.’ But mirror neurons are more than just the neural basis for our attitude to sport. It turns out that watching a great golfer makes us better golfers, and watching a great sprinter actually makes us run faster. This ability to learn by watching is a crucial skill. From the acquisition of language as infants to learning facial expressions, mimesis (copying) is an essential part of being conscious. The best athletes are those with a premotor cortex capable of imagining the movements of victory, together with the physical properties to make those movements real.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But how many of us regularly watch sports in order to be a better athlete? Rather, we watch sport for the feeling, the human drama. source.text: Jean Piaget

translation.text: Jean Piaget

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Seymour Papert looks at the work of the pioneering Swiss philosopher and psychologist
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: Seymour Papert 评述这位瑞士哲学家兼心理学先驱的工作

source.text: Seymour Papert looks at the work of the pioneering Swiss philosopher and psychologist

translation.text: Seymour Papert 评述这位瑞士哲学家兼心理学先驱的工作

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Jean Piaget spent much of his professional life listening to children, watching children and poring over reports of researchers around the world who were doing the same. He found, to put it most succinctly, that children don’t think like grown-ups. After thousands of interactions with young people often barely old enough to talk, Piaget began to suspect that behind their cute and seemingly irrational utterances were thought processes that had their own kind of order and their own special logic. Einstein called it “a discovery so simple that only a genius could have thought of it.”
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Jean Piaget 的职业生涯有很大一部分时间都用来倾听儿童、观察儿童，并仔细研读世界各地从事同类研究的学者所写的报告。用最简洁的话概括，他发现儿童的思维方式与成年人不同。在与儿童进行数千次互动后——这些孩子往往小到刚刚会说话——Piaget 开始怀疑，那些可爱而看似不合情理的话语背后，存在着具有自身秩序和独特逻辑的思维过程。爱因斯坦称这是“一项简单到只有天才才能想到的发现”。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Although not an educational reformer, Piaget championed a way of thinking about children that provided the foundation for today’s education-reform movements. It was a shift comparable to the way modern anthropology displaced stories of primitive tribes being ‘noble savages’ and ‘cannibals’. One might say that Piaget was the first to take children’s thinking seriously.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Piaget 虽然不是教育改革者，却倡导了一种看待儿童的方式，为当今的教育改革运动奠定了基础。这种转变，就像现代人类学取代了把原始部落描述成“高贵的野蛮人”和“食人族”的故事一样。可以说，Piaget 是第一个认真对待儿童思维的人。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: He has been revered by generations of teachers inspired by the belief that children are not empty vessels to be filled with knowledge (as traditional pedagogical theory had it) but active builders of knowledge—little scientists who are constantly creating and testing their own hypotheses about the world. And though he may not be as famous as Sigmund Freud or even B. F. Skinner, his influence on psychology may be longer lasting.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 一代又一代教师都十分推崇皮亚杰，因为他们认同这样一种观念：儿童并不是等待人们灌入知识的空容器——传统教育理论就是这样认为的——而是知识的主动建构者，是不断提出并检验自己对世界所作假设的小科学家。尽管皮亚杰或许不如 Sigmund Freud，甚至不如 B. F. Skinner 出名，但他对心理学的影响可能更加持久。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In 1920, while doing research in a child-psychology laboratory in Paris, Piaget noticed that children of the same age made similar errors on intelligence tests. Fascinated by their reasoning processes, he began to suspect that the key to human knowledge might be discovered by observing how the child’s mind develops. On his return to Switzerland he began watching children play, scrupulously recording their words and actions as their minds raced to find reasons for why things are the way they are. In one of his most famous experiments, Piaget asked children, ‘What makes the wind?’ A typical dialogue would be: Piaget What makes the wind? Julia The trees. Piaget How do you know? Julia I saw them waving their arms. Piaget How does that make the wind? Julia (waving her hand in front of his face) Like this. Only they are bigger. And there are lots of trees.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 1920年，Piaget 在巴黎一所儿童心理学实验室从事研究时，注意到同龄儿童在智力测试中会犯相似的错误。他对这些儿童的推理过程深感兴趣，并开始怀疑，观察儿童心智如何发展，或许能够揭示人类知识的关键。回到瑞士后，他开始观察儿童玩耍，一丝不苟地记录他们的言语和行动；与此同时，儿童的思维飞速运转，努力寻找事物之所以如此的原因。在一项最著名的实验中，Piaget 问儿童：“是什么产生了风？”一段典型对话如下： Piaget：是什么产生了风？ 朱莉娅：树。 Piaget：你怎么知道？ 朱莉娅：我看见它们在挥动手臂。 Piaget：那怎么会产生风呢？ 朱莉娅：（在他面前挥手）像这样。只不过树更大，而且有很多棵。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Piaget recognised that five-year-old Julia’s beliefs, while not correct by any adult criterion, are not ‘incorrect’ either. They are entirely sensible and coherent within the framework of the child’s way of knowing. Classifying them as ‘true’ or ‘false’ misses the point and shows a lack of respect for the child. What Piaget was after was a theory that the wind dialogue demonstrated coherence, ingenuity and the practice of a kind of explanatory principle (in this case by referring to body actions) that stands young children in very good stead when they don’t know enough or don’t have enough skill to handle the kind of explanation that grown-ups prefer.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Piaget 认识到，五岁的朱莉娅所相信的事情虽然不符合任何成年人的正确标准，却也不能说是“错误”的。在儿童的认知框架内，这些看法完全合乎情理，而且前后一致。把它们归为“真”或“假”并没有抓住要点，还表现出对儿童缺乏尊重。Piaget 试图建立的理论认为，这段关于风的对话体现了连贯性、创造力以及某种解释原则的运用——这里是借助身体动作来解释。幼儿在知识不足或尚不具备足够能力，无法运用成年人偏爱的那类解释时，这种原则会给他们带来很大帮助。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Piaget was not an educator and never laid down rules about how to intervene in such situations. But his work strongly suggests that the automatic reaction of putting the child right may well be counter-productive. If their theories are always greeted by ‘Nice try, but this is how it really is…’ they might give up after a while on making theories. As Piaget put it, ‘children have real understanding only of that which they invent themselves, and each time that we try to teach them something too quickly, we keep them from inventing it themselves.’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Piaget 并非教育工作者，也从未规定应当如何介入这类情况。但他的研究强烈表明，下意识地纠正儿童很可能适得其反。如果他们提出的理论总是得到这样的回应：“想得不错，不过事实其实是……”过一段时间后，他们或许就会放弃提出理论。正如 Piaget 所说：“儿童只有对自己发明的事物才有真正的理解；每当我们试图过快地教给他们某样东西时，都会妨碍他们自行发明它。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Disciples of Piaget have a tolerance for—indeed a fascination with—children’s primitive laws of physics: that things disappear when they are out of sight; that the moon and the sun follow you around; that big things float and small things sink. Einstein was intrigued by Piaget’s findings, especially by the idea that seven-year-olds insist that going faster can take more time—perhaps because this, like Einstein’s own theories of relativity, runs so contrary to common sense.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Piaget 的追随者能够容忍儿童那些朴素的物理定律，甚至会为之着迷：看不见的东西就消失了；月亮和太阳会一路跟着你；大的东西会浮起来，小的东西会沉下去。爱因斯坦对 Piaget 的研究发现很感兴趣，尤其是七岁儿童坚称速度更快反而可能花费更长时间这一观点；或许是因为它与爱因斯坦自己的相对论一样，都极其违背常识。

source.text: Disciples of Piaget have a tolerance for—indeed a fascination with—children’s primitive laws of physics: that things disappear when they are out of sight; that the moon and the sun follow you around; that big things float and small things sink.

translation.text: Piaget 的追随者能够容忍儿童那些朴素的物理定律，甚至会为之着迷：看不见的东西就消失了；月亮和太阳会一路跟着你；大的东西会浮起来，小的东西会沉下去。

source.text: Einstein was intrigued by Piaget’s findings, especially by the idea that seven-year-olds insist that going faster can take more time—perhaps because this, like Einstein’s own theories of relativity, runs so contrary to common sense.

translation.text: 爱因斯坦对 Piaget 的研究发现很感兴趣，尤其是七岁儿童坚称速度更快反而可能花费更长时间这一观点；或许是因为它与爱因斯坦自己的相对论一样，都极其违背常识。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Although every teacher in training still memorises Piaget’s successive stages of childhood development, the greater part of Piaget’s work is less well known, perhaps because schools of education regard it as ‘too deep’ for teachers. Piaget never thought of himself as a child psychologist. His real interest was epistemology—the theory of knowledge—which, like physics, was considered a branch of philosophy until Piaget came along and made it a science.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 尽管如今每位接受培训的教师仍要熟记 Piaget 划分的儿童发展连续阶段，但 Piaget 的大部分研究并不那么广为人知，或许是因为教育学院认为这些内容对教师来说“过于深奥”。Piaget 从未把自己看作儿童心理学家。他真正感兴趣的是认识论，即关于知识的理论。与物理学一样，在 Piaget 出现并使其成为一门科学以前，认识论一直被视为哲学的一个分支。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Through epistemology, Piaget explored multiple ways of knowing. He acknowledged them and examined them non-judgementally, yet with a philosopher’s analytic rigour. Since Piaget, the territory has been widely colonised by those who write about women’s ways of knowing, Afrocentric ways of knowing, even the computer’s ways of knowing. Indeed, artificial intelligence and the information-processing model of the mind owe more to Piaget than its proponents may realise.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The core of Piaget is his belief that looking carefully at how knowledge develops in children will elucidate the nature of knowledge in general. Whether this has in fact led to deeper understanding remains, like everything about Piaget, controversial. In the past decade, Piaget has been vigorously challenged by the current fashion of viewing knowledge as an intrinsic property of the brain. Ingenious experiments have demonstrated that newborn infants already have some of the knowledge that Piaget believed children constructed. But for those, like me, who still see Piaget as the giant in the field of cognitive theory, the difference between what the baby brings and what the adult has is so immense that the new discoveries do not significantly reduce the gap, but only increase the mystery.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Piaget 思想的核心，是相信仔细观察知识如何在儿童身上发展，将有助于阐明知识的一般本质。这实际上是否带来了更深入的理解，与 Piaget 相关的一切问题一样，仍有争议。在过去十年里，把知识视为大脑内在属性的观点成为潮流，对 Piaget 构成了强有力的挑战。一些设计巧妙的实验已经证明，新生儿已经拥有 Piaget 认为由儿童自行建构的某些知识。然而，对于像我一样仍把 Piaget 视为认知理论领域巨擘的人来说，婴儿与生俱来的东西和成年人最终拥有的东西之间差距极大，因此这些新发现并未显著缩小这道鸿沟，反而只让其中的奥秘更加深厚。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Armies of giant sand dunes are advancing across the world’s deserts, engulfing anything that crosses their path. They are tens of metres tall and hundreds of metres long. Fortunately, they aren’t going very fast. Even the smallest, speediest dunes only travel about 100 metres over the course of a year, while the bigger ones, which weigh something in the order of 10,000 tonnes, barely move one metre in that time. However, their insidious creep can have serious consequences if there is an oil installation or a railway line in their path.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 一支支巨型沙丘大军正在世界各地的沙漠中向前推进，吞没沿途的一切。它们高达数十米、绵延数百米。幸运的是，它们前进得并不快。即便是最小、移动最快的沙丘，一年也只能行进约100米；较大的沙丘重约1万吨，同期几乎只能移动1米。然而，如果前方有石油设施或铁路，这种不易察觉的缓慢侵袭可能造成严重后果。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: About 47% of the world’s land mass, including Antarctica, most of Australia and large areas of Africa, is classified as arid or semi-arid desert. Only around 20% of that is sand-covered, however, and over half of that is classified as ‘linear’ sand dunes. These form in a long curving wave, as a result of wind blowing strongly from several quarters, flipping them from side to side. Although linear dunes are static, sand blowing off them can cause problems for desert villages, burying crops and buildings.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 全球约47%的陆地被划为干旱或半干旱沙漠，其中包括南极洲、澳大利亚大部分地区和非洲大片地区。不过，这些土地中只有约20%被沙覆盖，而其中又有一半以上属于“线形”沙丘。强风从几个不同方向吹来，使沙丘左右翻动，形成长而弯曲的波浪状地貌。线形沙丘虽然本身静止不动，但从上面吹落的沙会给沙漠村庄带来麻烦，掩埋农作物和建筑物。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But even with strong winds, how can entire barchans move while retaining their form? That question was first answered in the mid-20th century by British explorer Ralph Alger Bagnold, and his answer hinges on the fact that dunes aren’t solid, but granular. Bagnold figured out how barchan dunes are able to move grain by grain. Imagine a single grain of sand being blown up the back of a dune by the wind and deposited on the top. More grains follow the same pattern, until the accumulated weight of piled-up sand finally pushes the top down the dune face. The grain tumbles, then stops on the face until subsequent mini-avalanches bury it. Eventually, it reappears at the back of the dune, ready to repeat the process. As this happens to every grain of sand in the dune, the whole thing creeps in the direction of the prevailing wind.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 可是，即使有强风，整座新月形沙丘怎么能在保持形状的同时移动呢？英国探险家 Ralph Alger Bagnold 在20世纪中叶首次回答了这个问题。他的答案取决于一个事实：沙丘不是固体，而是由颗粒组成。Bagnold 弄清了新月形沙丘如何一粒沙接一粒沙地移动。设想一粒沙被风沿着沙丘背面吹上去，落在顶部。越来越多沙粒以同样方式移动，直到堆积起来的沙重量够大，终于把顶部的沙推下坡面。这粒沙翻滚而下，停在坡面上，直至后来发生的小型沙崩将它埋住。最终，它会在沙丘背面再次出现，准备重复这一过程。当沙丘中的每一粒沙都经历这一过程时，整座沙丘便会朝盛行风的方向缓缓移动。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The relationship between the wind and barchan dunes is complex. As a dune grows, it modifies the speed and course of the wind, which in turn alters how that dune and its neighbours evolve. ‘Interestingly, the dune can regulate its own shape, and maintain it as it moves,’ says Dr Stéphane Douady, a physicist at École Normale Supérieure (ENS) in France. ‘Even when two dunes collide, they quickly take on their distinctive shapes again. It’s like a living organism.’
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 风与新月形沙丘之间的关系十分复杂。沙丘增大时，会改变风的速度和走向；反过来，这又会改变它自身及邻近沙丘的演变方式。法国巴黎高等师范学院（École Normale Supérieure，ENS）的物理学家 Stéphane Douady 博士说：“有意思的是，沙丘能够调节自己的形状，并在移动时保持这一形状。即使两座沙丘相撞，也会很快重新呈现各自特有的形状。它就像一个有生命的有机体。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Douady and his colleagues have also been studying an even odder phenomenon than moving dunes: some barchans actually sing. Local legends attributed the sounds to dangerous spirits which were trying to trap unwary travellers. Douady is more pragmatic. ‘It’s a strong booming noise with a low frequency,’ he explains, making a noise like a foghorn to demonstrate. ‘It can last for a long time – up to several minutes. It’s a very loud sound and you don’t understand where it’s coming from when you first hear it.’ There are about 50 dunes distributed across 35 deserts round the world that are known to sing. Douady says the sound is caused by the way sand avalanches down the faces of particular dunes. Rather than tumbling randomly, the sand grains flow in synchrony and set each other vibrating like the membrane on a gigantic loudspeaker. The synchronisation causes the air to move in and out between the grains, creating a powerful sound wave.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 杜阿迪和同事还在研究一种比沙丘移动更加奇异的现象：有些新月形沙丘真的会歌唱。当地传说把这种声音归因于企图困住粗心旅人的危险精灵。杜阿迪则更加务实。他模仿雾号的声音作示范，并解释说：“那是一种低频而强烈的轰鸣声，可以持续很长时间，最长可达数分钟。声音非常响，第一次听到时，你根本弄不清它从哪里传来。”据人们所知，全球35片沙漠中约有50座沙丘会歌唱。杜阿迪称，这种声音是沙子沿某些沙丘坡面崩落的方式造成的。沙粒并非杂乱无章地翻滚，而是同步流动，像巨型扬声器的振膜一样使彼此振动。这种同步运动使空气在沙粒之间进出，从而产生强劲的声波。

translation.text: 他模仿雾号的声音作示范，并解释说：“那是一种低频而强烈的轰鸣声，可以持续很长时间，最长可达数分钟。

source.text: It’s a very loud sound and you don’t understand where it’s coming from when you first hear it.’

translation.text: 声音非常响，第一次听到时，你根本弄不清它从哪里传来。”

source.text: There are about 50 dunes distributed across 35 deserts round the world that are known to sing.

translation.text: 据人们所知，全球35片沙漠中约有50座沙丘会歌唱。

source.text: Douady says the sound is caused by the way sand avalanches down the faces of particular dunes.

translation.text: 杜阿迪称，这种声音是沙子沿某些沙丘坡面崩落的方式造成的。

source.text: Rather than tumbling randomly, the sand grains flow in synchrony and set each other vibrating like the membrane on a gigantic loudspeaker.

translation.text: 沙粒并非杂乱无章地翻滚，而是同步流动，像巨型扬声器的振膜一样使彼此振动。

source.text: The synchronisation causes the air to move in and out between the grains, creating a powerful sound wave.

translation.text: 这种同步运动使空气在沙粒之间进出，从而产生强劲的声波。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: What really surprised the scientists, however, was that they were able to take samples of the singing sand back to France and replicate the sound at ENS, proving that it’s the sand, not the dune shape, that causes the sound. Their studies show the grains are a uniform shape, well-rounded from years of striking each other, and that the variations in size affect the tone. Crucially, the grains are coated with a special veneer, which Douady calls ‘desert glaze’, made from a precise combination of minerals from surrounding rocks including iron, aluminium, manganese, silicon and calcium. The team found that after a month or so, the veneer wore off and the grains lost their ‘voice’. ‘We managed to reproduce the desert glaze and then the grains started to sing again,’ says Douady. ‘We tried putting the coating onto different grains, but they weren’t round enough and it didn’t work. But some American colleagues made some artificial grains and managed to make them sing, after covering them in desert glaze.’ Douady has now made recordings of dunesong from all over the world which are to be made into a CD.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，真正令科学家吃惊的是，他们把会歌唱的沙子样本带回法国后，竟能在巴黎高等师范学院重现这种声音。这证明发声的是沙子，而不是沙丘的形状。研究表明，这些沙粒形状一致，经过多年相互碰撞已经变得十分圆润，而粒径差异会影响音调。关键在于，沙粒表面覆盖着一层特殊薄膜。杜阿迪称其为“沙漠釉层”；它由周围岩石中的矿物以精确比例组合而成，包括铁、铝、锰、硅和钙。团队发现，大约一个月后，这层薄膜就会磨损，沙粒也随之失去“歌声”。杜阿迪说：“我们成功重现了沙漠釉层，随后沙粒又开始歌唱。我们试着把这种涂层覆在其他沙粒上，但它们不够圆，所以没有奏效。不过，一些美国同行制作了人造沙粒，覆上沙漠釉层后成功让它们唱了起来。”如今，杜阿迪已经录下世界各地的沙丘之歌，这些录音将被制作成一张CD。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Stephen Oppenheimer explores the origins of human speech
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Stephen Oppenheimer 探索人类语言的起源

source.text: Stephen Oppenheimer explores the origins of human speech

translation.text: Stephen Oppenheimer 探索人类语言的起源

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: When did we start talking to each other and how long did it take us to become so good at it? One view of language development, held by linguists such as Noam Chomsky and anthropologists such as Richard Klein, is that language, specifically the spoken word, appeared suddenly among modern humans a mere 35,000 to 50,000 years ago and that the ability to speak words and use syntax was recently genetically hard-wired into our brains in a kind of language organ. This view of language is associated with the old idea that logical thought is dependent on words, a concept originating with Plato and much in vogue in the 19th century – that is, animals do not speak because they do not think. However, the abstract thought demonstrated in 20th-century experiments with chimpanzees and bonobos put this theory in doubt.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 人类何时开始彼此交谈，又花了多长时间才变得如此擅长交谈？Noam Chomsky 等语言学家和 Richard Klein 等人类学家对语言发展持有一种观点：语言，尤其是口语，直到区区3.5万至5万年前才突然出现在现代人类中；说出词语和使用句法的能力，是近来才通过遗传被固化在大脑中的，形成了某种语言器官。这种语言观与一个古老观念相关，即逻辑思维依赖词语。这一观念源于柏拉图，在19世纪极为盛行；也就是说，动物不会说话，是因为它们不会思考。然而，20世纪针对黑猩猩和倭黑猩猩开展的实验表明它们具有抽象思维，使这一理论受到质疑。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: An alternative to the Chomskian theory is that language developed as a series of inventions. This was first suggested by the 18th-century philosopher Etienne Bonnot de Condillac. He argued that spoken language had developed out of gesture language (langage d’action) and that both were inventions arising initially from the simple association between action and object. The theory sees gesture language as arising originally among apes as sounds accompanying gestures, with these sounds gradually becoming coded into ‘words’ as the new skill drove its own evolution. Subsequently, coded words developed into deliberate, complex communication. Evolutionary pressures promoted the development of an anatomy geared to speech – the larynx, vocal muscles and a specific part of the brain immediately next to the part responsible for gestures.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 与乔姆斯基理论相对的另一种观点认为，语言是一系列发明逐步发展而来的。18世纪哲学家 Etienne Bonnot de Condillac 最先提出这一观点。他主张，口语由动作语言（langage d’action）发展而来；二者都是发明，最初源自行动与物体之间的简单联系。按照这一理论，动作语言最初出现在类人猿中，表现为动作伴随声音；随着这种新技能推动自身演化，这些声音逐渐被编码成“词语”。此后，编码后的词语发展成有意且复杂的交流方式。进化压力又促进了适于说话的身体结构发展，包括喉部、发声肌肉以及大脑中紧邻动作控制区的特定区域。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The view that spoken language was ultimately a cultural invention like tool-making, which then drove the biological evolution of the brain and vocal apparatus, seems obvious when you think of the development of different languages. The unique features of a language such as French clearly do not result from any physiological aspect of being French but are the cultural possessions of the French-speaking community. Each language evolves from one generation to the next, constantly adapting itself to cope with the learning biases of each new set of young, immature minds.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 如果想想不同语言的发展，就会发现这样一种观点似乎很显然：口语归根结底与工具制造一样，是一项文化发明，随后又推动了大脑和发声器官的生物进化。法语等语言的独特特征，显然不是法国人在生理方面的任何特点造成的，而是法语社群拥有的文化财富。每种语言都从一代演变到下一代，不断调整自身，以适应每一批年幼、尚未成熟的新头脑在学习上的倾向。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Those anthropologists and fossil experts who accept that speech started early still tend to think of language evolution as a gradual 2-million-year process, with our own modern human species (Homo sapiens) way out at the top. A major reason for this is the perception that brain growth among humans was gradual over a similar period. Several recent changes in the fossil evidence, though, bring this into doubt.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 那些认同口语很早就已出现的人类学家和化石专家，仍倾向于把语言演化视为一个持续200万年的渐进过程，并把我们自己的现代人类物种智人（Homo sapiens）置于最顶端。一个主要原因是，人们认为人类的大脑在相近的时期内也是逐步增大的。然而，近期化石证据出现的几项变化，使这种看法受到质疑。

source.text: Several recent changes in the fossil evidence, though, bring this into doubt.

translation.text: 然而，近期化石证据出现的几项变化，使这种看法受到质疑。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The first of these is a re-dating of soil layers from the famous Olduvai Gorge in East Africa, where many key fossil remains have been found. A number of big-brained human species appear to be much older than previously thought, with several specimens dating from over a million years ago. When brain sizes for all available skulls are plotted against time using the revised dates, the result is startling: the bulk of increases in brain size was over by around 1.2 million years ago, with some African human species having brain volumes easily within the modern human range by that time.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 第一项变化，是重新测定东非著名的奥杜瓦伊峡谷土层年代；许多关键化石遗骸都是在那里发现的。一些大脑容量较大的人类物种似乎比此前认为的古老得多，其中有几个标本可追溯到100多万年前。利用修订后的年代，把所有已有头骨的脑容量按时间绘图，得到的结果令人震惊：到约120万年前，大脑容量增加的大部分过程已经结束；当时，一些非洲人类物种的脑容量已经完全处于现代人类的范围之内。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: So, we have the paradox that over the period when our brain was growing most rapidly, our material cultural development, as measured by stone tools, advanced only marginally; then, over a million years later, when the development of anatomically modern humans finally started to accelerate, artistically and technologically, our brains were actually getting smaller.

Over the period from 2.5 to 1.5 million years ago, brains were growing more rapidly than at any time since, within all the different human species. The logical conclusion is that there must have been a unique new behaviour driving brain growth, shared between all species of humans.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: So, what was driving rapid brain growth right at the beginning, 2.5 million years ago? The answer may have been staring us in the face. Namely, that not only early humans but their ancestors had started the trend in the very useful skill of verbal communication. Around 2.5 million years ago, the weather took a decided turn for the worse, becoming more variable and colder and drier. The search for food became more taxing, and there would have been a real need to communicate more effectively and cope with the worsening environment in a co-operative way. The near maximum in brain size achieved by 1.2 million years ago indicates that those early ancestors could already have been talking perfectly well. Our brain, which had developed to manipulate and organise complex symbolic aspects of speech internally, could now be turned to a variety of other tasks.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 那么，早在250万年前，究竟是什么推动大脑迅速增大？答案或许一直就在我们眼前：不仅早期人类，就连其祖先也已经开始发展口头交流这项非常实用的技能。大约250万年前，天气明显恶化，变得更加多变、寒冷和干燥。寻找食物愈发艰难，人类确实需要以更有效的方式交流，并通过合作来应对不断恶化的环境。到120万年前，大脑容量已接近最大值，这表明那些早期祖先当时可能已经能够十分流利地交谈。我们的大脑原本已经发展出在内部处理和组织语言复杂符号层面的能力，现在则可以转而承担各种其他任务。

source.text: The answer may have been staring us in the face. Namely, that not only early humans but their ancestors had started the trend in the very useful skill of verbal communication.

translation.text: 答案或许一直就在我们眼前：不仅早期人类，就连其祖先也已经开始发展口头交流这项非常实用的技能。

source.text: Around 2.5 million years ago, the weather took a decided turn for the worse, becoming more variable and colder and drier.

translation.text: 大约250万年前，天气明显恶化，变得更加多变、寒冷和干燥。

source.text: The search for food became more taxing, and there would have been a real need to communicate more effectively and cope with the worsening environment in a co-operative way.

translation.text: 寻找食物愈发艰难，人类确实需要以更有效的方式交流，并通过合作来应对不断恶化的环境。

source.text: The near maximum in brain size achieved by 1.2 million years ago indicates that those early ancestors could already have been talking perfectly well.

translation.text: 到120万年前，大脑容量已接近最大值，这表明那些早期祖先当时可能已经能够十分流利地交谈。

source.text: Our brain, which had developed to manipulate and organise complex symbolic aspects of speech internally, could now be turned to a variety of other tasks.

translation.text: 我们的大脑原本已经发展出在内部处理和组织语言复杂符号层面的能力，现在则可以转而承担各种其他任务。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: So what happened in the million-year gap after that? Why did we take so long to get to the moon? Cultural evolution aided by communication and teaching is a cumulative interactive process. If each new generation invented just one new skill or idea and passed it on with the rest to their children and cousins, you could predict exactly the same curve of cultural advance as we see from the archaeological and historical record – first very slow, then faster and faster.

passages.title: Looking at daily life in ancient Rome

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Looking at daily life in ancient Rome
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 探究古罗马的日常生活

source.text: Looking at daily life in ancient Rome

translation.text: 探究古罗马的日常生活

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In this preface to a history, the writer explains the factors affecting the scope of his study.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在这篇历史著作的序言中，作者解释了影响其研究范围的因素。

source.text: In this preface to a history, the writer explains the factors affecting the scope of his study.

translation.text: 在这篇历史著作的序言中，作者解释了影响其研究范围的因素。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: If our ideas on Roman life are not to become lost in confusion, we must study it within a strictly defined time. Nothing changes more rapidly than human customs. Looking at our own more familiar world, apart from the great scientific discoveries of recent centuries which have turned it upside down—steam, electricity, railways, motor cars and aeroplanes, for example—it is clear that the elementary forms of everyday life have been subject to increasing change. Potatoes, for example, were not introduced into Europe until the sixteenth century, coffee was first drunk there in the late sixteenth or early seventeenth, and the banana was used in desserts in Europe at the beginning of the twentieth. The law of change was not less operative in antiquity. It was a commonplace of Roman rhetoric to contrast the crude simplicity of the Republic (509BC–27BC) with the luxury and refinement of the imperial times which followed. There is no common measure, whether of home, or house, or furniture, between ages which are so different.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 如果不想让我们对罗马生活的认识陷入混乱，就必须把研究严格限定在某一时期。没有什么比人类习俗变化得更快。看看我们更熟悉的当今世界，且不说近几个世纪令世界发生翻天覆地变化的重大科学发现——例如蒸汽、电力、铁路、汽车和飞机——显而易见，日常生活的基本形式一直在经历越来越多的变化。例如，马铃薯直到16世纪才传入欧洲；咖啡到16世纪末或17世纪初才开始在那里饮用；香蕉则到20世纪初才被用于欧洲的甜点。变化的规律在古代同样发挥作用。罗马修辞中有一个常见说法，就是把共和国时期（公元前509年—公元前27年）的粗朴简约，与随后帝国时代的奢华精致相对照。如此不同的时代之间，无论家庭、住宅还是家具，都没有共同的衡量尺度。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Since a choice of time must necessarily be made, this history will confine itself to studying the generation which was born about the middle of the first century AD, toward the end of the reign of Claudius (41–54AD) or the beginning of the reign of Nero (54–68AD), and which lived on into the reign of Trajan (98–117AD) or of Hadrian (117–138AD). This generation saw the Roman Empire at its most powerful and prosperous. It was witness to the last conquests of the Caesars: the conquest of Dacia, in modern-day eastern Europe, which brought vast mineral wealth into the Empire, and the conquest of Arabia, which helped to bring the riches of India and East Asia flooding into Rome. In the material domain, this generation attained the pinnacle of ancient civilisation.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 既然必须选择一个时期，本书便把研究限定在这样一代人：他们大约出生于公元1世纪中叶，即克劳狄乌斯统治末期（公元41—54年）或尼禄统治初期（公元54—68年），并一直生活到图拉真（公元98—117年）或哈德良（公元117—138年）统治时期。这一代人见证了罗马帝国最强盛、最繁荣的时代，也目睹了历代凯撒最后的征服行动：征服位于今天东欧的达契亚，为帝国带来巨额矿产财富；征服阿拉伯，则推动印度和东亚的财富大量涌入罗马。在物质领域，这一代人达到了古代文明的巅峰。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: By a fortunate coincidence—all the more fortunate in that Latin* literature was soon to run nearly dry—this generation is the one whose records combine to offer us the most complete picture of Roman life that we possess. We have a profusion of vivid and picturesque descriptions, precise and colourful, in such works as the Epigrams of Martial, the Satires of Juvenal and the Letters of Pliny. In addition, the Forum of Trajan in Rome itself and the ruins of Herculaneum and Pompeii, the two prosperous resorts buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79AD, supply an immense fund of archaeological evidence. Later excavations have also restored to us the ruins of the city of Ostia, which date in the main from the time when the Emperor Hadrian created this great commercial city as a realisation of his town planning ideas. Fortune has favoured the historian of this time.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 一个幸运的巧合是，这一代人留下的各类记录共同为我们呈现了现存最完整的罗马生活图景；考虑到拉丁文学*不久后便几近枯竭，这一巧合更显幸运。马提亚尔的《警句集》、尤维纳利斯的《讽刺诗》和普林尼的《书信集》等作品，为我们提供了大量生动鲜明、准确而丰富多彩的描述。此外，罗马城内的图拉真广场，以及赫库兰尼姆和庞贝的遗址，也提供了极其丰富的考古证据；这两座繁荣的度假城镇在公元79年维苏威火山喷发时被掩埋。后来的发掘还让奥斯蒂亚城遗址重见天日。遗址主体可追溯至哈德良皇帝按照自己的城市规划理念，把这里建设成一座大型商业城市的时期。幸运眷顾了研究这一时代的历史学家。
