blocks.sourceNormalizedText: “The technical solutions just aren’t there yet for dealing with broadacre salinity, nor are the social and economic solutions. How do you introduce the land-use changes that are needed when people still need to make a living?” Howell asks. There is no satisfactory solution yet. These features help to reveal where groundwater is stored, dictate the direction of groundwater movement, and are critical to predicting or ruling out salinity hot-spots.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Using data from the Murray River region, scientists have revealed a network of ancient drainage systems that channelled water beneath the current land-surface. These buried channels may carry salt and sometimes run at right angles to channels on the surface. This implies that the salt could move underground in quite a different direction to what one would expect by looking at surface slope and drainage. One of the biggest advances in detection, says Professor Neil Phillips, has come with the integration of different techniques such as magnetics, electromagnetics and radiometrics, and ground mapping. Individually, these technologies only gave clues to what was going on underground. Together they provide a far more revealing picture of the subsurface landscape, several hundred metres deep. Advanced airborne electromagnetics, in particular, enables scientists to take “slices” of the landscape at depths of five metres, ten metres, fifteen metres and so on, to determine where salt may be stored at depth. This is building up a four-dimensional picture of the subsurface landscape, enabling researchers to understand movements of salt in length, breadth, depth and time. From such technologies it will be possible to locate salt stores, identify how saline they are, look at man-made and natural changes to the landscape that may cause it to mobilise, and then predict where it will head to and over what time span. This in turn will give the salt warriors time to model various ways of containing or curbing the menace, see what works best and then try it out on the ground.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 科学家利用墨累河地区的数据，揭示出一套古代排水系统网络；这些系统曾在如今的地表之下输送水流。被掩埋的河道可能携带盐分，有时甚至与地表河道成直角。这意味着，盐分在地下的移动方向可能与根据地表坡度和排水情况所预期的方向大不相同。 Neil Phillips 教授说，探测领域最大的进步之一，是把磁力、电磁、放射性测量和地面测绘等不同技术结合起来。单独使用时，这些技术只能提供地下状况的线索；结合起来后，它们便能呈现清晰得多的地下景观图像，深度可达数百米。尤其是先进的航空电磁技术，使科学家能够在五米、十米、十五米等不同深度对景观进行“切片”，从而确定盐分可能储存在地下何处。这正在构建一幅地下景观的四维图像，让研究人员可以从长度、宽度、深度和时间四个维度理解盐分的移动。 借助这些技术，人们将能够找到盐分储存区，确定其中盐分浓度，考察可能使盐分开始移动的人为和自然景观变化，继而预测盐分会流向何处、需要多长时间。这样一来，抗盐人员便有时间建立模型，比较控制或遏制这一威胁的不同方法，找出效果最佳的方案，再到实地试用。

source.text: One of the biggest advances in detection, says Professor Neil Phillips, has come with the integration of different techniques such as magnetics, electromagnetics and radiometrics, and ground mapping.

source.text: Individually, these technologies only gave clues to what was going on underground. Together they provide a far more revealing picture of the subsurface landscape, several hundred metres deep.

translation.text: 单独使用时，这些技术只能提供地下状况的线索；结合起来后，它们便能呈现清晰得多的地下景观图像，深度可达数百米。

source.text: Advanced airborne electromagnetics, in particular, enables scientists to take “slices” of the landscape at depths of five metres, ten metres, fifteen metres and so on, to determine where salt may be stored at depth.

translation.text: 尤其是先进的航空电磁技术，使科学家能够在五米、十米、十五米等不同深度对景观进行“切片”，从而确定盐分可能储存在地下何处。

source.text: This is building up a four-dimensional picture of the subsurface landscape, enabling researchers to understand movements of salt in length, breadth, depth and time.

translation.text: 这正在构建一幅地下景观的四维图像，让研究人员可以从长度、宽度、深度和时间四个维度理解盐分的移动。

source.text: From such technologies it will be possible to locate salt stores, identify how saline they are, look at man-made and natural changes to the landscape that may cause it to mobilise, and then predict where it will head to and over what time span.

translation.text: 借助这些技术，人们将能够找到盐分储存区，确定其中盐分浓度，考察可能使盐分开始移动的人为和自然景观变化，继而预测盐分会流向何处、需要多长时间。

source.text: This in turn will give the salt warriors time to model various ways of containing or curbing the menace, see what works best and then try it out on the ground.

translation.text: 这样一来，抗盐人员便有时间建立模型，比较控制或遏制这一威胁的不同方法，找出效果最佳的方案，再到实地试用。

passages.title: Some views on the use of headphones

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Some views on the use of headphones
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 对使用耳机的一些看法

source.text: Some views on the use of headphones

translation.text: 对使用耳机的一些看法

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Whether wearing headphones at work, or in other areas of everyday life, is a good thing or a bad thing has generated a lot of research and opinion
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 无论是在工作中还是在日常生活的其他场合，戴耳机究竟是好是坏，都引发了大量研究和看法。

source.text: Whether wearing headphones at work, or in other areas of everyday life, is a good thing or a bad thing has generated a lot of research and opinion

translation.text: 无论是在工作中还是在日常生活的其他场合，戴耳机究竟是好是坏，都引发了大量研究和看法。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: To visit a typical modern office today is to walk into a room with possibly a dozen songs playing simultaneously but to hear none of them. Up to half of younger workers listen to music on their headphones, and nearly all of them think it makes them better at their jobs. In survey after survey, people report with confidence that music makes them happier, better at concentrating, and more productive.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 如今走进一间典型的现代办公室，房间里可能同时播放着十来首歌，你却一首也听不见。年轻员工中，多达一半会戴耳机听音乐，而其中几乎所有人都认为，这能让自己工作得更好。一次又一次调查中，人们都自信地表示，音乐使他们更快乐、更能集中注意力，工作效率也更高。

source.text: To visit a typical modern office today is to walk into a room with possibly a dozen songs playing simultaneously but to hear none of them.

translation.text: 如今走进一间典型的现代办公室，房间里可能同时播放着十来首歌，你却一首也听不见。

source.text: Up to half of younger workers listen to music on their headphones, and nearly all of them think it makes them better at their jobs.

translation.text: 年轻员工中，多达一半会戴耳机听音乐，而其中几乎所有人都认为，这能让自己工作得更好。

source.text: In survey after survey, people report with confidence that music makes them happier, better at concentrating, and more productive.

translation.text: 一次又一次调查中，人们都自信地表示，音乐使他们更快乐、更能集中注意力，工作效率也更高。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Scientists do not share this belief; they maintain that listening to music hurts people’s ability to recall other things they should be doing, and any pop song, loud or soft, reduces overall performance for both extroverts and introverts. A Taiwanese study linked music that has lyrics to lower marks on concentration tests for college students, and other research has shown music with lyrics scrambles our brains’ verbal-processing skills. “As silence has the best overall performance, it would still be advisable that people work in silence,” another reporter dryly concluded.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 科学家并不认同这种看法。他们认为，听音乐会损害人们记住其他待办事项的能力；任何流行歌曲，无论音量大小，都会降低外向者和内向者的整体表现。台湾一项研究发现，带歌词的音乐与大学生专注力测试分数较低有关；其他研究也表明，带歌词的音乐会扰乱大脑处理语言的能力。另一名报道者不动声色地总结道：“既然安静环境下整体表现最佳，仍然应该建议人们安静地工作。”

translation.text: 科学家并不认同这种看法。他们认为，听音乐会损害人们记住其他待办事项的能力；任何流行歌曲，无论音量大小，都会降低外向者和内向者的整体表现。

source.text: “As silence has the best overall performance, it would still be advisable that people work in silence,” another reporter dryly concluded.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The question is therefore: if headphones are so bad for productivity, why do so many people at work have them? One factor to consider is that countries like the USA have moved from a farming and manufacturing economy to a service economy, with an emphasis on jobs in offices that require higher levels of concentration, reflection and creativity. As an estimated 70 percent of office workers work in open-plan office spaces, it is more important to create one’s own enclosing bubble of sound. Lending strength to the argument for headphones at work is evidence that music relaxes our muscles, improves our mood, and may even moderately reduce blood pressure, heart rate and anxiety.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 因此问题是：如果耳机如此有损工作效率，为什么职场中还有那么多人佩戴？需要考虑的一个因素是，美国等国家已经从农业和制造业经济转向服务经济，工作重点也转向需要更高专注力、思考能力和创造力的办公室岗位。据估计，70%的办公室员工在开放式办公空间工作，因此营造一个包围自己的声音气泡变得更加重要。支持工作中戴耳机这一主张的证据还包括：音乐能放松肌肉、改善情绪，甚至可能适度降低血压、心率和焦虑程度。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The story of headphones began in 1910, when the US Navy received an odd letter written in purple ink on blue-and-pink paper. The letter writer, an eccentric inventor and repairman named Nathaniel Baldwin, from the US state of Utah, made what at the time was an astonishing claim: he had built, in his kitchen, a new kind of headset that could amplify sound. This was an opportune invention for the Navy, which asked for a sound test and then enthusiastically adopted the headsets, later called headphones, and used them in World War I for naval radio communication.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 耳机的故事始于1910年。当时，美国海军收到一封奇怪的信，信中文字用紫色墨水写在蓝粉相间的信纸上。写信人是来自美国犹他州的古怪发明家兼修理工 Nathaniel Baldwin。他提出了一个在当时令人震惊的说法：自己在厨房里制造了一种能够放大声音的新型头戴设备。对海军来说，这项发明来得正是时候。海军要求进行声音测试，随后热情采用这种头戴设备；它后来被称为耳机，并在第一次世界大战期间用于海军无线电通信。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The purpose of headphones is to concentrate a quiet and private sound in the ear of the listener, which is a radical departure from music’s social purpose in history. “Music, together with dance, co-evolved biologically and culturally to serve as a technology of social bonding,” Nils L. Wallin and Björn Merker wrote in The Origins of Music. Songs don’t leave behind bones, but evidence of musical notation dates back to Sumeria, 3,500 years ago, and in 1995 archaeologists discovered a bone flute in southern Europe estimated to be 44,000 years old. If music evolved as a social glue for the species, as a way to make groups and keep them together, headphones have done what writing and literacy did for language – they made music private.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 耳机的用途，是把轻柔而私密的声音集中送入听者耳中，这与音乐在历史上的社会功能截然不同。Nils L. Wallin 和 Björn Merker 在《音乐的起源》中写道：“音乐与舞蹈在生物和文化层面共同进化，成为建立社会联结的技术。”歌曲不会留下骨骼，但音乐记谱法的证据可追溯到3,500年前的苏美尔；1995年，考古学家还在南欧发现了一支估计有44,000年历史的骨笛。如果音乐进化成了把人类群体组织起来并维系在一起的社会黏合剂，那么耳机对音乐所做的，就像文字和读写能力对语言所做的一样——它们使音乐变得私密。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Author and columnist Stephen Marche wrote that separation from other people is one of the first things ordinary Americans spend their money achieving. It is “a by-product of a long-standing national appetite for independence,” he said. Americans are not alone in their desire for personal independence and privacy. Marche is right; wealth can buy – and modern technology can deliver – personal independence, and it is this that people have always sought.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 作家兼专栏作者 Stephen Marche 写道，普通美国人花钱实现的首要目标之一，就是与他人分隔开来。他说，这是“一个国家长期渴求独立所产生的副产品”。希望拥有个人独立和隐私的并非只有美国人。Marche 说得没错：财富可以买到、现代技术也能带来个人独立，而人们一直追求的正是这一点。

source.text: Author and columnist Stephen Marche wrote that separation from other people is one of the first things ordinary Americans spend their money achieving.

translation.text: 作家兼专栏作者 Stephen Marche 写道，普通美国人花钱实现的首要目标之一，就是与他人分隔开来。

translation.text: 他说，这是“一个国家长期渴求独立所产生的副产品”。

source.text: Americans are not alone in their desire for personal independence and privacy.

translation.text: 希望拥有个人独立和隐私的并非只有美国人。

translation.text: Marche 说得没错：财富可以买到、现代技术也能带来个人独立，而人们一直追求的正是这一点。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Dr Michael Bull, an expert on personal music devices from the University of Sussex in the UK, has repeatedly made the larger point that personal music devices change how we relate to public spaces. Controlling our public spaces is more important now that more people are moving from the edges of cities to live in urban centres. “With the urban space, the more it’s inhabited, the safer you feel,” Bull says. “You feel safe if you can feel people there, but you don’t want to interact with them.” Headphones create shields for wearers, separating them from other people and their surroundings. Headphones have their own rules of good manners; they are like wearing a “Do not disturb” sign. We assume that people wearing them are busy and we should respect their privacy, so now people wear them to appear busy. In fact, it is now becoming quite common for people not to listen to anything at all, but just to wear headphones.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 英国苏塞克斯大学的个人音乐设备专家 Michael Bull 博士一再提出一个更宏观的观点：个人音乐设备改变了我们与公共空间相处的方式。随着越来越多人从城市边缘迁往市中心生活，掌控自己的公共空间如今变得更加重要。Bull 说：“城市空间里，住的人越多，你就越觉得安全。能感觉到人们在那里，你就会安心，但又不想与他们互动。”耳机为佩戴者形成一道屏障，把他们与其他人和周围环境隔开。使用耳机有其自身的礼貌规则；它就像挂着一块“请勿打扰”的牌子。我们会假定戴耳机的人正忙，并应尊重他们的隐私，因此如今有人戴耳机只是为了显得忙碌。事实上，只戴着耳机却什么也不听，正变得相当普遍。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: However, as pointed out at the beginning of this piece, although scientists have stated that headphones are bad for productivity, people still wear them at work. It is not just that headphones create privacy out of public areas, but also that music causes people to relax and reflect and pause. The outcome of relaxation, reflection and pausing at work won’t be captured in minute-to-minute productivity metrics. What must be considered is that in moments of extreme focus, our attention radiates outward, toward the problem, rather than inward, on how to solve the problem. However, with music “When our minds are at ease, we’re more likely to direct the spotlight of attention inward,” Jonah Lehrer wrote in his book Imagine: How Creativity Works. “The answers have been there all along. We just weren’t listening.” In a crowded world, real estate is the ultimate scarce resource, and a headphone is a small invisible fence around our minds – making space, creating separation, and helping us listen to ourselves.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，正如本文开头指出的，虽然科学家表示耳机会损害工作效率，人们在工作时仍会佩戴。原因不只是耳机能在公共区域中创造隐私，还在于音乐使人放松、思考和暂停片刻。工作中放松、思考和暂停所产生的结果，无法反映在逐分钟计算的生产率指标中。必须考虑的是，在极度专注的时刻，我们的注意力会向外投射，集中在问题本身，而不是向内思考如何解决问题。然而，听音乐时情况会有所不同。Jonah Lehrer 在《想象：创造力如何运作》一书中写道：“当心绪放松时，我们更可能把注意力的聚光灯转向内心。答案一直都在那里，只是我们没有倾听。”在拥挤的世界里，空间是最稀缺的资源，而耳机就像围绕心灵的一道无形小栅栏——开辟空间、制造分隔，也帮助我们倾听自己。

translation.text: 明星员工

source.text: Most organisations are looking for talent.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One widely held assumption about talent is that it is a reasonably fixed characteristic and it is therefore the job of organisations to identify, recruit and retain star performers. This belief affects the way people are managed in the workplace. Most recruitment decisions are influenced by the skills and abilities of an individual rather than their aptitude and attitude. In terms of career development, organisations invest in staff who have been selected to reach higher-level positions, while ignoring front-line employees and people with less perceived potential. This idea, that talent is a fixed, identifiable characteristic – and that those firms with the best people do the best – is both flawed and harmful to people and organisations. There is a lot of evidence on this point, and it is useful to highlight some of the most pertinent arguments.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 关于人才，一个广为接受的假设是，人才是一种相当固定的特质，因此机构的任务就是识别、招募并留住明星员工。这种观念会影响职场中的人员管理方式。大多数招聘决定看重个人已经具备的技能和能力，而不是资质与态度。在职业发展方面，机构会投资培养那些被选中进入更高职位的员工，却忽视一线员工和被认为潜力较小的人。这种观点认为，人才是一种固定且可以识别的特质，拥有最优秀员工的公司表现也最好；然而，它既有缺陷，又会伤害个人和机构。支持这一点的证据很多，下面有必要重点介绍一些最相关的论点。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: First, are there stars? There is no question that in every field, from sports to computer programming to music, there are people who are better than the rest. As psychologist Dean Keith Simonton, who has spent his career studying greatness, has said, ‘Wherever you look, the same story can be told. Identify the ten per cent who have achieved the most in a certain endeavour. Count the accomplishments they have to their credit. Now tally the accomplishments of the remaining 90 per cent. The first tally will equal or surpass the second.’ For instance, in music, 16 individuals have produced about 50 per cent of the Western classical music that is performed and recorded today, while another 235 composers have produced the remaining half. The more interesting questions concern not the existence of stars, but whether these stars can be reliably identified and, even more importantly, whether their talent is a fixed aspect or can be altered.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Identifying the best people is tricky. Quality of performance changes over time and this is true whether we are talking about professors or footballers. If performance naturally varies, any measurement taken at a single point in time, such as when someone is being hired, will have error and imprecision. Therefore, single assessments of talent are likely to contain mistakes in their categorisation of people. Also, judgements about performance and ability depend on the standards used to judge what is good and bad. It should surprise no-one that for Bach to be considered a great musician, standards of music needed to change to embrace the qualities that his compositions possessed. Similarly, artists and art come in and out of fashion, which means that what is genius depends not only on a person’s ability, but on the prevailing standards used to evaluate output.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 识别最优秀的人并不容易。表现质量会随时间变化，无论谈论的是教授还是足球运动员，都是如此。如果表现本来就会波动，那么在某个单一时点进行的任何测量——例如招聘时的测量——都会存在误差和不精确。因此，只评估一次人才，很可能会把人分错类别。此外，对表现和能力的判断取决于用来判定好坏的标准。巴赫要被视为伟大音乐家，音乐标准就必须发生变化，接纳其作品所具有的特质；这不应令任何人惊讶。同样，艺术家和艺术作品会时兴也会过时，这意味着，何为天才不仅取决于个人能力，也取决于当时用来评价成果的标准。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Finally, it is difficult to evaluate people and their abilities with precision. In the domain of work, research shows that the best predictors of job performance tend to be measures of intelligence. But even these measures correlate only loosely with performance, which means that more than 80 per cent of the variation in performance is unexplained by even the best predictors. Even in the sports arena, where one would think natural ability would be readily assessed because sports teams spend lots of resources on identifying talent, mistakes get made. Basketball star Michael Jordan was dropped by his high-school basketball coach and a number of top American football quarterbacks were available early in their careers because they were not considered good enough by various teams.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This leads on to the next question: is talent born or made? Should organisations assume that almost anyone can become a star performer, which implies that there ought to be a greater emphasis on motivation and development, or do they just figure out who is good and who isn’t? Here the evidence is clear: talent is at least as much ‘created’ as inherent and, more importantly, the customary way companies think about identifying talent almost certainly works to destroy a lot of untapped potential. Decades of research by K. Anders Ericsson, professor of psychology at Florida State University, show that exceptional performance doesn’t happen without around ten years of nearly daily, deliberate practice for about four hours a day, by people who, with the assistance of their coaches, have access to the best techniques. Once achieved, exceptional performance can’t be maintained without relentless effort. So performance may be as much a consequence of training as it is of innate ability, which suggests that performance can be altered by how people are managed.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这就引出了下一个问题：人才是天生的，还是后天造就的？机构是否应当假定几乎任何人都能成为明星员工，这意味着应该更加重视激励和培养；还是只需判断谁优秀、谁不优秀？证据在这里十分明确：才华由后天“造就”的程度至少不亚于天生因素；更重要的是，公司通常用来识别人才的思维方式，几乎肯定会摧毁大量尚未开发的潜力。佛罗里达州立大学心理学教授 K. Anders Ericsson 数十年的研究显示，一个人必须在教练帮助下接触最好的训练方法，并在约十年里几乎每天刻意练习约四小时，才可能取得非凡表现。达到这种水平后，如果没有坚持不懈的努力，也无法维持。因此，训练对表现的影响可能与天生能力不相上下；这说明，人员管理方式能够改变人的表现。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Further research by Stanford psychology professor Carol Dweck shows that the tendency of organisations to see performance results as an opportunity for an ‘assessment’ of ability, results in lower performance and poor motivation. Dweck identified two sets of goals that people bring to a performance context: ‘performance goals, where the purpose is to validate one’s ability or avoid demonstrating a lack of ability, and learning goals, where the aim is to acquire new knowledge and skills’. People with performance goals have been shown to be more prone to helpless behaviour and debilitation after a setback, while people with learning goals strive for higher performance. The implications for managing people and talent are clear. Seeing talent as fixed and job performance as a way of classifying people creates a self-fulfilling prophecy in which ability and intelligence do become fixed. By contrast, seeing ability as malleable leads to a different sort of self-fulfilling prophecy, in which individuals and their employers may invest in ways to enhance performance.

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Katelin Butler, returning to her home city of Hobart, reflects on how a new museum has brought about change.

source.text: Katelin Butler, returning to her home city of Hobart, reflects on how a new museum has brought about change.

translation.text: Katelin Butler 回到故乡霍巴特，思考一座新博物馆如何带来改变。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As an eighteen-year-old living in the small Australian island state of Tasmania, moving to the ‘mainland’ could not happen soon enough. Now, ten years later, I look forward to going home. This is probably because I’ve grown up, but also perhaps because the cultural landscape of Tasmania has matured. The latest addition to Tasmania’s cultural scene is David Walsh’s Museum of Old and New Art (MONA), a museum that has established Hobart, the capital city of Tasmania, on the global art circuit.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 18岁时，我住在澳大利亚的岛州塔斯马尼亚，只盼着尽快搬到“大陆”。如今十年过去，我却期待回家。这大概是因为我长大了，也可能是因为塔斯马尼亚的文化面貌已经成熟。塔斯马尼亚文化领域最新增添的成员，是 David Walsh 创办的古今艺术博物馆（MONA）。这座博物馆让塔斯马尼亚首府霍巴特进入了全球艺术版图。

source.text: The latest addition to Tasmania’s cultural scene is David Walsh’s Museum of Old and New Art (MONA), a museum that has established Hobart, the capital city of Tasmania, on the global art circuit.

translation.text: 塔斯马尼亚文化领域最新增添的成员，是 David Walsh 创办的古今艺术博物馆（MONA）。这座博物馆让塔斯马尼亚首府霍巴特进入了全球艺术版图。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This building is an example of how art and architecture can have an instant impact on the social and cultural reputation of a place. Andrew Bain of The Sydney Morning Herald wrote, ‘In a virtual blink, Hobart’s cultural landscape has been transformed, with art, wine, fine food and stylish accommodation becoming integral features of the city … If Hobart’s makeover has an origin, it’s the opening of MONA – the Museum of Old and New Art.’ MONA is said to have been solely instrumental in the reinvention of Hobart as a cultural hub.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: MONA made the national press and international blogs before it opened. After that, Tourism Industry Council of Tasmania’s chief executive, Luke Martin, claimed that MONA was proving so popular it was underpinning the tourism industry in Tasmania. However, MONA’s effect on Hobart has broader ramifications for Tasmania’s tourism industry. As reported in Hobart’s local paper, The Mercury, there is concern about how long people are staying in Tasmania. Rather than spending a week in the state and hiring a car to experience the beauty of the Tasmanian landscape, people are making short stays in Hobart only to visit the gallery. The next challenge for the state is how to entice holiday-makers to stay longer, and to venture further afield. Tasmania is more than a one-hit wonder.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: MONA 尚未开放便登上全国报纸和国际博客。开放后，塔斯马尼亚旅游业委员会首席执行官 Luke Martin 声称，MONA 正大受欢迎，已经成为塔斯马尼亚旅游业的支柱。然而，MONA 给霍巴特带来的变化，对塔斯马尼亚旅游业也有更广泛的影响。正如霍巴特当地报纸《水星报》报道的那样，人们担心游客在塔斯马尼亚停留的时间。游客没有在全州游览一周并租车欣赏塔斯马尼亚风景之美，而是仅为了参观这座美术馆，才在霍巴特短暂停留。该州接下来的挑战，是如何吸引度假者停留更久，并前往更远的地区。塔斯马尼亚不只有这一处亮点。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: According to Martin, possibilities for packaging up MONA with visits to other galleries around Tasmania are being investigated. Although not directly related to these investigations, the 1891 Queen Victoria Museum and Art Gallery at Royal Park in Launceston is currently being restored to its original condition; there are also plans to extensively redevelop the Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery in Hobart. In addition to this, there are up to twenty other existing quality galleries in the state. So there is more to see than just MONA.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Although large, the building is rather nondescript, sitting heavily on the edge of the Derwent River. MONA’s ‘wow factor’ comes from the notoriety of David Walsh, the museum’s millionaire founder, and his choice of unusual artworks. The architecture has more depth of meaning and does exactly as it should: it supports the vision of the museum, essentially the vision of Walsh. It’s a new building in the context of a maturing city. The dark, moody labyrinth of gallery spaces could be likened to the mind of the eccentric founder himself. Each artwork appears to be integrated into the dark materiality of the architecture – the interiors are far from light, bright and neutral, as might be seen in a more traditional gallery. The dim lighting and rough, rocky surfaces are a reminder that visitors are three levels underground.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这座建筑虽然很大，却相当不起眼，沉甸甸地坐落在德文特河边。MONA 令人惊叹之处，来自其百万富翁创办人 David Walsh 的名声，以及他对非同寻常艺术品的选择。建筑本身有更深层的含义，也恰如其分地发挥作用：它支撑着博物馆的愿景，而这本质上就是 Walsh 的愿景。在一座逐渐成熟的城市中，这是一栋新建筑。阴暗而情绪深沉的迷宫式展览空间，可以比作这位古怪创办人本人的内心。每件艺术品似乎都融入建筑幽暗的物质质感之中；这里的室内空间绝非传统美术馆中常见的明亮、通透和中性。昏暗灯光与粗糙岩石表面不断提醒参观者：他们正位于地下三层。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The warped, mirrored surface at the museum’s entry could be seen as the start of a journey of reflecting on one’s existence. Much of the art explores the human condition – there are uninhibited artistic descriptions of human relationships, death, and even the digestion process. Going to a gallery with such confronting artworks with your parents is an interesting experience; I was pleasantly surprised by my parents’ openness to the exhibitions. My father, who normally whisks through a gallery while my mother likes to take her time, happily spent almost five hours at MONA; the urge to linger is a common feeling here. This is because the gallery engages all of the senses, and visitors often pause to experience the effect each artwork has on them. This raises the question of who is actually visiting MONA – and it’s definitely not just the normal gallery-goers. People from all kinds of socioeconomic backgrounds are curious about what lies within the subterranean maze of MONA. Conservative minds are being opened, which is a good thing anywhere.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 博物馆入口处变形的镜面，可以被视为一段反思自身存在之旅的起点。许多艺术作品都在探索人的生存状态，毫不掩饰地以艺术形式描绘人际关系、死亡，甚至消化过程。和父母一起参观拥有如此直面现实作品的美术馆，是一种有趣的体验；父母对展览的开放态度令我惊喜。父亲平时总会匆匆走过美术馆，母亲却喜欢慢慢观看；这次父亲很愉快地在 MONA 待了近五小时。来到这里，人们普遍会想多停留一会儿。这是因为美术馆能调动全部感官，参观者往往会停下来，感受每件艺术品对自己产生的影响。这也引出了一个问题：究竟是谁在参观 MONA？答案肯定不只是平时常去美术馆的人。来自各种社会经济背景的人，都好奇 MONA 地下迷宫里藏着什么。思想保守的人也在逐渐敞开心扉，这无论在哪里都是好事。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Walsh’s antiquities collection is superb, but he knew that old coins would compete for attention against new works that are more challenging in scale and subject matter, hence the device of setting antiquities among twentieth- and twenty-first-century works. For me, one of the intriguing outcomes of this strategy was an intensified feeling that the makers of the coins and antiquities were the great contemporary artists of their time.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Walsh 收藏的古物极其出色，但他知道，古钱币必须与规模和题材都更具挑战性的新作品争夺注意力，因此采取了把古物放在20世纪和21世纪作品之间的办法。对我来说，这一策略带来的一个耐人寻味的结果，是让我更强烈地感到：制作这些钱币和古物的人，正是他们那个时代伟大的当代艺术家。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The so-called Bilbao Effect has worked its magic on Hobart because, just as Frank Gehry’s Guggenheim Museum has transformed the city of Bilbao in Spain, MONA has been a magnet for tourists in Hobart. However, the architectural ‘wow’ factor of the Guggenheim was the most famous component of that city’s transformation, whereas Fender Katsalidis’s MONA does not have the same spectacular impact as the shimmering metal surfaces of Gehry’s building. Walsh himself abhors descriptions of MONA as the Bilbao of the south, saying that Fender Katsalidis solved a problem when he designed MONA, in executing a project of this scale in an underground location. Walsh contrasts this with what he describes as the “architectural self-indulgence of Gehry when designing the Guggenheim in Bilbao.” Call it the Bilbao Effect, but this phenomenon has been around for thousands of years – good public architecture forms the centrepiece of a city. This is probably true, but like the Guggenheim, MONA has initiated something very important for Tasmania, and for Hobart in particular. Now the question is how Tasmania will build on David Walsh’s input into its cultural setting.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 所谓“毕尔巴鄂效应”已经在霍巴特显现魔力：正如 Frank Gehry 设计的古根海姆博物馆改变了西班牙毕尔巴鄂市，MONA 也成了霍巴特吸引游客的磁石。不过，古根海姆博物馆在建筑上令人惊叹的效果，是毕尔巴鄂转型中最著名的部分；Fender Katsalidis 设计的 MONA 却没有 Gehry 那座建筑闪亮金属表面所带来的同等壮观冲击。Walsh 本人非常厌恶把 MONA 称为“南方的毕尔巴鄂”。他说，Fender Katsalidis 设计 MONA 时，是在解决一个难题：如何在地下完成如此规模的项目。他把这一点与自己所谓“Gehry 设计毕尔巴鄂古根海姆博物馆时在建筑上的自我放纵”相对照。姑且把它称为毕尔巴鄂效应，但这种现象已经存在数千年——优秀的公共建筑会成为一座城市的核心。这种说法大概没错；但与古根海姆博物馆一样，MONA 已经为塔斯马尼亚、尤其是霍巴特开启了非常重要的新局面。现在的问题是，塔斯马尼亚将如何在 David Walsh 为当地文化环境作出贡献的基础上继续发展。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: To most of us, termites are destructive insects which can cause damage on a devastating scale. But according to Dr Rupert Soar of Loughborough University’s School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering, these pests may serve a useful purpose for us after all. His multidisciplinary team of British and American engineers and biologists has set out to investigate the giant mounds built by termites in Namibia, in sub-Saharan Africa, as part of the most extensive study of these structures ever taken.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在大多数人看来，白蚁是一种破坏性昆虫，能够造成毁灭性的损害。不过，拉夫堡大学机械与制造工程学院的 Rupert Soar 博士认为，这些害虫或许终究也能为我们派上用场。他带领一支由英国和美国工程师及生物学家组成的跨学科团队，开始研究撒哈拉以南非洲纳米比亚境内白蚁筑造的巨型蚁丘；这是迄今对此类结构开展的规模最大的一项研究。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Termite mounds are impressive for their size alone; typically they are three metres high, and some as tall as eight metres have been found. They also reach far into the earth, where the insects ‘mine’ their building materials, carefully selecting each grain of sand they use. The termite’s nest is contained in the central cavity of the mound, safely protected from the harsh environment outside. The mound itself is formed of an intricate lattice of tunnels, which split into smaller and smaller tunnels, much like a person’s blood vessels.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 白蚁丘仅凭其体量就令人惊叹：通常高达3米，有些甚至达到8米。它们还深入地下；白蚁在那里“开采”建筑材料，并仔细挑选所用的每一粒沙。白蚁巢位于蚁丘中央的空腔中，安全地免受外界恶劣环境影响。蚁丘本身由错综复杂的隧道网构成，这些隧道不断分叉成越来越细小的通道，很像人体的血管。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This complex system of tunnels draws in air from the outside, capturing wind energy to drive it through the mound. It also serves to expel spent respiratory gases from the nest to prevent the termites from suffocating, so ensuring them a continuous provision of fresh, breathable air. So detailed is the design that the nest stays within three degrees of a constant temperature, despite variations on the outside of up to 50 °C, from blistering heat in the daytime to below freezing on the coldest nights. The mound also automatically regulates moisture in the air, by means of both its underground ‘cellar’, and evaporation from the top of the mound. Some colonies even had ‘chimneys’ at a height of 20 m to control moisture loss in the hottest regions of sub-Saharan Africa.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这套复杂的隧道系统会从外界吸入空气，利用风能推动空气穿过蚁丘。它还能把巢内呼吸产生的废气排出，防止白蚁窒息，从而确保新鲜、可供呼吸的空气持续不断。其设计精细到，即使外界温差可达50 °C——从白天的酷热到最寒冷夜晚的零度以下——巢内温度也只在某一恒定温度上下3度的范围内变化。蚁丘还会通过地下“地窖”和丘顶水分蒸发自动调节空气湿度。在撒哈拉以南非洲最炎热的地区，有些蚁群甚至修筑高达20米的“烟囱”，以控制水分流失。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Furthermore, the termites have evolved in such a way as to outsource some of their biological functions. Part of their digestive process is carried out by a fungus, which they ‘farm’ inside the mound. This fungus, which is found nowhere else on earth, thrives in the constant and optimum environment of the mound. The termites feed the fungus with slightly chewed wood pulp, which the fungus then breaks down into a digestible sugary food to provide the insects with energy, and cellulose which they use for building. And, although the termites must generate waste, none ever leaves the structure, indicating that there is also some kind of internal waste-recycling system.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 此外，白蚁在进化过程中将部分生物功能交由外部承担。它们在蚁丘内“培育”一种真菌，由这种真菌完成部分消化过程。这种地球上其他任何地方都不存在的真菌，在蚁丘恒定而适宜的环境中生长旺盛。白蚁用稍加咀嚼的木浆喂养真菌，真菌随后将其分解为可消化的糖类食物，为白蚁提供能量，并产生供其筑巢使用的纤维素。而且，尽管白蚁必然会产生废物，却从来没有废物离开这座结构，这表明内部还存在某种废物循环利用系统。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Scientists are so excited by the mounds that they have labelled them a ‘super organism’ because, in Soar’s words, “They dance on the edge of what we would perceive as what’s living and what’s not.” He explains, “If you get too hot you need to perspire to cool down, or if you’re too cold you need to shiver: that’s called homeostasis. What the termites have done is to move that homeostatic function away from their body, into the structure in which they live.” As more information comes to light about the unique features of termite mounds, we may ultimately need to redefine our understanding of what constitutes a ‘living’ organism.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 科学家对这些蚁丘非常着迷，甚至把它们称为“超级有机体”。索尔说，蚁丘处在我们通常所理解的生命与非生命的边界上。人太热时会出汗降温，太冷时会发抖；这种维持内部状态稳定的机制叫作稳态调节。白蚁则把这种稳态调节功能从自己的身体转移到了它们居住的蚁丘结构中。随着有关白蚁丘独特特征的更多信息逐渐揭示，我们最终或许需要重新界定对何为“生命体”的理解。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: To reveal the structure of the mounds, Soar’s team begins by filling and covering their plaster of Paris, a chalky white paste based on the mineral gypsum, which becomes rock-solid when dry. The researcher then carves the plaster of Paris into half-millimetre-thick slices, and photographs them sequentially. Once the pictures are digitally scanned, computer technology is able to recreate complex three-dimensional images of the mounds. These models have enabled the team to map termite architecture at a level of detail never before attained.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 为揭示蚁丘的结构，索尔的团队先用熟石膏填充并覆盖蚁丘。这是一种以石膏矿物为原料、呈粉笔白色的糊状物，干燥后会坚硬如石。研究人员随后把凝固的熟石膏切成半毫米厚的薄片，并依次拍照。照片经数字扫描后，计算机技术便能重建蚁丘复杂的三维图像。这些模型使团队能够以前所未有的精细程度描绘白蚁建筑结构。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Soar hopes that the models will explain how termite mounds create a self-regulating living environment which manages to respond to changing internal and external conditions without drawing on any outside source of power. If they do, the findings could be invaluable in informing future architectural design, and could inspire buildings that are self-sufficient, environmentally friendly, and cheap to run. “As we approach a world of climate change and temperatures rise,” he explains, “there will not be enough fuel to drive air conditioners around the world.” It is hoped, says Soar, “that the findings will provide clues that aid the ultimate development of new kinds of human habitats, suitable for a variety of arid, hostile environments not only on the earth but maybe one day on the moon and beyond.”
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 索尔希望，这些模型能解释白蚁丘如何在不借助任何外部能源的情况下，营造一个可自我调节、并能应对内外条件变化的生存环境。如果能够做到，这些发现对于指导未来的建筑设计可能极具价值，并可能启发人们建造自给自足、环境友好且运行成本低廉的建筑。他解释道：“随着我们进入一个气候不断变化、气温持续上升的世界，燃料将不足以驱动全球各地的空调。”索尔说，人们希望“这些发现能提供线索，帮助人类最终开发出新型栖息地，使其不仅适用于地球上各种干旱、恶劣的环境，或许有朝一日还适用于月球乃至更遥远的地方。”

source.text: The Animal Connection

translation.text: 动物联系

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Professor of anthropology Pat Shipman looks at the ways in which our relationships with animals have shaped our own human evolution.
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 人类学教授 Pat Shipman 探讨了我们与动物的关系如何塑造人类自身的进化。

source.text: Professor of anthropology Pat Shipman looks at the ways in which our relationships with animals have shaped our own human evolution.

translation.text: 人类学教授 Pat Shipman 探讨了我们与动物的关系如何塑造人类自身的进化。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Travel anywhere and you see something so common it may not even catch your attention. Wherever there are people, animals are being walked, herded and fed. Many, such as dogs, cats and sheep, are domesticated, but you will also find people living alongside wild creatures like monkeys and wolves. Close contact with animals is not confined to one particular culture, region or ethnic group but is a universal human trait.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 无论到哪里旅行，你都会看到一种司空见惯、甚至不会引起注意的现象。只要有人居住，就有人遛动物、放牧动物、喂养动物。其中许多动物，如狗、猫和绵羊，已经被驯化；但你也会发现，有些人与猴子、狼等野生动物共同生活。与动物密切接触并不局限于某一种文化、地区或族群，而是人类共有的特征。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: On the face of it this makes little sense. No other mammal adopts individuals from another species, with good reason. Since the ultimate prize in evolution is perpetuating your genes, providing food for another species is counterproductive to success. Even if pets offer friendship, that cannot explain why our bond with other species arose in the first place. Who would bring a ferocious wolf into their home in the hope that thousands of years later it would become a loving pet?
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 乍看之下，这似乎毫无道理。其他哺乳动物都不会收养异种个体，而且不这样做是有充分理由的。由于进化中的终极目标是延续自身基因，为其他物种提供食物反而与这一目标背道而驰。即便宠物能带来陪伴，这也无法解释我们与其他物种的纽带最初为何会出现。谁会把一头凶猛的狼带回家，只因希望几千年后它会变成惹人喜爱的宠物呢？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As an anthropologist I have tried to understand this puzzle by looking to the past for the origins of our link with animals. What I found was a long and unbroken evolutionary trail of evidence I call the ‘animal connection’. This trail links to three important developments in human evolution: tool making, language and domestication. If I am correct, and I believe that further research will conclusively show that I am, the animal connection is a hugely significant force instrumental in our global success.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 身为人类学家，我一直试图通过回望过去、追寻人类与动物联系的起源来理解这个谜题。我发现的是一条漫长而从未中断的进化证据链，我称之为“动物联系”。这条线索将人类进化中的三项重要发展联系起来：工具制造、语言和驯化。如果我的观点正确——而我相信进一步研究会最终确证这一点——那么动物联系便是一股极其重要的力量，对人类在全球范围内取得成功起到了关键作用。

source.text: As an anthropologist I have tried to understand this puzzle by looking to the past for the origins of our link with animals.

translation.text: 身为人类学家，我一直试图通过回望过去、追寻人类与动物联系的起源来理解这个谜题。

source.text: What I found was a long and unbroken evolutionary trail of evidence I call the ‘animal connection’.

translation.text: 我发现的是一条漫长而从未中断的进化证据链，我称之为“动物联系”。

source.text: This trail links to three important developments in human evolution: tool making, language and domestication.

translation.text: 这条线索将人类进化中的三项重要发展联系起来：工具制造、语言和驯化。

source.text: If I am correct, and I believe that further research will conclusively show that I am, the animal connection is a hugely significant force instrumental in our global success.

translation.text: 如果我的观点正确——而我相信进一步研究会最终确证这一点——那么动物联系便是一股极其重要的力量，对人类在全球范围内取得成功起到了关键作用。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The trail begins at least 2.6 million years ago. That is when the first tools appear in the archaeological record. This development required the intellectual breakthrough of realizing that the properties of an object can be altered. Man learnt how to turn stone into small, sharp items that could cut up animal carcasses, providing them with an evolutionary shortcut to becoming predators.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这条线索至少始于260万年前，考古记录中最早的工具正是在那时出现。这一发展需要一次认知上的突破，即意识到物体的性质可以改变。人类学会把石头制成小巧锋利、能够切割动物尸体的工具，从而得到一条进化上的捷径，成为捕食者。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: There were many consequences of the new hunting lifestyle. On the plus side, eating more meat and fat was a requirement for the increase in relative brain size. And since meat tends to come in bigger packages than leaves and roots, meat eaters could spend less time finding food and more on activities like learning and social interaction. On the minus side, preying on animals put our ancestors into direct competition with the other predators that shared their ecosystem, animals such as lions and hyenas. To get the upper hand, they needed more than just tools, and that is where the animal connection comes in. What made it possible for our ancestors to compete successfully with true carnivores was the ability to pay very close attention to the habits of both potential prey and competitors. Knowledge was power, so we acquired a deep understanding of the minds of other animals. Another significant consequence of becoming more predatory was the need to live at lower densities, as successful predators soon exhaust food supplies. The record of the geographic distribution of our ancestors provides further support for my idea that the animal connection has shaped our evolution. Early man lived in Africa and nowhere else, but then underwent a dramatic expansion in territory, forced by the search for new hunting grounds.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Throughout the period of these enormous changes in the lifestyle of our ancestors, gathering, sharing and recording knowledge became increasingly advantageous, and examples of prehistoric art that appear in Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia allow us to eavesdrop on their conversations. Through the art, we realize the main topic was animals: their colours, shapes, postures and habits. This focus is even more striking considering that scenes of human life are rarely depicted. Pictures of people, social interaction and ceremonies are rare.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This leads me on to the development of language. Nobody doubts this proved a major adaptive advantage to our ancestors in developing complex behaviours. How it arose, however, remains a mystery. I believe I am the first to propose a continuity between the strong human-animal link that appeared 2.6 million years ago and the origin of language. The complexity and importance of animal-related information, indicated in the predominance of animal images, spurred early humans to move beyond what other species could achieve. Vervet monkeys, for example, have different cries for eagles and snakes, but they cannot discuss what threats might appear tomorrow. The property of full language is that it is comprised of vocabulary and grammatical rules that can be combined in an infinite number of ways to convey fine shades of meaning.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这就把我引向了语言的发展。没有人怀疑，语言在祖先发展复杂行为的过程中是一项重大的适应优势。然而，它如何产生仍是个谜。我相信，我是第一个提出这种延续关系的人：一端是260万年前出现的牢固人类—动物联系，另一端则是语言的起源。动物图像占主导地位，显示出动物相关信息既复杂又重要，这推动早期人类突破其他物种所能达到的水平。例如，黑长尾猴会用不同叫声分别警示鹰和蛇，却无法讨论明天可能出现哪些威胁。完整语言的特性在于，它由词汇和语法规则组成，而二者能以无穷多种方式组合，传达细微的意义差别。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As our ancestors became more involved with animals, the third product of the animal connection appeared: domestication, which has long been linked with the keeping of animals like sheep. Domestic animals are usually considered as ‘walking larders’, or easy food sources, reflecting the idea that the basis of this change was a drive for greater food security. Looking at the origins of domestication for clues to its underlying reasons, I found fundamental flaws in this idea. Instead, my analysis suggests domestication emerged as a natural progression of our close association with, and understanding of, other species. If domestication was about knowing where your next meal was coming from, the first domesticate ought to have been a food source, yet analysis of fossils shows that the domestication of dogs pre-dated that of any other species, even plants, from wolves. Furthermore, if the objective was to have meat to eat, you wouldn’t select an animal that eats two kilograms of meat a day. It was familiarity with this species that led to eventual domestication.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 随着祖先与动物的联系日益深入，动物联系的第三项产物——驯化——随之出现；长期以来，人们一直把驯化与饲养绵羊等动物联系在一起。家养动物通常被视为“会走路的食品储藏室”，也就是容易获得的食物来源，这反映出一种观点：这一变化的根本动力是提高食物保障。我考察了驯化的起源，希望从中找出其深层原因的线索，却发现这种观点存在根本缺陷。相反，我的分析表明，驯化是我们与其他物种密切交往并了解它们之后自然发展的结果。如果驯化只是为了知道下一顿饭从哪里来，那么最先被驯化的理应是食物来源；然而化石分析表明，由狼驯化而来的狗早于所有其他物种、甚至植物被驯化。此外，如果目标是获得肉食，人们不会选择一种每天要吃两千克肉的动物。正是人类对这个物种的熟悉最终促成了驯化。

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Do tiny changes of facial expression show whether someone is telling lies?

source.text: Do tiny changes of facial expression show whether someone is telling lies?

translation.text: 面部表情的细微变化能否显示一个人是否在说谎？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Forty years ago, the research psychologist Dr Paul Ekman was addressing a group of young psychiatrists in training when he was asked a question, the answer to which has kept him busy ever since. Suppose the group wanted to know whether a particular patient who swears they are telling the truth really is. They look and sound sincere. So here is the question: is there any way you can be sure they are telling the truth? Ekman did not know the answer then, but he wanted to find out.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 40年前，研究心理学家 Paul Ekman 博士正在给一群接受培训的年轻精神科医生授课，其间有人向他提出了一个问题；此后，他一直忙于寻找答案。假设这群医生想知道，某位发誓自己说的是实话的患者是否真的在说实话。患者看起来、听起来都很真诚。那么问题来了：有没有办法确定对方说的就是实话？Ekman 当时不知道答案，但他想弄清楚。

source.text: Ekman did not know the answer then, but he wanted to find out.

translation.text: Ekman 当时不知道答案，但他想弄清楚。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: As part of his research, he had already filmed a series of 12-minute interviews with psychiatric patients. In a subsequent conversation, one of the patients told him that she had lied to him. So Ekman sat and looked at the film but saw nothing noteworthy. Then he slowed it down and looked again. Then he slowed it down even further. And suddenly, there, across just two frames of the film, he saw it: an intense expression of extreme anguish. It lasted less than a fifteenth of a second, but once he had spotted the first expression, he soon found three more examples in that same interview. He termed his discovery “micro-expressions”: very rapid, intense demonstrations of emotion that the subject intended to conceal.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 作为研究的一部分，他此前已拍摄了一系列与精神科患者进行的12分钟访谈。在随后的一次交谈中，一名患者告诉他，她曾对他说谎。于是 Ekman 坐下来观看录像，却没有发现任何值得注意之处。随后他放慢播放速度又看了一遍，接着把速度放得更慢。突然间，他就在仅仅两帧画面中看到了：一种极度痛苦的强烈表情。它持续了不到十五分之一秒，但发现第一个表情后，他很快又在同一次访谈中找到了3例。他把这项发现称为“微表情”：受访者本想掩饰、却极其迅速而强烈地显露出来的情绪。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Over the course of the next four decades, Ekman successfully demonstrated a proposition first suggested by Charles Darwin: that the ways in which we express rage, disgust, contempt, fear, surprise, happiness and sadness are universal. The facial muscles triggered by those seven basic emotions are, he has shown, essentially standard, regardless of language and culture, from the US to Japan and Brazil to Papua New Guinea. What is more, expressions of emotion are impossible to suppress and, particularly when we are lying, micro-expressions of powerfully felt emotions will inevitably flit across our face before we get the chance to stop them.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Most recently, Ekman’s research has resulted in a new television series about the exploits of the fictional Dr Cal Lightman, a scientist who studies involuntary body language to discover not only if you are lying, but why you might have been motivated to do so. According to the publicity blurb, Lightman is a human lie detector, even more accurate than a polygraph test. Ekman concedes he was sceptical when the producer first approached him with the idea of turning his life’s work into a TV series, and initially would have stopped the project if he could. In particular, he was fearful that the show would exaggerate the effectiveness of his techniques and create the quite inaccurate impression among audiences that criminals could no longer hope to get away with lying. In the worst-case scenario, he was concerned about unfair convictions—that one day someone not properly trained in his techniques might be sitting on a jury and wrongly find someone guilty of a crime simply on the basis of a television programme.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Ekman, incidentally, professes to have been a terrible liar ever since he was a small boy and observes that the ability to detect a lie and the ability to lie successfully are completely unrelated. He has been asked by people running for high office if he could teach them to become more credible with the public but has always refused to use his skills in that way on ethical grounds. He also insists that there are various kinds of lies. A “true” lie can be identified by having two essential characteristics: there must be a deliberate intent to mislead and there must be no notification that this is what is occurring. This means that an actor or a poker player isn’t a true liar. They are supposed to deceive you—it’s part of the game—and the same is true of flattery. He prefers to focus on the kinds of lies where the liar would be in grave trouble if they were found out, and where the target would feel properly aggrieved if they knew.

source.text: The Causes of Linguistic Change

translation.text: 语言变化的成因

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: All living languages undergo changes of various kinds, for which there are various reasons. The changes that have caused most dispute are those in pronunciation. We have various sources of evidence for the pronunciations of earlier times, like the evidence of spellings, the treatment of words borrowed from other languages or borrowed by them, the descriptions of contemporary grammarians, and the modern pronunciations in all the languages and dialects concerned. These, combined with a knowledge of the mechanism of speech production, can often give us a very good idea of the pronunciation of an earlier age, though absolute certainty is never possible. When we study the pronunciation of a language over any period of a few generations or more, we find that it is subject to change. Moreover, there are always large-scale regularities in the changes: for example, over a period of time, all the long a sounds in a language may change into long o sounds, or all the b sounds in a certain position (for example, at the end of a word) may change into p sounds. Such regular changes are often called sound laws. There are no universal sound laws, but simply particular sound laws for one given language at one given period.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 所有活的语言都会因各种原因发生多种变化，其中引发最多争议的是语音变化。我们有多种证据可以推断早期的发音，例如拼写证据、从其他语言借入或被其他语言借走的词如何处理、当时语法学家的描述，以及所有相关语言和方言的现代发音。把这些证据与对言语产生机制的认识结合起来，我们往往能相当准确地了解早期某个时代的发音，不过绝不可能达到完全确定。研究一种语言跨越数代或更长时期的发音时，我们会发现它会发生变化。而且这些变化总存在大范围的规律性：例如，经过一段时间，一种语言中所有长元音a都可能变成长元音o，或处于某一位置的所有b音——例如词尾——都可能变成p音。这类有规律的变化常被称为音变规律。世上并不存在普遍适用的音变规律，只有适用于某一特定语言、某一特定时期的具体规律。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One cause of change is the influence of one language on another. We learn our mother tongue very thoroughly, and acquire a whole set of speech habits which become second nature to us. When later we learn a foreign language, we inevitably carry over some of these speech habits into it, and so do not speak it exactly like a native. Consequently, in bilingual situations the second language tends to be modified. Such modifications may not persist, of course: an isolated Polish or German immigrant to Britain will usually have grandchildren who speak English like natives because the influence of the general speech environment (playmates, school, work) is stronger than that of the home. But if a large and closely knit group of people adopt a new language, then the modifications they make in it may persist among their descendants, even if the latter no longer speak the original language that caused the changes. This can be seen in Wales, where the influence of Welsh has affected the pronunciation of English, and the very characteristic melody of Welsh English has been carried over from Welsh.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It is also possible that fashion plays a part in the process of change. When a social group goes up or down in the world, its pronunciation will gain or lose prestige. Some of the changes in accepted English pronunciation in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries have been shown to consist of the replacement of one style of pronunciation by another style already existing, and it is likely that such substitutions were a result of the great social changes of the period: the increased power and wealth of the middle classes, and their steady infiltration upwards into the ranks of the landed gentry probably carried elements of middle class dialect into upper class speech. blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One such force, which is often suggested, is known as the principle of ease. We are all naturally lazy, it is argued, and so we tend to take short cuts in the movements of our speech organs, to replace movements calling for great accuracy or energy by less demanding ones, to omit sounds if they are not essential for understanding, and so on. For example, the word scant was once skamt, but the m has been changed to n under the influence of the following t. An economy of effort has thereby been achieved, because n and t are articulated in the same place (with the tip of the tongue against the teeth-ridge), whereas m is articulated elsewhere (with the two lips). The change from skamt to scant would be an example of assimilation, which is a very common kind of change. Assimilation is the changing of a sound under the influence of a neighbouring sound.

source.text: The Costs of Brand Loyalty

translation.text: 品牌忠诚的代价

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A Londoner with a sudden urge for giant African snails could do worse than head to the bustling marketplace in Brixton, a part of south London that is home to many people from Africa. Markets like Brixton Market that cater to migrants are a testament to the fact that people often retain very strong preferences for the kinds of food they grew up eating. Just ask the expatriate Britons who flock to ‘Tea and Sympathy’ in New York’s Greenwich Village for pots of Marmite, a yeast-based spread whose delights baffle other nationalities (and many of their own compatriots).

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Past research has shown that people are often willing to pay much more for a favoured brand than for seemingly identical alternatives. It is not always obvious why. However, there is ample evidence to support the theory that certain food preferences form in childhood. Children have a predisposition to fear new foods, which is only overcome when they are repeatedly presented with, and encouraged to consume, a particular food. Evidence shows that children’s instinctive wariness of new foods dates back to the times when humans had to forage for food, and it was important that they learnt which foods were safe to eat. In the modern world, people routinely express a strong liking for a brand even though they are unable to tell the brand apart from rival brands in blind tests, and many studies have found that advertising alone cannot explain the strength of brand loyalty.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A new study by economists from the universities of Tilburg and Chicago tracks the consumption patterns of 38,000 US households over two years, and confirms the theory that such brand loyalty is widespread, deep and long-lasting. There were clear local patterns in consumption, although the same brands were available everywhere. But 16% of people studied were migrants: they had grown up in one state and moved to another. These migrants had the same options, in terms of what was on offer and at what price, as everyone else in their adopted home, but although they consumed local favourites, they bought fewer than longtime residents. This gap between purchases of migrants and those of the locally born was quite stubborn: although it faded the longer a person lived in their new state, it still took 20 years to halve in magnitude. Even 50 years on, it was still large enough to show up in the data. This could mean that the benefits of being the first brand into a market could last longer than might be assumed.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: David Atkin of Yale University has identified some important implications of local food favourites. He suggests in a recent paper that the effects of people being loyal to known brands may also lead economists to rethink the way they calculate the benefits resulting from trade. This is because opening up to trade is in some ways very similar to migrating, as it changes the composition and prices of the foods that are available to a person. In particular, trade can cause local foods to become relatively more expensive. Atkin’s data show something many economists do not take into account: when a traditional food has to compete with imported foods, it may no longer be the cheapest food available for people to choose to eat. Atkin decided to look at this situation in the context of developing countries.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: However, there has been some opening up of internal trade in India in recent years, and this has revealed that for every rupee spent on food, people’s intake of calories declined most in regions where prices of local favourite foods had risen. source.text: The hazards of multitasking

translation.text: 多任务处理的危害

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Doing more than one thing at once – is it always a good idea?

source.text: Doing more than one thing at once – is it always a good idea?

translation.text: 同时做不止一件事——这总是个好主意吗？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: You arrive at the office, review your to-do list and start to feel a headache coming on. You resolve to tackle the items as quickly as possible. While you return calls, you sort e-mail and other letters. You begin keying in slides for tomorrow’s presentation. Then your manager comes in wanting an immediate update on sales figures. You have just opened the spreadsheet when a very important customer calls. With the receiver held between your shoulder and your ear, you continue adding up the sales totals until, 15 minutes later, you finally manage, politely, to get rid of the client. You’ve been multitasking again.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: You may believe that anyone who wants to get ahead today should master the art of multitasking. However, a recent study by the Families and Work Institute in New York City has found that 45 per cent of US workers believe that they are asked or expected to work on too many tasks at once. Managers may be surprised to learn that they are actually wasting their workers’ time. As it turns out, the human brain cannot really master the computer’s art of crunching data in the background while moving between process windows. Instead, a growing number of studies show that trying to juggle jobs rather than completing them sequentially can take longer and leave workers with a reduced ability to perform each task. In addition, the stress associated with multitasking may contribute to short-term memory difficulties. The combination results in inefficiency, careless thinking and mistakes – not to mention the possible dangers of divided attention for drivers, air-traffic controllers and others who handle machinery.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: How can a time-management strategy that has become part of the common wisdom actually be so wrong? Exploring that question requires a closer look at an area of consciousness research that examines how the brain focuses attention. One of the modern foundations of current knowledge of multitasking was laid in 1935, when the American psychologist John Ridley Stroop reported that processing information from one task could cause interference with another. Stroop noticed that when study participants were asked to name the colour of a word – such as ‘green’ – printed in a different colour – red, for example – they experienced difficulty saying the name of the colour. This phenomenon is thought to occur when two tasks get tangled: the brain must suppress one that has been learned so well that it has become automatic (reading) to attend to a second task that requires concentration (naming the colour).

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: During the past couple of decades, psychologists have probed more deeply into the nature and limitations of multitasking. Psychologist and brain-researcher Ernst Pöppel, of the Ludwig-Maximilian University in Munich, believes that it is impossible to carry out two or three different tasks simultaneously with the same degree of concentration. He says that seemingly simultaneous awareness and processing of information actually take place in ‘three-second windows’.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In these three-second segments, the brain takes in, as a block, all the data about the environment streaming in from the sensory systems; subsequent events are processed in the next window. So a person can concentrate on a conversation for three seconds, then for three seconds on a crying child, and three seconds on a computer screen. While one subject at a time occupies the foreground of consciousness, the others stay in the background until they, in turn, are given access to the central processor.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在这些3秒片段中，大脑把感官系统源源不断传来的全部环境数据作为一个整体接收；之后发生的事件则在下一个窗口中处理。因此，一个人可以用3秒专注于一段对话，再用3秒关注一个哭泣的孩子，然后用3秒看电脑屏幕。每次只有一个主题处在意识前景，其他主题则留在背景中，直至轮到它们获准进入中央处理系统。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Another experiment by psychologist David E. Meyer, of the University of Michigan, quantified just how much time we can lose when we shuttle between tasks. The researchers asked test participants to write a report and check their e-mail at the same time. Those individuals who constantly jumped back and forth between the two tasks took about one and a half times as long to finish as those who completed one job before turning to the other. Each switchover from one task to another meant re-thinking and thus involved additional neural resources. In effect, the brain needs time to shut off the rules for one task and to turn on the rules for another. ‘Multitasking saves time only when it is a matter of relaxed, routine tasks,’ Meyer says. It also takes the brain longer to adapt when switching rapidly back to an interrupted task rather than waiting longer before switching back.

Meyer 开展的另一项实验，量化了我们在任务间来回切换究竟会损失多少时间。研究人员让参与测试者一边写报告，一边查看电子邮件。那些不断在两项任务间来回切换的人，完成任务所用时间约为先做完一项再做另一项者的1.5倍。每次从一项任务转到另一项任务都意味着重新思考，因而需要额外的神经资源。实际上，大脑需要时间关闭一项任务的规则，再启用另一项任务的规则。Meyer 说：“只有面对轻松的常规任务时，多任务处理才能节省时间。”而且，与隔较长时间再切回相比，快速切回一项被打断的任务也需要大脑花更长时间适应。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: By its nature multitasking is stressful, and the area in the brain most involved with multitasking is also most affected by the resulting stress. Located behind the forehead, the prefrontal cortex – which neuroscientists call the ‘executive’ part of the brain – helps us to assess tasks, prioritise them and assign mental resources. It also ‘marks’ the spot at which a task has been interrupted, so that we can return to it later. This stress can also affect brain cells in another region, the hippocampus, which is important for forming new memories; damage in that area also makes it difficult for a person to acquire new skills.

passages.title: The New Zealand writer Margaret Mahy

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: The New Zealand writer Margaret Mahy

source.text: The New Zealand writer Margaret Mahy

translation.text: 新西兰作家 Margaret Mahy

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In a career spanning some fifty years, Margaret Mahy has come to occupy a unique place in New Zealand writing with innovative fiction and original characterisation. In our solidly realist tradition, the linguistic fireworks of Mahy’s children’s fiction and the explorations of human behaviour at the heart of her supernatural teen fiction stand gloriously alone. Mahy’s clearest heir, I have always thought, is Elizabeth Knox — and maybe the true inheritance is the sheer singularity. Just as there is no one else like Knox in New Zealand writing, Mahy, too, has ventured into imaginative territory unknown to other local writers. So it was with great pleasure that I visited Mahy recently at her Governor’s Bay home to talk about her new book. As with all journalists, she is generous to a fault with her time and attention; and, as always — despite her careful consideration of questions and thoughtful answers — I’m reminded she isn’t truly comfortable making herself or her life the heart of any conversation.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 在约50年的写作生涯中，Margaret Mahy 凭借创新的小说和独到的人物塑造，在新西兰文学中占据了独一无二的位置。在我们根基深厚的现实主义传统中，她的儿童小说绽放出绚丽的语言烟花，以超自然题材写成的青少年小说则把对人类行为的探索置于核心，两者都卓然独立。我一直认为，Elizabeth Knox 最明确地继承了 Mahy 的衣钵——或许真正传承下来的，正是这种无可比拟的独特性。正如新西兰文学中无人可与 Knox 相比，Mahy 也曾闯入本地其他作家从未涉足的想象疆域。因此，最近我怀着极大的喜悦前往 Mahy 位于总督湾的家中，与她谈论新书。她对所有记者都慷慨得过了头，毫不吝惜时间和关注；而且一如既往，尽管她会仔细思考问题并认真作答，我仍意识到，她其实并不自在于让自己或自己的生活成为任何谈话的中心。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Certainly, any consideration of the style of Mahy’s novels and picture books throws up some irresistible theories. As a writer committed to supporting herself through her art, she has seldom had the time for formal research. Rather, it has been a matter of going out and finding inspiration from her immediate environment: the writing on the side of a bus; a spelling mistake in a note to herself; the similarity between a cat and a fur hat. But despite these sometimes mundane origins, the settings for her stories are delightfully varied, as the books celebrate the dramatic plot twists and unpredictability of adventures on the high seas or in Antarctica, and also in quiet, unassuming places like the library or even down the back of a chair at home. Mahy has a lifelong affection for characters who are agents of upheaval and disturbance. Her junior and picture books are peppered with pirates, robbers and lions, though they appear alongside librarians, mothers and children, working against comfortable stereotype. Her fictions often have at their heart a young adult burdened with special powers, such as the ability to cast spells in order to transform their world in supernatural and fantastical ways. Another common feature is that, while the conclusions of her tales are usually predictable, they leave the reader feeling absolutely complete, the moral questions resulting from our hero’s powers having been resolved.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 当然，只要思考 Mahy 小说和图画书的风格，就会涌现出一些令人难以抗拒的推断。作为一名致力于靠创作养活自己的作家，她很少有时间开展正式研究。她更多是走出去，从身边环境中寻找灵感：公交车车身上的文字、写给自己的便条里一个拼写错误、猫与皮帽之间的相似之处。然而，这些灵感有时虽源自平凡日常，她的故事背景却多姿多彩，令人愉悦。书中既有公海或南极洲冒险那戏剧性的情节转折和不可预测性，也有图书馆这样安静、不起眼的地方，甚至还有家中椅背后面的空间。Mahy 一生都喜爱那些带来动荡与骚乱的角色。她为低龄儿童创作的书和图画书中遍布海盗、强盗和狮子，但这些角色又与图书管理员、母亲和孩子同时出现，颠覆了人们习以为常的刻板印象。她的小说常以一名身负特殊力量的年轻人为核心，例如拥有施展法术的能力，能以超自然的奇幻方式改变自己的世界。另一个常见特点是，她的故事结局通常可以预料，却会让读者感到圆满无缺，因为主人公的力量引发的道德问题都得到了解决。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Many of these themes can be found in her new novel, The Magician of Hoad. The book was begun more than 15 years ago and envisioned as an ‘entire’ fantasy — one set in a fully imagined world with detailed history and complex tribal inter-relationships, a classical hero quest at its heart. The story ballooned at one point to 800 pages and has been through at least two substantial rewrites. Now half its original size, it is a fascinating read — an adventure, a romance, and a gold mine of Mahy literary preoccupations.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 她的新小说《霍德的魔法师》中可以看到许多这类主题。这本书始于15年多以前，最初构想为一部“完整的”奇幻作品：故事设在一个完全虚构的世界中，有详尽的历史和复杂的部族关系，核心是一场经典的英雄探索之旅。故事篇幅一度膨胀到800页，至少经历了两次大幅重写。如今它只有原来一半的篇幅，读来十分迷人——既是冒险故事，也是爱情故事，更是一座蕴藏 Mahy 文学关注主题的金矿。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The other splendid Mahy publication this year is a re-issue of Bubble Trouble in a now illustrated edition. This tongue-twister tale first appeared in 1991, was included in 100 New Zealand Poems (1993) and has been recited by Mahy at countless private and public functions. Perhaps more than any other work, Bubble Trouble is the Mahy that New Zealand children and their parents know so well, the rollicking story of a clown who serves up a joyous torrent of word play and unexpected rhyme.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Mahy 今年出版的另一部佳作，是重新发行的《泡泡麻烦》，这次推出了插图版。这个绕口令般的故事最早发表于1991年，后被收入《新西兰诗歌100首》一书，1993年出版；Mahy 也曾在不计其数的私人和公共活动上朗诵它。新西兰儿童及其父母所熟悉的 Mahy，或许在《泡泡麻烦》中体现得比任何其他作品都更鲜明。这是一个热闹欢腾的小丑故事，奉上一股令人愉悦的文字游戏与意外押韵的洪流。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Of course, readers are important to any working writer, but Mahy’s espousal of the act of reading goes beyond that: a book is not properly finished, she has often said, until it has been read, because a reader brings something important to the book. So, doubtless out of need to build a market – she’s not ignorant of her popularity – but out of genuine care for that other dynamic part of the author-reader relationship, Mahy has, until recently, kept up a punishing schedule of public appearances.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Private conversation with Mahy has always been a wild ride — marvellous, in the true sense of the word, the product of a hungry head and an infinite capacity to be astonished. She races away at one stage to consult an encyclopedia for L M Montgomery’s date of death, and speculates about the ‘real’ Montgomery, creator of the ever-popular Anne of Green Gables. Although I’d come to talk about her new book, I couldn’t help but be captivated by her infectious curiosity.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A few years ago, the writer David Hill told a funny story. Though his writing was, he conceded, very different from Mahy’s, he had been affected by her peculiarly alert way of looking at the world, particularly the mad, slippery life of language. Once, Hill said, in a motel room, a sign on a door caught his eye: ‘This door is alarmed.’ Mahy would like that, thought Hill. She would enjoy the comedy just below the surface of the formal warning; she would leap immediately to the possibilities for story and language play: ‘Yes, and this window is concerned, this light fitting is irritated.’ His story was a wonderful comment on Mahy’s vision.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 几年前，作家 David Hill 讲过一个有趣的故事。他承认，自己的写作与 Mahy 截然不同，却受到她那种格外敏锐的观察世界方式影响，尤其是她看待语言那疯狂而难以捉摸的生命力的方式。Hill 说，有一次在汽车旅馆房间里，门上的一块告示吸引了他的目光：“This door is alarmed。”这句话既表示门装有警报器，也可理解为门“受惊了”。Hill 心想，Mahy 一定会喜欢。她会欣赏正式警示语表层下方的喜剧意味，并立刻跃入故事和文字游戏的种种可能：“是啊，这扇窗很担心，这盏灯具很恼火。”他的故事是对 Mahy 观察世界方式的绝妙评说。

source.text: The origin of language

translation.text: 语言的起源

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The archaeologist Stephen Mithen talks about the ideas behind his new book on the origin of language.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 考古学家 Stephen Mithen 讲述他那本探讨语言起源的新书所依据的观点。

source.text: The archaeologist Stephen Mithen talks about the ideas behind his new book on the origin of language.

translation.text: 考古学家 Stephen Mithen 讲述他那本探讨语言起源的新书所依据的观点。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Theories on the origin and evolution of language have been a major area of my research for many years. By 1859, when British scientist Charles Darwin published The Origin of Species, there was already a great deal of interest in this subject. However, the debate became plagued by strange theories, so much so that in 1866 the influential Société de Linguistique de Paris banned all discussions about the origin of language. The ban lasted for more than a century, before a surge of research began during the 1990s. Linguists, psychologists, anthropologists and archaeologists now frequently debate the origin of language and have published many articles and books on this topic. And yet, despite almost frenzied activity, limited progress has been made.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 多年来，语言的起源与演化理论一直是我的主要研究领域。到1859年英国科学家查尔斯·达尔文出版《物种起源》时，人们对这个主题已经兴趣浓厚。然而，争论后来饱受各种奇怪理论困扰，以至于颇具影响力的巴黎语言学会在1866年禁止一切有关语言起源的讨论。这一禁令持续了一个多世纪，直到20世纪90年代研究热潮兴起。如今，语言学家、心理学家、人类学家和考古学家经常讨论语言起源，并发表了许多相关文章和著作。然而，尽管活动近乎狂热，取得的进展仍十分有限。

source.text: Theories on the origin and evolution of language have been a major area of my research for many years.

translation.text: 多年来，语言的起源与演化理论一直是我的主要研究领域。

source.text: By 1859, when British scientist Charles Darwin published The Origin of Species, there was already a great deal of interest in this subject.

source.text: However, the debate became plagued by strange theories, so much so that in 1866 the influential Société de Linguistique de Paris banned all discussions about the origin of language.

source.text: Linguists, psychologists, anthropologists and archaeologists now frequently debate the origin of language and have published many articles and books on this topic.

translation.text: 然而，尽管活动近乎狂热，取得的进展仍十分有限。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: I believe there are four reasons for this. The first is an insufficient concern with the archaeological and fossil proof of the brains and behaviour of our human ancestors. Many theories to date rely on an assumed association between brain size and language abilities, without acknowledging the problem this creates: fossil evidence indicates that the Neanderthals had larger brains than modern humans, Homo sapiens, but archaeological evidence indicates that the Neanderthals lacked a capacity for language. So something is seriously amiss with those theories.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 我认为这有4个原因。第一个原因，是对有关人类祖先大脑和行为的考古及化石证据关注不足。迄今许多理论依赖一种假定，即大脑大小与语言能力相关，却没有承认这会造成一个问题：化石证据表明，尼安德特人的大脑比现代人类智人更大，但考古证据却显示尼安德特人缺乏语言能力。因此，这些理论存在严重问题。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: That 'something' might relate to the second reason for limited progress: insufficient concern with the other major aural and vocal communication system of modern humans: music. Even though the Société de Linguistique de Paris had nothing to say about studying the origin of music, academics appear to have had a self-imposed ban, with limited discussion of this issue during the 19th and 20th centuries. However, there are notable exceptions that should be acknowledged. One is the aforementioned Charles Darwin who, in his 1871 book on human evolution, The Descent of Man, devoted several pages to the development of music. Another is the renowned ethnomusicologist John Blacking, whose 1973 book, How Musical is Man?, broached the idea that music is an inherent and universal human quality.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这个“问题”或许与进展有限的第二个原因有关：对现代人类另一套主要听觉与发声交流系统——音乐——关注不足。虽然巴黎语言学会从未禁止研究音乐的起源，学术界似乎却自行施加了禁令，19和20世纪对此问题的讨论十分有限。不过，也有一些值得肯定的显著例外。其中之一就是前面提到的查尔斯·达尔文，他在1871年出版的人类进化著作《人类的由来》中，用数页篇幅探讨了音乐的发展。另一位是著名民族音乐学家 John Blacking，他在1973年的著作《人有多大音乐性？》中提出，音乐是人类与生俱来且普遍具有的特质。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The origin of music deserves as much attention as that of language, as we cannot treat one without the other. Those writers who had evidently annoyed the Société de Linguistique de Paris were quite aware of this. For them, music and language were intimately linked; the French writer and philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau's On the Origin of Language (1781) was a reflection on both music and language. In contrast, Morten Christiansen and Simon Kirby's book, Language Evolution (2000), which they conceived as 'a definitive book on the subject', failed to mention music in any of its 17 chapters. Those authors have an important lesson to learn from Rousseau and other writers of his time who addressed the origin of language.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 音乐的起源值得获得与语言起源同等的关注，因为我们无法把两者割裂开来研究。那些显然惹恼巴黎语言学会的作者十分清楚这一点。在他们看来，音乐与语言密不可分；法国作家兼哲学家 Jean-Jacques Rousseau 的《论语言的起源》，出版于1781年，便同时思考了音乐与语言。相比之下，Morten Christiansen 和 Simon Kirby 2000年出版的《语言演化》一书，被二人构想为“一部有关这个主题的权威著作”，却在全书17章中只字未提音乐。这两位作者应当从 Rousseau 以及同时代其他探讨语言起源的作家那里吸取重要教训。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Music is a universal feature of human society and plays a significant role in the lives of all individuals. Indeed, music is perhaps in even greater need of study than language: the latter has a self-evident function—the transmission of information—and can be readily accepted as a product of evolution, even if its specific evolutionary history remains unclear. But what is the point of music?
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 音乐是人类社会的普遍特征，在每个人的生活中都发挥重要作用。事实上，音乐或许比语言更需要研究：语言有一种不言自明的功能——传递信息——即使其具体演化历程仍不清楚，也很容易被视为进化的产物。但音乐的意义何在？

source.text: Music is a universal feature of human society and plays a significant role in the lives of all individuals.

translation.text: 音乐是人类社会的普遍特征，在每个人的生活中都发挥重要作用。

source.text: Indeed, music is perhaps in even greater need of study than language: the latter has a self-evident function—the transmission of information—and can be readily accepted as a product of evolution, even if its specific evolutionary history remains unclear.

translation.text: 事实上，音乐或许比语言更需要研究：语言有一种不言自明的功能——传递信息——即使其具体演化历程仍不清楚，也很容易被视为进化的产物。

source.text: But what is the point of music?

translation.text: 但音乐的意义何在？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: That question leads directly to a third reason for our lack of progress in understanding how language evolved, and indeed the human mind in general: an insufficient concern with emotion. If music is about anything, it is about expressing emotion. But while archaeologists have put significant effort into examining the intellectual capacities of our ancestors, their emotional lives have been sorely neglected. This has contributed to the neglect of music, which, in turn, has constrained our understanding of language.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这个问题直接引出了我们在理解语言如何演化、乃至总体理解人类心智方面进展不足的第三个原因：对情感关注不足。如果音乐表达了什么，那就是情感。然而，考古学家虽投入大量精力考察祖先的智力能力，他们的情感生活却一直遭到严重忽视。这导致音乐也受到忽视，进而限制了我们对语言的理解。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: There is one further reason why progress has been limited: those who have been most influential regarding the evolution of language have simply got it wrong, and misled everyone else. Linguist Derek Bickerton has made an important contribution towards our understanding of the origin of language by bringing his profound knowledge of linguistics to the discussions that have occurred. But Bickerton's idea that the precursor of modern language consisted of words strung together with limited, if any, grammar is, I believe, fundamentally mistaken. Bickerton refers to this precursor as 'proto-language' and suggests that it was similar to the type of language spoken by young children today, and mastered by apes through the use of computer keyboards. This idea has dominated the field of language origins for the last two decades, and is one that I once found persuasive. But I now understand that it is not only flawed but has severely limited the progress that should have been made.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 进展有限还有一个原因：在语言演化问题上影响最大的人根本就错了，并且误导了其他所有人。语言学家 Derek Bickerton 把自己深厚的语言学知识带入相关讨论，为我们理解语言起源作出了重要贡献。但他认为现代语言的前身由一串串单词组成、几乎没有或完全没有语法；在我看来，这一观点从根本上就是错误的。Bickerton 把这种前身称为“原始语言”，并认为它与当今幼儿使用的语言类型相似，也类似于类人猿借助电脑键盘所掌握的语言。这一观点在过去20年里一直主导语言起源领域，我也曾觉得它很有说服力。但现在我明白，它不仅存在缺陷，还严重限制了本应取得的进展。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: My book therefore provides an alternative view, one that draws on the ideas of a linguist who has, I believe, identified the true nature of proto-language. Her name is Alison Wray. She argues that proto-language was 'holistic' rather than compositional in character. By this she means that the precursor to language was a communication system composed of 'messages' rather than words; each message was uniquely associated with an arbitrary meaning, as are the utterances of language today. But in Wray's proto-language, they were not composed out of smaller units of meaning (i.e. words) which could be combined together using a rule system (i.e. grammar) to make more complex messages with emergent meanings. For Wray, proto-language was semantically complex and agrammatical. I believe this insight enables us to understand the origin of music as well as language, and to relate both to the emotional lives of our human ancestors.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 因此，我的书提出了另一种观点，借鉴了一位语言学家的思想；我认为，她找到了原始语言的真正本质。她名叫 Alison Wray。她主张原始语言的特征是“整体式”，而不是组合式。她的意思是，语言的前身是一种由“信息”而非单词构成的交流系统；每条信息都与一个任意意义形成独一无二的关联，就像今天语言中的话语一样。但在 Wray 所说的原始语言中，这些信息并不是由较小的意义单位——也就是单词——构成，也不能利用一套规则系统——也就是语法——将这些单位组合起来，形成具有新生意义的更复杂信息。在 Wray 看来，原始语言在语义上复杂，却没有语法。我认为，这一洞见使我们既能理解音乐的起源，也能理解语言的起源，并把二者都与人类祖先的情感生活联系起来。
