headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 巴塔哥尼亚的人类定居

source.text: The Peopling of Patagonia

translation.text: 巴塔哥尼亚的人类定居

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Anthropologists continue to investigate human migration to Patagonia at the southern tip of South America
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 人类学家继续研究人类向南美洲最南端巴塔哥尼亚迁徙的历程。

source.text: Anthropologists continue to investigate human migration to Patagonia at the southern tip of South America

translation.text: 人类学家继续研究人类向南美洲最南端巴塔哥尼亚迁徙的历程。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The human settlement of the southern extremity of the Americas has always fascinated prehistorians. Viewed from a global perspective, this was the last major continental land mass to be reached by human beings. The earliest occupation of Patagonia carries obvious implications for understanding when the North and South American continents were peopled, because it gives a baseline that all calculations regarding the rate of dispersion of humans throughout both continents must take into account.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 人类在美洲最南端定居一直令史前史学家着迷。从全球视角看，这里是人类最后抵达的一块主要大陆。巴塔哥尼亚最早有人居住的时间，对于理解人类何时在北美洲和南美洲定居显然意义重大，因为它提供了一条基准线；计算人类在两块大陆扩散的速度时，都必须把这条基准纳入考量。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: For many years the human settlement of North and South America has been conceived of as beginning in the far north and travelling progressively southwards to Patagonia. However, fundamental disagreements developed concerning the length of time involved. Some scholars accepted a human presence in the Americas as early as 20,000 years ago, while others proposed that it could date no earlier than 8,000 years ago, and the debate is still with us today.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 多年来，人们一直设想，人类在南北美洲的定居始于遥远的北方，随后逐步南下直至巴塔哥尼亚。然而，对于这一过程持续了多长时间，各方产生了根本分歧。一些学者认为，人类早在20000年前便已出现在美洲；另一些人则提出，最早也只能追溯到8000年前。直到今天，这场争论仍未结束。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The idea of a relatively ‘late’ settlement of the Americas (around 8,000 years ago) implies that a rapid process of migration took place. Herein lies a second debate, which revolves around the question of how migration is to be understood. The ‘late’ model demands a hypothetical migration conceived of as a single, continually advancing wave of settlement. This has always been difficult to take seriously, and many scholars now support the idea of an ‘early’ model that sees the migration as a less ordered migration, and this is surely the most realistic scenario as migrants slowly adapted to the diverse natural habitats they would have met while travelling through the continent.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 认为美洲定居相对“较晚”——约在8000年前——这一观点意味着迁徙过程十分迅速。这又引出第二场争论，焦点是应当如何理解迁徙。“晚期”模型要求我们假设，定居者如同一道不断向前推进的单一浪潮般迁徙。这种设想始终很难令人信服，如今许多学者支持“早期”模型，认为迁徙过程没有那么井然有序。迁徙者穿越大陆时，会缓慢适应沿途遇到的各种自然生境，这无疑是最符合现实的情景。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Those who argue for an earlier settlement, however, must contend with the lack of unequivocal evidence for archaeological sites older than around 14,000 years. Nevertheless, evidence for human occupation of the centre of South America is now securely dated to around 12,500 years ago at the Monte Verde site, which casts doubt on the ‘late’ model. The lack of archaeological evidence further south for this time period may be explained by the obstacle to humans on foot posed by the huge glacial streams that were present at that time.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，主张人类更早定居的人必须面对一个问题：对于年代早于约14000年前的考古遗址，目前缺乏确凿无疑的证据。尽管如此，南美洲中部的Monte Verde遗址现已可靠测定，人类约在12500年前便在那里活动，这使“晚期”模型受到质疑。再往南的地区缺少这一时期的考古证据，或许是因为当时巨大的冰川融水河流构成障碍，阻止人类徒步前行。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: We can speculate then that the retreat of the Patagonian glaciers around 14,000 years ago allowed the initial human intrusion into a pristine environment, which was similar to that of early post-glacial Europe. Human settlement of the vast horizontal expanse of treeless high country must have been tenuous at best, and the evidence for this occupation remains relatively scant, most of it coming from rock shelters in Argentina and Chile. There is, however, reliable evidence from these sites to confirm the presence of humans by around 11,000 years ago in different habitats, and some hints of an even older occupation. However, some other sites where evidence for even earlier human occupation was initially posited have recently come under fresh scrutiny. This is because anthropologists have come to recognise that bones or other evidence may be deposited in caves by natural agency—in other words, by other forces such as floods or predators—and not necessarily by humans.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 因此，我们可以推测，大约14000年前巴塔哥尼亚冰川退缩，使人类得以首次进入一片原始环境；那里与冰期刚结束时的欧洲相似。在广袤横展、没有树木的高地上，人类定居充其量也必定十分脆弱，相关证据至今仍相对稀少，大多来自阿根廷和智利的岩棚。不过，这些遗址提供了可靠证据，确认约在11000年前，人类已存在于不同生境中；还有一些迹象暗示定居时间甚至更早。但另外一些遗址最初也被认为留有更早期的人类活动证据，近来却受到重新审视。这是因为人类学家逐渐认识到，骨骼或其他证据可能是经自然作用沉积在洞穴中的——换言之，是洪水或捕食动物等其他力量造成的——并不一定出自人类。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: We shall turn now to a more detailed discussion of the archaeological evidence found in various parts of Patagonia. At the site located beside Chinchihuapi Creek, excavations have produced convincing evidence of human occupation, including hut foundations and wooden artefacts. They were buried in layers of peat, which has the property of preserving wood remarkably well, and as a result, radiocarbon dating tests have shown these artefacts to date from around 12,500 years ago. One of the most famous Patagonian sites is a cave known as Los Toldos. However, the evidence from this site has recently been called into question, because dispersed flecks of carbon used in the test process were taken unsystematically from many different places at the site. As a result, the association of this material with the artefacts is not at all clear. About 150 kilometres to the south is the site called El Ceibo, where a similar collection of artefacts to that found at Los Toldos has been discovered from the lowest levels of the dig, but as yet no radiocarbon dates are available, and this sort of analysis of the existing evidence is required before the site’s value can be confirmed.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The Arroyo Eeo site is located very close to the high plateau. The artefacts from the earliest occupations were found at the same depth and have the same origins as those from Los Toldos, and have been securely dated to around 9,000 years ago. Another site that is mentioned in the debate is at Las Buitreras, where a number of stone flakes associated with bone remains of various animals have been discovered. However, anthropologists now believe that presumed cut marks on the bones are somewhat dubious, and despite detailed testing there is no way of securely relating any of these remains to human occupation. Finally, some 50 kilometres to the south is the site at Cueva Fell, which was the first Patagonian site to be systematically studied by modern archaeological methods. However, it is now recognised that the utility of this site must be restricted to its direct vicinity, given changes to the nearby area caused by flooding, and findings cannot be freely extrapolated further afield.

source.text: The Pirahã people of Brazil

translation.text: 巴西的皮拉罕人

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The Pirahã language has stirred up debate among experts
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 皮拉罕语在专家中引发了争论。

source.text: The Pirahã language has stirred up debate among experts

translation.text: 皮拉罕语在专家中引发了争论。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The Pirahã tribe live deep in Brazil’s Amazon forest, and their language is hotly debated by linguists. Since 1977, the ethnologist Daniel Everett has spent a total of seven years living with the Pirahã and has committed his career to studying their puzzling speech. Indeed, he was uncertain for so long about what he was actually hearing while living among the Pirahã that he waited nearly three decades before publishing his findings.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 皮拉罕部落生活在巴西亚马孙森林深处，他们的语言在语言学家中引发了激烈争论。自1977年以来，民族学家 Daniel Everett 与皮拉罕人共同生活的时间累计达7年，并把自己的职业生涯投入到研究他们令人费解的语言上。事实上，与皮拉罕人共同生活时，他有很长时间都不确定自己听到的究竟是什么，以至于等待了将近30年才发表研究结果。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The debate over the Pirahã language goes right to the core of the riddle regarding how Homo sapiens managed to develop vocal communication. Although bees dance, birds sing and whales even sing with syntax, human language is unique, if only for the reason that it enables humans to piece together never-before-constructed thoughts, and be infinitely imaginative - think of Shakespeare’s plays or Einstein’s theory of relativity.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 围绕皮拉罕语的争论直指一个谜题的核心：智人究竟如何发展出声音交流。蜜蜂会跳舞，鸟会歌唱，鲸甚至会遵循句法歌唱，但人类语言仍独一无二，单凭一点便足以说明：它让人类能够拼合出前所未有的思想，并展开无穷想象——想想莎士比亚的戏剧或爱因斯坦的相对论。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Linguistics generally focuses on what features all human languages have in common, but the Pirahã language departs from what some academics have long maintained are essential and inalienable features of all human languages. Most of all, it may be unique for not employing subordinate clauses. Instead of saying, ‘When I have finished eating, I will speak to you,’ the Pirahã say, ‘I finish eating, I speak with you.’ Equally perplexing, the Pirahã appear not to use numbers. During the time he spent with them, Everett never heard words like ‘all’, ‘every’ and ‘more’. There is one word, ‘hoi’, that comes close to the numeral 1, but it can also mean ‘small’. And they were never observed to count without language, on their fingers for example, in order to determine important tasks in village life like how many pieces of meat to grill.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 语言学一般关注所有人类语言共有的特征，但皮拉罕语偏离了某些学者长期以来认定为一切人类语言必不可少、不可剥离的特征。最突出的一点是，它可能是唯一不使用从句的语言。皮拉罕人不会说“等我吃完饭，我会和你说话”，而是说“我吃完饭，我和你说话”。同样令人困惑的是，皮拉罕人似乎不使用数字。Everett 与他们共同生活期间，从未听到类似“全部”“每一个”和“更多”的词。有一个词hoi接近数字1，却也可以表示“小”。人们也从未观察到他们在没有语言的情况下计数，例如用手指来确定烤多少块肉这类村庄生活中的重要事务。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Everett is at pains to point out that the Pirahã are not unintelligent, for their thinking is not any slower than that of the average university student. And although they reside in a remote part of the forest, they do not live in complete genetic isolation, but mix with people from the surrounding populations and share similar intellectual capacities with their neighbours whose languages do contain numbers.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Eventually, after some 30 years of research, Everett has come up with a surprising explanation for the peculiarities of the Pirahã language. Language, he believes, is created by a people’s way of life, their belief system and values. In this way, variety in human language is almost limitless, a function of the human capacity to live in different ways, such as in the forest. What Everett’s research has revealed is that the central tenet of the Pirahã culture is to live in the here and now. The only thing of importance that is worth communicating to others is what is being experienced at that very moment, though this can often be described with great care and detail. In consequence, the language has no means to conjugate verbs in order to describe ‘yesterday’ or ‘last week’ or ‘when I was a child’. Their very literal view of the world curtails abstract thought, and many features taken for granted among other peoples are absent among the Pirahã, such as a creation myth, storytelling and painting. One manifestation of their beliefs is that by tradition the names they give their children are not particularly imaginative. Often they are named after other members of the tribe with whom they share similar character traits. Standing out or being different is not encouraged by the Pirahã, and this is reflected in their perhaps colourless choice of names.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 经过约30年的研究，Everett 最终为皮拉罕语的特殊之处提出了一个令人惊讶的解释。他认为，语言由一个民族的生活方式、信仰体系和价值观塑造。由此，人类语言的多样性几乎没有限度，它取决于人类以不同方式生活的能力，例如生活在森林中。Everett 的研究揭示，皮拉罕文化的核心信条是活在此时此地。唯一重要且值得告诉别人的，是当下这一刻正在经历的事物，不过他们往往能非常认真而细致地描述这些经历。因此，这种语言没有通过动词变位来描述“昨天”“上周”或“我小时候”的手段。他们极其按字面理解世界，这限制了抽象思维；其他民族视为理所当然的许多特征，在皮拉罕人中并不存在，例如创世神话、讲故事和绘画。他们信仰的一种体现是，按照传统，给孩子起的名字并没有多少想象力。孩子常以部落中性格特征相似的其他成员命名。皮拉罕人不鼓励引人注目或与众不同，这一点也反映在他们或许颇为平淡的名字选择上。

source.text: Their very literal view of the world curtails abstract thought, and many features taken for granted among other peoples are absent among the Pirahã, such as a creation myth, storytelling and painting.

translation.text: 他们极其按字面理解世界，这限制了抽象思维；其他民族视为理所当然的许多特征，在皮拉罕人中并不存在，例如创世神话、讲故事和绘画。

source.text: One manifestation of their beliefs is that by tradition the names they give their children are not particularly imaginative.

translation.text: 他们信仰的一种体现是，按照传统，给孩子起的名字并没有多少想象力。

source.text: Often they are named after other members of the tribe with whom they share similar character traits.

translation.text: 孩子常以部落中性格特征相似的其他成员命名。

source.text: Standing out or being different is not encouraged by the Pirahã, and this is reflected in their perhaps colourless choice of names.

translation.text: 皮拉罕人不鼓励引人注目或与众不同，这一点也反映在他们或许颇为平淡的名字选择上。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Everett anticipated that these findings would be controversial and the reaction came as expected. Until this point, many linguists had defended the theories of Noam Chomsky, according to which all human languages have a universal grammar. What exactly makes up this universal grammar is the subject of debate, but at its heart is the concept of ‘recursion’, which is defined as replication of a structure within its single parts. Without it, humans would not be able to view separate thoughts as subordinate parts of a complex whole. And, most pertinent to Everett’s work, there would not be subordinate clauses, which are responsible for translating the concept of recursion into grammar. But if the Pirahã do not form subordinate clauses, then recursion cannot explain the uniqueness of human language, and this would negate Chomsky’s theories.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Everett 预料这些发现会引发争议，反应也果然如他所料。在此之前，许多语言学家一直捍卫 Noam Chomsky 的理论；该理论认为，所有人类语言都具有普遍语法。普遍语法究竟由什么构成仍有争议，但其核心是“递归”概念，即在一个结构的组成部分中复制该结构。没有递归，人类便无法把彼此分离的思想视为一个复杂整体中的从属部分。而与 Everett 的研究关系最密切的是，如果没有递归，就不会有把递归概念转化为语法形式的从句。但如果皮拉罕人确实不构成从句，递归便无法解释人类语言的独特性，这将否定 Chomsky 的理论。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The logical way forward now would be to try to prove that the Pirahã can think in a recursive fashion. The only problem is, nobody can confirm or deny Everett’s observations since no other researcher can speak Pirahã as well as he does. Despite this, several researchers - including two of Chomsky’s colleagues - will soon travel to Brazil to check his claims. My concern is that soon the Pirahã will simply become one more scientific oddity with every aspect of their lives being exploited and analysed.

source.text: A review of a famous study into group behaviour

translation.text: 回顾一项著名的群体行为研究。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Group self-centredness seems to occur the minute people are divided into groups. It doesn’t matter what the group is, or on what basis it was formed, we perceive the group we belong to as being superior to other groups and we develop an ‘in-group’ bias.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 人们似乎一被分成不同群体，群体自我中心倾向就会立即出现。无论是什么群体，也无论依据什么划分，我们都会认为自己所属的群体优于其他群体，并形成“内群体”偏见。

source.text: It doesn’t matter what the group is, or on what basis it was formed, we perceive the group we belong to as being superior to other groups and we develop an ‘in-group’ bias.

translation.text: 无论是什么群体，也无论依据什么划分，我们都会认为自己所属的群体优于其他群体，并形成“内群体”偏见。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Probably one of the most famous pieces of research looking at group behaviour was a field study conducted by Sherif in 1956. This study involved 22 boys aged between 11 and 12, who were divided into two groups. The groups were roughly matched in terms of sporting ability, camping experience and general popularity among their peers. Their parents were told that they were going to a three-week summer camp to see how well they would work alongside other boys when put into different teams. The parents were also told that the boys would not be allowed to be visited during that time, but would be able to go home if they wanted to. It was intended that the data for the study would be collected by participant observers.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 研究群体行为最著名的工作之一，可能是谢里夫于1956年开展的一项实地研究。研究对象为22名11至12岁的男孩，他们被分成两组。两组在运动能力、露营经验以及在同龄人中的总体受欢迎程度方面大致相当。研究人员告诉家长，孩子们将参加一个为期3周的夏令营，以观察他们被分入不同队伍后能否与其他男孩良好合作。家长还被告知，这段时间不允许探望孩子，但孩子若想回家则可以离开。研究原计划由参与式观察者收集数据。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: At first, neither set of boys knew of the existence of the other set. They were taken to their respective campsites, which were located on a 200-acre, densely wooded area in Robbers Cave State Park, Oklahoma. The first week was spent doing a variety of activities, such as pitching tents and cooking. During this week, the two groups seemed to develop different group norms, one group being more ‘tough’ than the other, from which two boys went home early, as they were homesick. The groups were given a set of caps and T-shirts, and gave themselves names: the ‘Eagles’ and the ‘Rattlers’ (the latter being the tougher group).
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 起初，两组男孩都不知道另一组存在。他们被分别带到各自营地，营地位于俄克拉何马州罗伯斯洞穴州立公园内一片占地200英亩、森林茂密的区域。第一周用来开展各种活动，例如搭帐篷和做饭。在这一周，两组似乎形成了不同的群体规范，其中一组显得比另一组更“强悍”；较弱的那组有两名男孩因想家而提前回去。两组都获发了一套帽子和T恤衫，并分别为自己取名“雄鹰队”和“响尾蛇队”，后者正是更强悍的那组。

Sherif noticed that already the groups had started to refer to the other group as ‘them’ and their group as ‘us’. This marked the beginning of phase two of the experiment.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 第一周结束时，他们通过发现另一组留下的垃圾或无意中听到说话声，知道了彼此的存在。谢里夫注意到，两组已经开始把另一组称为“他们”，把自己所在组称为“我们”。这标志着实验第二阶段开始。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The groups were told that they were going to take part in a ‘Grand Tournament’, which involved ten different sporting events, and they were shown the prizes for winning. The tournament was also to include in the final scores points which would be awarded for other activities, such as how tidy the cabins were kept. These scores were displayed on big scoreboards in what now became a joint hall where the two groups ate their meals together. This was necessary so the two groups would think they were on almost equal scores in the time leading up to the final event, which would increase the sense of competition. Needless to say, these scores were manipulated by the experimenters.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 两组被告知，他们将参加一场包含10个不同体育项目的“盛大锦标赛”，并看到了获胜奖品。锦标赛最终总分还会计入其他活动的得分，例如小木屋保持得有多整洁。这些分数公布在大厅里的大型记分牌上；那座大厅此时已经成了两组共同用餐的食堂。这样做是为了让两组以为，在临近最后一个项目时双方得分几乎相同，从而增强竞争感。不必说，这些分数受到实验人员操纵。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: In order to check how high the levels of group self-centredness were in the groups at this time, a number of tasks were set up which involved the groups rating their own members and members of the other group. Each time, group members rated the boys in their own group much better at the tasks than the other boys, even though there was no real difference between them. They were also asked to rate all others in terms of how desirable they were as friends, and 93 per cent of friendship preferences were in-group preferences.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 为了检查两组此时的群体自我中心程度有多高，研究人员安排了多项任务，让各组评价本组成员和另一组成员。每一次，组员对本组男孩完成任务表现的评价都远高于对另一组男孩的评价，尽管两者其实没有真正差别。他们还被要求从是否适合作为朋友的角度评价其他所有人，结果93%的交友偏好都指向本组成员。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: When the tournament started, the first game was basketball. The group that was thought to be less tough lost the game and claimed that they had lost only because the other group were bigger and older than they were. The Eagles won the next ball game and then were said to be cheating in the tug-of-war. This resulted in visits by both groups to each other’s cabins over the course of the next 24 hours, where they ripped the mosquito nets, turned over the beds and generally made a mess. The Eagles devised a new weapon in the conflict which consisted of ‘rocks in socks’ – and so it went on. Eventually, the Eagles won the tournament (with some help from the experimenters) and it was time for phase three to begin.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 锦标赛开始后的第一项比赛是篮球。被认为不那么强悍的一组输掉比赛，并声称落败只是因为另一组成员比他们更高大、年龄也更大。雄鹰队赢得下一场球赛，随后又被指责在拔河中作弊。接下来的24小时里，两组都闯入对方的小木屋，扯破蚊帐、掀翻床铺，到处弄得一团糟。雄鹰队还在冲突中发明了一种新武器——“袜子里装石块”——事情就这样不断升级。最终，雄鹰队在实验人员提供一些帮助的情况下赢得了锦标赛，实验也到了开始第三阶段的时候。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Research has suggested that the best way to reduce group conflict is by non-competitive contact. This required two conditions: that the groups had equal status and that they had a common goal to work towards. This was exactly what Sherif engineered. There were actually seven situations organised which gave the groups equal-status contact; these were things like having meals together or watching films together. The meals resulted in food fights; the films were enjoyed by both groups sitting totally apart from each other.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 有研究认为，减少群体冲突的最佳方式是开展非竞争性接触。这需要满足两个条件：各群体地位平等，并有一个共同努力的目标。谢里夫安排的正是这种情形。研究人员一共设计了7种情境，让两组在地位平等的情况下接触，例如一起吃饭或一起看电影。一起吃饭演变成了食物大战；看电影时，两组虽然都看得开心，却各自坐在完全分开的地方。

source.text: The strange world of sight

translation.text: 奇异的视觉世界

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Seeing is believing, it is said. But, asks Richard Gregory, could it be the other way round?

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Two of the great British men of the 17th century, the philosopher John Locke and the physicist Isaac Newton, were both aware that objects are not coloured, and that against all appearances light is not coloured either. This is still not generally recognised even now, 400 years later, because it seems so implausible. Yet it tells us something very important — that perceptions are not identical with what we perceive, and may be very different.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The most accurate historical account of perception is that of the 19th-century German scientist Hermann von Helmholtz. However, it was ridiculed at the time. Von Helmholtz thought that perceptions are unconscious inferences we make based on a combination of clues provided by the eyes and other senses, and knowledge of the world. This idea of unconscious inference for perception preceded, by several years, the psychoanalyst Freud’s notion of the unconscious, which was also initially treated with derision because it undermined the notion of humans as pre-eminently rational beings who could be held responsible for their actions and awarded blame or praise accordingly.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Crucially, perception of the present depends on rich, though of course not always correct or appropriate, knowledge from the past. We interpret sense data (what we hear, touch, taste, see and smell) from the present according to what we already know. This raises the question: if we see the present through memory, why aren’t past and present confused? The pioneering Russian neurologist Alexander Luria described the case of Mr S, who had a remarkable memory. However, he was prone to just such confusions, for example mistaking seeing his clock for remembering it, and so failing to get up in the morning. This suggests that perhaps an important function of perception is to underline the present. Individual perceptions have a vividness that is rare for memories, which might be how we are able to separate them. Try this: look at something for a few seconds, and then shut your eyes and visualise it in memory. You will almost certainly find that the memory is pale by comparison with the perception. Perhaps this is why past and present are not normally confused. Luria’s Mr S had exceptionally vivid memories, and rich synaesthesia (experiencing perceptions from another sense as well as the one being stimulated, such as musical notes experienced as colours), which may be why he confused seeing with having seen.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 关键在于，我们对当下的感知依赖过去积累的丰富知识，当然，这些知识并非总是正确或恰当。我们会依据已有知识，解读当下的感官数据，也就是我们此刻听到、触到、尝到、看到和闻到的一切。这就提出了一个问题：如果我们透过记忆看待当下，为何不会把过去与现在混淆？俄罗斯神经病学先驱 Alexander Luria 描述过S先生的病例，此人有着非凡的记忆力。然而，他正容易出现这种混淆。例如，他会把看见时钟误当成自己只是记起时钟，结果早晨没有起床。这表明，感知的一项重要功能或许是凸显当下。单次感知具有一种记忆很少具备的鲜明感，这可能就是我们能把两者区分开的原因。请试一试：看某件东西几秒钟，然后闭上眼睛，在记忆中想象它。几乎可以肯定，你会发现记忆中的形象比实际感知苍白得多。或许正因如此，我们通常不会混淆过去与现在。Luria 研究的S先生有着异常鲜明的记忆和丰富的联觉；所谓联觉，是除受刺激的感官外，还会产生来自另一感官的感知，例如把音符体验为颜色。这或许解释了他为何混淆正在看见与曾经看见。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The complexity of processes involved in how we see first impressed itself on me 45 years ago. With my colleague Jean Wallace, I studied the rare case of Sydney Bradford, a man who had been born blind but, through a corneal graft at the age of 52, suddenly found himself able to see. Almost immediately after the operation he was able to ‘see’ but he could only see those things that he already knew about, having experienced them through touch. It was his touch memories that enabled him to perceive them with his eyes. When Bradford was first taken to the zoo, he proved utterly unable to see an elephant as he had no knowledge to make sense of his perceptions.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 45年前，我第一次深刻认识到视觉过程何等复杂。我和同事 Jean Wallace 研究了 Sydney Bradford 这个罕见病例。他先天失明，却在52岁时接受角膜移植，此后突然能够看见。手术后几乎立即，他就能“看见”，但只能看见那些他已经了解、曾通过触摸体验过的事物。正是触觉记忆使他能够用眼睛感知这些事物。Bradford 第一次被带到动物园时，完全无法看出大象是什么，因为他没有可用来理解这一感知的相关知识。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The more recent case in California of Mike May, who was also born blind, is similar. Since his operation, his sight has gradually improved as he learns to see, for example, by understanding how shadows represent depth and tell us about the shape of things. Some of the consequences of May’s new-found vision were less happy. He had been a champion blind skier, but following the operation, he would have to shut his eyes while skiing to block out what he now found was a terrifying sight.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But acceptance of this intimate connection between memory and perception, even though it was first noticed in the 17th century, has been slow in brain science. Despite the fact that state-of-the-art brain imaging shows that perception animates parts of the brain associated with both present information and memory, most research on memory and perception is still undertaken as if these were separate processes. Seeing used to be thought of as taking place only in the eyes, and in quite specialised brain regions; but now it seems that half the brain is occupied with seeing, requiring a lot of energy. Perhaps this is why we shut our eyes for a rest.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 记忆与感知之间的紧密联系虽然早在17世纪就有人发现，但脑科学一直迟迟没有接受这一点。最先进的脑成像技术已经显示，感知会激活与当下信息和记忆都有关的脑区；尽管如此，大多数记忆与感知研究仍仿佛两者是相互分离的过程。过去人们认为，视觉只发生在眼睛和一些非常专门化的脑区中；但现在看来，半个大脑都在忙于看，这需要消耗大量能量。也许这就是我们闭眼休息的原因。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It is not just extreme cases like Mike May, but also much more common errors of seeing — illusions — that can reveal the crucial role of memory in governing what we (think we) see. Perception depends on specific knowledge and probabilities. Our brains calculate the likelihood of what is out there, and when too far-fetched, perceptions are rejected.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: A dramatic and discomforting example is looking at the two sides of a face-mask. From the front it is a convex shape with the nose sticking out. Then if the mask is rotated, the back of the mask will be seen as convex, though we know that it must be concave. It is almost, if not quite, impossible to sketch the back of a hollow mask to look as it is — hollow. Science often learns from what does not happen: people not seeing a hollow face as hollow is the most revealing experiment on perception. The unsettling truth from brain science is that even people with no visual impairment see what, at some level, they expect to see, and often miss things as they really are.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 观察一张人脸面具的正反两面，是一个效果强烈而令人不安的例子。从正面看，面具呈凸形，鼻子向外突出。把面具转过去后，尽管我们知道背面必定是凹的，看到的却仍像是凸面。要把空心面具的背面画成它本来的凹陷模样，即使并非绝对不可能，也几乎做不到。科学常从没有发生的事情中学习：人们看不出一张空心面孔是凹的，正是最能揭示感知机制的实验。脑科学揭示了一个令人不安的事实：即便视觉没有任何障碍，人们在某种程度上仍会看到自己预期看见的东西，并经常忽略事物的真实面貌。

translation.text: 科学常从没有发生的事情中学习：人们看不出一张空心面孔是凹的，正是最能揭示感知机制的实验。

source.text: The unsettling truth from brain science is that even people with no visual impairment see what, at some level, they expect to see, and often miss things as they really are.

translation.text: 脑科学揭示了一个令人不安的事实：即便视觉没有任何障碍，人们在某种程度上仍会看到自己预期看见的东西，并经常忽略事物的真实面貌。

source.text: The tuatara – past and future

translation.text: 楔齿蜥——过去与未来

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The New Zealand species of lizard, the tuatara, is firmly embedded in the national psyche: an icon for today which dates from the age of dinosaurs; an ancient reptile commemorated on the back of the five-cent coin. New Zealanders feel an affinity with the tuatara, and accept that active conservation management is required to ensure it will be among the legacies left to future generations.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 新西兰的蜥蜴物种楔齿蜥已深深融入这个国家的集体意识：它是当今的一个标志，却可追溯至恐龙时代；这种古老爬行动物的形象还铸在5分硬币背面。新西兰人对楔齿蜥怀有亲近感，也认同必须采取积极的保护管理措施，确保它能成为留给后代的遗产之一。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: When European explorers reached New Zealand in 1769 they found two large islands, which together they called the mainland, and many tiny offshore islands around the coast. The naturalists who came with the explorers disregarded the tuatara, though it is improbable none were seen. Only several decades later did a tuatara specimen reach the British Museum, where it was eventually classified as just another type of lizard.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 1769年欧洲探险家抵达新西兰时，发现了两座大岛——他们将两岛合称为本土——以及海岸四周许多小小的近海岛屿。随探险家而来的博物学家忽视了楔齿蜥，虽说他们不大可能一只也没见到。直到数十年后，一件楔齿蜥标本才送抵大英博物馆，并最终被归类为又一种普通蜥蜴。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One of the first scientists who realised that aspects of tuatara anatomy were odd—unchanged for tens of thousands of years—was Albert Gunther in 1876. Gunther believed the tuatara was one of the most valuable objects in zoological anatomical collections, and also noted, in passing, the reptile was likely to become extinct. From today’s perspective, it is striking that Gunther expressed no concern about the probable demise of the tuatara. He and his contemporaries were products of their age, strongly influenced by Charles Darwin’s theory, which had only recently been published. Their views were something like this: ‘Extinction is a natural process. It is sad that species disappear, but that is part of nature.’

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: There is a second important aspect of Gunther’s work. He recorded, correctly, that some of the mammals introduced by Europeans were predators of the tuatara—particularly rats. But what he did not realise was that New Zealand has two species of rat, both introduced, both with an appetite for tuatara: the ship’s rat came with European explorers and settlers; but the kiore rat had already been in the country for hundreds of years, brought by Polynesians from the Pacific Islands. Gunther failed to recognise the distinction, believing all rats to be a relatively recent introduction.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Gunther 的工作还有第二个重要方面。他正确记录到，欧洲人引入的一些哺乳动物会捕食楔齿蜥，尤其是鼠类。但他没有意识到，新西兰有两种鼠，两者都是外来物种，也都爱吃楔齿蜥：船鼠随欧洲探险家和定居者而来，而kiore鼠早已在这里生活了数百年，是波利尼西亚人从太平洋岛屿带来的。Gunther 未能识别这种区别，以为所有鼠类都是相对近期才引入的。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Little further research was conducted until Ian Crook of the NZ Wildlife Service published his findings in 1973, which can be summarised as follows. Tuatara thrive on offshore islands with no rats. Tuatara never survived on islands with ship’s rats. On a few islands, small and declining populations of tuatara occur with the kiore. This should not be seen, however, as evidence that tuatara and kiore can coexist. Rather, Crook proposed, kiore probably only arrived recently on such islands, and thus the small populations represent extinctions in progress.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 此后几乎没有进一步研究，直到新西兰野生动物管理局的 Ian Crook 在1973年发表研究结果。其要点可以概括如下：在没有鼠的近海岛屿上，楔齿蜥繁衍兴旺；在有船鼠的岛上，楔齿蜥从未存活下来；在少数岛屿上，楔齿蜥与kiore鼠同时存在，但种群规模很小且不断缩减。不过，这不应被视为楔齿蜥与kiore鼠能够共存的证据。Crook 提出，kiore鼠很可能只是最近才抵达这些岛屿，因此，那些小规模楔齿蜥种群代表的是正在发生的灭绝。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Throughout the 1990s, Richard Holdaway and his colleagues at Victoria University in Wellington documented the surprising discovery that kiore probably arrived about 1,800 years ago, although the human population of New Zealand is thought to be no older than 800 years. How is this possible? Presumably, Holdaway argued, the kiore were brought by Polynesian explorers who visited the country but did not settle. Thereafter, the rats were agents of ecological warfare, exterminating perhaps 1,000–3,000 species. Thus, tuatara and many other species were already rare or extinct when permanent human inhabitants—the Maori—arrived around 1300. This hypothesis is still being debated, but the evidence continues to accumulate in its favour.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 整个20世纪90年代，惠灵顿维多利亚大学的 Richard Holdaway 及其同事记录了一项惊人发现：kiore鼠可能在约1800年前便已抵达，而一般认为新西兰的人类定居史不超过800年。这怎么可能？Holdaway 推测，kiore鼠是由曾到访新西兰、却未在此定居的波利尼西亚探险者带来的。此后，这些鼠成了生态战争的实施者，或许消灭了1000至3000个物种。因此，约在1300年永久定居的人类居民毛利人到来时，楔齿蜥和许多其他物种已经十分稀少或已经灭绝。这一假说仍在争论中，但支持它的证据不断增加。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Conservation practice has changed dramatically since Crook’s findings were published in 1973. Eradication of rats from any given environment was believed to be virtually impossible until about 1980, but since then has become routine. Enormous conservation benefits are accruing as newly rat-free offshore islands are providing sanctuaries for the country’s rarest species. In 1995, for example, Nicola Nelson of the Department of Conservation established 68 tuatara on Titi Island. Since then, four more populations of tuatara have been established elsewhere under similar conditions. Today, numbers of tuatara are still a fraction of what they once were, but for the first time in 1,800 years the decline has been reversed.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 自 Crook 的研究结果于1973年发表以来，保护实践发生了巨大变化。直到约1980年，人们还认为要在任何一个特定环境中彻底清除鼠类几乎不可能，但此后这已成为常规做法。随着新近清除鼠类的近海岛屿成为该国最稀有物种的庇护所，保护工作正取得巨大的成效。例如，1995年，自然保护部的 Nicola Nelson 在蒂蒂岛安置了68只楔齿蜥。此后，其他地方又在类似条件下建立了4个楔齿蜥种群。如今楔齿蜥的数量仍只是过去的一小部分，但1800年来，这种下降趋势首次得到扭转。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: While the recovery of rare species is itself a good thing, the truly significant outcome of this research is that it liberates the imagination. If we can remove predatory introduced mammals from islands, why not from the mainland too? Perhaps the questions we ask should demonstrate even more visionary ambition. Can non-mammalian pests also be removed from the mainland? Our rivers, for example, are full of surrogate rats, in the form of introduced species of fish called trout. Some day more people will understand that trout have replaced a whole native fauna in our waterways, just as rats replaced tuatara on the mainland. Will such knowledge lead to the creation of mainland ‘aquatic islands’ where we can once again establish those species of indigenous fish that used to live in our rivers? Similarly, can bellbirds and tuis replace birds like starlings and mynahs?
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 稀有物种得以恢复本身当然是件好事，但这项研究真正重要的成果在于，它解放了人们的想象力。如果我们能从岛屿上清除外来掠食性哺乳动物，为什么不能也从本土清除？或许我们提出的问题应该展现出更富远见的雄心。非哺乳类害兽也能从本土清除吗？例如，我们的河流里充斥着鼠类的替代角色——一种名为鳟鱼的外来鱼类。总有一天，会有更多人明白，鳟鱼已经取代了水道中的整个本土动物群，就像鼠类在本土取代了楔齿蜥一样。这种认识会不会促成人们建立本土“水生岛屿”，让曾经生活在河流中的本土鱼类再次在其中安家？同样，铃鸟和tui鸟能否取代椋鸟和八哥等鸟类？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The answers to such questions are uncertain, and opposing sides will doubtless be fiercely debated. But the role of scientific knowledge in illuminating the past will be crucial. Just as we no longer tolerate extinction, in the future we may no longer accept a mainland devoid of the biological wonders of our past such as tuatara. Conservation is thus not primarily about the past but about imagining and then creating the future we wish for our children and ourselves. For 80 million years until humans arrived, tuatara occurred throughout New Zealand—might they do so again?
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这些问题的答案尚不确定，对立双方无疑会展开激烈争论。但科学知识在照亮过去方面的作用至关重要。正如我们已不再容忍物种灭绝，将来我们或许也不会再接受本土缺少楔齿蜥等昔日生物奇观。因此，保护工作主要关乎的不是过去，而是想象并继而创造我们希望留给孩子和自己的未来。在人类到来以前的8000万年间，楔齿蜥遍布新西兰——它们还能再次做到吗？

source.text: Voynich Manuscript

translation.text: 伏尼契手稿

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The starkly modern Beinecke Library at Yale University is home to some of the most valuable books in the world: first folios of Shakespeare, Gutenberg Bibles and manuscripts from the early Middle Ages. Yet the library’s most controversial possession is an unprepossessing vellum manuscript about the size of a hardback book, containing 240-odd pages of drawings and text of unknown age and authorship. Catalogued as MS 408, the manuscript would attract little attention were it not for the fact that the drawings hint at esoteric knowledge, while the text seems to be some sort of code — one that no-one has been able to break. It is known to scholars as the Voynich manuscript, after the American book-dealer Wilfrid Voynich, who bought the manuscript from a Jesuit college in Italy in 1912.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It is certainly strange: page after page of drawings of weird plants, astrological symbolism and human figures, accompanied by a script that looks like some form of shorthand. What does it say — and what are the drawings about? Voynich himself believed that the manuscript was the work of the 13th-century English monk Roger Bacon, famed for his knowledge of alchemy, philosophy and science. In 1921 Voynich’s view that Bacon was the writer appeared to win support from the work of William Newbold, Professor of Philosophy at the University of Pennsylvania, who claimed to have found the key to the cipher system used by Bacon. According to Newbold, the manuscript proved that Bacon had access to a microscope centuries before they were supposedly first invented. The claim that this medieval monk had observed living cells created a sensation. It soon became clear, however, that Newbold had fallen victim to wishful thinking. Other scholars showed that his “decoding” methods produced a host of possible interpretations.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The Voynich manuscript has continued to defy the efforts of world-class experts. In 1944, a team was assembled to tackle the mystery, led by William Friedman, the renowned American code-breaker. They began with the most basic code-breaking task: analysing the relative frequencies of the characters making up the text, looking for signs of an underlying structure. Yet Friedman’s team soon found themselves in deep water. The precise size of the “alphabet” of the Voynich manuscript was unclear: it is possible to make out more than 70 distinct symbols among the 170,000-character text. Furthermore, Friedman discovered that some words and phrases appeared more often than expected in a standard language, casting doubt on claims that the manuscript concealed a real language, as encryption typically reduces word frequencies.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 伏尼契手稿继续挫败着世界一流专家的努力。1944年，一个团队组建起来破解这个谜团，由著名美国密码破译专家 William Friedman 带领。他们从最基本的密码破译任务入手：分析构成文本的字符各自出现的相对频率，寻找底层结构的迹象。然而，Friedman 的团队很快就陷入困境。伏尼契手稿“字母表”的确切规模并不清楚：在全篇170000个字符中，可以辨认出70多个不同符号。此外，Friedman 发现，有些单词和短语的出现频率高于标准语言中的预期水平，这使人怀疑手稿中隐藏着真实语言的主张，因为加密通常会降低单词出现频率。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Friedman concluded that the most plausible resolution of this paradox was that “Voynichese” is some sort of specially created artificial language, whose words are devised from concepts rather than linguistics. So could the Voynich manuscript be the earliest-known example of an artificial language? “Friedman’s hypothesis commands respect because of the lifetime of cryptanalytic expertise he brought to bear,” says Rob Churchill, co-author of The Voynich Manuscript. That still leaves a host of questions unanswered, however, such as the identity of the author and the meaning of the bizarre drawings. “It does little to advance our understanding of the manuscript as a whole,” says Churchill.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The insights so far have been perplexing. For example, in 2001 another leading Voynich scholar, Dr Gabriel Landini of Birmingham University in the UK, published the results of his study of the manuscript using a pattern-detecting method called spectral analysis. Yet the following year, Voynich expert René Zandbergen of the European Space Agency in Darmstadt, Germany, showed that the entropy of the text (a measure of the rate of transfer of information) was consistent with Friedman’s suspicions that an artificial language had been used.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Many are convinced that the Voynich manuscript is not a hoax. For how could a medieval hoaxer create so many tell-tale signs of a message from random nonsense? Yet even this has been challenged in new research by Rugg. Using a system first published by the Italian mathematician Girolamo Cardano in 1150, in which a specially constructed grille is used to pick out symbols from a table, Rugg found he could rapidly generate text with many of the basic traits of the Voynich manuscript. Publishing his results in 2004, Rugg stresses that he had not set out to prove the manuscript a hoax. “I simply demonstrated that it is feasible to hoax something this complex in a few months,” he says.

source.text: Whale Culture

translation.text: 鲸类文化

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Most social scientists stubbornly resist the idea that animals have culture. Even such advanced cetacean mammals as whales and dolphins clearly don’t have art, literature, or architecture. But patient observation over many years has begun to reveal behaviours that can only be learnt from other whales. And that, say whale biologists, constitutes culture.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: So far, humpback and killer whales provide the best evidence of culture in cetaceans, and the song of the male humpback is among the most striking examples. Humpback populations in different oceans sing different songs, but within the same ocean they all stick to the same one. However, during the breeding season the sounds change, as it appears that females are drawn to novel songs. One male might add an extra set of groans; another might drop a series of grunts. Soon all the other males have altered their own rendition to incorporate the changes until they are once again singing the same song. Since this occurs among thousands of whales spread across a vast part of the planet, the change cannot be in response to any factor in the animal’s environment. The latest version of the song can be learnt only from other whales – almost certainly by imitation.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Culture plays an even bigger part in the life of killer whales. Nowhere is this more obvious than along the north-west coast of America, where killer whales are split into two distinct populations – ‘residents’ and ‘transients’. They live in the same stretch of water, but they don’t mingle. In effect, they belong to two quite separate cultures. Residents live in stable groups, or ‘pods’, made up of two or three mothers and their offspring – perhaps 20 whales in all. Calves stay with their mothers throughout adulthood, and in many years of observation no one has ever seen a whale switch pods. Transients travel in smaller, more changeable groups of between three and six.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One of the most obvious distinctions between the transient and resident societies is the way they impart information. Killer whales detect prey with a range of echo-locating clicks, but converse with a vocabulary of squeaks, whistles and whines. Despite regular interaction between them, each resident pod sticks firmly to its own dialect. Research shows these dialects are maintained for at least 40 years.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: To qualify as part of killer whale culture, dialects must be learnt from other members of the pod. Animals with different dialects share the same waters, so the variation can’t be a product of physical environment. ‘And we can throw out the notion that dialects are inherited,’ says Lance Barrett-Lennard of the University of British Columbia. blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The question still remains – is this culture? It is, according to Frans de Waal of Emory University in Atlanta, who argues that culture is just another biological adaptation that has evolved in many creatures. One benefit of viewing culture in this way is that you can start to understand how and why it might have arisen in these creatures. Whales have several biological attributes that give them an advantage in social learning. Apart from their advanced mental abilities, they are adept at recognising sounds: ideal for communicating in the marine environment. Many species spend years rearing their offspring, and live in small, stable, multi-generational societies, a social system that provides ample opportunity for teaching and learning.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 但问题依然存在——这算文化吗？亚特兰大埃默里大学的 Frans de Waal 认为算。他主张，文化只是另一种生物适应性特征，已经在许多生物身上演化出来。这样看待文化的一项好处是，我们可以开始理解它可能如何、又为何会在这些生物中出现。鲸具有若干有利于社会学习的生物属性。除了心智能力发达之外，它们还善于辨别声音，这非常适合在海洋环境中交流。许多鲸类会花数年时间抚育后代，并生活在规模小、关系稳定且由多代成员组成的社会中；这种社会体系为教与学提供了充足机会。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But why have cetaceans evolved the ability to learn from other group members? Experts in whale biology believe that ecological factors and the need to adapt to sudden changes in the environment played a large part in the emergence of culture. Although the ocean is a relatively stable habitat in many ways, it is highly changeable in one crucial respect – the availability of food. One moment there might be a plentiful supply of fish, the next they’ve disappeared. When that happens, the past experience of senior members of the group – and the ability to share this knowledge – is a huge asset. The dialects of killer whales allow members of the group to identify each other, enabling them to share information about food hot spots. Among resident killer whales, it also allows females to avoid inbreeding by picking out a mate with a strange dialect from outside their pod, says Barrett-Lennard.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 但鲸类为什么演化出了向群体其他成员学习的能力？鲸类生物学专家认为，生态因素以及适应环境突然变化的需要，在文化的出现过程中发挥了很大作用。尽管从许多方面看，海洋是相对稳定的栖息地，但在一个关键方面却变化极大——食物是否充足。前一刻鱼类可能还供应充足，下一刻便消失无踪。出现这种情况时，群体中年长成员以往的经验，以及分享这些知识的能力，就会成为巨大的优势。虎鲸的方言使群体成员能够相互识别，从而可以分享有关食物富集区的信息。巴雷特-伦纳德说，对定居型虎鲸而言，这还能让雌鲸从鲸群以外辨认出方言陌生的配偶，以避免近亲繁殖。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Ever since its elevation to the status of an academic discipline, history has been very largely concerned with problems of its own making. blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Social history is quite different. It touches on, and arguably helps to focus, major issues of public debate. It mobilises popular enthusiasm and engages popular passions. It prides itself on being concerned with everyday things rather than sensational events and is directed against the ‘Great Man’ theories that originally characterised history, and the tedious focus on bureaucratic issues that subsequently dominated the 1920s and 30s. This is also reflected in the way it is taught, through the adoption of multi-disciplinary perspectives rather than a narrow historical interpretation.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 社会史则很不一样。它会涉及公共讨论中的重大议题，而且可以说有助于聚焦这些议题。它能调动大众热情，激发大众强烈的情感。社会史以关注日常事物而非轰动事件为傲，并反对历史学最初具有的“伟人”理论，也反对后来主导20世纪20年代和30年代、令人乏味的官僚事务取向。这一点也体现在社会史的教学方式上：它采用多学科视角，而不是狭窄的历史学解释。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Social history emerged, both as a popular enthusiasm and as a scholarly practice, from the cultural revolution of the 1960s in North America and Europe, and reproduces its leading inspirations. The spirit of social history was pre-eminently a modernising one, as reflected in its choice of subject matter. Whereas traditional history had focused on the 12th to 17th centuries, social history was apt to make its historical homeland in the 19th century. Latterly, it has even begun to extend its inquiry up to contemporary events and movements.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 无论作为一种大众热潮还是学术实践，社会史都发端于20世纪60年代北美和欧洲的文化革命，并延续了这场革命带来的主要思想。社会史的精神首先是一种现代化精神，这反映在它对研究对象的选择上。传统历史学关注的是12至17世纪，而社会史则往往把19世纪当作自己的历史主场。近来，它甚至开始把研究延伸到当代事件和运动。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The subject matter favoured by the new social history, with its move away from the aristocracy and the establishment, corresponds to other cultural manifestations of the 1960s, such as New Wave British cinema, with its working-class protagonists, or ‘Pop art’, with its use of everyday artefacts. Similarly, the anti-institutional bias of the new social history—the renewed determination to write the history of ‘ordinary’ people as against that of statecraft—could be said to echo a much more widespread collapse of social deference, and a questioning of authority figures of all kinds.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 新社会史不再以贵族和权势集团为中心，它所偏爱的研究对象与20世纪60年代的其他文化表现相呼应，例如以工人阶级人物为主角的英国新浪潮电影，或使用日常物品的“波普艺术”。同样，新社会史所具有的反制度倾向——重新下定决心书写“普通人”而非治国活动的历史——也可以说呼应了一种广泛得多的社会现象：社会上的恭顺态度大幅瓦解，人们开始质疑各种权威人物。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Another major 1960s influence on the new social history—very different in its origins and effects—was the ‘nostalgia industry’, which focused on the sale of memorabilia and artefacts from recent history. This emerged as a kind of negative counterpart to the otherwise dominant modernisation of the decade and reflected a disenchantment, no less apparent on the Left of the political spectrum than on the Right, with post-war social change.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 20世纪60年代对新社会史的另一项重大影响，是“怀旧产业”；它的起源和影响都截然不同，关注的是出售近代历史中的纪念品和旧物。它的出现，成了当时占主导地位的现代化潮流的一种反向对应，也反映出人们对战后社会变迁的不满；这种不满在政治光谱左翼一侧表现得不比右翼一侧少。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Industrial archaeology, an invention of the 1960s, elevated disused factories and mills to the status of national monuments. Following in the same track, property restorers turned houses built for 19th-century factory workers—once emblems of poverty, overcrowding, and ill-health—into picturesque residences. In another sphere, one could point to the proliferation of folk clubs and the discovery of industrial folk songs, prefiguring one of the major themes of the new social history—the dignity of labour.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 工业考古学是20世纪60年代的产物，它把废弃的工厂和磨坊提升到了国家纪念建筑的地位。沿着同一思路，房产修复者把19世纪为工厂工人建造的住宅——这些房屋曾是贫困、拥挤和疾病的象征——改造成了风景如画的居所。在另一个领域，还可以看到民间音乐俱乐部大量涌现，以及工业民歌得到发掘；这些现象预示了新社会史的一大主题——劳动的尊严。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: So far as historical work was concerned, by the 1970s the sense of disenchantment had crystallised into an idealised view of the past, fostering a nostalgic regard for disappearing communities. The restoration of vanished components of ‘the world we have lost’ became a major impetus in historical writing and research. The dignity of ordinary people could be said to be the unifying theme of this line of historical inquiry and retrieval—a celebration of everyday life, even, perhaps especially, when it involved hardship and suffering.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 就历史研究而言，到了20世纪70年代，这种失望感已经凝结成一种理想化的历史观，促使人们怀念那些正在消失的社区。重现“我们失去的世界”中已经消逝的组成部分，成为历史写作与研究的一项主要动力。可以说，普通人的尊严是这条历史探究与寻回路径的共同主题——它赞颂日常生活，即使其中包含艰难与苦难，甚至或许尤其是在这种情况下。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Despite the novelty of its subject matter, social history reproduces many of the characteristic biases of its predecessors. Social historians are good at amassing details on household artefacts, budgets, daily purchases, but at times the evidence is assumed to speak for itself, and the simple reproduction of fact masquerades as explanation. The facts accumulated may leave no conceptual space for the great absences, for the many areas where the documentary record is silent.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 尽管研究对象颇为新颖，社会史仍重现了前辈学派的许多典型偏见。社会史学家善于收集有关家庭用品、收支预算和日常采购的细节，但有时却假定证据本身就能说明一切，把简单罗列事实伪装成解释。积累起来的事实可能没有为那些巨大的空白留下概念空间，也就是文献记录沉默不语的许多领域。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The indulgence which social historians extend towards their subjects, and the desire to establish ‘empathy’—seeing the past in terms of its own values rather than those of today—can also serve to flatter our self-esteem, making history a field in which, at no great cost to ourselves, we can demonstrate our enlarged sympathies and benevolence. Recognising our kinship to people in the past, and tracing, or discovering, their likeness to ourselves, we are flattered in the belief that underneath we are all lovable; eccentric perhaps and even absurd, but large-hearted, generous and frank. This sense of integration with the past can thus serve as a comfortable alternative to critical awareness and self-questioning, allowing us to dignify the present by illegitimate association with the past.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 社会史学家对研究对象所抱的宽容态度，以及建立“共情”的愿望——也就是根据过去自身的价值观而非今天的价值观来理解过去——也可能用来满足我们的自尊，使历史成为这样一个领域：我们无需付出多大代价，就能在其中展示自己扩展了的同情心和善意。我们承认自己与过去的人们同属一类，并追寻或发现他们与我们的相似之处，于是便因相信人人本质上都讨人喜爱而感到自得；人或许古怪，甚至荒唐，却心胸宽广、慷慨坦率。因此，这种与过去融为一体的感觉可能成为批判意识和自我质疑的一种安逸替代品，使我们通过与过去建立并不正当的联系，来抬高当下。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Social history, if it is to fulfil its subversive potential, needs to be a great deal more disturbing. If it is to celebrate a common humanity, and to bring past and present closer together, far more weight needs to be given to the effects of insecurities and emergencies—the fears that shadow the growing up of children, the oppositions we encounter during our lives—experiences which may be hard for an individual to categorise but which nevertheless have a significance which goes beyond that individual.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 社会史若要发挥其颠覆性的潜力，就必须更具冲击性，让人远为不安。如果它要赞颂人类共有的人性，并拉近过去与现在的距离，就需要大幅提高对不安全感和紧急状况所产生影响的重视——例如伴随儿童成长的恐惧，以及我们一生中遇到的对立。这些经历或许很难由个人归类，却仍具有超越个人层面的意义。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Perhaps too we might recognise that there is a profound condescension in the notion of ‘ordinary people’—that unified totality in which social historians are apt to deal. Implicitly it is a category from which we tend to exclude ourselves, although in fact we are exceptional only by our privilege of hindsight. ‘There are … no masses,’ Raymond Williams wrote, ‘only ways of seeing people as masses.’ It is perhaps time for historians to scrutinise the term ‘ordinary people’ in the same way.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 也许我们还可以认识到，“普通人”这一概念中含有一种根深蒂固的居高临下态度；社会史学家往往把他们当作一个统一的整体来处理。这个类别暗中把我们自己排除在外，尽管事实上，我们唯一的特殊之处只在于拥有事后回顾的便利。Raymond Williams 写道：“并不存在……所谓大众，只有把人视为大众的不同方式。”或许，历史学家也该以同样方式仔细审视“普通人”这个词了。

source.text: What makes a musical expert?

translation.text: 什么造就了音乐专家？

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: How does someone become expert in music? And is it really possible to have a talent for music?
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 一个人怎样才能成为音乐专家？音乐天赋真的存在吗？

source.text: How does someone become expert in music?

translation.text: 一个人怎样才能成为音乐专家？

source.text: And is it really possible to have a talent for music?

translation.text: 音乐天赋真的存在吗？

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Does that class of people acknowledged to be musical experts just have more of the same basic skills we are all endowed with, or do they have a set of abilities — or neural structures — that are totally different from those of the rest of us? Are high levels of musical achievement simply the result of training and practice, or are they based on innate brain structure — what we refer to as talent? Talent can be defined as something that originates in genetic structures and that is identifiable by trained people who can recognize its existence before a person has achieved exceptional levels of performance. The emphasis on early identification means that to investigate it, we study the development of skills in children.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 那些公认的音乐专家，只是把我们人人与生俱来的同类基本技能发展到了更高程度，还是具备一套与我们其他人完全不同的能力——乃至神经结构？高水平的音乐成就是单纯训练和练习的结果，还是建立在先天脑结构，也就是我们所说的天赋之上？天赋可以定义为某种源于遗传结构的特质；在一个人的表现达到非凡水平之前，受过训练的人就能识别出这种特质的存在。由于重点在于及早识别，要研究天赋，我们就要考察儿童技能的发展。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: It is evident that some children acquire skills more rapidly than others: the age of onset for walking and talking varies widely, even between children in the same household. Similar factors can influence musical development and can mask the contribution of genetics to musical ability.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The evidence against talent comes from research on how much training the experts do. Like experts in mathematics, chess, or sports, experts in music require lengthy periods of instruction and practice. In several studies, the very best music students were found to have practised more than twice as much as the others. In another study, students were secretly divided into two groups based on teachers’ perceptions of their talent. Several years later, it was found that the students who achieved the highest performance ratings had practised the most, irrespective of which talent group they had been assigned to, suggesting that practice does not merely correlate with achievement, but causes it.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Anders Ericsson, at Florida State University, approaches the topic of musical expertise as a general problem in cognitive psychology. He takes as a starting point the assumption that there are certain issues involved in becoming an expert at anything; that we can learn about musical expertise by studying expert chess players, athletes, artists, mathematicians, as well as the musicians themselves. The emerging picture from such studies is that ten thousand hours of practice is required to achieve the level of mastery associated with being a world-class expert — in anything. In study after study, of composers, ice-skaters, concert pianists, chess players and master criminals, this number comes up again and again. Someone would do this amount of practice if they practised, for example, roughly 20 hours a week for ten years. Of course, this does not address why some people do not seem to get anywhere when they practise, and why some people get more out of their practice sessions than others. But no-one has yet found a case in which true world-class expertise was accomplished in less time. It seems that it takes the brain this long to assimilate all that it needs to know to achieve true mastery.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 佛罗里达州立大学的 Anders Ericsson 把音乐专长视为认知心理学中的一个普遍问题来研究。他的出发点是这样一种假设：无论要成为哪一领域的专家，都会涉及某些共同问题；因此，我们不仅可以研究音乐家本人，也可以通过研究国际象棋高手、运动员、艺术家和数学家来了解音乐专长。这些研究逐渐呈现出的图景是：无论在哪个领域，要达到世界级专家所代表的精通水平，都需要练习1万小时。一项又一项针对作曲家、滑冰运动员、音乐会钢琴家、国际象棋棋手乃至犯罪高手的研究，都一再得出这个数字。例如，一个人如果连续10年每周练习约20小时，就能达到这一练习量。当然，这并没有解释为什么有些人练习了似乎仍毫无进展，也没有解释为什么有些人比另一些人从练习中收获更多。但到目前为止，还没有人发现真正的世界级专长能在更短时间内形成。看来，大脑需要这么长时间，才能吸收达到真正精通所需的全部知识。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The ten-thousand-hour theory is consistent with what we know about how the brain learns. Learning requires the assimilation and consolidation of information in neural tissue. The more experiences we have with something, the stronger the memory/learning trace for that experience becomes. blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The classic rebuttal to this theory goes something like this: What about Mozart? I hear that he composed his first symphony at the age of four! First, there is a factual error here: Mozart did not write it until he was eight. Still, this is unusual, to say the least. However, this early work received little acclaim and was not performed very often. In fact, the only reason we know about it is because the child who wrote it grew up to become Mozart. And Mozart had an expert teacher in his father, who was renowned as a teacher of musicians all over Europe. We do not know how much Mozart practised, but if he started at age two and worked thirty-two hours a week (quite possible, given that his father was a stern task-master) he would have made his ten thousand hours by the time he composed his first symphony. This does not mean that there are no genetic factors involved in Mozart’s greatness, but that inborn traits may not be the only cause.

source.text: When people are ‘deaf’ to music

translation.text: 当人们对音乐“失聪”时

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Music has long been considered a uniquely human concept. In fact, most psychologists agree that music is a universal human instinct. Like any ability, however, there is great variation in people’s musical competence. For every brilliant pianist in the world, there are several people we refer to as ‘tone deaf’. It is not simply that people with tone deafness (or ‘amusia’) are unable to sing in tune, they are also unable to discriminate between tones or recognize familiar melodies. Such a ‘disorder’ can occur after some sort of brain damage, but recently research has been undertaken in an attempt to discover the cause of congenital amusia (when people are born with the condition), which is not associated with any brain damage, hearing problems, or lack of exposure to music.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 长期以来，音乐一直被视为人类独有的概念。事实上，大多数心理学家都认同，音乐是人类普遍具有的一种本能。然而，与任何能力一样，不同人的音乐能力差异很大。世界上每有一位杰出的钢琴家，就有好几个人被我们称为“五音不全”。音调失聪的人，也就是患有“失歌症”的人，并非只是唱不准音；他们还无法分辨不同音调，也认不出熟悉的旋律。某种脑损伤可能引发这种“障碍”，但近来研究人员一直试图找出先天性失歌症的成因，也就是人一出生就有这种状况。先天性失歌症与任何脑损伤、听力问题或缺少音乐接触都没有关系。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: According to the research of Dr. Isabelle Peretz of the University of Montreal, amusia is more complicated than the inability to distinguish pitches. An amusic (a person who has the condition of amusia) can distinguish between two pitches that are far apart, but cannot tell the difference between intervals smaller than a half step on the Western diatonic scale, while most people can easily distinguish differences smaller than that. When listening to melodies which have had a single note altered so that it is out of key with the rest of the melody, they do not notice a problem. As would be expected, amusics perform significantly worse at singing and tapping a rhythm along with a melody than do non-amusics.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 根据蒙特利尔大学 Isabelle Peretz 博士的研究，失歌症比无法区分音高更为复杂。失歌症患者能够分辨相距较远的两个音高，却无法判断西方自然音阶中小于半音的音程差异，而大多数人很容易辨别比半音更小的差异。如果旋律中有一个音被改动，因而与其余旋律不在同一调上，他们也察觉不到问题。不出所料，在跟着旋律唱歌和打拍子方面，失歌症患者的表现明显不如非失歌症者。

translation.text: 失歌症患者能够分辨相距较远的两个音高，却无法判断西方自然音阶中小于半音的音程差异，而大多数人很容易辨别比半音更小的差异。

source.text: When listening to melodies which have had a single note altered so that it is out of key with the rest of the melody, they do not notice a problem.

translation.text: 如果旋律中有一个音被改动，因而与其余旋律不在同一调上，他们也察觉不到问题。

source.text: As would be expected, amusics perform significantly worse at singing and tapping a rhythm along with a melody than do non-amusics.

translation.text: 不出所料，在跟着旋律唱歌和打拍子方面，失歌症患者的表现明显不如非失歌症者。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: The most fascinating aspect of amusia is how specific to music it is. Because of music’s close ties to language, it might be expected that a musical impairment may be caused by a language impairment. Studies suggest, however, that language and music ability are independent of one another. People with brain damage in areas critical to language are often still able to sing, despite being unable to communicate through speech. Moreover, while amusics show deficiencies in their recognition of pitch differences in melodies, they show no such deficiencies in tonal languages. Amusics who speak tonal languages, such as Chinese, do not report having any difficulty discriminating between words that differ only in their intonation. The linguistic cues inherent in speech make discrimination of meaning much easier for amusics. Amusics are also successful most of the time at detecting the mood of a melody, can identify a speaker based on his or her voice and can discriminate and identify environmental sounds.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 失歌症最令人着迷之处，在于它仅针对音乐，具有很强的特异性。由于音乐与语言联系紧密，人们或许会以为音乐能力受损可能由语言能力受损引起。然而，研究表明，语言能力与音乐能力彼此独立。大脑中对语言至关重要的区域受损后，人即使无法通过言语交流，往往仍能唱歌。此外，失歌症患者虽然在辨认旋律中的音高差异时存在缺陷，但在声调语言中却没有这种缺陷。以汉语等声调语言为母语的失歌症患者，并未表示自己难以区分仅在声调上不同的词语。言语中固有的语言线索，使失歌症患者更容易辨别意义。大多数时候，他们也能成功判断旋律的情绪，能根据声音辨认说话者，还能区分和识别环境中的声音。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Recent work has been focused on locating the part of the brain that is responsible for amusia. The temporal lobes of the brain, the location of the primary auditory cortex, have been considered. It has long been believed that the temporal lobes, especially the right temporal lobe, are most active when engaged in musical activity, so any musical disability should logically stem from here as well. Because it has been shown that there is no hearing deficit in amusia, researchers moved on to the temporal neocortex, which is where more sophisticated processing of musical cues was thought to take place. New studies, however, have suggested that the deficits in amusics are located outside the auditory cortex. Brain scans of amusics do not show any reaction at all to differences smaller than a half step. When changes in tones are large, their brains overreact, showing twice as much activity on the right side of the brain as a normal brain hearing the same thing. These differences do not occur in the auditory cortex, indicating again that the deficits of amusia lie not in hearing impairment, but in higher processing of melodies.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: So what does this all mean? Looking only at the research of Peretz in the field of neuropsychology of music, it would appear that amusia is some sort of disorder. As a student of neurobiology, however, I am skeptical. Certainly the studies by Peretz that have found significant differences between the brains of so-called amusics and normal brains are legitimate. The more important question now becomes one of normality. Every trait from skin color to intelligence to mood exists on a continuum—there is a great deal of variation from one extreme to the other. Just because we recognize that basic musical ability is something that the vast majority of people have, this doesn’t mean that the lack of it is abnormal.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 那么，这一切意味着什么？如果只看佩雷茨在音乐神经心理学领域的研究，失歌症似乎是某种障碍。然而，作为一名神经生物学学生，我对此持怀疑态度。当然，佩雷茨的研究发现，所谓失歌症患者的大脑与正常大脑之间存在显著差异，这些研究是可信的。现在更重要的问题变成了：何谓正常。从肤色到智力再到情绪，每一种特征都存在于一个连续谱上——从一个极端到另一个极端之间差异巨大。尽管我们知道绝大多数人都具备基本音乐能力，却不能仅凭这一点就说缺少这种能力属于异常。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: What makes an amusic worse off than a musical prodigy? Musical ability is culturally valued, and may have been a factor in survival at one point in human history, but it does not seem likely that it is being selected for on an evolutionary scale any longer. Darwin believed that music was adaptive as a way of finding a mate, but who needs to be able to sing to find a partner in an age when it is possible to express your emotions through a song on your iPod?

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: While the idea of amusia is interesting, it seems to be just one end of the continuum of innate musical ability. Comparing this ‘disorder’ to learning disorders like a specific language impairment seems to be going too far. Before amusia can be declared a disability, further research must be done to determine whether lack of musical ability is actually detrimental in any way. If no disadvantages can be found of having amusia, then it is no more a disability than having poor fashion sense or bad handwriting.

passages.title: Who looks after the children in today's Britain

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: Who looks after the children in today's Britain
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 当今英国由谁照看孩子

source.text: Who looks after the children in today's Britain

translation.text: 当今英国由谁照看孩子

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: When Simon Baron-Cohen recently published a book, The Essential Difference, in which he claimed that the female brain is predominantly hard-wired for empathy, the male brain is predominantly hard-wired for understanding and building systems, he caught the mood of the moment. His team's experiments on day-old babies, and the finding that the male babies looked for longer at a hanging toy and the female babies longer at a face, has been repeatedly cited in the press since his book's publication. However, Elizabeth Spelke is one expert who is sceptical about whether this experiment deserves such attention. This is one isolated experiment, she says. 'Its findings fly in the face of dozens of studies on similar aspects of cognition carried out on young babies over decades. It is astonishing how much this one study has been cited, when the many studies that show no difference between the sexes, or a difference in the other direction, are ignored.'
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Simon Baron-Cohen 最近出版了《本质差异》（The Essential Difference）一书，声称女性大脑天生主要倾向于共情，男性大脑则天生主要倾向于理解和构建系统；这一观点正好迎合了当时的社会情绪。他的团队以出生仅一天的婴儿为对象进行实验，发现男婴注视悬挂玩具的时间更长，女婴注视人脸的时间更长。自该书出版以来，这一发现不断被媒体引用。然而，专家 Elizabeth Spelke 怀疑这项实验是否值得受到如此关注。她说，这只是一项孤立的实验。“它的发现与几十年来针对幼儿认知相似方面所做的数十项研究背道而驰。令人惊讶的是，这一项研究被引用了这么多次，而那些显示两性没有差异，或显示差异方向相反的众多研究却遭到忽视。”

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: One of Baron-Cohen's other main studies was conducted by collecting and examining responses to questionnaires completed by adults on their own behaviour: the sort of quiz well known to readers of magazines. The answers recorded in such cases will reflect differences formed by cultural assumptions and socialisation: it is hard to see what they tell us about innate differences. Nevertheless, they have become a fashionable reference point, and recently Princess Anne, patron of Women into Science and Engineering, gave a speech in which she quoted Baron-Cohen's research as proof that six out of ten men have a systemising brain. This kind of science has passed into everyday culture, often outrunning the intentions of those who did the original work.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 巴伦-科恩的另一项主要研究，是收集并分析成年人就自身行为填写的问卷答案；这类测验为杂志读者所熟知。在这种情况下，记录下来的答案会反映由文化假设和社会化过程形成的差异，很难看出它们能告诉我们什么有关先天差异的信息。尽管如此，这些研究已经成为时髦的参考依据。最近，“女性投身科学与工程”组织的赞助人安妮公主发表演讲，引用巴伦-科恩的研究来证明，每10名男性中有6人的大脑偏向系统化思维。这类科学已经进入日常文化，而且其传播常常超出了原研究者的本意。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Social expectations play heavily with young men and women, and expectations are in some ways more conventional in Britain today than they were ten or 20 years ago. It is particularly when they have children that women find out how society reinforces traditional expectations of their behaviour. They discover that many pressures - including the work schedule of their male partner and the expectations of his employer that it should be maintained - make it hard to combine work and home without giving their paid work a lower priority than their male colleagues do. blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Provine’s early discoveries can be summarized as follows: the yawn is highly stereotyped but not invariant in its duration and form. It is an excellent example of the instinctive fixed-action pattern of classical animal-behaviour study, or ethology. It is not a reflex (short-duration, rapid, proportional response to a simple stimulus), but, once started, a yawn progresses with the inevitability of a sneeze. The standard yawn runs its course over about six seconds on average, but its duration can range from about three seconds to much longer than the average. There are no half-yawns: this is an example of the typical intensity of fixed-action patterns and a reason why you cannot stifle yawns. Just like a cough, yawns can come in bouts with a highly variable inter-yawn interval, which is generally about 68 seconds but rarely more than 70. There is no relation between yawn frequency and duration: producers of short or long yawns do not compensate by yawning more or less often. Furthermore, Provine’s hypotheses about the form and function of yawning can be tested by three informative yawn variants which can be used to look at the roles of the nose, the mouth and the jaws.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Subjects are asked to clench their teeth when they feel themselves start to yawn but allow themselves to inhale normally through their open lips and clenched teeth. This variant gives one the sensation of being stuck mid-yawn. This shows that gaping of the jaws is an essential component of the fixed-action pattern of the yawn, and unless it is accomplished, the programme will not run to completion. The yawn is also shown to be more than a deep breath, because, unlike normal breathing, inhalation and exhalation cannot be performed so well through the clenched teeth as through the nose.

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: This variant tests the adequacy of the nasal airway to sustain a yawn. Unlike normal breathing, which can be performed equally well through mouth or nose, yawning is impossible via nasal inhalation alone. As with the clenched-teeth yawn, the nose yawn provides the unfulfilling sensation of being stuck in mid-yawn. Exhalation, on the other hand, can be accomplished equally well through nose or mouth. Through this methodology Provine demonstrated that inhalation through the oral airway and the gaping of jaws are necessary for normal yawns. The motor programme for yawning will not run to completion without feedback that these parts of the programme have been accomplished.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 这种变体用来检验鼻腔气道是否足以维持一个哈欠。正常呼吸通过口或鼻都能同样顺利地完成，打哈欠却不可能只靠鼻腔吸气完成。与咬紧牙关的哈欠一样，鼻吸哈欠也会带来一种无法满足的感觉，仿佛哈欠打到一半就卡住了。另一方面，呼气通过鼻或口都能同样顺利地完成。普罗文用这种方法证明，要正常打哈欠，必须通过口腔气道吸气，并张开双颌。如果没有反馈表明程序的这些部分已经完成，控制打哈欠的运动程序就不会运行到底。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: But yawning is a powerful, generalised movement that involves much more than airway manoeuvres and jaw-gaping. When yawning you also stretch your facial muscles, tilt your head back, narrow or close your eyes, produce tears, salivate, open the Eustachian tubes of your middle ear and perform many other, yet unspecified, cardiovascular and respiratory acts. Perhaps the yawn shares components with other behaviour. For example, is the yawn a kind of ‘slow sneeze’, or is the sneeze a ‘fast yawn’? Both share common respiratory and other features including jaw gaping, eye closing and head tilting.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 不过，打哈欠是一种强有力的全身性动作，远不只是对气道的控制和张开双颌。打哈欠时，人还会伸展面部肌肉、头向后仰、眯起或闭上眼睛、流泪、分泌唾液、打开中耳的咽鼓管，并进行许多其他尚未明确的心血管和呼吸活动。哈欠的某些组成动作或许也存在于其他行为中。例如，哈欠是否是一种“慢喷嚏”，或者喷嚏是一种“快哈欠”？二者共有呼吸和其他方面的特征，包括张开双颌、闭眼和头部后仰。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Yawning and stretching share properties and may be performed together as parts of a global motor complex. Studies by J. I. P. de Vries et al. in the early 1980s, charting movement in the developing foetus using ultrasound, observed a link between yawning and stretching. The most extraordinary demonstration of the yawn-stretch linkage occurs in many people paralysed on one side of their body because of brain damage caused by a stroke: the prominent British neurologist Sir Francis Walshe noted in 1923 that when these people yawn, they are startled and mystified to observe that their otherwise paralysed arm rises and flexes automatically in what neurologists term an ‘associated response’. Yawning apparently activates undamaged, unconsciously controlled connections between the brain and the motor system, causing the paralysed limb to move. It is not known whether the associated response is a positive prognosis for recovery, nor whether yawning is therapeutic for prevention of muscular deterioration.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 打哈欠和伸懒腰具有共同特征，也可能作为一套全身运动组合的组成部分同时发生。20世纪80年代初，J. I. P. de Vries 等人利用超声波绘制发育中胎儿的动作，观察到打哈欠与伸展身体之间存在联系。许多因中风所致脑损伤而出现半身瘫痪的人，最为惊人地展示了哈欠与伸展之间的联系：英国著名神经学家 Francis Walshe 爵士在1923年指出，这些人打哈欠时，会惊讶而困惑地看到原本瘫痪的手臂自动抬起并弯曲；神经学家把这称为“联合反应”。打哈欠显然会激活大脑与运动系统之间未受损且由无意识控制的连接，从而使瘫痪肢体活动起来。目前还不知道联合反应是否意味着康复前景良好，也不知道打哈欠能否起到防止肌肉退化的治疗作用。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Provine speculated that, in general, yawning may have many functions, and selecting a single function from the available options may be an unrealistic goal. Yawning appears to be associated with a change of behavioural state, switching from one activity to another. Yawning is also a reminder that ancient and unconscious behaviour linking us to the animal world lurks beneath the veneer of culture, rationality and language.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: 普罗文推测，总体而言，打哈欠可能具有多种功能，要从现有选项中选出一种单一功能，或许是不现实的目标。打哈欠似乎与行为状态的改变有关，也就是从一种活动转向另一种活动。它还提醒我们：在文化、理性和语言的表层之下，潜藏着把我们与动物世界联系起来的古老而无意识的行为。

source.text: The life of Beatrix Potter

translation.text: Beatrix Potter 的一生

headerUnits.sourceNormalizedText: The children’s author and illustrator who created Peter Rabbit
headerUnits.translationNormalizedText: 创造了彼得兔的儿童文学作家兼插画家

source.text: The children’s author and illustrator who created Peter Rabbit

translation.text: 创造了彼得兔的儿童文学作家兼插画家

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Beatrix Potter is one of the best-selling children’s authors of all time. Her popular series of books that includes The Tale of Peter Rabbit was first published over one hundred years ago, and has never been out of print. Generations of children have enjoyed her many stories and illustrations, all of which celebrate the English lifestyle and rural landscape through the adventures of animals.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Beatrix Potter 是有史以来最畅销的儿童文学作家之一。她广受欢迎的系列图书包括《彼得兔的故事》（The Tale of Peter Rabbit），一百多年前首次出版，此后从未绝版。一代又一代儿童都喜爱她创作的众多故事和插图；这些作品通过动物的冒险，赞颂英格兰的生活方式和乡村景观。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Born to a comfortable middle-class family in London in 1866, Potter spent much of her early life in her own company. She was educated in her parents’ house by a governess and rarely saw her brother Bertram, who was sent to boarding school. Having little social contact with children of her own age, Potter began to be drawn into her own world of writing. When Beatrix was 15, she began to keep a diary written in a secret code of her own invention. Even Beatrix herself, when she read back over it in later life, found it difficult to understand. It was not until 15 years after her death that the code was cracked. To the outside world Beatrix appeared a shy and reserved person, but in her diary she was able to express herself openly, and she was critical of the paintings of a number of artists of the day.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Potter 1866年出生在伦敦一个生活优裕的中产阶级家庭，早年大部分时间都独自度过。她在父母家中由家庭女教师授课；她的兄弟 Bertram 被送去寄宿学校，因此两人很少见面。由于很少与同龄孩子交往，Potter 开始沉浸在自己的写作世界中。15岁时，她开始用自己发明的密码写日记。就连 Beatrix 本人晚年重读时，也觉得难以理解。直到她去世15年后，这套密码才被破解。在外人眼中，Beatrix 显得害羞而拘谨，但在日记中，她能坦率表达自己，还批评了当时多位艺术家的画作。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: Potter was a naturally gifted artist, and with the aid of some art lessons she also learnt the technical side of drawing. During her childhood, she looked after many animals, such as rabbits, frogs, and even bats. She drew these animals throughout her childhood, gradually improving the standard of her work by sketching in museums. She was also interested in natural history. She would spend many hours drawing wildlife such as fungi and flowers, and at one time she had an ambition to develop this scientific interest. An uncle tried to help her become a student at the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew in London, but she was rejected because of her gender. Nevertheless, she achieved a measure of respect from the scientific establishment for her illustrations and contribution to mycology, the study of fungi.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Potter 天生具有艺术才华，借助一些美术课程，她也学到了绘画技法。童年时期，她照料过许多动物，例如兔子、青蛙，甚至蝙蝠。整个童年，她一直画这些动物，并通过在博物馆里写生，逐步提高作品水平。她还对自然史感兴趣，常常花许多小时描绘真菌和花卉等自然生物，也曾立志进一步发展这项科学兴趣。一位叔叔曾设法帮助她成为伦敦邱园皇家植物园（Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew）的学生，但她因性别而遭到拒绝。尽管如此，她的插图以及对真菌学，也就是研究真菌的学科所作的贡献，仍为她赢得了科学界一定程度的认可。

blocks.sourceNormalizedText: When Potter was in her early 20s, her parents tried to arrange a partner for her to marry. Many likely suitors were found: however, Potter turned them all down. She was a fiercely independent woman, and she disliked the idea of being tied down to a domestic life that, at that time, consisted mostly of staying at home and bringing up children. Thus, unusually for British women of those times, she remained single and lived in her parents’ home.
blocks.translationNormalizedText: Potter 20岁出头时，父母试图为她安排结婚对象。他们找到了许多看似合适的求婚者，Potter 却把所有人都拒绝了。她是一位极其独立的女性，不喜欢被家庭生活束缚；在当时，这种生活主要就是待在家中抚养孩子。因此，她与那个时代大多数英国女性不同，一直保持单身，住在父母家中。

source.text: Thus, unusually for British women of those times, she remained single and lived in her parents’ home.
